The spine is divided into several sections by raised bands and is richly decorated with <term>gold-tooling|the technique of pressing gold leaf into leather using heated brass stamps</term> featuring floral and <term>filigree|intricate, lace-like patterns</term> designs.

# Front Cover of a Leather-Bound Volume

->[Illustration of the front cover]<-

This manuscript is protected by a historical binding made of dark brown mottled leather, likely **calfskin**. The leather shows the distinct patina of age, with scuffing and surface loss visible at the corners and along the edges. The spine is divided into panels by five <term>raised bands|the horizontal ridges on a book's spine created by the cords used to sew the pages</term>, and each panel is richly embellished with <term>gold-tooling|the technique of pressing gold leaf into leather using heated brass stamps</term> in floral and <term>filigree|intricate, lace-like patterns</term> designs.

Centered on the front board is a prominent, gold-stamped owner's mark <note>original: "supralibros"</note>. This mark consists of a stylized **monogram** featuring the interlaced letters "A" and "H," identifying the original owner of the volume. The monogram is enclosed within an ornate, Baroque-style <term>cartouche|an oval or decorative frame with scrolled edges</term> composed of scrolled foliage and decorative flourishes. Traces of a delicate gold-tooled border are also visible running along the bottom edge of the board.

->centered text<- A Short Remembrance

# Of the Life and Conduct of JACOB BÖHME,
->centered text<- named *Teutonicus* <note>Latin: "The German." Böhme was known as the *Philosophus Teutonicus* because he wrote his profound mystical philosophy in his native German rather than Latin.</note> by the scholars hereafter.

Jacob Böhme was born in the year 1575 in Old Seidenburg, approximately two miles from Görlitz—a city located in <term>Upper Lusatia</term> <note>A historical region in what is now eastern Germany and western Poland.</note> that is highly renowned among learned men. He was fathered by Jacob and born to his mother Ursula, both of whom were poor peasant folk. In his youth, he herded cattle and was finally, upon the advice of his family, sent to school. There, alongside the "fear of God," he grasped the basics of reading and writing. Afterward, he was apprenticed to the shoemaking trade; in which, once he became a master in the year 1594, he also entered into marriage with the maiden Catharina, the legitimate daughter of Johann Kunschman, a butcher in Görlitz. He lived well and peacefully with her for 30 years and fathered four sons, whom he saw taught various trades.

This man, having been devoted to the "fear of God" <note>A phrase common in the 17th century describing a life of deep piety and reverence.</note> from his youth and having very gladly attended sermons, was finally awakened through the saying and promise of our Savior in **Luke 11, verse 13**: *The Father in heaven will give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him for it.* At the same time, he was moved by the diversity and conflict of religions—into which he could not fit himself—to pray, seek, and knock fervently and incessantly in simplicity of spirit in order to recognize the Truth. By this means, according to the Divine pull and will, he was translated in spirit into the **Holy SABBATH**; where, according to his own confession, he remained for seven whole days in the highest state of joy. When he afterward came back to himself and laid aside the folly of youth, he was

### Explanation of the Life and Conduct of J. B.

...he was driven by Divine zeal, such that he very vehemently rebuked shameful and blasphemous speech, and earnestly turned away from all dishonorable behavior out of a love for virtue. Because this way of life and his actions were so contrary to the ways of the world, he became only an object of their mockery and laughter. Meanwhile, he supported himself by the labor of his hands in the sweat of his brow, until, at the beginning of the sixth century <note>original: *VI. Seculi* (Latin). This refers to a millenarian or chronological period in Böhme’s mystical timeline.</note>—namely in the **Year 1600**—he was for a second time seized by Divine Light. Through a sudden glimpse of a pewter vessel, he was introduced into the innermost ground or <term>center</term> <note>original: *Centro* (Latin). In Böhme's philosophy, the "center" is the essential point from which all nature and spirit originate.</note> of secret nature. At this, because he did not trust his vision enough, he went out into the open fields and saw the wonder-works of the Creator revealed quite purely and clearly in the <term>signatures</term> <note>The "Doctrine of Signatures" is the belief that the outward appearance of things in nature reveals their hidden spiritual essence or "inner soul."</note> of all created things. He was overwhelmed with great joy at this, but remained silent, praised God, and for the time being let this be enough for him.

But according to God’s holy counsel, which conducts His work in secret, ten years later—namely in the **Year 1610**—he was touched and renewed by God for a third time through the overshadowing of the Holy Spirit. Consequently, because he had been so enlightened, and so that he would not let such great grace bestowed upon him slip from his memory, nor resist his God, he wrote at home for himself. He did this with few resources and was provided with no books at all, except for the Holy Scripture.

**Anno 1612.** He wrote his first book, *AURORA*, which means the <term>Day-Spring</term> <note>original: *AURORAM*, a Latin title meaning the dawn or the rising of the sun.</note>. When the author was accused because of it, this book was taken into custody at the town hall by the magistrate of Görlitz. They gave him an order that he, as an <term>idiot</term> <note>In the 17th century, "idiot" (from the Latin *idiota*) was not an insult to intelligence, but a technical term for a "layman"—someone without a formal university education or clerical rank.</note>, should henceforth abstain from such book-writing, as it did not befit his station. Following this, he paused for seven years; but afterward, when he was as if awakened again by the promptings of the Holy Spirit of God, and also urged and requested by several God-fearing people, he took up the pen again, continued writing, and produced his works with good leisure and deliberation.

<summary>This page recounts Jacob Böhme’s three spiritual illuminations, including the famous vision of the pewter vessel, and the legal suppression of his first book, Aurora, by the Görlitz authorities.</summary>

# Remembrance of the Life and Conduct of J. B.

For the following two entries, the year was not recorded.

29. A book on the error of the sects of Ezechiel Meths, addressed to A.P.A., or an Apology to Esaias Stiefel. <note>Esaias Stiefel and his nephew Ezechiel Meths were leaders of a perfectionist sect that Böhme critiqued for their views on the nature of Christ and the human soul.</note>
30. A book on the Last Judgment.

->There are more:<-

31. Letters to various persons, written at different times, with several <term>keys</term> <note>original: *Clavibus* (Latin). Böhme often used the term "key" to describe explanations or interpretive guides for his more "hidden" or obscure spiritual vocabulary.</note> regarding several hidden words.

(The books that the author did not bring to a completion are marked with this sign: ( ).)

By this, he has—to proclaim the honor of God and promote the salvation of mankind, for both present and future times—deposited such a dear and noble talent or pound <note>A reference to the Parable of the Talents (or Pounds) in the Gospels, suggesting that Böhme did not hide the spiritual "wealth" God gave him but invested it for others.</note> that since the time of the Apostles, more highly and deeply founded mysteries of the Godhead have hardly been revealed. He mostly maintained acquaintances with theologians and people experienced in the study of nature; with whom he associated—as well as with some of the nobility from Upper Lusatia and Silesia—in all fear of God. Although several common preachers, according to their custom, did not cease to pour out their poison against his writings and to disparage him with all sorts of blasphemy and calumnies among the foolish common folk: yet the truth lives and has overcome, and will finally triumph in secret.

But he, the blessed J. B. T. <note>Jacob Böhme Teutonicus, the name he often signed.</note>, passed away in Görlitz in his house located on the waters of the Neisse, in the year 1624, on the 18th day of the month of November, New Style <note>original: *S. N.* (Stilo Novo). The calendar had recently been reformed, and this notation distinguishes the date from the Old Style.</note>, at 6 o'clock in the morning. It was the 24th Sunday after Trinity. Having previously heard an exceedingly lovely music outside his chamber and having refreshed himself with the holy practice of the Testament of Christ in his Last Supper, amid the prayers and weeping of his sons and several good friends, with these last and comforting words—"Now I depart into Paradise"—sighing gently, he blessedly passed away in the 50th year of his age.

# Remembrance of the Life and Conduct of J. B.

[He was] buried in Görlitz, and upon the grave a wooden cross was placed, upon which a secret threefold figure was depicted as:
->An Eagle with a lily branch /<-
->A Lion with a sword /<-
->A Lamb with a bishop's mitre /<-
The inscription on the cross was this: **O.S.I.L.J.C.I.U.** <note>original: "V.H.I.L.I.C. I.V." standing for *Unser Heyl im Leben Jesu Christi in uns*.</note>—that is: Our Salvation in the Life of Jesus Christ in Us—which was J.B.’s motto or usual saying and inscription in his missives:
> Born of God,
> Died in Jesus,
> Sealed with the Holy Spirit:

Here rests **Jacob Böhme** of Old Seidenberg, etc.
(Note 1. The Southern Eagle, which stood upon a high rock and stepped with one foot upon a snake’s head, and with the other held a palm, received with its beak—offered from the sun—a lily branch. <note>The lily is a central symbol in Böhme's work, representing the "Lily-time," a future age of spiritual purity and peace.</note>
2. The Northern Lion was crowned and marked with a cross; he bore before him in his right hand a fire-flaming sword and in his left a fiery heart; he rested with his right foot (at the hip or hindquarters) upon a cube, and with the left upon a globe.
3. A Lamb with a bishop’s mitre walked beneath the two figures mentioned above upon the meadows, and by the streams of grace, quiet and simple.)
His seal or signet <note>original: *Pitschafft*</note> was a hand out of heaven, with a lily branch. In the friendship albums <note>original: *Stambücher*—common in the early modern period for collecting signatures and quotes from friends and scholars.</note> of good friends, he used to write these rhymes:
> To whom time is like eternity,
> And eternity like time,
> That man is freed from all strife.
His external physical form had almost no distinguished appearance (or adornment); he was small and thin in person, with an almost sunken forehead, prominent temples, and a somewhat crooked or hawk-nose. His eyes were grayish and almost sky-blue, otherwise like

<meta>This page continues the physical description of Jacob Böhme from the previous page and provides an account of his death on November 18, 1624, based on the records of Michael Curtz.</meta>

...the windows of Solomon's Temple <note>This is a metaphorical description of Böhme's eyes, suggesting they were deep and full of spiritual light.</note>: He had a thin and short beard: A quiet voice: A lovely way of speaking. Was modest in gestures, humble in conduct, and gentle of heart. His spirit, highly enlightened by God, can be recognized from his writings in the Divine Light, etc.

From a record made by M. C. <note>original: "M. C."—likely Michael Curtz, a contemporary and biographer of Böhme.</note>, the following is taken:

->Concerning what occurred at the end of the blessed J. B.<-

On Sunday (the 18th of November) early in the morning, he called his son Tobias and asked whether he also heard the beautiful music? When the son said "No," Böhme said that the door should be opened so that the singing could be heard better. Afterward, he asked what time it had struck; when they answered that it had struck two, he said: "That is not yet my time; in three hours is my time." In the meantime, he spoke these words once:

> O thou strong God of Sabaoth <note>original: "Zebaoth"—a Hebrew title for God meaning "Lord of Hosts."</note>, save me according to thy will. O thou crucified Lord Jesus Christ, have mercy on me and take me into thy kingdom!

When it was hardly six o'clock, he took leave of his wife and son, blessed them, and spoke thereafter: "Now I journey hence into Paradise." He told his son to turn him over, and he sighed deeply and passed away quite gently and quietly from this world.

### On the death of the Author.

Nysiad Muses <note>original: "Nissiades Musæ"—nymphs of Mount Nysa, often associated with the upbringing of Dionysus; here they are invoked in a classical poetic style to lead the mourning.</note>, if any of you do not have hearts of iron, hasten here quickly, and redouble with me the sad lament, which strikes the stars with pitiful wailing. Who will stop the tears for the mourners, and block the fountains of sorrow? Who will turn the blind omens toward something better?

Behold, fierce Autumn, who strips the fields of grass and the groves of their leaves, and the woods of their beauty, brings too-sad fates to the wretched, and stirs up complaints while the urn snatches away such a man as you, Jacob—O Böhme, an honor, and recognized by the few better souls. Therefore I shall place my limbs beneath the sad Cypress tree, singing sad songs to you with a complaining voice, O father Böhme, and the greatest part of our life.

I will not boast of an ancient lineage or a more noble family tree, which the world loves and descendants brag about: for under a father who was a farmer <note>original: "Agricola"—referring to Böhme’s father, George Böhme, who was a peasant/farmer.</note>, even such a poor mother brought you forth into the breezes of light. What wonder is there? For it is not this worldly noble lineage that pleases; piety is the whole lineage and family tree of the good. This piety accompanied you as a boy and youth and right through to old age; through this you will live, illustrious among the mindful, after death.

Who taught the boy? A learned schoolmaster? <note>original: "Ludinè Magister"—a play on the Latin term "ludi magister" for a primary school teacher.</note> What school made you so? Was it the refined Lyceums? Or Plato the Philosopher, or any more recent Sage? You were stuck in the smallest tasks, and in the lowest dust, scorned, you handled the work of your hands <note>A reference to Böhme’s career as a shoemaker, a "manual" trade traditionally looked down upon by the academic elite.</note>: But that your holy writings are now read everywhere upon the wide earth was the work of Him alone, by whom all pride is despised, and who loves the humble, preparing praises from the mouths of children and gifts of tongues pleasing to Himself in the lowest places.

On earth three sons survive you from one wife, but I doubt whether your three male offspring or your writings will extend your life further into the ages.

*What God and powerful Nature are, what Earth and Heaven are,*
*Angel and Satan, what Man is, what the gates of the Abyss <note>original: "Barathri"—a Greek-derived Latin term for a deep pit or the underworld.</note> are,*
*And by what way the wretched go to Christ, and by what path one must travel—*
*All these you taught by divine warning and guidance.*

Satan opposed you in vain: because the right hand of the Mighty...

# Preface.

<note>The page begins mid-sentence, continuing a thought on how the visible emerged from the invisible.</note> ...from the comprehensible has come the visible comprehensible, which arose from the expression or the breathing-out of the invisible **Power**; the invisible **Spiritual Word** of the **Divine Power** works with and through the visible **Being** <note>original: "Wesen"—this refers to the essence or fundamental nature of reality.</note>, just as the soul works with and through the body.

5. The inner spiritual **Soul-Man** was spoken into the visible image through the "in-speaking" <note>original: "Einsprechen"—a key concept in Böhme’s thought where God ‘speaks’ the soul into the body.</note> or breathing-into from the invisible **Word** of the **Divine Power**. This was done to give the created image understanding, wherein man's <term>science<note>original: "Scienz"—from the Latin *scientia*, meaning structured knowledge or divine insight.</note></term> and recognition of the invisible and visible Being resides.

6. Thus, man has now received the authority from the invisible **Word of God** to "speak-back" <note>original: "wideraußsprechen"—to echo or re-articulate God's creative act.</note>, so that he speaks the hidden Word of the **Divine Science** out again into formations and distinctions, in the manner of temporal creatures. He forms that same **Spiritual Word** according to living and growing things, whereby the invisible **Wisdom of God** is modeled into distinct formations through this shaping. This is evident before our eyes: that human understanding speaks out all powers in their specific property <note>original: "Eigenschafft"—a technical term for the inherent qualities or "signatures" of a thing.</note> and gives names to all things according to the property of each. Through this, the hidden **Wisdom** is recognized and understood in its power, and the hidden **God** becomes manifest along with invisible things, as a play of the **Divine Power**, so that the invisible with the

# THE GREAT MYSTERY,
<note>original: *Mysterio Magno* — the title of Böhme's commentary on the first book of Moses (Genesis), exploring the hidden spiritual meaning behind the creation story.</note>

->That is<-

## Concerning the Revelation of the Divine Word / through the Three Principles of the Divine Essence.

### The 1st Chapter.

->What the revealed God is / and concerning the Trinity.<-

1. If we wish to understand the **New Birth** <note>original: *Newgeburt* — a central concept in Böhme’s theology referring to the spiritual transformation and regeneration of a person through divine grace</note>: what it is and how it happens: We must first know what man is, and how he is **God's image** <note>Referring to the biblical concept in Genesis 1:26-27</note>, and how the Divine inhabits him; Also what the revealed God is, of whom man is an image.

<image-desc>A vertical bracket consisting of five small braces or pointers on the right margin, highlighting the text describing the nature of God in the second paragraph.</image-desc>
</margin>
2. When I consider: what God is, I say: He is the **One** <note>original: *das Eine*</note> in contrast to the creature, as an **Eternal Nothing** <note>original: *Ewig Nichts* — Böhme uses this term to describe God's state before any creation or manifestation; it is a "nothing" that contains the potential for everything</note>; He has neither ground, beginning, nor place; and possesses nothing but only Himself: He is the **will of the unground** <term>Unground (Ungrund): Böhme’s term for the absolute, bottomless abyss of the divine nature that exists before any form, thought, or creation</term>; He is in Himself only One: He requires no space nor location: He generates Himself within Himself from eternity to eternity. He is like or similar to no thing, and has no particular place where He dwells: The **Eternal Wisdom** or understanding is His dwelling: He is the Will of Wisdom, and Wisdom is His revelation.

3. In this eternal generation, we are to understand three things: As 1. an Eternal Will. 2. An Eternal Mind of the will. 3. The proceeding from the will and mind, which is a Spirit of the will and mind.

4. The **Will** is Father: the **Mind** is that which is conceived by the Will as the Will’s seat or dwelling, or the Center toward **Something** <note>original: *Etwas*</note>, and is the Will’s Heart; and the proceeding from the Will and Mind is the Power and the **Spirit**.

5. This threefold Spirit is a single essence / and yet He is no essence, but rather the Eternal Understanding / An understanding of the **Something** <term>Ichts: A Böhmean wordplay on *Nichts* (Nothing); it represents the first stirring of "Something" or "I-ness" emerging from the void</term>, and is yet the eternal hiddenness, just as the understanding of man is not graspable or in time, or in place, but is itself its own graspability and seat; and the outgoing of the Spirit is the eternal, understandable contemplation as a **Delight** <note>original: *Lust* — in Böhme’s usage, this signifies a holy joy or the divine "pleasure" to manifest</note> of the Spirit.

6. That which has proceeded is called the Delight of the Godhead or the **Eternal Wisdom**, which is the eternal understanding of all power, colors, and virtue, through which the threefold Spirit becomes desiring in this Delight, namely of the power, colors, and virtue; and His desiring is an *impressen* <note>original Latin/German: *impressen* — to imprint, compress, or conceive</note>, a grasping of Himself: the Will grasps the Wisdom into the Mind, and that which is grasped in the understanding is the

## The 2nd Chapter.

### Concerning the Word or Heart of God.

1. This is now what **St. John** says in the 1st Chapter / In the beginning was the Word / and the Word was with God / and God was the Word / the same was in the beginning with God. # Concerning the Word or Heart of God.
A 2
<meta>catchword: will be /</meta>

<margin>Chapter 2</margin> Now take that same light of life, which was in the Word and is eternal, and behold the **Essence of all essences** <note>original: *Wesen aller Wesen* — Böhme uses this to describe God as the fundamental reality or "beingness" underlying all physical and spiritual things</note>, and especially yourself, for you are the image, life, and essence of the groundless Divine, and a likeness after Him. Consider here time and eternity, heaven, hell, and the world, light and darkness, pain and torment, life and death, **Something and Nothing** <note>original: *Ichts vnd Nichts* — "Ichts" is Böhme’s invented term for "something," created to contrast perfectly with "Nichts" (nothing)</note>: Examine yourself here, whether you have the life and light of the Word within you, so that you may see and understand all things. For your life was in the Word, and has become manifest in the image (which God created): it was breathed into him by the Spirit of the Word. Now raise your understanding in the light of your life, and behold the formed Word; consider its inner birthing, for in the light of life everything stands revealed.

3. Do you say: "I cannot; I am corrupt"? Hear then: you are not yet born again out of God; otherwise, if you had that same light again, you would be able. Well then, we all surely lack the glory that we should have in God, but I will show you something: only pay attention and grasp it; do not be a scorner, like the confused **Babel** <note>original: *Babel* — used by Böhme to represent the confusion of competing religious dogmas and worldly "Reason" that lacks spiritual insight</note>. See, when we wish to speak of the essence of all essences, we say: all things are from God and through God. For St. John also says: Without Him nothing was made that was made.

4. Now **Reason** <term>Reason (Vernunfft): In this context, the limited human intellect that tries to understand divine mysteries through logic alone, without spiritual illumination</term> says: Out of what, or how, did God make good and evil, pain and torment, life and death? Is there then such a will in God that makes evil? Here Reason begins to speculate and wants to grasp it, but she only goes around the circle from the outside and cannot enter in, for she is outside, and not within the circle of the Word of life.

5. So look now at yourself, what you are, and look at the outer world with its governance, what it is: thus you will find that you, with your outer spirit and essence, are the outer world. You are a small world out of the large one; your outer light is a **Chaos** <note>original: *Chaos* — the primordial "yawning void" or source-potential containing all the energies of the sun and stars</note> of the sun and the stars; otherwise you could not see by the sunlight. The stars provide the essence of distinction in intelligible sight. Your body is fire, air, water, earth; therein also lies the metallic property; for that of which the sun and the stars are the spirit, the earth and the other elements are the essence—a **coagulated power** <note>original: *Coagulirte Krafft* — the idea that physical matter is simply spiritual energy that has slowed down and "thickened" or solidified</note>. That which is above is also that which is below, and all creatures of this world are the same.

6. When I pick up and look at a stone or a clod of earth, I see the above and the below, yes, the whole world within it; only that in every thing, one property or another is the greatest, after which it is also named. The other properties all lie within it as well, only in different degrees and centers, and yet all degrees and centers are but a single center; there is but a single root from which everything comes; it only divides itself in the **compaction** <note>original: *Compaction* — the process of becoming dense or solid</note>, where it coagulates.

10. Therefore, nothing is far from God or near to Him. One world is within the other, and all are but the **One**. ### The Third Chapter.

#### How an evil arose out of the Eternal Good, which has no beginning for evil within the good; and of the origin of the dark world or hell, in which the devils dwell.

1. Since, then, light and darkness occurred in the outer world, along with pain and torment—and yet all of it originates from the **Eternal Mystery**, as from the inner spiritual world, and the inner spiritual world originates from the eternally birthing and speaking Word—so we must now consider: How does an evil arise out of the Eternal Good, which yet has no beginning for evil within the Good? From where do darkness, pain, and torment arise? And then, from where does a radiance or light arise within the darkness?

2. For we cannot say that the Eternal Light or the Eternal Darkness was created, otherwise they would exist within a time and within a contained beginning, which is not the case. For they are part of the birthing, yet not within the Wisdom or the birthing of the Word of the Godhead; rather, they take their <term>origin</term><note>original: *vhrstandt* (Urstand) — Böhme's term for the primordial foundation or pre-condition of a thing.</note> in the <term>desire</term><note>original: *Begierde* — In Böhme's thought, Desire is the fundamental attractive force that causes spiritual energy to contract and become manifest or material.</note> of the speaking Word.

3. For in the eternally speaking Word—which is outside of all nature or beginning, being only the divine understanding or sound—there is neither darkness nor light, neither thick nor thin, neither joy nor sorrow, nor any sensibility or perception; but it is simply a power of the understanding in a <term>source-condition</term><note>original: *Qual* — Böhme uses this word not only to mean 'torment' but also to mean 'quality' or the 'welling up' of a force (connected to the German *Quelle* for source and *Qualität* for quality).</note>, will, and dominion. It has neither friend nor enemy, for it is the Single Good, and nothing more.

4. Since, then, that same Eternal Good cannot be an unfeeling being (for then it would not be manifest to itself), it leads itself within itself into a delight toward its own self-beholding or seeing what it is, in which delight stands the **Wisdom**. And when the delight thus sees what it is, it leads itself into a desire to sense what it is—such as to a feeling of scent, taste, colors, powers, and virtue—and yet no sensation could arise in the free spiritual delight if it did not lead itself into a desire (like a hunger).

It is a terrible anguish within itself, and yet here no "true feeling" is yet understood until the Fire. ## Chapter 4.

1. In this shock or ignition of fire, two realms separate, and yet they are only one; but they divide in essence, quality <term>Qual</term> <note>Böhme uses this word to imply both a "source" (*Quelle*) and "torment" or "tension" (*Qual*), describing the active forces of nature.</note>, and will. 3. The upper Cross signifies the unformed Word in the Trinity <note>Böhme frequently uses geometric symbols to explain the nature of God before creation. 5. Therefore, the great angle <note>original: *Angel* — In Böhme's writing, this can mean both "angle" (referring to the points of the triangle) and "hook" or "hinge." This now indicates to us true yieldedness <term>Gelassenheit</term> <note>A central concept in German mysticism, meaning a state of letting go, surrender to God, and inner serenity.</note> under the **T**: where we are born anew in the light in the Spirit of Christ through the great humility of God.

And the shock in the re-conception toward the free desire <note>original: *Lust* — In Böhme's vocabulary, this is a neutral term for a longing or "delight" that seeks to manifest.</note> becomes the highly-triumphing Divine realm of joy within that free desire. For thus the free desire becomes elevating, and is led into a wrestling play of love; and thus it becomes active and working.

8. Now, however, with the ignition of the fire, we are to understand two kinds of fire, two kinds of spirit, and two kinds of essence: namely, a love-fire in the free desire, which becomes substantial through the impression <note>original: *Impression* — This refers to the first property of nature: a contracting, pulling force that "compacts" spirit into substance.</note> or longing; and in the fire, spirit and essence divide, and yet they are within one another, just as spirit and body are one. And as the spirit is, so also is that same essence. And as there is a holy, sweet essence and a holy, sweet spirit in the impression of the free desire: so also in the dark impression there is a harsh, stern, raw, and bitter essence and spirit. As the essence is, so also is the mind of the understanding and the will within that essence.

For the will introduces itself into substance and essence for this reason: so that it may be manifest to itself.

10. Now we must consider the distinctness within the Fire: when the Fire ignites, the fire-flash or shock is salnitric <note>original: *Salnitrisch*—a term Böhme uses to describe the explosive, sulfurous, and saltpeter-like quality of the initial spiritual ignition.</note> where all powers yield from one another and enter into division; there, the Eternal, One Power of God manifests itself and divides into distinct qualities, both spiritual and substantial, as can be seen in this world. Then the various Salts originate: which, with the Creation, entered into such materials—which in Eternity was only a Spiritual Being, but with the beginning of time became coarse and hard.

11. From this eternal root also originate the various spirits, both good and evil, as well as the various stars along with the four elements and everything that lives and moves. But the division within itself is to be understood by us thus: When the flash rises, the separation goes out from the Fire; the fire-shock is devouring, it attacks the grasped being—both that which is in the free desire <note>original: *freyenlust*</note> and that which is in the harshness—and devours it instantly. For here in the Fire, the Eternal Will, which is a "No-Ground" <term>Ungrund</term> <note>The *Ungrund* is Böhme’s term for the absolute, bottomless void or the primal nature of God before any manifestation or "grounding" occurs.</note>, becomes manifest; before it no being may stand; It swallows everything into its Nothingness.

12. And here is the origin of Eternal Death or devouringness; and within this devouring is the highest Arcanum <note>original: *Arcanum*—a secret or hidden mystery.</note> or secret: for the true substantial living spirit and understanding proceeds out of this devouringness and makes another beginning. For the first beginning is God’s, who leads Himself from the "No-Ground" into a "Ground" for His own contemplation. But this beginning which goes out again from the devouring is a spiritual beginning, and yields three worlds: first, the dark Fire-World in heat and cold, <margin><image-desc>A small circular symbol with a cross and radiating lines, possibly representing a world or a spiritual principle.</image-desc></margin> a total harshness without substance; second, the other world is the Spiritual Light-World or Angelic World; 3. and the third has taken its beginning with the start of time. When God moved both inner worlds, He then brought forth and created this outer visible world from them, into the form of a Time.

13. Now, however, the division in the Fire of devouring is to be understood thus: The powers which the first Impression had made substantial are introduced into spirituality in the Fire. As I: out of the free desire goes forth a Spiritual Mystery—which is according to the Godhead as a spiritual Eternal understanding—and it is the Angelic life and light, as well as the true human life, and everything that resembles them, for they are the powers of God. Therefore the Angels bear the great Name of God within them, as do also the righteous humans who possess the Divine power.

14. II. # Chapter 5.
## Of the Five Senses.

->Love Fire Venus.<- <note>Venus is used here as the alchemical and astrological symbol for Love, the fifth property in Böhme’s system.</note>

1. The fifth form or quality is the Love-Desire, as the Holy Life or the unfolded Light-fire. This takes its awakening or receives its beginning in the fierce, consuming Fire; that is, it becomes visible out of the fire, just as we see in the likeness of all outward fires: the light originates in the fire, but it has a completely different quality <note>original: *qual*</note> than the fire. 2. The fire gives light and air, and from air comes water because of the gentleness of the light. For the Delight <note>original: *Lust*—The primal will or joy of the Groundless.</note> for the fire has died in the fire-flash. Thus, that which has died in the fire is a gentle being, yet only as a spirit. But when it proceeds from the fire in the light, it coagulates; then it is a "death" of the fire, by which the fire is extinguished. However, as long as it remains in the nature of a spirit, it is the fire’s food and refreshment. We see this before our eyes: every burning fire gives off an air, and from the air, a water. This air, together with the water-spirit, the fire draws back into itself for its life and luster. Otherwise, if it cannot reach this, it goes out—that is, it suffocates—for the air is its life, and yet the fire itself gives birth to it.

The animal nature is nearly equal to the Abyss <note>original: *Abgrunde* — Böhme's term for the *Ungrund*, the "groundless" nothingness from which God emerges.</note>; we are to understand the resonance of darkness in the same way. We recognize that God in His own essence is not an "essence" <note>original: *Wesen* — being, substance, or essence.</note>, but merely the Power or the Understanding toward essence, like a groundless eternal Will in which everything lies. He is Himself All and yet only One, but He desires to manifest Himself and lead Himself into a Spiritual Essence, which occurs through the fire in the desire-of-love within the power of the Light.

2. Yet, the true Divine Essence (understand here the "essence" and not the Spirit of God) is nothing other than the manifested Understanding, or the formation of the powers. It stands in desire—that is, in the desire-of-love—wherein one power recognizes the other in taste, smell, feeling, seeing, and hearing, within the essence and quality of that property. From this, the great, longing desire arises. Within these properties, the manifested God is understood as being in a fiery flame of love-desire, wherein there is nothing but pleasant tasting, pleasant smelling, joyful hearing, lovely and friendly seeing, and soft well-being or feeling. Yet it is only a Spiritual Essence, where only the powers—which have introduced themselves into a specific quality through "impression" <note>original: *impression* — the "contraction" or "thickening" of spiritual force into something more solid.</note> and were manifested by the fire in the light—wrestle in and with one another in a play of love. This is like a lovely song or a birthing harmony, full of joy. This is therefore only the Spirit-Essence of the manifested God, as the powerful, all-essential Word manifests itself out of itself in its own self-birthing; within this, the Play of Divine Wisdom <note>original: *Weißheit* — Böhme often identifies "Wisdom" (Sophia) as the mirror or "playmate" of God.</note> is understood.

### I. Form/Astringency/Desire.

14. See, the desire of the eternal Word—which is God—is the beginning of eternal nature. It is the comprising <note>original: "Fassung" — the act of grasping or giving form to something abstract</note> of the eternal Nothing into Something. It is the cause of all beings, as well as of cold and heat, of water and air; it is the forming of the powers and a cause of taste—the mother of all salts <note>In alchemy and Böhme's thought, "Salt" represents the principle of physical substance and stability.</note>.

### II. Form/Bitter/Stinging.

15. The mobility of the desire, acting as attraction, is the second form of nature. It is a cause of all life and movement, as well as of the senses and the ability to distinguish between things.

### III. Form/Anguish/Sensibility.

16. The anguish <note>original: "Angst" — here meaning the mechanical tension or friction created when the first two forces (contraction and movement) collide</note>, as sensitivity, is a cause of the mind, wherein the senses become active.

### IV. Form/Fire/Spirit/Reason/Desire.

17. The fire is a cause of the true spiritual life, where the holy powers of the free pleasure <note>original: "freyen Lust" — the divine will's desire to manifest joy</note> are released from the harsh roughness. For the fire, in its essence, swallows the dark substance of the impression <note>term: <term>Impression</term> (the spiritual "compression" of energy into dense matter)</note> and leads it out of itself, transforming it into spiritual powers within the light.

### V. Form/Light/Love.

18. The holy spiritual love-desire occurs where the holy will of God has sharpened itself in the strict impression and revealed itself through the fire with the power of omnipotence. It now leads itself through the fire into the light and has thus introduced itself into the powers, into life, and into movement within the desire. Within this stands the holy birthing and the kingdom of joy of the great love of God, and here it is revealed.

### VI. Form/Sound/Reverberation/Word.

19. This is the sound of the Divine Word coming out of the Divine powers, which forms itself within the love-desire and introduces itself into a resonant Word of all powers. Within this stands the revelation of the Divine kingdom of joy in the free pleasure of the Wisdom of God.

### VII. Form/Essence/Casing.

20. 22. Gentle reader, understand the meaning rightly and well: it does not mean that the seven properties are divided, or that one exists alongside the other, or one before the other. All seven are only as one, and none is the first, second, or last; for the last is again the first. Just as the first leads itself into a spiritual essence, so the last leads into a bodily essence; the last is the first body. One must only speak in "piece-work" <note>original: "stückwerck" — a reference to 1 Corinthians 13, meaning human knowledge is fragmentary and incomplete</note> so that it can be written and depicted for the senses of the reader to contemplate; they are all together only the revelation of God, according to Love and Wrath, according to eternity and time.

23. But this is well to be noted: that every property is also substantial. In the Kingdom of Heaven, that same essence is among one another as one being, and is a **Mystery** <note>original: "Mysterium" — Böhme uses this to describe a hidden, chaotic "womb" or source from which specific realities grow</note>, out of which heavenly growths sprout from every power and property. Just as the earth is a **mystery** of all trees and herbs, as well as of grass and worms; and the four elements are a **mystery** of all living things; and the stars are a **mystery** of all operations in the living and growing.

24. Every property is substantial for itself, and in its essence also possesses the essence of the other six forms; it makes the essence of the other forms substantial within its own essence. We see this in earth and stones, and especially in metals, where often in one **solidification** <note>original: "Compaction" — the alchemical process of spiritual forces hardening into physical matter</note> all seven metals are found within one another...

### Chapter 7.

### On the Holy Trinity and Divine Being.

Eternal and also temporal Nature is primarily understood through the dark world and fire-world: as in the first 4 Forms / namely 1. in the harsh Desire / 2. in the bitter stinging / 3. in Anguish or Sensibility / 4. in Fire where, in the ignition within the Terror, the separation <note>original: "Scheidung" — the point where light and dark or different properties split apart</note> goes forth; the Powers, however / both in the inner and outer world / are all understood in the light-fire or love-fire as in the love-desire.

2. For their first Ground is the eternal Word / as the One / in which everything lies: The second Ground is the free Longing <note>original: "Lust" — in Böhme's usage, this refers to a divine "pleasure" or "inclination" that initiates creation</note> of the Word / as Wisdom, where all the colors of the single Power are manifest in the Will of the Deity: The 3rd Ground is the love-Desire / where the free Longing, with its colors and virtues of the powers, has sharpened itself through Nature / and through the ignition of the Fire has been led into a Spiritual Government / which carries itself out in the light with the powers in an eternal Kingdom of Joy.

3. The 4th Ground is the *Olic* <note>term: <term>Olic</term> (from "Oleum" or oil; Böhme uses this to describe the "oil" of the light-fire which provides the mildness or fuel for the divine light)</note>, in which the free Longing in the fiery love-desire captures itself in Gentleness as in its own Form / and captures the Fire's and Light's luster and essence with it / and leads it into the first Being; which Power from the Fire and Light in the Gentleness of the free Longing in the *Delic* <note>term: <term>Delic</term> (likely referring to "Delos" or clarity; Böhme's term for the manifest, clear spiritual essence)</note> Property is the true and holy Tincture <note>term: <term>Tincture</term> (the highest medicinal or spiritual essence that can transform or "tinge" other substances)</note>.

4. The 5th Ground is the watery one from the dying-away in the Fire / where the first Spiritual Being in the harsh, stern, dark Desire was consumed in the Fire. So now, out of the consumability of the Fire, there goes forth a Spiritual Being / that is the *Delic* Ground / and a watery Being / out of the deathliness which takes the Wrath <note>original: "Grimm" — the fierce, burning quality of the divine fire</note> away from the fire-spirit / so that it may not ignite itself in its wrathful properties in the *Delic* Ground / so that the Fire must burn through death and be only a Light / otherwise the *Delic* Ground would be ignited; thus the Fire in its consumability must give birth to the Water as its death / and yet must also have it again for its life: otherwise neither the Fire nor the Light could subsist / and thus it is an eternal birthing / consuming and taking again / and consuming; and yet also thus eternally given / and is no beginning nor end.

He introduces the "Olic" and "Delic" grounds to explain how the fierce wrath of the divine fire is tempered into a holy, life-giving light.</summary>

-># On the Holy Trinity.<-

5. Thus we now understand what God and his **Essence** <note>original: "Wesen" — refers to the fundamental being or substance of God</note> are. We Christians say: God is **Triune**, but one in Essence. However, what is commonly said—that God is three persons—is often misunderstood by the unlearned and even by some scholars. For God is not a "person" except in Christ; rather, He is the **Eternally Birthing Power**, and the Kingdom together with all Essence: everything takes its **origin** <term>Vhrstandt: a primordial origin or "foundational standing"</term> from Him.

6. That which is said of God—that He is **Father, Son, and Holy Spirit**—is quite correctly said, but it must be explained; otherwise, the unenlightened mind cannot grasp it. The Father is, first of all, the **Will of the Abyss** <note>original: "Vngrundes" — the Groundless or Abyss; Böhme’s term for the absolute, undifferentiated nothingness before creation</note>. He is, outside of all nature or beginnings, the Will to the **Something** <note>original: "Ichts" — a term Böhme coined to contrast with "Nichts" (nothing); it represents the first move toward existence</note>, which conceives itself into a **Longing** <note>original: "Lust" — can mean pleasure, delight, or a divine inclination</note> for its own self-revelation.

7. And this Longing is the conceived power of the Will or the Father, and is his **Son, Heart, and Seat**, the first eternal beginning within the Will. He is called a **Son** because He takes an eternal beginning within the Will, through the Will’s own act of conceiving itself.

8. So the Will now expresses itself out of itself through this conceiving, as an **out-breathing** or **revelation**. And this same outgoing from the Will in the speaking or breathing is the **Spirit of the Deity**, or the third person, as the ancients have named it.

9. And that which is breathed out is **Wisdom**, acting as the power of the colors and the virtue of the Will. The Will conceives this Wisdom into a **Life-Center** or **Heart** for its eternal dwelling, and from that conception—as from its eternal form—it speaks it out again eternally, yet also eternally conceives it back into the Center of its Heart.

10. Thus, the conceiving of the Will as the Father is from eternity to eternity; He conceives his speaking **Word** from eternity to eternity, and speaks it out from eternity to eternity. This **Speaking** is the mouth of the Will’s revelation, and the outgoing from the speaking or birthing is the **Spirit** of the formed Word, and that which is spoken is the power, colors, and virtue of the Deity, known as **Wisdom**.

<note>The following paragraph is marked with a large curly bracket in the left margin.</note>
11. Here one can say with no rational ground that God is three persons; rather, He is **Threefold** in his eternal birthing. He births himself in Trinity, and yet in this eternal birthing, only a single Essence and birthing is to be understood—neither Father, Son, nor Spirit, but the **one eternal Life or Good**.

12. The Trinity is only truly understood in his **eternal revelation**: specifically when He reveals himself through eternal nature, through the **fire** in the **light**.

13. There, one understands three properties in a single essence: namely the **Father** with the **fire-world**, and the **Son** with the **love-desire** in the light (as with the **light-world**, or with the great **gentleness** within the fire), and the

He introduces the concept of the Ungrund (Abyss) and explains how God moves from nothingness to self-revelation through Wisdom and the interplay of Fire and Light.</summary>

In the fire He is called a **wrathful God**; but in the light or the fire of love, He is called the **Holy God**; and in dark nature, He is called **not-God**.

15. One must maintain a distinction: each world has its own **Principle** <term>Principium: the foundational beginning or ruling power of a particular realm</term> and governance. Although everything comes from one **primordial origin** <term>Vhrstandt: Böhme's term for the original source from which all things 'stand forth'</term>, it separates into two kinds of **quality** <note>original: "Qual" — Böhme uses this word to mean both a 'quality' and 'pain/torment,' suggesting that existence itself involves a kind of tension</note>, just as we see a likeness in fire and light: where the fire is painful and consuming, and the light is gentle and giving; yet one would be nothing without the other.

16. 17. Though I have written here of the **forms of nature** (meaning the eternal ones), it should not be understood as if the Godhead were confined by limit or measure; His wisdom and power in the Divine property are without limit or measure, countless and inexpressible. I write only of the properties as God has revealed Himself through the inner and outer worlds, which are the foremost forms of His revelation.

18. These **seven properties** are found in all things, and he who denies it has no understanding. These seven properties produce the **holy element** in the inner world—the holy, natural life and weaving—but in this outer world, that single element separates into four manifest properties, the **four elements**. Though it remains but one, it divides into the four source-fountains: fire, air, water, and earth.

19. From the fire originates the air, and from the air the water, and from the water the earth, or a being that is earthly; these are merely a revelation of the inner, single element. Compared to the inner element, they are like an ignited smoke or **vapor** <note>original: "Brodem" — an exhalation, steam, or breath</note>. ### Chapter 8.

### On the Creation of the Angels and their Governance.

The creation <note>original: "Erschöpffung" – literally an "out-scooping" or pouring forth from the divine source into form</note> of the angels has a beginning: but the powers out of which they were created have never had a beginning, but are in the midst of the birth of the Eternal beginning. Not that they are the Holy Trinity, or exist within it, but they are from the manifested Word, out of the Eternal dark, fiery, and light-nature, seized by the longing for Divine Revelation, and brought into creaturely images.

2. God, who is a Spirit, has introduced Himself through and out of His revelation into distinct spirits, which are the voices of His Eternal birthing Harmony in His manifested Word of His great kingdom of joy; they are God's instruments, in which the Spirit of God plays in His kingdom of joy; they are flames of fire and light: but in a living, intelligent governance.

3. For the powers of the Godhead are in them just as they are in man, as John 1 says: "The life of men was in the Word" <note>John 1:4</note>: thus the life of the angels has also been in the Word from eternity: for Matthew 22, v. 30 stands: "In the resurrection they are like the angels of God," meaning human beings.

4. And just as we understand principal forms <note>archetypal structures</note> through the Eternal Nature within the Divine revelation: so too are we to understand Prince-Angels with many legions, but especially with three hierarchies according to the property of the Holy Trinity, and according to the three **Principles** <term>Principles: Böhme's system of three "worlds"—the dark-fire world, the light-love world, and the external-visible world</term> as all this is undeniable.

<margin>{</margin> 5. As 1. one hierarchy is understood according to the dark world with the kingdom of Lucifer, who bedeviled himself therein <note>turned himself into a devil through his own will</note>; and the second is understood with the light-fiery world of love; and the 3rd with the **Mystery** <term>Mysterio: the hidden spiritual essence or the "Great Mystery" that underlies physical creation</term> of the external world, through which the inner world has revealed itself.

<margin>{</margin> 6. 7. Those in the dark world bear the name (or names) of the great wrath of God according to the properties of Eternal Nature in its grimness; and those in the light bear the names of the Holy God, as of the Divine power; and those in the creation of the wonders of the external world, bear—

21. Thus, the angels are also as "nothing" in the darkness; they are indeed within it, but they do not see it, nor do they feel it. There is a great gulf between them, which is an entire birth <note>Böhme uses "birth" (German: *Geburt*) to describe a complete state of being or a specific level of reality being generated.</note>. <image-desc>A series of horizontal arrow-like decorative flourishes in the right margin.</image-desc>

22. For what else can separate the light from the darkness, except only a birth of seeing or shining? The light dwells in the darkness, and the darkness does not comprehend it (John, Chapter 1). Just as the light of the external sun dwells and shines in the darkness of this world, and the darkness does not comprehend it; but if the sun’s light withdraws, then the darkness is manifest. 23. However, it separates itself into distinct <term>Principles <note>original: "Principia" — Böhme's term for the fundamental layers of existence (Darkness, Light, and the Material world).</note></term> and properties. For the Scripture says: "To the holy, God is a good fragrance unto life" — understand this as the holy Divine life, as in the power of the Light; "and to the godless, God is a good fragrance unto death" — that is in His wrath, as in the essence, torment, and governance of the dark world.

24. For the God of the holy world and the God of the dark world are not two Gods: there is but one single God. He Himself is all being; He is evil and good, heaven and hell, light and darkness, eternity and time, beginning and end. Where His love is hidden in a being, there His wrath is manifest. In many a being, love and wrath are in equal measure and weight, as we are to understand regarding the essence of this external world. <image-desc>A large, elaborate vertical stack of semicircular decorative flourishes in the right margin.</image-desc>

25. Now, however, He is called a "God" only according to His light in His love, and not according to the darkness, nor according to this external world. Although He is all things Himself, one must nevertheless consider the <term>degrees <note>original: "gradus" — steps or levels of manifestation.</note></term>, how they proceed out of one another. For **I** can say neither of heaven nor of the darkness, nor even of the external world, that they *are* God. None of these is God; rather, they are God’s formed and spoken essence, a mirror of the Spirit who is called God, with which the Spirit reveals Himself and plays in His delight before Himself with this revelation as with His created essence. And yet, the essence is not separated from the Spirit of God, and yet the essence also does not comprehend the Divinity.

26. Just as body and soul are one, and yet neither is the other; or as fire and water, or air and earth, are from one origin <note>original: "uhrstande" — the primal source or standing-place of a thing.</note>, and yet none is the other; but they are bound together, and one would be nothing without the other. This is how we are to understand the Divine essence and the Divine power.

28. Thus it is for us to understand: that the evil and good angels dwell near one another, and yet there is the greatest immeasurable distance between them. For Heaven is in Hell, and Hell is in Heaven, and yet neither is manifest to the other. And if the Devil were to travel many hundreds of thousands of miles and wished to enter into Heaven so that he might see it, he would still only be in Hell and would not see it. Likewise, the angels do not see the darkness, for their sight is pure light of Divine power; and the Devil’s sight is pure darkness of God’s wrath. It is also to be understood in the same way with the holy, and then conversely with the godless people. Therefore, because we had lost the Divine sight in Adam—where Adam saw out of Divine power—Christ said: *You must be born anew, otherwise you cannot see the kingdom of God.* <note>Reference to John 3:3. Böhme believes salvation is a literal "re-birth" of spiritual perception.</note>

<margin>β</margin>
29. The angelic creation is to be understood by us as coming from the Spirit-fire, where the will of the <term>Groundless <note>original: "vngrund"—The primal, abyssal void of God before any creation or manifestation.</note></term> introduced itself into a Ground, and revealed the Eternal-speaking Word or Life with the fiery birth, as with the First Principle where the spiritual government is made manifest through the birth of fire. All angels originate in this spiritual fire as if from the qualities of the <term>fire-source <note>original: "Fewerquall"—A wordplay Böhme uses to mean both the "source" (Quelle) and the "torment/quality" (Qual) of the spiritual fire.</note></term>. For nothing can be created out of the fire [itself], because it is not a substance; but out of the properties leading to the fire, a creature can be grasped in the desire—as in the <gloss>Word "Let there be" <note>original: "Verbo fiat"—The Latin phrase for God's creative command in Genesis.</note></gloss>—and be introduced into a creaturely form and property.

30. Therefore, there are many and varied angels, also in many different offices; and just as there are three forms in the fire-source, so also there are three hierarchies, and within them their princely governments; and also three worlds in one another as one, which make three Principles or beginnings. For every property of Eternal Nature has its degrees: for in the flash of fire they go out from one another, and from those same degrees the distinction of the spirits was created.

31. And we are to understand nothing else by the creation of the angels and all other spirits, but that the groundless God, in His revealed properties, has introduced Himself out of those properties into living creatures. With these He occupies the degrees and plays within the properties; they are His strings <note>Böhme uses a musical metaphor here, likening the different types of angels to strings on an instrument.</note> in the all-present Speaking Word, and they are all directed into the great harmony of His Eternal-speaking Word. So that in all degrees and properties, the voice of the unsearchable God may be manifest and known; they are all created for the praise of God.

# On the Creation of the Angels.

[Dark]ness is God's fire of wrath, and yet it is only a single fire, but it divides itself into two <term>principles <note>original: "Principia"—the fundamental states of existence: the dark, fiery world and the light, holy world.</note> so that one may be manifested in the other: For the flame of the wrath is the manifestation of the great love; in the darkness the light is recognized, otherwise it would not be manifest to itself.

<margin>,, ,, ,, ,, ,, ,, ,, ,, ,, ,, ,, ,,</margin>
28. Thus we are to understand: that the evil and good angels dwell near to one another, and yet there is the greatest immeasurable distance. For heaven is in hell, and hell is in heaven, and yet neither is manifest to the other. And if the devil were to travel many hundred thousand miles and wished to enter into heaven so that he might see it, he would still only be in hell and not see it. Likewise, the angels do not see the darkness, for their sight is pure light of Divine power; and the devil’s sight is pure darkness of God's wrath; thus it is also to be understood with the holy and then conversely with the godless people in the same way. Therefore, since we had lost in Adam the Divine seeing—where Adam saw out of Divine power—Christ said: *You must be born anew, otherwise you cannot see the kingdom of God.*

<margin>β</margin>
29. The angelic creation is to be understood by us from the spirit-fire, where the will of the <term>Unground <note>original: "vngrundes"—Böhme’s term for the absolute Divine source that precedes all created things, including light and darkness.</note></term> introduced itself into a foundation [or ground], and with the fiery birth the eternally-speaking Word or life manifested, as with the First Principle where the spiritual government is manifested through the fire-birth. In this spiritual fire all angels originate as from the forms of the <term>fire-source <note>original: "Fewerquall"—a term Böhme uses to describe the agonizing tension or "quality" of the fire before it transforms into light.</note></term>: For nothing can be created out of the fire itself, for it is not a substance; but out of the properties tending toward the fire, a creature can be grasped in the desire as in the *Word of Creation* <note>original: "Verbo fiat"—literally "let it be done by the Word."</note>, and be introduced into a creaturely form and property.

30. Therefore the angels are many and of various kinds, also in many different offices; and just as there are three forms toward the fire-source, so there are also three hierarchies, and within them their princely governments, and also three worlds in each other as one, which make three principles or beginnings; for every property of the eternal nature has its <term>degrees <note>original: "gradus"—the ranks or steps of spiritual intensity and authority.</note></term>: For in the flash of fire they go out from one another, and out of these same degrees the distinction of the spirits was created.

31. And we are to understand nothing else by the creation of the angels and all other spirits, than that the <term>Abyssal God <note>original: "vngründliche Gott"—the God who is beyond any human foundation or measurement.</note></term> in His manifested properties has introduced Himself from those properties into living creatures, with which He occupies the degrees, and plays within the properties; they are His **strings** <note>original: "Seyten"—Böhme often uses the metaphor of a musical instrument (the Monochord) to describe how creatures are parts of God's cosmic harmony.</note> in the omnipresent speaking Word, and are altogether directed into the great **harmony** of His eternally-speaking Word. So that in all degrees and properties the voice of the unsearchable God may be manifested and known; they are all created for the praise of God.

# Of the Fall of Lucifer with his Legions.

...in His Love a devilish or hellish fierce desire; which is not at all the case: but in the *Center* <note>original: "Centro"—referring to the internal point of origin or core of a being's nature</note> of Eternal Nature, as in the forms leading to fire, there is indeed such a property within the dark impression.

4. Every good angel has the *Center* within himself, and is perhaps manifest in a certain degree in the *Center* in a creaturely property; which property is the greatest in the creature, and according to this is also his office and governance.

5. Yet the angels, who were created out of the *degrees* <note>original: "gradibus"—the ranks or levels of the spiritual hierarchy</note> of the *Center*, were all created into the Light; the Light was manifest in all of them, and they had free will from the manifested Will of the Will of God.

6. Lucifer would certainly have remained an angel, had his own will not led him into the fire-power, wishing to rule as a singular God in darkness and light in strong fire-power, over and in all things: had he remained in the *Harmony* of God, in which God had created him.

7. So Reason speaks: He could not. Then tell me, who forced him? For he was the most beautiful prince in Heaven; had he led his will into God's gentleness, he could have [remained]; but because he would not, he could not: for his own desire went into the *Center*, he wanted to be God himself; he went with his will into selfhood, and in selfhood is the *Center* of nature; as the properties therein, his will wanted to be Master of the house.

8. But God created him into His *Harmony*: that He might play with His Spirit of Love within him, as upon the <term>stringed instrument <note>original: "Seyten Spiele"—literally 'string-play,' a metaphor for a musical instrument like a lute, where the angel is the instrument and God is the player.</note></term> of His manifested and formed Word; and the Self-Will did not want that.

9. Now Reason speaks: How did that happen? Did he not know then of God’s judgment and the Fall? Yes, he knew it: but *he did not have the Fall in his perception, but only as a* <term>science <note>original: "wissenschafft"—here meaning abstract or theoretical knowledge rather than experiential understanding.</note></term>. The fiery delight, which was strong in him, enticed him; for it wanted to be manifest in the *Essence* of wrath (as in the fire-root). The darkness also wanted to be creaturely; it pulled its musician—the great power of fire, *Lucifer*—not indeed outside of him, but into his own fiery and dark property of *Essence* and will. The Fall arose within the creature and not outside of the creature, just as it also happened in *Adam*. Self-will was the beginning of <term>pride <note>original: "Hoffarth"—literally 'high-faring' or arrogance.</note></term>.

10. You ask: what caused it within him? His great beauty: that the free will looked at itself in the fire-mirror, [seeing] what it was; this brilliance made him movable: so that he moved according to the properties of the *Center*, which immediately began to <term>qualify <note>original: "qualificiren"—a term used by Böhme to describe the internal movement or interaction of spiritual forces.</note></term>. For the harsh, severe desire—being the first form or property—impressed itself, and awakened the sting and the desire of anguish: Thus this beautiful star overshadowed its light, and

11. He should have remained yielded <term>yieldedness: from the German "Gelassenheit," a central concept in Böhme’s thought meaning the surrender of one's own will to the Divine Will</term> in the holy power of God, and listened to what the Lord spoke and played through His unique Spirit within him; but his own will did not want this. For his gentleness, out of which the willing of love arises, is locked away and has vanished into nothing, returning as it were to its original source <note>original: "Uhrstandt," referring to the primordial state before manifestation</note>.

12. Now the creature only stands out from the center <note>original: "Centro"—the internal point of origin or core of a being's nature</note>, as if out of Eternal Nature. 13. That was precisely the death of which God told him: that he would die on that very day if he ate from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. So it was also in Lucifer: he died to the holy Divine world and awoke in the fierce world of God’s wrath.

14. You might ask: why did God not hold him and draw him away from this evil inclination? Dear friend, tell me with what? Should He have introduced more love and gentleness into this torment of fire? Had he not known this, he would have remained an angel in humility.

16. Therefore, the children of darkness—as well as the children of this world—are wiser than the children of light, as the Scripture says. You ask why? They have the magical root of the origin <note>original: "Uhrstandes"</note> of all beings manifest within them. This is also what Adam desired, though the Devil persuaded them of it: that they would become wiser; their eyes would be opened and they would be as God Himself.

25. Also, in that same place within the elements, another King has been appointed for him, immediately upon the exhaustion <note>or "bringing forth"—the process of depleting the spiritual potential to form material matter</note> of the stars and the four elements; who, although one could indeed point to him, still rightly remains silent now for the sake of false magic, as well as for the sake of other idolatry; we wish to remain silent about this here, and yet be sufficiently understandable to our own.

## Chapter 10.

### Of the Creation of Heaven and the Outer World.

It seems strange to Reason when it observes how God has created the stars and the four elements: especially when it considers the Earth with its hard stones and entirely rough, severe nature, and sees how great rocks and stones are created, some of which may be used for nothing and are only a hindrance to the use of the creatures of this world. Thus it thinks: out of what could such a <term>compaction: the "thickening" or solidification of spiritual essence into heavy matter</term> have arisen in so many forms and properties? For there are various stones, various metals, and various earths, from which also various trees and herbs grow.

2. When it [Reason] examines itself thus, it finds nothing except to recognize: there must be a hidden power and might which is unfathomable and unsearchable, which has created all things thus; it leaves it at that and runs back and forth in the creation like a bird flying in the air, and looks at it as a cow looks at a new <margin>stable</margin> ~~thorn-gate~~ <note>The author corrected "thorn-gate" to "stable," referencing a German idiom about staring blankly at a new door without understanding.</note>; and it never considers what it itself is; and it seldom comes so far as to recognize that Man is an image out of all this essence. It runs along like the cattle that have no understanding, which only desire to fill themselves and to breed; and when it goes furthest with its inquiries, it searches into the outer play-work of the stars, or otherwise some carving <note>an external detail or surface ornament</note> of outer nature; it simply will not learn to know its Creator; and if it happens that a person comes to know Him, it calls him foolish; and forbids him noble understanding of God, and even counts it as sin, and mocks him for it.

3. We have become such cattle-humans after the Fall of Adam: so that we do not even consider that we were created in God’s image; and were gifted with true natural understanding according to both Eternal and Temporal Nature: so that we might think of [recovering] the lost [image] through great earnestness...

18. This belongs to the first form of nature, according to the coagulated essence of the dark world; it is the stony essence (meaning the coarseness of the stone) and of all metals, as well as of the earth, wherein the deadly quality (or the death of being "enclosed") is understood.

### II. Mercury.

19. Secondly, according to the second form and property of the dark nature and worldly essence, I find in the **compaction** <note>the solidification of spiritual forces into physical matter</note> of metals and stones a bitter, stinging, raging essence, like a poison, which gives a harsh and hostile taste to the earth and the foul water; it is the cause of growth, acting as the stirring life. Its property is called **Mercury**, and the astringent property in the first form is called **Salt**.

### III. Sulphur.

20. Thirdly, I find the third property as the **anxiety**, which is the **torment of sulphur** <note>original: "Schweffelqual." Böhme often plays on the word "Qual" (torment) and "Quelle" (source), suggesting a source that wells up with intense energy</note>, in which the division of the properties—that is, the essence—exists.

### IV. Saltpeter.

21. Fourthly, I find the fire or the heat which awakens the **saltpeter** in the torment of sulphur, which separates the compaction, acting as the **fire-terror** <note>the sudden shock or "crack" of ignition</note>. This is the origin of saltpeter from the sulphurous, watery, and earthly property; for it is the awakener of death, as it exists in the deadly property, and it is the first origin of life in the fire. Up to this point—to the fire—the property of the dark world reaches; it can go no further.

### V. Oils.

22. Fifthly, we find in the compaction of metals and stones an **Oil**; this is sweeter than any sugar could be, so far as it can be separated from the other properties. This is the first heavenly, holy essence, which took its origin from the **free desire** <note>the unconditioned will or joy of God</note>. It is beautiful and translucent. If the fire-torment could be separated from it (though it is not possible to separate it entirely, for the bond of the great realm of joy dwells within it), it would be whiter than anything in nature can be. But because of the fire, it remains rose-red, which the light transforms into yellow, and then into red and white, due to the earthly property and the power of the sun.

23. If the **artist** <note>the alchemist or spiritual seeker</note> is able to dissolve it and free it from the fire of wrath and the other properties, then he possesses the little pearl of the whole world—that is to say, the <term>Tincture</term> <note>the hidden spiritual essence or "Philosopher's Stone" capable of perfecting and healing all things</note>. For Lady Venus has her treasure chest lying there: it is the Virgin with her beautiful little wreath.

24. O you earthly man, if only you still possessed this! Here, Lucifer and Adam gambled it away! O man, if you only knew what lay here, how you would strive for it! But it belongs only to those whom God has chosen for it! O noble pearl, how sweet you are in the **new rebirth**, how beautiful is your radiance!

### VI. The Living Mercury, the Sound.

25. Sixthly, we find in this **oily property** a glorious power from the origin of the revealed, powerful **Divine Word** that dwells in the **Heavenly property**; in this power, the **sound** or **resonance** in metals becomes distinct, and within this resonance their growth consists: <margin>323</margin> For here is the **Holy Mercury** <note>In Böhme’s thought, Mercury represents movement and the "Life-sense." In the dark world, it is a stinging poison; in the light world, it is the "Holy Mercury" or the harmony of the Divine Word.</note>, in which the second form of nature was previously stinging, hostile, and a poison in the darkness; but here, after the fire has divided love and wrath in the **saltpeterish crack** <note>original: "Salnitrischen Schracke." This refers to the sudden, explosive flash of light that transforms the "dark fire" into the "light fire" of the spiritual realm.</note>, it is a joyful **Mercury** in the property of **free desire**, wherein the joyfulness of the creature consists.

<margin>{</margin> 26. And here, you **philosophers** <note>Böhme is addressing alchemists and seekers of wisdom.</note>, lies the power and effect of your **Noble Stone**; here it is called **Tincture** <note>A spiritual substance believed to have the power to "tinge" or transform base matter into gold, or the soul into a divine state.</note>. This effect can **tinge** the faded water in **Luna** <note>Moon/Silver</note>: For here your **Jupiter** <note>Tin</note> is called a prince, and **Sol** <note>Sun/Gold</note> a king, and **Lady Venus** <note>Copper/Love</note> the king's sweetest consort. But **Mars** <note>Iron/War</note> must first lay down the scepter, just as the devil must first go to hell; for **Christ** must bind him, and **tinge** the simple **Luna** whom he has defiled with his **oil of heavenly blood**, so that the wrath may be transformed into joy. Thus is the **Art of the Artists** <note>The alchemical "Great Work."</note> born, understood here by the children of the mystery.

27. Seventhly, we find in the separation of the **solidification** of the metals a **white crystalline water**; this is **Heavenly Water**, like the water above the firmament of heaven, which is separated from the **Oil** as a body of the oily substance. <margin>2</margin> In the metals and stones, it produces a **white crystalline glass**; and **Venus**, with its property, makes it entirely white, and it is of a **silver nature**: and **Venus** in **Sol** makes a **golden** nature; and **Mars** in **Venus** a **coppery** one; and conversely, **Venus** in **Mars** an **iron** one; **Jupiter** in **Venus** a **tin** nature; **Saturn** in **Venus** a **leaden** one; **Mercury** in **Venus** **quicksilver**; and without **Venus** there is no metal, neither among the fixed nor the minerals.

28. Thus, understand by **Venus** the **heavenly essence**, which exists in an **Oil** and **crystalline water**; it gives a body to all metals—understand this as the spiritual, beautiful body of its own essence; without the influence of the others, it is great gentleness and sweetness. Its true, own essence is a sweet, clear water: but the power of the **revealed Word** separates the most holy through the <margin>gr</margin> **fire** into an **Oil**: For in the **Oil**, the fire gives a luster or shine; when the fire tastes the water within itself, it produces an **Oil** from the taste. Thus the **Oil** is spiritual and the **water** is bodily: The **Oil** is a **body of power**, and the **water** is a **body of the properties**, which are living in the **Oil**, and which use or make the water into a housing. In the water stands the **elemental life**, and in the **Oil** the **spiritual life**; and in the power of the **Oil** the **Divine Life**, as the life of the **spoken Word**, as a revelation of the Godhead.
