# Of the Creation of Heaven and the Outer World.

...there are many dark stars, which we do not all see, and also many bright ones, which we see.

<margin>.qbd.</margin>
37. As we see this in the <term>matter</term> <note>original: "Materia."</note> of the earth, how it is of so many kinds, from which manifold fruit grows, according to the properties of the powers above; for thus also the earth is the coarsest essence, wherein the deadly water has been <term>coagulated</term> <note>original: "coaguliret"—meaning the spiritual forces have thickened or solidified into physical form.</note> along with it.

38. The earth was coagulated in the seventh property of nature, as an essence: for it is that same essence which the other six properties produce in their desire. It stands first in seven properties, as previously mentioned; but in the <term>salnitric fire</term> <note>original: "Salnitriſchen Fewer." A term unique to Böhme, referring to a spiritual, explosive energy like lightning that initiates the unfolding of material life.</note> is the unfolding of the properties, where each property unfolds again into seven; there the infinity and the great potency begin, such that out of one thing another can be made which was not there in the beginning.

39. The essence of all essences is only a <term>magical birth</term> <note>original: "Magiſche geburt." In Böhme's vocabulary, "magic" is the power of the Will to manifest something out of nothing.</note>, out of one single thing into infinity: the One is God, the infinity is time and eternity; and it is a revelation of the One, where every thing may be brought out of one into many, and again out of many into one.

40. Fire is the <term>master-builder</term> <note>original: "Werckmeiſter."</note> for this, which drives a little branch out of the earth from a small power, and leads it out into a large tree with many branches and fruit, and also consumes it again; and makes it into one thing again, such as ash and earth from which it had come: So also all things of this world go back into the One from which they proceeded.

41. The essence of this world is indeed to be searched out: But the <term>Center</term> or the point of movement will remain silent to human reason, unless another Light be within it. ## Chapter 11.
### Of the Secrecy of Creation.

The reason of the outer man says: How is it that God has not revealed the creation of the world to man? Why have *Moses* and the children of God written so little about it, since it is the greatest and most distinguished work, upon which everything depends?

2. Yes, dear Reason, reach into your own bosom—what are you reaching for? Behold your mind—what does it lust after? Perhaps after the devil’s mockery. Had the devil not known this ground <note>The "ground" (Grund) refers to the fundamental underlying reality or origin of spiritual power.</note>, he might perhaps still be an angel; had he not seen the *magical* birth in his high light, he would not have desired to be his own lord and maker in the essence.

3. Why does God now cover His children, who receive His Spirit of knowledge, with the cross, and cast them into tribulation and the mire of vanity? Certainly for this reason: that they may play the <term>Miserere</term> <note>original: "Miserere." Latin for "Have mercy," referring to the penitential Psalm 51. Böhme means that God keeps believers in a state of humble repentance.</note> and remain in humility, and not play in the light of nature at this time. Otherwise, if they beheld what <term>Divine Magic</term> <note>original: "Magia divina." For Böhme, this is not sorcery, but the holy power of the Word that brings spirit into form.</note> is, they might well desire to practice art after the devil as *Lucifer* did; for this reason it is hidden from them. And neither *Moses* nor any other was permitted to write more clearly until the beginning of creation sees the end of the world within itself; then it must stand open.

4. And let no one scold us for this, for the time is born when *Moses* throws away the veil from his eyes, which he hung before his face when he spoke with *Israel* after the Lord had spoken with him. *Moses* desired to see it, saying: "Lord, if I have found favor in your sight, let me see your face." But the Lord would not, and said: "You shall look after me <note>A reference to Exodus 33:23, where God allows Moses to see His "back" but not His face.</note>, for no one can see my face."

5. But now the eye of God was in *Moses* and in the children of the holy ones; they saw and spoke in the Spirit of God, and yet they did not have the vision of the spiritual birth except at times: when God wanted to work wonders, as with *Moses* when he performed the wonders in *Egypt*. Then <term>Divine Magic</term> stood open to him, in the manner and way as in the creation.

# Of the Secrecy of Creation.

6. And that was precisely the fall of Lucifer: that he wanted to be a God of Nature and live in the transformation of things. And this was also the idolatry of the Heathens, in that they understood the **Magical** birth: they stole from the One God the **Magical** birth of Nature and chose for themselves idols out of the powers of Nature.

7. For this reason, creation has remained so obscure; and God has covered His children, in whom the true light has shone, with tribulation: so that they would not be revealed to themselves. Since Adam also imagined a desire to know and test **Magic** <note>original: "Magiam." For Böhme, "Magic" refers to the spiritual power of the will to act upon matter and essence.</note>, and wanted to be like God, God permitted it: so that he felt his Heavenly image within the vanity of Nature and became entirely dark and Earthly, just as Lucifer also did with the Center of Nature, when he made a devil out of an angel.

# Of the Secrecy of Creation.

62. For the worst must be the cause of the best: eternal joy exists in the fact that we are redeemed from pain. God did not eternally cast away His holy essence, but only the wickedness that mingled itself within it. When the <term>Crystalline Earth</term> <note>This refers to Böhme’s vision of a future, glorified state of the world where matter becomes transparent and filled with divine light.</note> appears, then shall that be fulfilled which is said: that it belongs in the <term>Point of the Sun</term> <note>original: "Punct Solis." In alchemical and mystical terms, this represents the heart of the light or the perfected center of the spirit.</note>. This is understood well enough by our own people; we shall remain silent on further details here.

### Chapter 11.

## Of the Secrecy of Creation.

The reason of the external man says: How is it that God has not revealed the creation of the world to man? Why have Moses and the children of God written so little of it, since it is the very greatest and most important work, upon which everything depends?

2. Yes, dear Reason, look into your own bosom—what do you smell there? Behold your mind; what does it lust after? Perhaps after the Devil’s jugglery. Had the Devil not known this ground <note>In Böhme’s writing, "ground" often means the underlying reality or origin of a thing.</note>, he might perhaps still be an angel; had he not seen the **Magical** birth in his high light, he would not have desired to be his own lord and creator within the essence.

3. Why does God now cover His children, who receive His spirit of knowledge, with the Cross? Why does He cast them into tribulation and the sludge of vanity? Assuredly it is so that they may play the <term>Have Mercy</term> <note>original: "Miserere." A reference to the penitential Psalm 51, "Miserere mei, Deus." Böhme means they must remain in a state of humble prayer.</note> and remain in humility, and not play with the light of nature in this time. Otherwise, if they saw for themselves what <term>Divine Magic</term> <note>original: "Magia divina."</note> is, they might well desire to practice arts after the Devil’s fashion as Lucifer did; for this reason, it is hidden from them. And neither Moses nor any other was permitted to write more clearly until the beginning of creation sees the end of the world within itself: then it must stand open.

4. And no one should scold us for this, for the time is born when Moses throws the veil away from his eyes—the veil he hung before his face when he spoke with Israel after the Lord had spoken with him. Moses desired to see it when he said: "Lord, if I have found grace before you, let me see your face." But the Lord would not, and said: "You shall look after me <note>That is, "you shall see my back."</note>; for no one can see my face."

5. But now the eye of God was in Moses and in the children of the holy; they saw and spoke in the Spirit of God, and yet they did not have the vision of the spiritual birth except at certain times. This happened when God wished to work wonders—as with Moses when he performed the wonders in Egypt; then <term>Divine Magic</term> stood open to him, in the same manner and way as in the Creation.

14. I will provide an example: Suppose someone takes a small bit of poison. The poison already in the body—which was previously at rest—will immediately receive it with great desire. It will strengthen itself within it and begin to operate, destroying and ruining the opposing good. And what the evil is able to do in its own quality, the good can also do in its own quality; when it is released from the <term>wrath</term> <note>original: "grimme." 15. The essence of this world consists of both evil and good, and one cannot exist without the other. But this is the great evil of this world: that the evil outweighs the good, that wrath is stronger within it than love. This is because of sin, the Devil, and humanity, who have stirred up nature through false desire so that it operates powerfully in wrath, like a poison in the body.

16. Otherwise, if nature stood in its forms in equal weight—in the same <term>concordance</term> <note>original: "concordanz." Heat and cold would be in equal balance in their operation, and Paradise would still be upon the Earth. Even if it were not visible outside of man, it would be within man; if his qualities stood in equal balance, he would be unbreakable and immortal.

17. <margin>that</margin> That is the death and misery of man and of every creature: that the qualities are in conflict, each one elevating itself and operating in its own will. From this, sickness and woe arise. All of this has emerged from this: when the single element manifested itself in four qualities and became mobile, each quality desired its own likeness as an essence according to and out of itself. This the harsh <term>Fiat</term> <note>original: "Fiat," Latin for "let it be done." 18. Now, however, we must consider the greatest secret of the outer world, between the elements and the stars. The <term>Elemental Spirit</term> <note>original: "Elementische Geist." Also known as the astral spirit or the spirit of the macrocosm/constellations.</note>, and yet they are not separate. They dwell in one another like body and soul, but neither is the other. The Star-spirit creates its own "bodies" just as the Elemental Spirit does, and this occurs in all creatures, both the living and the growing.

19. All things in this world possess a two-fold body: an elemental body from fire, air, water, and earth; and a spiritual body from the stars. They also possess a two-fold spirit, from both the stars and the elements.

->The 12th Chapter.<-

## Of the Six Days' Works of Creation.

That God created heaven and earth and all things in six days, as Moses says, is the greatest mystery and is entirely hidden from external reason. In the depths above the moon, there is no night, nor morning nor evening, but rather an everlasting day, from the beginning of the outer world until its end.

2. And although the creation was completed in such a time as six days, the day-works nevertheless have a much more subtle meaning: For the seven properties are understood through them, of which six belong to the active governance of good and evil; and the seventh (as the Essence) is the Rest, in which the other properties rest; these God has spoken forth and made visible.

3. In the governance of the <term>Planetary Wheel</term> <note>original: "Planetischen Rades." This is a central concept in Böhme's work, representing the cyclical, formative forces that govern the physical and spiritual world.</note> we have the figure of how the six properties of active life (which rest in the seventh) introduced and revealed themselves in six days from the inner spiritual world into an outer, visible, four-elemental one. For the Planetary Wheel proceeded from the **point of the sun** <note>original: "Puncto Solis."</note>; for there was the royal place of the **hierarchies** <note>original: "Hierarchien." Refers to the celestial orders of angels.</note>, of which the whole circle (between the stars, both inner and outer) is a member or **body** <note>original: "Corpus."</note>.

4. Because the Prince of the hierarchies <note>Lucifer, the fallen angel.</note>, while he sat at rest in the heavenly essence, fell and exalted himself around the center of Eternal Nature, he was thrust into darkness; and God, through His movement, created another Prince for him out of this place, but one without Divine understanding, to be a ruler of the essence—that is the sun.

### The 12th Chapter.

# Of the Six Days’ Works of Creation.

That God created Heaven and Earth and all things in six days, as Moses says, is the greatest mystery and is completely hidden from outer <term>reason</term> <note>original: "Vernunfft." Often used by Böhme to describe human logic or natural intellect, which cannot grasp divine mysteries without spiritual illumination.</note>. In the depth above the moon there is no night, neither morning nor evening, but rather an everlasting day, from the beginning of the outer world until the end of the same.

2. And although the creation was completed in such a time as six days in length, the days’ works nevertheless have a much more subtle understanding: for the seven <term>properties</term> <note>original: "Eigenſchafften." These are the seven qualities or "source-spirits" of Böhme's nature-philosophy.</note> are understood therein, of which six belong to the active government for good and evil; and the seventh (as the essence) is the Rest, in which the other properties rest; these God has spoken forth and made visible.

3. In the government of the <term>Planetary Wheel</term> <note>original: "Planetiſchen Rades." The cyclical system of the seven planets which Böhme believes governs the material world.</note> we have the figure of how the six properties of active life (which rest in the seventh) have introduced and revealed themselves in six days from the inner spiritual world into an outer visible four-elemental world. For the planetary wheel proceeded from the <term>Point of the Sun</term> <note>original: "Puncto Solis." The mystical and physical center of the solar system.</note>; for there was the royal place of the <term>hierarchies</term> <note>original: "Hierarchien." The angelic orders or celestial structures.</note>, of which the whole circle (between the stars in the inner and outer) is a member or body.

4. Because the Prince of the Hierarchies <note>Referring to Lucifer.</note>, while he sat in rest in the heavenly essence, fell and raised himself up around the center of Eternal Nature, he was thrust into the darkness; and God, through His movement, created another prince for him out of this place—but without divine understanding—to be a ruler of the essence: that is the Sun.

### Of the Second Day.

19. We call the second day Monday: and for this reason, that the Moon rules the first hour of the day; and it may well be that the ancient wise men understood something of this in the light of nature, which they kept secret and depicted with symbols rather than explaining it. That they certainly understood it is to be seen in the names of the seven planets, in that they gave them names according to the seven properties of nature, which so completely agrees with nature (as well as with the creation) that it seems to me they rightly understood a part of the foundation of creation, since the names of the planets originate so precisely from the "language of nature." But the reason it was not clearly brought to light is, as mentioned before, because of false **Magic** <note>original: "Magia"</note>, so that it would remain hidden from those who perform sleight-of-hand with nature on account of the great abuse; we should also leave it at that, and yet we wish to be sufficiently intelligible to our own people.

27. Now the outer water is the tool of the inner; the inner water is what is truly meant here. For it is the moving Spirit in the Word that governs the inner water in Baptism. Dear Christians, let this be told to you: this is the true foundation of the matter.

28. Regarding what Moses says—that God created the Firmament <term>Beste</term> <note>The original German uses "Beste" (a variant of "Veste"), meaning a "firm place" or "expanse," typically translated in Bibles as the Firmament.</note> and called it Heaven—this refers to the innermost hidden mystery, which the earthly-minded person cannot understand. Understanding exists only within the power of the water above the Firmament, as if in Heaven or, as I might put it, in the Spirit of God. If the Spirit awakens within a person in that water above the Firmament—the same water where the divine light of Adam’s life once faded <note>The author suggests that Adam's spiritual life "paled" or lost its luster during the Fall, and only through the Spirit can this vision be restored.</note>—then that person can see through it. Otherwise, there is no understanding here; everything remains silent.

29. The creation of Heaven is understood as how the "speaking Word" has gathered the revealed powers of the Spiritual World, within which it is manifest, active, and ruling. Secondly, it is understood through the revealed powers of the outer world, which the Spirit gathered into the four-elemental being and enclosed within the outer Firmament. This was done so that the Devil, as the Prince of Wrath, might not seize them—for he wished to work through the inner water. Thus, the powers of Eternity work through the powers of Time, just as the sun shines through water, and the water does not "grasp" the sun but only feels it; or as fire glows through iron, and the iron remains iron. So it is with the outer heaven: it undergoes the influence, while the inner works through it, drawing forth an outward fruit from the exterior, even though the inner Heaven lies hidden within the Firmament, just as God is hidden within Time.

30. In this second day’s work, we are to understand the revelation of the inner and outer heavenly beings as the revelation of the "water-source." In the outermost heaven toward the Earth, this working is attributed to the Moon—not the physical moon we see, which was only created as a ruler on the fourth day, but rather the "lunar property" within the silent, outer life, such as in growing things. This growing life was opened on the third day.

# Of the Third Day of Creation.

32. In the primordial origin of Eternal Nature—which is an eternal origin—one clearly finds the revelation of the six days’ works, and how the Eternal Word <note>original: "ewige Wort"</note> led them out from the invisible spiritual realm into the visible. Furthermore, one finds the form of this in the planetary wheel <note>The "planetary wheel" refers to the astrological and alchemical cycles that Böhme believed mirrored the divine process of creation.</note>, for whoever is able to grasp it.

33. For within the eternal birth of nature, there is one Eternal Day. That which God has divided into six parts—which are called the days’ works—and has revealed and made visible, exists within Eternal Nature in six distinct degrees within the Being, or the seventh property. In this seventh property, the six degrees of nature work, yet they also eternally rest from working; they themselves are the very activity which they have poured into the Seventh as their own proper rest, wherein their perfection and revelation reside.

34. Regarding the Creation, we are to understand nothing other than that the Fiat Word <note>original: "Verbum Fiat," Latin for "The Word: Let there be."</note> grasped the spiritual birth and introduced it into a visible, external governance and being. He distinguished and grasped the waters as the spiritual essence, and led them out from the first day—as if out of holy power—into a "time," moving from the Eternal Day into a day that has a beginning.

35. The third manifestation of the third day’s work is now the moving, growing life. In this, the Light of Nature—which on the first day had become shining in an external way within the essence of being—now shone through the second day, that is, through the water and the heaven. In this shine, the Spoken Word moved within the essence and was active. There, the power of the Spoken Word turned green <note>Literally "grünete," suggesting the springing up of plants and vitality.</note> out of the light of inner nature, through outer nature, and out of the heavens through the earth. Now the Mighty One <note>Böhme refers here to Lucifer, the fallen prince who once ruled the primordial fire-world.</note> has lost his dominion, he who was a king and a great prince; for the essence of wrath <term>Grimm</term> <note>"Grimm" is Böhme’s term for the harsh, consuming quality of fire and anger in its raw, unbalanced state.</note> was captured in the light of nature, and he was captured with it. Thus, he lies imprisoned in the darkness between time and eternity until the Judgment of God.

Within the fire-shock occurs the division of powers, where every property became revealed within itself. ## Chapter 13.

### Of the Creation of the Fourth Day.

On the fourth day, Mercury <note>original: "Mercurius." In alchemy, Mercury represents the principle of movement, communication, and the "vital spirit" that allows for sensation.</note> governs the first hour of the day; it brings about sentient life <note>original: "fühlende Leben," literally "feeling life." This refers to the ability of a creature to perceive through senses, moving beyond the stationary life of plants.</note>. Here one truly understands the foundation of the revelation of the inner Nature into the outer; for on the fourth day the Sun and Stars were created, which are the true Mercurial life. Here, the property of Fire has opened itself within the sulfur-torment <note>original: "Schweffelquaal." This describes the state of tension and "labor" within base matter before it is transformed into light or spirit.</note> through the Water, and the fifth essence <note>original: "fünffte Essenz" or quintessence—the purest, most refined substance that permeates all things.</note> has become manifest through the Light of Nature, as an oil from Fire and Water out of the sulfur—which is a Mercury of salt-nitre <note>original: "Mercurius Salnitri." Salt-nitre refers to the explosive, creative energy within matter.</note>, an ignitable Mercury, a living and sentient one.

2. In the third form of nature there is an unfeeling life in sulfur and mercury; but in the fourth there is a sentient life. For in the Fire, the properties become painful <note>original: "peinlich," meaning full of torment or laboring under the heat of existence.</note>, and in the oily state <note>original: "Oelischen." Böhme uses "oil" to represent the gentle, soothing principle that provides fuel for the light.</note> they become gentle and joyful. Thus, the movement in the oily state is made sentient by the pain.

<margin>it</margin>
3. Here one now understands quite thoroughly: how the separation in the Fire of the Eternal Nature has revealed itself with a formal shape within the visible being of the outer world. For in the ignition of the fire within the Salnitric Shock <note>original: "Salnitrischen Schracke." This is the sudden flash or "crack" where the divine fire ignites life within the dark properties of matter.</note>, two beings separate: one is watery, resulting from the consumability in the fire; as the fire consumes the harsh torment of the "impression" <note>The magnetic force that pulls spirit into solid form.</note> into itself, a great gentleness issues forth from that consumption. This gentleness is "dead" to the fire and is unfeeling, and it provides the water-torment <note>original: "Wasserquaal," referring to the source or "welling up" of the water principle.</note>.

4. Secondly, the fiery torment separates—that is, the properties belonging to the fire-torment, which have now become painful and sentient through the ignition of the fire—and enters into its Principle <note>original: "Principium."</note>. This fire-torment could not subsist if it did not swallow the water back into itself to strengthen itself; from this, the Salnitric Shock also arises, as the Fury <note>original: "Grim." The dark, wrathful aspect of nature.</note> is terrified before the being of the Gentleness of the Water, from which sentience, as well as the luster of the fire, arises.

5. For that which is swallowed from the water into the fire is resolved into a spiritual light-oil <note>original: "Geistlicht Oele."</note>, in which the fire shines; and out of the oil goes the Air <note>original: "Lufft."</note>, as the weaving spirit of the fire, which has become mobile within the fire.

6. The Air is nothing other than the mobile life, where the Speaking Word <note>original: "sprechende Wort." The divine creative Logos or command that resonates through nature.</note> raises itself through Nature, through the powers of Nature, through the fire in the oil of the nature of light, within the water-source. It is the life of the fire: but it is dead to the fire, and yet is [driven] by the fire...

...might [awaken] a Nature-God <note>original: "Natur-Gott." In Böhme’s thought, this refers to a secondary, fashioned ruler of the physical world—a demiurge-like manifestation of divine power within nature.</note> awakened and born with six counselors, who are his helpers; that is, the Sun with the other six planetary stars, which are spoken forth from the seven properties out of the place of the Sun <note>original: "loco Solis."</note>, and led into a turning wheel during the speaking, according to the property of the Eternal Birth in the Center of Nature; and this was opened in seven degrees out of the birth: for then the first degree of movement in the Light of Nature, from the inner spiritual Fire- and Light-world, was the Sun, which takes its brilliance from the Tincture <note>original: "Tinctur." 17. 18. She gives a body to all seven metals, and essence to all six planets, as is to be seen in the metals; for every planet makes its essence in its property after itself: the Sun in **Gold**, the Moon in **Silver**, Jupiter in **Tin**, Saturn in **Lead**, Mercury in **Quicksilver**, Mars in **Iron**; and yet it is only the essence of the single property of Venus, but they put their power and spirit into it, and hold the body <note>original: "Corpus."</note> as their own, because they rule it.

19. 20. These properties stood in the speaking-forth, in the turning-around, in the manner that the birth of nature is in its essence; these the word "Let there be" <note>original: "Verbum fiat."</note> seized and grasped into a body, and ordered into the four stars for governance.

## The 14th Chapter.

### Of the Creation of the fifth Day.

1. Once God had revealed the stars and the four elements as a weaving life, in which the upper stars imparted the distinction within that weaving life; and set the four stars <note>Böhme often refers to the four "stars" or planetary influences corresponding to the four elements.</note> in motion within the four elements; he then led forth the resonance—or the out-sounding—from the essence of all stars and elements. This was done through the movement of his speaking Word in the *Word: Let there be* <note>original: "Verbo: Fiat." The divine command of creation.</note>, as the power of that same life, which was free from pain. He grasped this through the Word *Fiat* <note>the "Fiat" is the "divine desire" or attracting force that pulls spiritual essence into material form.</note> and, with the holy eternal speaking Word, through the *Fiat*, he spoke that same life into forms according to the properties of the stars in the spiritual body <note>original: "Geistlichen Corpore."</note>, in which the *Fiat*—or the Desire—drew the elements to itself as an outer essence, forming a body.

2. And from this, creatures were made in all four elements, in each star according to its property: such as birds in the star of the Air, fish in the star of the Water, and animals and quadrupeds from the star of the Earth and all four elements; as well as spirits in the Fire-star, which is also present in the other elements. And one sees this very clearly in the distinction of creatures, just as the degrees <note>original: "gradus."</note> of the stars are so diverse. For the worms of the earth live in the third degree, such as in the fire-fright <note>original: "Fewerschrack." This refers to the sudden, sharp ignition or "crack" that marks the beginning of individual life or motion in Böhme’s cosmology.</note>, in Sulfur, Mars, and Mercury <note>Böhme uses these alchemical terms to describe the fundamental qualities of nature: Sulfur for the burning desire, Mars for the driving force/wrath, and Mercury for the restless movement and communication.</note> in an uncomprehending life; and yet they possess an understanding through the ignition of the upper stars. In this same third star-property, grass, herbs, and trees also stand, yet they are also aided by the ignition of the upper [stars], through which they are qualified differently.

3. And we see how each species has a spirit and body according to the degree of its star; for it is understood that many species come from one star; this is because every star contains all other stars within itself. For in every star lies everything that all stars are, but in different degrees in their revelation; therefore, the properties in every star are manifold: thus, many kinds of species have come forth from every star. ### Chapter 15.

The sixth day in the Creation is Friday, on which **Venus** governs the first hour of the day; this rightly indicates to us the order of the <term>degrees</term> <note>original Latin: "gradus." Böhme uses this to describe the progressive stages of spiritual development.</note>, how the eternally-speaking Word has revealed itself with Nature through time. It shows how the Spirit led the six properties of Nature out through six degrees or days into an active life, and yet has led them all back again into the seventh, as into rest or into the place where they are meant to work. This indicates that everything which they worked and revealed out of the wonders of Eternal Wisdom should enter again into the One as into rest; this is the seventh property, acting as a housing for the active life, in which it should stand as a figure for the contemplation of God’s great glory <note>The original "Herzlichkeit" likely means "Herrlichkeit" (Glory), though it literally translates to "heartiness."</note>.

2. As from the fifth star He led out the sixth: namely, the fiery love-desire out of the Jovial power. Through this He governs all stars, so that all life has become desirous after its own likeness—striving toward such a creature as each life is within itself.

3. This refers to the creative command in Genesis.</note>: "Let us make man": that is, out of the mixture of all beings, out of the properties of all powers and stars, a <term>slime</term> <note>original Latin: "limum." Böhme uses this to refer to the "dust of the earth" (Genesis 2:7), which he views as a quintessence of all cosmic materials.</note> out of all beings. The love-desire longed for a living image, an image that would be equal and similar to us, and they shall rule over the fish in the sea, and over the birds of the heaven, and over the cattle and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that crawls upon the earth.

7. Understand this thus: The sixth property of nature (acting as the love-desire) was born out of, or spoken out of, or breathed out of all properties, and was the desirous life in joys, as in the light of nature; that was not itself a "slime," but it was the desire for the slime, for the Resounding Word that God had spoken hovered within it as the rational life; God was revealed within it.

<margin>$\beta$</margin>
8. That same revealed Word of God desired, within this love-desire, a "slime" from the earth and from all created beings—out of all stars and <term>degrees</term> <note>original Latin: "gradus," referring to the various levels or stages of being.</note>—to form a <term>body</term> <note>original Latin: "Corpus."</note> for itself. Therefore God said: An image that shall rule over fish, birds, animals, worms, and all the earth, and the essence of all stars. If it were to rule therein, it must also be from there; for every spirit rules in its mother from which it originated, and eats from its mother.

9. Yet one must rightly understand this love-desire here in the spoken Word. The spoken Word had the desire of all heavens—that is, of all <term>beings</term> <note>original Latin: "Entium," the essential qualities of things.</note> or properties—within this <term>Venus-desire</term> <note>In Böhme’s system, Venus represents the sixth property of nature: the sweet, longing, and formative power of love.</note>, as of the inner spiritual holy heaven, which is the dwelling place of God’s power, and of the outer created heaven with the heavens of all stars and elements. Yet this was not yet substantial, but existed as a spiritual desire; and those same properties desired to be substantial within that spiritual desire.

10. Thus the text in Moses sounds quite clear and complete when he says: "And God created man in his image, in the image of God created he him." By "creating," one understands the body, which is twofold: both a spiritual body and a physical one; for the Venus-desire is a spiritual body. And that which it has drawn to itself through the "Let it be" <note>the creative "Fiat"</note> into the desire of the spiritual body—that is a fleshly body. The Word "Let it be" has itself shaped it into a spiritual human being out of all three <term>principles</term> <note>Böhme’s "Three Principles": the dark/fire world, the light world, and the physical world.</note>, according to the inner divine world—both the fiery and the light-filled—and according to the outer world.

11. This refers to the "dust of the ground" from Genesis 2:7, viewed here as a physical manifestation of all cosmic properties.</note> of the earth, along with the other elements and the visible stars of the <term>Third Principle</term> <note>In Böhme’s cosmology, the Third Principle is the physical, visible universe.</note>.

12. The inner, holy man was in the heaven of God, and the outer man was in the outer heaven, a "slime" of the outer heavens; the inner was a "slime" of the holy, spiritual heaven. Therefore Moses says very well that God created man in His image, as the image of God: for He was known from eternity in the <term>Mystery of Wisdom</term> <note>original: "Mysterio der Weißheit." This refers to "Sophia," the divine mirror or blueprint of all things.</note> as a star of magical power by the Spirit of God in that same essence. Into that same knowledge, God introduced essence, and created that essence into the image of the <term>magical image of God</term>.

13. Thus, by the "inner creation," understand the true heavenly image: a holy man made from all the properties of the angelic, divine world. Understand the "inner body" to be the <term>unique element</term> <note>The "One Element" or quintessence from which the four physical elements are derived.</note> out of which the four elements were spoken forth. And understand the "outer man" to be the outer world with the stars and four elements—namely fire, air, water, and earth—and the outer <term>tincture</term> <note>original: "Tinctur." A vitalizing spiritual essence that gives quality and life to matter.</note>, which is bound to the inner tincture in the holy spoken Word and is separated only by a "principle" (just as the inner gives birth to an outer life from itself). The inner is holy, and the outer in the tincture would also be holy if the curse had not entered into it because of awakened vanity; however, if vanity can be separated from the tincture, it is holy and a <term>paradise</term>, which will reveal itself at the end of this world.

<margin><image-desc>A vertical decorative typographic ornament, featuring repeating stylized floral or foliate motifs, runs alongside the start of paragraphs 14 and 15.</image-desc></margin> 14. And Moses says further: "God breathed into man the living breath, and man became a living soul." This refers to the living, speaking, understanding spirit drawn from all three principles: namely, from the inner fire-world (which is revealed through the dark world), from the holy light-world, and from the outer air-world—that is the soul.

15. The inner fire-breath is the true, eternal, creaturely soul; and the light-breath is the true, understanding spirit of the soul, in which the soul is an angel; and the outer air-breath is the rational soul in its growth and animal life, by which man rules over all creatures of this world. This is a single soul in three principles, according to the likeness of God.

16. Just as the single understanding of the <term>abyssal Godhead</term> <note>original: "vngrundlichen Gottheit." The "Ungrund" is the absolute, unfathomable depth of God before differentiation.</note> reveals itself with three principles, so too has He revealed that same spirit—as the true life—out of all three principles and breathed it into the created image.

The dark/fire world (divine wrath/potential), 2. The light world (divine love/revelation), and 3. The physical world (the visible universe).</note>. 18. **And the soul stands in three realms, regarding its true life and understanding. This turned the fierce, dark, and fiery property into a kingdom of joy, which is the true revelation of the Godhead; it is called the Holy Heaven of the angelic dwelling.**

From this, the five <term>senses</term> <note>original Latin: "Sensus."</note> take their origin, and within this stands the growing and the rational life. This is the "animal soul," which rules in all creatures of the outer world, as well as in all outer heavens or stars, and in all the earth or substances of the outer world.**

21. **Understand it thus: The fire-breath from the first principle rules in its own origin, as if in its own mother, from which the Spirit of God grasped it—namely, in the center of Eternal Nature, in the power of the dark and fire-world. It is the cause of the light-life and also of the outer air-life; if it were not there, neither of the others would exist.**

22. **And the light-breath rules in the second principle, in the holy kingdom of the revealed power of God. This is the housing of the Holy Spirit of God, the temple of God; understand this as being within the heavenly holy essence, in the holy spiritual body of the holy pure element.**

### Of the Sixth Day’s Work of Creation.

...which stands with its properties in equal weight and measure, like a prepared instrument of the Spirit, wherein he reveals God’s wonders out of the Eternal Wisdom and introduces them into a play of joy—as if into the holy harmony of the eternally-speaking Word, into the Divine Kingdom of Joy, as the revelation of Divine powers, in which the Holy Spirit is the true musician.

23. And the breath of the air also rules in its "mother" out of which it originates—that is, in the outer world, which is the figure and likeness of the inner world, serving as the outer <term>mystery</term> <note>original: "Mysterium." For Böhme, a Mystery is a hidden core or "chaos" from which a specific reality is produced.</note> of time. This reveals its mother, who is from eternity but has been introduced into "time" so that the wonders of God’s wisdom may be contemplatively beheld.

<margin><image-desc>A vertical stack of 11 manicule symbols (pointing hands) directed at the beginning of paragraph 24.</image-desc></margin>
24. And yet these are not three souls, but only one; however, it stands in <term>three principles</term>, namely: in the realm of God’s wrath, in the realm of God’s love, and in the realm of this world. If this were not so, one could not say that the soul "travels to heaven or hell," for those places would not be within it. When the "air"—the outer realm of time—breaks away from the soul at death, the soul is then revealed either in the dark fire-realm of God or in the holy light-realm (the fire of love of God’s power), depending on where it has committed itself during this lifetime. There it remains once it leaves the outer life.

25. Yet we must not think in any way that the soul is God Himself. God is neither "nature" nor "creature" and dwells in nothing but Himself, yet He also dwells through everything, being neither far from nor near to any thing. Rather, the soul is the "spoken Word," the "formed Word." It is the spirit and the life of the three principles of Divine revelation. If the soul were God Himself, it would be <term>without reason</term> <note>original: "unvernünfftlich." Böhme means that if the soul were the absolute, unmanifest God, it would lack the distinct, contrasting properties required for self-awareness and judgment.</note>, and no judgment could be passed upon it.

26. But a judgment can indeed pass upon the soul if it removes itself from the order into which God introduced it in the beginning. In doing so, it departs from the Divine harmony and the order of the revealed Word of God’s power, revealing a different "will" within itself—specifically, properties drawn from the harsh power of Eternal Nature.

27. The whole man, with body and soul, is threefold, yet remains a single human being. The body is composed of three kinds of essence, and the soul is composed of three kinds of spiritual property. You see an example of this in fire, light, and air; fire has a different property than light or air. The "fiery" spiritual body is the Eternal Constellation—the <term>Magical Constellation</term> or Great Mystery—out of which the outer stars were born and entered into a created form.

These are the three primary alchemical principles representing expansion/fuel (Sulfur), movement/imagination (Mercury), and contraction/physicality (Salt).</note> and is a temple of God. And in the outer body—which is a <term>slime of the earth</term> <note>original: "Limus der Erden," a reference to the Latin Vulgate's description of Adam being formed from the dust or mud of the ground.</note> and of the other elements—the outer soul dwells as the true spirit of the outer world, existing within the outer <term>constellations</term> <note>original: "Gestirne." Böhme uses this term to refer to astral influences that govern the physical senses.</note> of the five <term>senses</term> <note>original: "Sensus."</note>.

29. Every property of the soul also possesses a bodily property, which may be called a "heaven," acting as a particular magical constellation. For example, the fiery property of the soul has a body drawn from the inner constellation of the dark and fire-world, which is a spiritual body.

30. And the light-property of the soul has a spiritual <term>Delian</term> <note>original: "Delischen." This term refers to the "Glassy Sea" or the pure, transparent spiritual matter of the divine realm, often associated with clarity and light.</note> and watery body. This same water is the "water above the firmament" of which Moses speaks; and this same oil is the holy oil of Divine powers. The Old Testament dealt with this archetype, in which the true Delian body of heavenly property existed in Adam, though it faded away when he awakened into vanity. Therefore, God ordained the archetype of the new rebirth through a Delian anointing, in which He worked powerfully through the promised Covenant, as if through a prefiguration.

31. The third, outer property of the soul possesses in every way a body made of many constellations, just as the inner properties do; many of these properties may all be called "heavens." For every property of the outer body has its own magical constellation. For instance: there is a body from the sulfurous constellation of the earth; likewise, a body or constellation from the <term>mercurial poison-life</term> <note>original: "Mercurialischen Gifftleben." In Böhme's philosophy, "poison" or "sting" is the necessary friction or movement required for life to manifest.</note>; likewise, a body from the salty powers of <term>physical bodies</term> <note>original: "Corporum."</note>; and finally, a body of the soul of the outer world, originating from the upper created constellations—all according to how the outer powers of the outer soul are composed. Thus, every power has a bodily property attached to it:

### Chapter 16.

## Of the distinction between the Heavenly and Earthly Man.

If we consider the **Image of God**, which God created in **Paradise** for eternal, unbreakable life, we can in no way say of the coarse, fleshly image that this coarse property of **earthliness** is the Image of God that can possess the holy world. For it is not of that same **essence** and being of which Christ speaks in John 6: <note>original: "Der Geist ist das Leben / das Fleisch ist kein nütze." A reference to John 6:63.</note> *The Spirit gives life; the flesh counts for nothing.* Likewise: <note>original: "Fleisch vnd Blut soll das Himmelreich nicht erben." A reference to 1 Corinthians 15:50.</note> *Flesh and blood shall not inherit the kingdom of heaven.* And yet, the true body indeed lies within this animalistic, coarse property, like **gold** within a coarse stone.

<margin>{</margin> 2. Everything about man that is **earthly** is animalistic and fragile, and is not "Man." Although God created an external body for man from the <term>slime of the earth</term> <note>original: "Limo der Erden." From the Latin *limus*, referring to the dust or mud from which Adam was formed in Genesis 2:7.</note>, we are not to view him as he is now. For the true human body, according to the inner world, is a spiritual <term>Sulfur</term>, a spiritual <term>Mercury</term>, and a spiritual <term>Salt</term>: <note>In Böhme’s thought, these are the "Three Principles" of all matter: Sulfur (the combustible/expansive energy), Mercury (the fluid/imaginative movement), and Salt (the stabilizing/materializing force). Here, they represent the spiritual anatomy of the perfect human.</note> Every property of the soul has a bodily or essential quality attached to it.

<margin>{</margin> 3. God created such a body as the soul was in its **essence**, as it existed in the "out-spoken word" of understanding, and He breathed the soul into it for the sake of understanding. Thus, the outer Sulfuric body is by no means the coarse animal that passes away and does not return. The right, true body that lies hidden within the coarseness is to be regarded as a spiritual body in comparison to that coarseness. It is indeed contained within flesh and blood, but was created in a fixed, constant state.

4. Through **Adam's** lust, this coarseness was revealed by means of the <term>imagination</term>; <note>For Böhme, "imagination" is not just fantasy, but a powerful, creative act of the will that can "form" or "model" reality.</note> the true outer body is a Sulfuric, Mercurial, and Salt-like property—a pure, essential power after the manner of the soul. What the soul is in spirit, the true human body is in essence: a housing for the soul.

5. All properties of the inner holy body, together with the outer, true ones (in the **First Man**), were directed into a single **harmony**. None lived in its own desire; instead, they all gave their desire into the soul, in which the Divine light was revealed, as in the holy heaven. This Light shone through all properties and created an equal <term>temperament</term> <note>original: "Temperanz." This refers to a state of perfect balance where no single element dominates the others.</note> within them. All properties gave their desire into the Light, as into God's revealed sweetness, which penetrated through all properties, in which

### Of the Completion of the Seventh Day.

16. God created all things in six days out of the seven properties, and he introduced the six days’ work of the revelation of His creation into the seventh, wherein all life shall work as in one body. For the seventh day and the first belong to one another as one, for the six properties of Eternal Nature all lie within the seventh, as in a product of the other six. The seventh property is a <term>mystery</term> <note>original: "Mysterium." A hidden spiritual essence or "womb" that contains the potential of all things.</note> or essence of all the others; and from the seventh day, the first day took its <term>origin</term> <note>original: "vhrstandt."</note> and beginning.

...of the sevenfold birth of <term>Eternal Nature</term> <note>original: "Ewigen Natur." 20. 21. Each of these has introduced itself into a particular degree of a particular property, and such a degree may be called a "Heaven" or a <term>Magical Spirit-constellation</term> <note>original: "Magisch Geistgestirne." This refers to an internal, spiritual set of influences that mirror the physical stars.</note>.

22. Thus, the exhaling or speaking was led into six <term>degrees</term> <note>original: "gradus."</note> or "day-works."

23. Each exhaling lasted for a time, such as the length of a day and a night (in its grasping and forming), and each property of a day was spoken or exhaled out of the previous one, until the sixth. In this forming, the <term>Image of God</term> (Man) was created as an image of the formed Word. This image God led into the Sabbath—that is, into the seventh day—introducing it into the <term>Word "Let there be"</term> <note>original: "Verbum Fiat."</note> as the first Divine Desire toward Nature, wherein Paradise and the Eternal Day existed.

# The 17th Chapter.

## On Paradise.

Moses says: When God had made man, He planted a garden in Eden, and placed man therein, to cultivate and to keep it; and He caused all kinds of fruit to grow in the garden, pleasant to look upon and good to eat, and planted the Tree of Life and the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil in the midst.

2. Here the veil lies over Moses’ face, wherein he has a glorified countenance, so that sinful Israel may not look into his face: For the man of <term>vanity</term> <note>German: *Eitelkeit*. In this context, it refers to the transient, fallen state of human nature which is obsessed with worldly things rather than eternal ones.</note> is not worthy to know what Paradise is; and though it is given to us to recognize according to the hidden man, we shall yet remain silent to the <term>beast</term> <note>German: *Thiere*. Böhme often uses "the beast" or "animal man" to refer to the carnal, unspiritual part of human nature.</note> with this description; but to our own, it shall be understood enough.

<margin><image-desc>A manicule (pointing hand) symbol pointing towards paragraph 3.</image-desc></margin>

3. **The Garden of Eden** was a place upon Earth where man was tested, and Paradise was in Heaven, and yet was also in the Garden of Eden. For just as Adam, before his Eve and before his sleep, was in Heaven according to the inner man, and upon Earth according to the outer; and as the inner, holy man permeated the outer, just as fire glows through an iron: so also the heavenly power from the pure element permeated the four elements, and bloomed through the earth and bore fruits that were truly heavenly and earthly; but they were <term>qualified</term> <note>German: *qualificiret*. A technical term for Böhme meaning "endowed with specific qualities" or "harmonized."</note> by the Divine power; and the vanity in the fruit was held as if half-swallowed up, just as the day hides the night and holds it captive within itself, so that it is not recognized.

4. Paradise was nothing other than the quality of the seventh day; the heavenly essence of the <term>second Principle</term> <note>Latin: *secundi Principii*. The "Second Principle" in Böhme’s system is the world of Light, Love, and the Son, which exists alongside the "First Principle" (Darkness/Fire).</note> lies locked within the earth; the curse of God has hidden it. This same essence bloomed (in the beginning of the world) through the earthly essence, just as eternity is in time, and the Divine power is through everything, and yet is not grasped or understood by any earthly thing in its <term>selfhood</term> <note>German: *selbheit*. The state of being centered on one’s own ego or separate material existence.</note>.

5. But in Paradise, the Divine world-essence permeated the essence of time, just as the sun's power permeates a fruit on the tree, and qualifies it into a loveliness, so that it is pleasant to look upon and good to eat: Thus are we to understand the same concerning the Garden in Eden.

Böhme is playing on the phonetic similarity between "Eden" and "öde" (desolate/waste).</note>; that is, it should not manifest its power according to the wrath of vanity; it should hold still as a mother for birthing. ## Of Paradise.

Moses says: When God had made man, He planted a garden in Eden and placed man within it, to till and to keep it, and caused all kinds of fruit to grow in the garden, pleasant to look upon and good to eat; and He planted the Tree of Life and the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil in the midst of it.

This is so that the soul learns to be humble and remains in Divine Harmony, rather than becoming a devil.

# The 18th Chapter.
## Of the Paradisiacal Rule / how it might well have been, had Adam not fallen.

1. I know the <term>Sophist <note>Böhme uses this term to describe rationalist scholars or theologians who rely on academic logic rather than spiritual revelation.</note></term> will find fault with me here, and cry out that it is an impossible knowledge, since I was not there and did not see it myself. To him let it be said: that in the essence of my soul and body—when I was not yet who I am, but when I was Adam's <term>essence <note>The fundamental spiritual and physical "stuff" or substance of a person.</note></term>—I was indeed there, and I myself trifled away my glory in Adam. But because Christ has restored it to me, I see in the Spirit of Christ what I was in Paradise, what I became in sin, and what I shall become again. And no one should cry us out as ignorant; for though I myself do not know it, Christ knows it in me, and from that knowledge I shall write.

2. Adam was a man and also a woman, and yet neither of them, but a virgin, full of chastity, modesty, and purity, as the image of God. He had both <term>tinctures <note>original: "Tincturen" — In alchemy and Böhme’s theology, these are the two fundamental spiritual energies: the "fire" (masculine/wrath/strength) and the "light" (feminine/love/beauty).</note></term> of the fire and the light within himself; in which <term>conjunction <note>A union or joining together.</note></term> self-love stood as the virginal center, like the beautiful paradisiacal rose and pleasure-garden, in which he loved himself. For we shall be like this in the resurrection of the dead, as Christ tells us in Matthew 13 and 22: that we shall neither marry, nor be given in marriage, but are like the angels of God.

3. Such a human being, as Adam was before his Eve, shall rise again and take possession of Paradise once more, and possess it eternally; not as a man or a woman, but as the Scripture says: "They are virgins and follow God and the Lamb"; they are like the angels of God—yet not merely pure spirit as the angels are, but in heavenly bodies, in which the spiritual angelic body dwells within.

4. Since Adam was created into Paradise for eternal life, in the image of God, and God himself had breathed his life and spirit into him; we may well describe how he was in his innocence, how he fell, what he is now, and what he shall finally become again.

5. Had God created him for this earthly, fragile misery—this naked, sick, beast-like, toilsome life—He would not have brought him into Paradise. Had He desired beast-like impregnation and procreation, He would have created man and woman right at the beginning, and the two sexes would have gone into the division of the two tinctures through the <term>Word "Let it be" <note>original: "Verbo Fiat" — the divine command of creation from Genesis.</note></term>, just as with other earthly creatures.

6. Every creature brings its own clothing from its mother's womb; but man comes into the world miserable, naked, and bare, in the highest poverty and impotence. He is capable of nothing, and at his arrival into this world, he is the most impoverished, miserable, and forsaken creature among all species, unable to help himself at all. This sufficiently indicates to us that he was not created by God into this misery, but rather into his perfection, like all other creatures. The very first man forfeited this through false lust, whereupon God later—during his sleep—first formed him for natural life as man and woman, according to the characteristics of all earthly creatures in the external <term>Fiat <note>original: "Fiat"; Latin for "let it be done." In Böhme's thought, the Fiat is the creative word or "attraction" that gives form to spirit.</note></term>. He attached to him the <term>maggot-sack <note>original: "Madensack"; Böhme’s vivid term for the mortal, biological body which is subject to decay and "worms."</note></term> with animal members for reproduction, of which the poor soul is still ashamed today—that it must carry an animal form upon its body.

7. Two fixed and constant essences were in Adam: the spiritual body from the essence of love of the inner heaven, which was God’s temple; and the outer body, the <term>Limus <note>original: "Limus"; Latin for "slime" or "mud," referring to the "dust of the earth" from which Adam was formed in Genesis 2:7.</note></term> of the earth, which was the casing and dwelling-house of the inner spiritual body. This was in no way manifest according to the vanity of the earth; for he was a *Limus*, <gloss>an extract of the good part of the earth</gloss>, which at the Last Judgment shall be separated from the vanity of the curse and the corruption of the Devil.

8. These same two essences—the inner heavenly and the outer heavenly—were married to one another and contained in one *Corpus* <note>original: "Corpus"; Latin for "body."</note>. Within them was the most holy <term>Tincture <note>A spiritual "dye" or life-force that transforms and enlivens matter.</note></term> of the Divine Fire and Light, serving as the great, joyful desire of love which ignited the essence. Thus, the two essences desired each other quite fervently in this love-desire and loved one another: the inner loved the outer as its manifestation and sensitivity; and the outer loved the inner as its great sweetness and joy-realm, its noble pearl and most beloved consort. And yet they were not two bodies, but only one; though of two kinds of essence—one inner, heavenly, and holy, and one from the essence of time—which were married together into an eternal one.

9. And in this fiery love-desire stood the **Magical Impregnation and Birth**; for the Tincture penetrated through both essences, through the inner and the outer, and awakened the desire. And the desire was the <term>Fiat</term> that grasped the pleasure of love and brought it into a substance. Thus, the likeness of the Image was captured in this substance, as a spiritual image according to the first. Just as the <term>Fiat</term> had grasped and formed the first image, Adam: so also was the likeness from the first grasped for reproduction. And in this grasping, the **Magical Birth** occurred immediately, wherein the spiritual body became outward in the birth.

# Of the Animalistic Man #

<margin>Chapter 21</margin>
In the Beginning <note>original: "Principio"</note> take hold / otherwise the Heavenly Image <term>Heavenly Image (Himmels Bilde): the divine spiritual form in which humanity was originally created, representing our true, unfallen nature</term> that God created in Adam / is not capable of the Kingdom of God / nor can it possess it outside of that. It does not help to put on a show, to be a hypocrite, to flatter, or to offer empty comfort; one must be born [anew] or be lost / for the Pearl-tree <term>Pearl-tree (Perlenbaum): a symbol of the divine seed or Christ-spirit within the soul that must grow and flourish to bear spiritual fruit</term> has withered in Adam and Eve; it must receive Divine Essence <term>Essence (Essenz): the spiritual substance or "food" that sustains the soul's divine life</term> once again and die to the beast / or it cannot turn green and bear fruit / from which the soul eats.

15. Now when Adam and Eve had awakened in the Animalistic Property / the beast stood there naked and bare / for previously the Heavenly Image had completely permeated and clothed the outward man with Divine Power / for the beast was not manifest before; that same property lay hidden in Temperance <term>Temperance (Temperanz): the state of perfect, harmonious balance where no single quality dominates another</term> / just as it is also outside of the creature: But now as the image from the Heavenly Essence faded / the beast became manifest as the Animalistic Property; thus the poor soul from the first Principle <term>Principle (Principio): the dark, fiery root of existence; the soul's raw state before being illuminated by divine light</term> now stood there surrounded by this beast / completely naked and bare.

16. ### The 22nd Chapter. ###

## Of the origin of actual sins, and of the awakening of God’s wrath in human nature. ##

<margin>the</margin>
1. The Scripture says, God made all things through His Word, and without the same is nothing made that is made: John 1. Out of His spoken Word (which became substantial in the **Word: Let there be** <term>Word: Let there be (Verbo Fiat): the creative command of God that brings potentiality into physical existence</term>) all things went into formations: First into an **Essence** <term>Essence (Ens): the fundamental spiritual seed or "being-ness" of a thing before it takes physical form</term> or the desire of a property, and out of that same property into a **Solidification** <term>Solidification (Compaction): the process by which spiritual energy condenses into tangible matter</term> of **Sulfur**, **Mercury**, and **Salt**, as into a formed nature; and out of that same **Essence** in the formed nature, the Word becomes a creatural life, and leads itself out of the **Solidification** of **Sulfur**, **Mercury**, and **Salt** out from the body—that is, it manifests itself in an audible being, for which purpose God created nature and the creature.

<margin>✝</margin>
2. Thus every creature has a center for its own speaking or resonance of the formed Word within itself, both the eternal and the temporal; the irrational animals as well as man: For the first **Essence** was spoken out from God’s resonance through the Wisdom from the Center, toward fire and light, and was grasped in the **Let there be** <note>original: "Fiat"</note>, and entered into a **Solidification**.

3. In each is the first **Essence**, from which the form of the **Solidification** (which has arisen out of time) is an Eternal thing from the eternally speaking Word, spoken through Wisdom out of the Spiritual World-being into a "time," as into a formed being, according to the Spiritual **Essence**; which **Essence** cannot be broken by any element or by anything.

4. And although the elemental **Solidification** of the body (which the **Essence** has drawn to itself—that is, breathed out of itself as an outward degree) passes away and becomes nothing (because it has a temporal beginning), yet the first **Essence** cannot pass away: Just as one sees that all things return again into their Mother from which they arose and went forth, namely into the 4 elements.

# On the origin of actual sins, etc.

Child of God's Love: All greedy craving of all estates <note>social classes or ranks</note>, as they are called in <margin>Chapter 22</margin>, are all from the serpent's <term>Ens: A Latin term meaning "essence" or "being." For Böhme, this refers to the spiritual substance or "spiritual fuel" that determines a person's nature.</term>.

72. I am not speaking of the offices <note>positions of authority or professional roles</note> themselves, but of the falsehood within those offices: An office in its proper standing is God's ordinance, provided it is conducted in holy desire and arises from a Divine root toward the good; but where it is not so—where it arises only from a root toward <term>selfhood: "Selbheit," Böhme’s term for the egoistic, self-centered nature that turned away from God.</term> and pride—then it is from the serpent’s cunning and leads to destruction.

<margin>46</margin>
73. All war, however raging it may be, originates from God's wrath; and whoever begins it does so from a personal desire for selfhood, out of the serpent's essence. Unless such a war arises by God's command—that a people has risen up in His <term>grimness: "Grimmigkeit," the harsh, dark, and wrathful quality of nature apart from God’s light.</term> so that He might swallow up His own wrath and ordain a holier state in its place, as happened with Israel and the Heathens—otherwise, it is all born of the internal <term>Turba: Latin for "turmoil" or "disturbance." In Böhme's thought, this is the destructive power of God's wrath that breaks things apart when they fall away from His love.</term> within selfhood. *No true Christian born of Christ is meant to awaken the sword of the Turba*, unless the Spirit of Zeal from God awakens it within them, as He often wishes to punish sin. Everything that rises in wrath for the sake of self-honor and pride and leads to revenge is of the devil—be it noble or ignoble, none are excepted; before God, they are all equal.

74. Earthly government originates from the Fall into the serpent's cunning; when man, out of self-will, departed from Divine obedience, he had to have a judge who would punish the false desire in its substance and break the false substance. Therefore, authority and lordship are ordained by God as a protection for righteous substance and will, and not for selfhood and self-will to perish in luxury through the destruction of <term>civil order: "Policeyen," referring here to the governance and moral regulation of a community.</term> and the oppression of the wretched and powerless. All that do this have arisen from the serpent's essence, no matter how it might glitter, even if it were entirely covered with gold, pearls, and the sun itself; it is born from the serpent’s essence, has the serpent's being in its government, and leads to destruction, unless it be <term>born anew: "New gebohren," referring to the spiritual rebirth in Christ.</term>.

75. Everything is idolatrous that is not born from the essence of love and does not carry a will of righteousness and truth—a will that seeks to work something good on earth to serve its neighbor; for in Adam we are all one tree, all arisen from a single root.

77. Everything else is communal. Whoever has two coats, and sees that his brother has none, then the second coat belongs to his brother, just as Christ teaches us.

78. For we come naked into this world and take hardly even the shirt with us, which is the cover for our shame. All else we possess either through the necessity of our office <note>professional or social duties</note> or out of greed, arising from the serpent’s false desire. Every person should seek the benefit and care of his neighbor, how he may serve and be useful to him, just as one branch on a tree gives its strength, <term>essence: Original: "Essenz," referring to the spiritual substance of a thing</term>, and being to the other, and they grow and bear fruit in a single desire. ## Chapter 23.

# How God called back Adam and his Eve—after they had entered into vanity and awakened within the serpent's <term>Ens: Latin for "being" or "essence"; here referring to the spiritual fuel or substance of the serpent</term>—and imposed the order of this troublesome world upon them; and ordained the Crusher of the Serpent as a helper.

As Adam and Eve had now eaten from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil and had become <term>monstrous: In Böhme's vocabulary, "monstrous" refers to a distorted, unnatural state that deviates from the original divine image</term> because of the serpent: Moses writes of it thus: Their eyes were opened, and they became aware that they were naked, and they wove fig leaves together and made themselves aprons. There, the soul recognized the monstrous image and was ashamed that such a coarse animal had awakened in its tender body, with gross flesh and hard bones, and with an animalistic <term>maggot-sack: "Madensack," a common Baroque-era term for the mortal, decaying body</term> of vanity. They wished to hide this from God’s eyes and crept behind the trees in shame. Thus, they were ashamed of the deformity of the animal, for the animalistic Ens had swallowed the heavenly one and raised itself up; because they had not recognized this before, they now knew not what to do for shame.

2. The serpent's cunning did not wish to cover the shame here, but only revealed it and accused them as apostates and faithless ones; for God's wrath woke up within them and now placed them before the strict judgment, to swallow them into itself, into the dark world, just as happened <margin>as</margin> to Lucifer.

4. And here was the heavy state before God's wrath, the state in which Christ was in the garden when He prayed and was to overcome this wrath,

5. 7. In Adam, God’s will was also meant to be done; but through the serpent's cunning, he raised up his own will instead. That same self-will the humanity of Christ now had to give over to the wrath of God on the Cross to be swallowed up: But the holy name *Jesus* led it into the death of selfhood, so that it had to die in the fierce death, and through death in His resurrection, enter again into true <term>resignation: "Gelassenheit," a key mystical term meaning the state of yielding one's will entirely to God</term>, as if into the Divine harmony.

8. After the awakening of wrath, Adam stood in Paradise before God and all the holy angels in great shame. The devils mocked him, because this image of God—which was intended to occupy its Royal throne—had become a monstrous animal. And into this mockery Christ had to enter, allowing himself to be scorned, mocked, spit upon, scourged, and crowned with thorns as a false king; for Adam was a king and <term>Hierarch: A leader or ruler in a sacred spiritual order</term>, but he became false and apostate.

9. Here Christ stood in his place and let himself be condemned to death; for Adam was to be judged by God's wrath. Here stood Adam—that is, Christ in Adam's humanity—in his place. Adam was to be cast out as a curse: Christ allowed himself to hang as a curse on the Cross, as a mockery before heaven and earth. And in summary, the entire <term>Process: The transformative spiritual journey or sequence of events leading from the Fall to salvation</term> of Christ, from his Incarnation to his Ascension and the sending of the Holy Spirit, is the state of Adam: whatever Adam had forfeited, Christ had to place himself into that same state in Adam’s person and lead life out of death once more.

16. Therefore Moses now says: *And the Lord God called Adam and said to him: Where are you?* Why does He not say: "Where are you both, Adam and Eve?" No: He called Adam as the first image that He created in Paradise, and not as "man and woman"; for the one who called was the one walking in the garden, as the Word of the light-world, the voice of the second <term>Principle: Böhme divides reality into three 'Principles': the dark fire-world, the light-world of God's love, and the outer visible world.</term>. That voice called back into the ignited wrath and wedded itself again into the faded heavenly being, so that it might awaken itself therein in the name of JESUS <note>original Latin: "IHESV"</note>, as in the deepest love of the Godhead. In the fullness of time, this voice intended to marry into the faded being <note>original: "Ente"; from the Latin *ens*, meaning essence or substance</note> by introducing the holy divine being of the heavenly world-essence, to become manifest, to open Paradise again, and meanwhile to crush the head of the serpent’s being. This Crusher of the Serpent said to Adam: "Where are you?"

17. Thus speaks Reason: "Surely He saw him well; why then did He say, 'Where are you?'" He saw him well, but Adam did not see Him, for his eyes had departed from Adonai <note>original: "Adonay"; a Hebrew name for God, meaning 'Lord'</note>—out of the divine world and into time, as if into the outer world, into the serpent’s being, both evil and good, into death and fragility. Out of these monstrous eyes, Adam looked into the property of the fire’s tincture <term>Tincture: In alchemy and Böhme’s theology, a 'tincture' is the spiritual power or inner quality that gives a substance its life and characteristics.</term>. But the property of the light’s tincture, which he had lost, spoke to him: "Where are you, Adam?" This is as much as to say: "Seek me and look upon me again; I have come to give myself to you once more." And <margin>To Him</margin> Adam said: "I heard the voice in the garden and I am afraid, for I am naked."

18. This calling was nothing other than the resonance of the holy Word introducing itself back into the light of life; otherwise, Adam would not have been able to hear this voice. Therefore he said: "I am naked and I am afraid."

<margin>felt</margin> 19. Of what was he afraid? He feared within himself the world of God’s wrath; he feared it would fully ignite and swallow him up, just as happened to Lucifer. Therefore he trembled before the call of the holy voice, just as wrath trembles before love, as can be seen at the Cross of Christ. For the fruit of the serpent was already here, for it recognized the voice which called into Adam’s being, and it feared God’s face; for it knew the falsehood within itself and wanted to hide it.

20. And God said: "Who told you that you are naked?" That is to say: the serpent’s being has told you that you should imagine <note>original: "imaginiren"; Böhme uses this to mean 'to form' or 'to give shape to' a spiritual desire</note> yourself into the animalistic property and awaken it.

## The 24th Chapter.

->On the Curse of the Earth and the Body of Sickness /<-
->how it came to be?<-

<image-desc>Decorative initial 'D' featuring elaborate foliage and scrollwork. Along the right margin of the first three paragraphs is a vertical decorative woodcut border consisting of stylized foliate or floral motifs repeating along a central line.</image-desc>

That God cursed the field for the sake of man's sin / so that it should bear thorns / and thistles / and that he only commands man to eat the herb of the field after the committed sin / and to eat his bread in the sweat of his face; testifies to us enough / that the same would not have been so in Paradise / the field would not have borne thorns and thistles / and other evil herbs that are poisonous / but in the curse these properties become manifest: For as the body was after the Fall / so also was its food / the half-serpent man must now eat such food / as his desire required.

2. 3. Thus the heavenly became a *mystery* <note>original: "Mysterium"</note> to man / and he remained thus standing in the curse between time and eternity / as if half-dead to the heavenly: Yet at the goal of the Covenant <note>A reference to God's promise of a Savior</note> he was encompassed anew with the promise / and on the earthly side bound hard to the bond of the stars and the four elements / infected with the sickness of the serpent and the devil; bound hard with three strong chains / from which he may not be released / until the total breaking of his earthly body; for the curse of the earth and the serpent also pressed into the earthly man / as into the *earthly mass* <gloss>Limus</gloss> of the earth.

5. Thus an earthly body is now sown into the earth, and the earth accepts it as its own property. But the *Ens* <term>original: *Ens*; the essential, eternal substance or inner "being" of a thing</term> from eternity (which cannot be broken) lies within this earthly sown body. Only the coarse flesh breaks apart, as the essence of time, just as a fixed metal does not break in the earth; so also the fixed part of the human body does not; and as the Artist <note>In Böhme’s writing, the "Artist" often refers to an alchemist, symbolizing God’s power to refine and resurrect the pure essence from the "coarse" material.</note> brings forth a beautiful gold out of the earth, so also the human gold lies buried in the earth and waits for the Artist for its awakening.

6. And as the metallic properties in the earth are many and of various kinds, so also is the human property of the *Ens*. Therefore, everything must be tested through the fire; whatever property each person has taken upon themselves during this time and impressed into their bodies (as if with the desire of the *Fiat*), that shall be tested in the fire of God; whether they have impressed into themselves a fixed, constant property from the Divine *Ens*, or a hellish, beast-like one; all of that shall be tested in the fire of God; and as the *Ens* will be in each body, so also such a fire will ignite itself in that same *Ens*.

7. And as mercury <note>original: *Quecksilber*; in alchemy, mercury represents the volatile, transformative principle.</note> vanishes in the fire, so also does all godless, devilish, serpentine work, which has been impressed from the dark world and the devil's desire.

And just as the outer stars always break one another's *Ens* and transmute it into another, all according to the greatest power: So also herewith the human mind (which is also a magical star) is affected.
