->How God drove Adam out of Paradise<-

## Chapter 25.

# How God drove Adam out of Paradise and placed the Cherub before the Garden.

When God had cursed the serpent together with the earth, the **animal-man** <note>Böhme uses the term "animal-man" (*Thier-Mensch*) to describe the state of humanity after the Fall, governed by earthly instincts and physical needs rather than divine spirit.</note> was of no more use in Paradise, for he could no longer enjoy the fruit of Paradise; so God laid upon him the labor and toil of the world and drove him out of the Garden of Eden, and stationed the **Cherub** with the **flaming sword** of judgment before it. This was done so that, when the newborn **Virgin-child** <note>The "Virgin-child" represents the Christ-like nature or the "new man" born within the believer through spiritual transformation.</note> from the **woman's seed** should return and enter Paradise again, this angel with the flaming sword would cut the serpent's animal nature away from it and allow it to enter Paradise no further.

2. The angel with the sword is the true **destroying angel** <note>original: *würgEngel*, literally a "strangling" or "slaying angel" who executes divine judgment.</note> who carries both death and life in his sword; he holds within it both God’s love and His wrath. When a person dies in this world, they come before the gates of Paradise, before this angel, and there the soul must pass through this judgment.

<margin>
<image-desc>A vertical series of decorative calligraphic flourishes marking the paragraph.</image-desc>
</margin>
3. If the soul is now caught in God’s wrath, it cannot pass through this judgment. But if it is a **Virgin-child** born of the woman’s seed, it can pass through this sword, and the angel cuts away the animal nature begotten of the serpent’s **essence** <note>original: *Ente*, likely from the Latin *ens* or *entia*, referring to the fundamental being or "substance" of the fallen nature.</note>. Then the soul becomes an angel of God and serves Him in His temple in Paradise, awaiting the Day of Judgment and the resurrection of the external body. When this angel with the flaming sword separates the earth from its curse, the true human body will return, for it too must pass through this sword; and the sword will cut away its animal nature, so that it may be solely a human and no longer an animal.

4. To the earthly man, the words of Moses regarding this mystery are entirely hidden. For Moses speaks of an angel and a sword, and though the external figure was certainly as he described—for thus was Adam driven out—it has a very different **A. B. C.** <note>Böhme frequently uses "A. B. C." to mean the fundamental spiritual principles or the "alphabet" of divine wisdom that must be learned to understand the inner meaning of Scripture.</note> within. The natural man, without God's light, understands nothing of it.

5. That same sword is within a person when they turn back and enter into repentance for their committed sins, casting away vanity and entering into the **child’s garment** <note>original: *Kinder Hembde*, literally "child's shirt," symbolizing a return to innocence, humility, and the state of being a child of God.</note>. Then the **Morning Star** <note>A symbol for Christ and the dawning of spiritual enlightenment within the soul.</note> rises in the virgin-like, enclosed essence, in the true seed of the woman, in the Spirit of Christ.

<meta>catchword: 6. And</meta>

<summary>This page reinterprets the expulsion of Adam from Eden as a spiritual allegory for the soul's journey, where the Cherub's flaming sword acts as a filter that strips away the "animal" nature to allow the "Virgin-child" (the reborn spirit) back into Paradise.</summary>

6. And in this anxious gateway of true repentance stands the angel with the **flaming sword**; and the **Virgin-branch** <note>Böhme uses "Virgin-branch" or "Virgin-child" to represent the budding spiritual life within a person, born from the "seed of the woman" mentioned in Genesis.</note> presses through this flaming sword into Paradise—into the light, into the life of Christ—and grows through this sword.

7. Thus the **Virgin-child** stands with its beautiful roses in the new growth within Paradise; and the poor soul, which gives birth to this child, stands the entire time within the flaming sword, bound fast by a bond to the outer world—to the **coarse beast**. <note>The "coarse beast" refers to the physical, animalistic body and its earthly instincts.</note> There, the Virgin-child is often stung by this flaming sword; for the **fire-soul**, <note>The "fire-soul" (*Feuerseele*) is Böhme’s term for the soul’s primary energetic nature, which can either burn with the fire of God's wrath or be lightened by divine love.</note> which stands bound to the **serpent monster** <note>original: *Schlangen Monstro*</note> within the flaming sword of God’s wrath, gazes daily upon that serpent monster and sins. Then this flaming sword cuts the sin away and swallows it into God’s wrath, where it is pressed and judged as in a winepress.

8. So must the poor Virgin-child, which is born from the soul under the **cross of Christ**, stand in the death of Christ; and the **sword of tribulation** passes through it. It must allow itself to be pulled through this flaming sword, and the fire constantly burns away the loathing which the soul introduces from the serpent monster. This is a painful process when that which the fire-soul desires from its monster is cut away from it.

9. There, the Virgin-child must plead with the fire-soul and offer it love, so that it might abandon the monster of the serpent; then conflict and reluctance begin, for the part of the fire-soul has brought in the serpent monster and wishes to have its joy within it, loving the **evil beast**.

10. Then **Sophia** <note>Sophia, or Divine Wisdom, represents the second "Principle" of God—the realm of light and love—acting as the spiritual bridge back to the divine.</note> speaks against it as the second Principle—the part of the Light-world—and so the struggle between the **seed of the woman** and the **seed of the serpent** begins. Then the person walks in sadness and tribulation; sometimes the Virgin-child triumphs, and sometimes the serpent-child triumphs.

11. At this, the Devil incites all the "monsters" <note>Here referring to worldly people or demonic influences.</note> against the Virgin-child to strike it, to mock it, to scorn and laugh at it, and to treat it as a fool, so that it may not be recognized—and so that his own kingdom, the Devil’s, is not revealed.

12. The Virgin-child must endure this in the spirit of Christ, allowing itself to be scourged, persecuted, and scolded; it must often let itself be called "one possessed by the Devil," let itself be cursed, and always be held as a **cleansing sacrifice** <note>original: *Fegeopffer*; a sacrifice intended to scour or purify.</note> for the world, until the outer beast has completed its course in its **constellation**. <note>The "constellation" refers to the predestined lifespan and external influences governed by the stars over the physical body.</note> Then the Cherub cuts the coarse beast away and lets it fall away until the Judgment of God. This experience is "purgatory" <note>original: *Fegefeuers*</note> enough for anyone; yet the current "too-clever" world does not believe this, wanting only to be an "adopted child" from the outside, receiving a mere external washing away of sins through grace. However, the whole world was also such a Paradise before the curse; but because God recognized the Fall, the holy Paradise was only revealed to them in a certain place. For why should the entire outer world bear Paradisiacal fruit when there was no creature on Earth capable of enjoying it?

# On the Propagation of Mankind in this World

...to wake up from the conclusions of Reason <note>Böhme often personifies "Reason" (Vernunfft) as a limited, worldly way of thinking that fails to grasp divine mysteries.</note>, and yet to see God's clear countenance, who desires no evil nor can desire it, and who has set Himself as judge over all evil, godless being; such a conclusion will shatter all things in the sword of His wrath and remove the Cherub.

4. Here it is now considered how it came to pass that Adam and Eve for the first time bore an evil child and a murderer. For Reason says: it happened by God's decree; that He made a choice and chose a host of people for damnation, and others for His love.

5. Yes, dear Reason: from what are you born? And from what do you speak under the cover of Scripture? Do you not speak from the Serpent's essence <note>original: *Ente*; a term Böhme uses for the fundamental substance or "being-ness" of a thing</note> and words? Who brought the false essence <note>original: *Ens*</note> into Eve's womb <note>original: *Matricem*</note>, in which Cain was conceived? Did not the Devil do it through the Serpent, and made Eve's womb <note>original: *Matricem*</note> monstrous?

6. Do you not understand how the Word of promise immediately embodied itself in Eve's womb <note>original: *Matricem*</note>, in her seed, and that the struggle between God's wrath and God's love soon began? For God's love embodied itself in the monster of the Serpent in God's wrath, to crush the head <note>A reference to Genesis 3:15, the prophecy that the seed of the woman would crush the serpent's head.</note>, into which the fire-soul <term>Feurseele: the soul seen as a fiery spark of divine power that can either burn in wrath or shine in light</term>—which lay captive in God's wrath—should submit its free will.

<margin>❦ ❦ ❦ ❦</margin>
7. **For the fire-soul is a root out of Divine Omnipotence, and therefore it has free will, and that may be taken from it by nothing: it may draw its essence from the Fire or the Light.**

8. But you say: why did the Crusher of the Serpent not immediately crush the head in the first seed of the Serpent's essence <note>original: *Enti*</note>, and why did He allow the Serpent’s murderous, poisonous <gloss>poisonous</gloss> will to rise up in the soul's essence <note>original: *Ente*</note>? That is spoken exactly as if I said: Why, when God saw that Adam became evil, did He not cast him out, or make him into nothing and create a new Adam? In the same way, Reason wishes to judge concerning the devils: that it pleased God that there should be devils, so that it might be known what an Angel is.

9. Listen, Reason: I have answered you above, that if God had been required to move Himself once more for the sake of man, and to lead the first movement into a stillness in the human and earthly essence <note>original: *Ente*</note>, then the six days' work of Creation would have had to go backward and be led into an inactive rest. God did not want that; the whole Creation should and must persist in its first movement; His first formed essence <note>original: *Ens*</note> in the "Let it be done" Word <note>original: *Verbo Fiat*; the creative command of God</note> should persist. Whether it happens in Love or Wrath, whichever one would grasp: the Wrath was open, and so also was the Love.

->### and of Cain the Firstborn and Brother-Murderer.<-

10. Love alone is called God; Wrath is called His strength and power. Whatever the free will desires, it shall be confirmed in that very thing—either in Love or in Wrath.

11. For the free will was born out of Love and Wrath, as if out of the Fire-world and Light-world. Thus, it could also choose for itself a place for its active life. Had God’s Love drowned the free will in the Essence <note>original: *Ente*; a term Böhme uses for the fundamental substance or "being-ness" of a thing</note> within Eve’s seed—in the Love where He had been ignited in Wrath—then the fiery movement in the womb <note>original: *Matrice*</note> would have had to cease; but from the Light-Essence alone, no soul can be born.

12. Also, the corrupted Essence <note>original: *Ens*</note> of the Earthly Slime <note>original: *Limi*; referring to the Latin *limus*, the "dust of the ground" from which man was made</note> would have had to be judged through fire immediately. This could not happen, for the movement of the new Rebirth, the opening of Divine sweetness, and the overcoming of the Fire (which is the Wrath of God) belonged alone to the Name of Jesus.

13. The Word that had embodied itself had the fiery sword (like the Cherub) on the outside, and Jesus on the inside, who was to overcome the fiery sword with Love. Thus, the Name of Jesus stood hidden within the fiery sword and was not manifest until the time when God wished to move within it and reveal Him.
<margin>immanent</margin>

14. Thus, the introduced Serpent-Essence <note>original: *Ens*</note>, which Eve had brought in through her imagination and lust, had to be cast away; for in Cain, the murderous image of the Serpent was manifest, which cannot inherit the Kingdom of God. On the other hand, the soul—in its free will and in the Heavenly faded Essence <note>original: *Ente*</note>—was manifest as the goal of the Covenant in the promised Word, into which the free will was meant to enter.

15. And although the Serpent-Essence <note>original: *Ens*</note> had to be cast away—as must happen in all of Eve’s children—there still lay that part of the Heavenly world-being hidden in the Covenant of the Word, within the faded Essence, as a possibility for the new Rebirth. Therefore, God said to Cain when the murderous spirit advised him: *Rule over sin.* <note>A reference to Genesis 4:7, where God warns Cain that sin is crouching at the door, but he must master it.</note>

16. So you ask: "With what? He could not!" But why could he not? The Serpent’s desire held him and led him to brother-murder. Why? Because the free will had surrendered itself into the Serpent-Essence <note>original: *Ens*</note>, which held him captive.

17. Thus Reason <note>Böhme's term for limited, worldly logic that fails to see divine truth.</note> says: "God wanted it to be so, otherwise He would have turned Cain's will away from it." No: God’s wrath-will within the Serpent-Essence wanted it, and it captured the free will. But God’s love-will speaks within him: *Rule over sin*—that is, over the grimness and wrath of the Serpent—and do not give her the power.

<header>Of Man’s reproduction in this world.</header>

18. And here it is right for us to recognize how God’s Love and Wrath—understand, within the revealed Word in the Slime <note>original: *Limo*; from the Latin *limus*, the "dust of the ground" or "earthly mud" from which Adam was formed</note> of the Earth and in the Essence <note>original: *Ente*; Böhme’s term for the fundamental "being-ness" or quality of a substance</note> of human property—are in constant struggle out of the Earth. For the Wrath-Essence <note>original: *Ens*</note> is stirred and driven by the Devil, and constantly seeks to swallow up the Love-Essence and possess this kingdom within the Wrath-Essence.

<image-desc>Decorative triple-pronged bracket and flourishes in the left margin next to paragraph 19.</image-desc>
<margin>and</margin>
19. The Wrath-Essence <note>original: *Ens*</note> wants to have man, for it has its king in Lucifer. Likewise, the Love-Essence wants him too, for it has its king in Christ. Therefore, Christ had to lead the human Love-Essence through death and the Wrath-Essence, to unlock another Principle <note>original: *Principium*; a fundamental spiritual realm or starting point</note> as another Kingdom, and leave the prince Lucifer in his Wrath, for his free will chose it for himself.

20. Thus also the free will in Cain chose falsehood, as the Devil’s will. So you ask: Was the murderous will then entirely cast off? It cast itself off; but had the free will drawn again from the Love-Essence <note>original: *Ente*</note>, then he would have been born anew, even after the murder. We leave this to the judgment of God, whether it happened or not, because the text in Moses gives him such a harsh name in despair. For the Word, from which the name of Jesus was revealed, was given to call the poor lost sinner to repentance, and not to lay hold of those already righteous in Love, as Christ said.

21. Cain was an image of the first corrupted Adam in sin, and Abel an image of Christ, the second Adam, as the child of the Virgin. For the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil began in Adam; thus the fruit also manifested immediately as the children of Christ and the children of the Devil and the Serpent.

30. Look at the irrational *creatures*, such as worms, toads, spiders, heathens <note>original: *Heyden*; here likely referring to "wild ones" or creatures of the heath/wilderness, rather than non-Christians.</note>, and other cruel beasts; you will surely see something there, if you are not dead. You say: "God created it." Yes, rightly; His desire in love and wrath has seized the essence with movement and, according to the free will, has *compacted* each essence into a form. No other maker was there than the free will in the Word.

31. The desire in the Word was the *Fiat* <note>Latin: "Let it be"; the creative command of God.</note>, which introduced the free will into an essence. Thus, that same revealed Word is still in all things and has the *Fiat*—the desire—within itself, just as the free will in every thing introduces itself into a spirit; so the *Fiat* forms and marks all things. Every root brings forth from itself a branch of its own kind; but when the branch is to be born and takes its beginning in the *essence* <note>original: *Ente*; a grammatical variation of *Ens* (essence).</note> of the root, the essence forms itself into a branch according to how the root is seized in its power and free will at that time, by both the upper and lower constellations <note>original: *Gestirne*; referring to astrological or celestial influences believed to shape a person's character at birth.</note>.

Thus, a spirit is also *formed* in the essence of the seed; often an angel, if the parents are in holy desire, but often also an animal, a serpent, and an image of the devil, according to both the soul’s essence and the essence of the outer flesh.

With the holy you are holy, and with the perverse you are perverse* <note>original: *Bey den heiligen bistu heilig und bey den verkehrten bistu verkehret*; a reference to Psalm 18:25-26.</note>. <margin>Chapter 26.</margin>
God’s purpose now belongs to the holy <term>Fiat<note>original: *Fiat*; Latin for "Let it be," the creative command from Genesis.</note></term> in the newly introduced Word. For it does not depend on anyone’s own willing, making, nor running or striving, but on God's mercy: He has mercy on whom He will—namely, those who, with their free will, die to their own <term>selfhood<note>original: *selbheit*; Böhme’s term for the ego or the selfish, separate will that is detached from God.</note></term> in His grace and surrender themselves to Him. And He hardens whom He will—namely, those who, like Cain, run by their own power and wish to take the Kingdom of God for themselves in their own evil will, and do not wish to die to their own will in their selfhood.
<image-desc>A vertical series of five small decorative woodcut icons, resembling stacked bells or architectural finials, is printed in the right margin next to the first paragraph.</image-desc>

35. So the Scripture speaks: Has not a potter, from a lump of clay, the power to make what He will—one vessel for honor or another for dishonor? That is to say: if the personal will wishes to be angry (since it is evil), then the *Fiat* in the Word makes it a vessel of wrath. Or, if the holy *Fiat* (in the holy Word) makes the will—which sinks itself into God’s love and mercy and dies to its "I-ness"—into a vessel for honor, should the first will be angry about that? Indeed, this Potter has the power to do as He will with His clay (as with the <term>essence<note>original: *Ente*; a term Böhme uses for the spiritual substance or "being" of a thing.</note></term> or the seed). For whatever purpose any seed is good and useful, He makes it into a vessel: either for the use of His wrath or for the use of His love.

36. To God, the holy person is a "sweet savor" unto life, and the godless person is a "sweet savor" unto death in His wrath. They must all enter into His glory and praise Him: one in the quality of His wrath, who must call the evil "good"; the other in the quality of His love, who must call the good "good." For it must be so, in order that the distinction between good and evil, light and darkness, life and death may be known. For if there were no death, life would not be manifest to itself; and if there were no darkness, the light would not be manifest to itself.

37. Therefore, the eternal free will has introduced itself into darkness, pain, and torment, as well as through the darkness into fire and light, and into a kingdom of joy. This was done so that the "Nothing" might be known as "Something," and so that the will might have a play <note>Böhme often describes the universe as a "divine play" or "wrestling" of opposing forces.</note> in its "counter-will"—so that the free will of the <term>Unground<note>original: *vngrund*; Böhme’s central concept of the "Groundless" or "Abyss"—the absolute, undifferentiated origin of God and all things before manifestation.</note></term> might be manifest to itself in the "ground." For without evil and good, there could be no foundation.

38. For the evil creates pain and movement, and the good creates substance and power. Yet these two essences are but one single essence, just as fire and light are only one essence; likewise, darkness and light are only one, yet they divide into two mighty distinctions. However, there is no separation; for one dwells in the other and yet does not grasp the other. One denies the other, for it is not the other.

# Of Man’s Procreation in This World.

The free will is not bound; for if it were bound, then no judgment could pass over it with justice. Man has laws and teachings which are given to him not for death, but for life; but if he transgresses them and persists in that transgression, judgment now passes over him, for every judgment arises from the transgression of the Commandment.

<margin>q. f. d. <note>likely an abbreviation for "quod facit deus" (what God does) or a similar cross-reference notation.</note></margin>
52. Thus you say: "He cannot keep the law, he is being pulled [by external forces]." Yes, quite right; yet Truth also scolds him to his face as a faithless one who allows himself to be pulled toward evil. The law to do right stands in the light of life as a constant mirror. He sees it and knows that he is a liar and runs upon the paths of the Devil. It shows him the way of Truth, but the free will rejects it; now he becomes **predestined** <note>original: *Prædestiniret*</note> to damnation. However, this occurs in such a way that the will remains free while it is in this tabernacle <note>original: *Hütten*, referring to the physical body as a temporary shelter or hut.</note>. But the heavy bond of God’s wrath, caught in the tug of the Devil’s desire, draws many toward the damnation of death.

53. Reason <note>original: *Vernunfft*. Böhme often treats "Reason" as the limited, earthly logic that struggles to understand divine mysteries.</note> says: "If man has free will, then God is not Almighty over him, such that He may do with him what He wills." The free will is not grasped out of any beginning, nor out of any foundation in nothingness, nor formed by anything. It is its own origin <note>original: *vhrstandt*, a Böhme term for the primal "standing forth" or origin of a thing.</note> out of the Word of Divine Power, out of God’s love and wrath. It forms for itself, in its own will, a center for its seat. It bears itself in the first **Principle** <note>original: *Principio*. In Böhme’s cosmology, the First Principle is the dark, fiery source of power/strength.</note> toward fire and light. Its true origin is in the Nothing, where the Nothing—as the Trinity <note>original: $\Delta$. Böhme uses the Greek letter Delta to symbolize the Triangle of the Trinity or the Divine Eye.</note>, or however one might unfold it: A. O. V. <note>These letters likely represent mystical vowel sounds or a variation of "Alpha and Omega," representing the totality of the divine name.</note>—leads itself into a delight for contemplation; and that delight leads itself into a will, and the will into a desire, and the desire into a being <note>original: *Wesen*.</note>.

54. Now the Eternal Origin, as God, is a judge over the being. If the delight (having deviated from Him) has led itself into an evil being, then He judges that being in its **Principle**—into whatever torment and quality, or into whatever essence <note>original: *Ens*.</note> the delight from the deviated Trinity <note>$\Delta$</note> has led itself into a **Principle**. Therein it is confirmed by the universal Eternal Free Will, which is the Unground <note>original: *vngrundt*. One of Böhme’s most famous terms, referring to the absolute abyss or "bottomless" nothingness that exists before and beyond all created nature and even before God's self-manifestation.</note> and the cause of all grounds.

55. That which is "ungroundly" <note>pertaining to the *Unground*</note> judges that which leads itself into a ground <note>i.e., into a fixed, limited existence</note>. It separates the good, which leads itself into a good **essence** <note>original: *Ens*</note>, into the good (as into the Divine Love); and the evil (which has led itself into an evil **essence** and placed and formed itself into a center as an evil spirit and will) into His fury and wrath.

56. For how may one judge a thing that does not belong to him? How would God judge the will of the creature if that will had not originated from Him? Or, how may a judgment pass over a thing that is bound, and is not free in its willing and doing?

57. The human and angelic will emerged with the movement of the **Unground** <note>original: *Ungrund*; Böhme’s term for the primal, bottomless abyss or "nothingness" that precedes the existence of God as a person or the world as a thing</note> (when the Deity moved itself in its state of contemplation and perceptibility, and with that movement introduced a beginning to spirits). As they arose from that same beginning, so every beginning now proceeds toward its end; and the end is that which was before the beginning. Therein lies the **test** <note>original: *Proba*; a trial or demonstration of quality</note> of the beginning: into whatever state the beginning has introduced itself.

58. Thus, God is before and outside of all beginnings, and from Him proceeds every beginning; He is also the end of all beginnings. Therefore, the "middle" of all begun things stands between the beginning and the end; for everything must return with its beginning through the end and back into that from which it originated.

59. Since God is an "earnest" <note>or "jealous"</note> God and a consuming fire, and also a dear, merciful God: now, within every free will—through the **Center** <note>original: *Centro*; the focal point of an individual's spiritual being</note> it has introduced—its judge is born within itself, either Divine Love or Divine Wrath. For when a thing begins, it enters into time; but when that same time is seized by the end (that is, by eternity), it then exists in its own Eternal state, from which it has formed itself into a **solidification** <note>original: *Compaction*; the process of a spiritual will becoming a tangible "thing" or essence</note>, and is thus confirmed for eternity.

60. Therefore, the free will carries its own judgment for good or evil within itself. It has its judgment within; it has God’s Love and Wrath within. Whatever it grasps and desires, that it forms within itself; and thus it merely forms itself into a center according to its own longing.

61. For this is also how the world had its origin: namely, in the free will of the two eternal principles, out of the dark fire-desire and out of the divine light fire-desire. Gebährerin*; the spiritual matrix or "mother" of nature</note>, just as the will grasped itself at each place within the Birth-giver through the creative Word. Thus an essence came to be, and from that essence its spirit arose according to the nature of that essence, as if by God’s breathing or awakening within the principles.

62. But because the principles were as one with each other, no thing was grasped in the free will that did not have both a good and an evil within itself, according to the nature and power of the Eternal Birth-giver, toward both light and darkness.

63. Now, however, every spirit with its free will first arises from the solidification of its center, and is free after its resultant birth; it may draw into itself either from God’s Love or from God’s Wrath and introduce its will however it chooses. But this is the catch: as the mother (the essence) is, from which the spirit is born, such a longing also arises within the spirit.

God also gave him laws, so that he should break his craving <note>original: *Lust*; in Böhme’s writing, this refers to a strong, often disordered desire or "will" toward earthly things</note> and, through the understanding of the Light, rule over the craving of the darkness.

65. If he does not do this, but instead follows his craving out of the understanding and into a "selfhood" of desire, then that craving solidifies into a **Substance**, from which a new, false will is born. This is a bastard child <note>original: *Hurenkind*; literally "whore-child," used by Böhme to describe a spiritual state or will that is illegitimate because it was not born from the divine order</note> before God and Eternal **Nature**. For it does not originate from the laws of Eternal **Nature**, but from selfhood; and over this passes the judgment of Eternal **Nature**. In the end—when the **Center** <note>original: *Centrum*; the core or focal point of the spirit</note> of the spirit must return to its beginning—it will be spewed out from the free will of eternity.

66. Understand us correctly: The first free will that was breathed into Adam was good. It was indeed derived from God’s Love and Wrath, as from the **Center** of the Eternal Birth-giver <note>Böhme’s term for the creative aspect of Eternal Nature</note>, the Eternal Spiritual **Nature**. However, it possessed the understanding within itself to govern itself so that it could exist eternally.

67. But the craving introduced by the Devil was in the **Essence** <note>original: *Ente* or *Ens*; a philosophical term for the fundamental "stuff" or being of a thing</note> of the earth, from which Adam’s outer body was formed. Into that same earthly **Essence**, the Devil introduced his desire through the serpent, as if through the serpent’s cunning **Essence**, so that a craving arose in the **Essence** of the body. The first free will of the breathed-in soul entered into this and accepted the craving of the body, and introduced that craving into a desire for **Substance**.

68. And out of that same **Substance** there now arose another, new, private will, like a bastard child, a false serpent-child. Adam bequeathed this same bastard child to his Eve, and Eve to her son Cain, and so one human has inherited it from another. Thus, we now have in our earthly flesh this same false will from the serpent's **Substance**, into which the Devil introduces his desire; he sifts us and makes us constantly lustful after the Devilish nature, so that the desire he introduces into us might become **Substance** and being within the false bastard child. From this, such a bastard child and the Devil’s "serpent-seed" is continually fathered—and from that same false **Essence**, a Devilish will is born.

69. Thus the Devil "rides" within and over man—over both body and soul. Yet the first introduced free will, which God breathed into Adam, still lies within all people; for it is the true soul, the **Center** of the fire and the light, a spark of Divine Power and Omnipotence. However, it is captured within this evil, introduced bastard child and entirely surrounded by it.

### and concerning Cain, the Firstborn and Brother-Slayer.

70. ...into the faded [nature], the promise was incorporated, so that the first free will <margin>(see Chapter 26)</margin> (which now lies imprisoned in the harlot- and serpent-child <note>Böhme uses "serpent-child" to describe the corrupted, ego-driven nature inherited from the Fall, which acts in opposition to God's will</note>) should direct its desire toward this goal of the promised covenant (which He fulfilled in the humanity of Christ). It must introduce its desire back into its faded heavenly **Essence** <note>original: *Ens*; a technical term in alchemy and Böhme's theology meaning the fundamental "being" or "substance" of a thing</note>, meeting the holy **Essence** of Christ (which He introduced into our faded essence through the seed of Mary). If this occurs, then from that introduced **Essence** of Christ, the Spirit of Christ arises, which breaks the false will of the serpent-harlot-child (in the flesh) and treads upon its head.

71. Thus Reason says: "God gives this holy new **Essence** of Christ to whom He wills, and leaves whom He wills hardened and imprisoned in the serpent's essence." Yes, that is quite right: He gives this holy essence to no one within the "selfhood" of their serpent-child's will. A different kind of earnestness is required for that, because selfhood can no longer take anything from God for itself.

72. But this is the process the free will must undergo if it wishes to receive the holy **Essence**: It must wind itself out of the serpent's desire (out of selfhood and "I-ness" <note>original: *Ichheit*; the state of being focused entirely on the individual ego</note>) and wind itself into God’s mercy. It must die to its own fleshly desire and become weary of it; it must go completely out of the private lust of the flesh and direct its hunger only into the death of the "I" <note>original: *Ichts*; a play on words suggesting the "nothingness" of the self</note>. It must desire to continually die to its own malice and false desires (which reside in the fleshly serpent-child) and desire to rise as a new will in Christ's **Essence**.

74. But if you were to say that you cannot desire good, that is not true. It is only that you allow the serpent-will to hold you in your true, eternal soul-will. It wants God to forgive its sins from without through a mere spoken word, while it remains clinging to its dalliance with the serpent (in its false lust). Such a soul God elects for judgment.

## The 27th Chapter.

# Concerning Cain's and Abel's Offering / and concerning the false and Antichristian Church / as well as concerning the true holy Church.

### A Mirror of the World.

Here once again a veil <note>original: *Deckel*; literally "lid" or "cover," but here referencing the "veil of Moses" from 2 Corinthians 3, signifying a hidden spiritual meaning</note> lies before the face of Moses regarding the offering of the two brothers: why they actually wanted to offer to God, and yet reconciliation stands alone in the earnest will toward God's mercy, in prayer and pleading to God, so that the human being departs from the evil will, turns back, and does penance, and introduces their faith and hope into God’s mercy.

2. So they must indeed have known why they burned incense, and what pleasure God took in the burning of incense; this remained quite appropriately silent in Moses' account according to God's purpose, and yet it was not hidden from the children of the Saints, nor from Moses himself, but he has a veil hanging before his eyes.

3. Israel (because they were also mostly evil children, and moreover idolatrous, as was seen immediately with their Golden Calf) was not to know it, because of the false <term>Magia</term> <note>Böhme uses "Magia" to describe the spiritual power of the will to manifest or "image" itself into a physical or substantial form</note>; and as we shall also write only for our own, yet clearly enough. Note this thus:

4. The soulful free will is as thin as a Nothing; and although in its body it is surrounded by the "Something," its grasp or substance is in a false-seeking essence, from the <term>origin</term> <note>original: *vhrstande*; the primal source or beginning</note> of sin.

5. If the free will is now to go toward God with the desire, it must first depart from its false "Something"; and as it now departs thus, it is naked and powerless, for it is back in the first Nothing. For if it wants to go toward God, it must die to the false selfhood and leave it behind; and as it leaves the same, it is merely as a Nothing, and thus cannot travel, work, or weave. If it wants to show its power, it must be in Something in which it grasps and forms itself.

6. As we have an example of this in faith: if there is to be a faith that works, it must grasp itself in Something in which it works. God's free will has grasped itself with the inner spiritual world and works through it; and the inner world's free will has grasped itself with the outer world and works through it. Thus the soulful free will, which also has its origin from the <term>Abyss</term> <note>original: *vngrunde*; Böhme’s term for the "Unground" or "Groundless," the primal nothingness before all creation</note>, must grasp itself in Something,

29. Thus, the material of the offering—the wood and smoke—was earthly in its external essence, just as man was earthly in his external body. And within that earthliness lay the curse, both in man and in the offering.

30. But when the offering was ignited, it became spiritual; for from the wood came the fire, which accepted and consumed the offering. From this consumption, first the smoke arose from the fire, and afterward the light. This was the "figure" or symbolic form into which both human and divine imagination entered, acting as a <term>conjunction</term> <note>original: *Conjunction*; a joining together or union of two different substances or natures</note>.

### Of Cain’s Sacrifice.

41. In Cain’s sacrifice, we rightly understand **Mouth-Christianity** <term>Mouth-Christianity</term> <note>original: *MaulChristenheit*; Böhme’s term for hypocrites who speak the words of faith but lack the inner transformation</note>, the "Title-Christians" in the spiritual Babylonian Whoredom, of whom Cain is the image. Just as Cain sought only the outer world, power, and earthly pleasure in his sacrifice, and wanted to be a son or child accepted by God from the outside, he expected God to let his **evil beast** <note>The "inner beast" refers to the selfish, fallen nature of man.</note> be acceptable and sacrificed. He wanted to be God's acceptable child while remaining in self-interest, within the **serpent-nature** <note>original: *Schlangen Ente*; the "sting" or "essence" of the serpent, referring to the fallen ego.</note> and falsehood. He was an unrepentant, proud man who thought to become a lord of the world and to rule over Abel and his descendants. Just so is the **Antichristian Church** on earth now; it also builds churches and altars, preaches, sings, and rings bells; it also offers within the bequeathed Covenant and Testament of Christ, and thus drapes the sacrifice of Christ over itself, wanting to be a son accepted from the outside; regardless of the fact that its sacrifices within the Covenant and Testament of Christ are not acceptable, nor are they brought into **Substance**.

42. For the reason is this: one relies solely and purely upon the sacrifice and teaches that the sacrifices take away sin, or that Christ's **Testaments** <note>Referring to the Sacraments, such as Baptism and Communion.</note> take away sin. It must be an **Abel** who enjoys it; the Mouth-Christian catches only the outer smoke of the true sacrifice. It must be a truly hungry, thirsty, reversed soul, which desires to depart entirely from the serpent-nature and all the vanity of this world, and desires to die to the serpent-will and vain will in Christ’s death, and to arise in a new will, entirely **resigned** <note>original: *gelassen*; "Gelassenheit" is a central concept for Böhme, meaning a total yielding or letting go of the self to God.</note> beneath and within God.

44. When human desire introduces its hunger into the sacrifice of Christ with earnest sighing and prayer, <gloss>with a surrender</gloss> and by departing from vanity: there, the soul’s desire grasps itself in the heavenly essence, in the humanity of Christ, into a substance upon the high altar of God. In the Word of God, within Christ’s Testaments <note>The "Testaments" usually refer to the Sacraments, particularly Baptism and the Lord's Supper.</note>, the hungry desire becomes flesh—a heavenly, supernatural flesh—and that same flesh is the true sacrifice of God, which God accepts as His dwelling, and not the animal-like, mortal man.

45. In this holy substance alone is the true faith of Abel; anything else is merely a historical, learned faith and a sacrifice of Cain that takes away no sin. For sin must always be placed into the judgment of God, wherein it was born, and the holy love-fire of God must consume and drown it. Otherwise, there is no forgiveness, and neither sacrifice nor covenant helps; even going to church, neither singing nor ringing bells achieves it, but only and alone the hungry, desiring faith through the unique sacrifice in the blood and death of Christ. There, the desire dies entirely to its **Selfhood** <note>original: *Jchheit*; the ego or the state of being centered on the "I"</note> in the death of Christ, and rises in Christ’s resurrection into a true faith and Christianity—not in hypocritical appearance, but in essence, words, and deeds.

46. For he is far from being a Christian who merely calls himself a Christian; rather, he is one in whom Christ is born out of his humanity through Christ's sacrifice. Neither covenant nor law counts for anything before God, but only a **new creature** <note>A reference to Galatians 6:15.</note>. No **stone-walled church** <term>stone-walled church</term> <note>original: *Mawer-Kirche*; Böhme uses this to contrast the physical institution of the church with the spiritual "living temple" of the believer's heart.</note>, or hypocrisy, by whatever name it is called, can inherit God’s kingdom; only and alone the true living sacrifice of the new rebirth, from the covenant of promise in Paradise, through the life-giving Word in the sacrifice of Christ.

47. The temple of the Holy Spirit is solely where God’s Word is taught and grasped within; outside of this is Cain with his glittering stone-walled church full of pride and stinking ambition. This is the great building at **Babylon** <note>Böhme uses "Babylon" to represent the "city of confusion," his term for the warring, institutionalized denominations of his time.</note>, where the language of the Word of God—as the written word—is confused into many quarrels and tongues, where there is nothing but vain quarreling and biting over the letters, and no true, living, active knowledge.

### Of Cain’s and Abel’s Sacrifice, etc.

54. St. Paul must <gloss>has to</gloss> serve them in this, where he says: *I do that which I do not want; if I then do it, it is not I who do it, but the sin that dwells in my flesh*; but as for his saying: *So now I serve God with the mind <gloss>disposition</gloss>, and with the flesh the law of sin*: that, Cain does not want to understand—specifically, how the mind should rule without ceasing over the sinful will and desire of the flesh, and kill its lust. <note>original: "Ich thue das Ich nicht wil..." - Böhme is referencing Romans 7:15-25 to explain the conflict between the spiritual mind and the physical urges.</note>

55. St. Paul speaks of a heavenly, Abelian <note>Refers to the nature of Abel, the righteous brother, who symbolizes the "New Man" or the spiritual seeker.</note> desire: how sin must be put to death in the flesh and not rule over the mind, as it did with Cain. When Cain saw that his brother was pleasing to God and he was not, the spirit of murder emerged in his mind—the very spirit that should have been killed in the sacrifice through true repentance and conversion.

<margin>yet</margin>
56. So it also goes with Babel <note>Böhme uses "Babel" to describe the confused and corrupt state of institutionalized churches that emphasize outward ritual over inward transformation.</note> under the mantle of Christ; she also offers sacrifice to God and thanks Him for Christ’s sacrifice. But she herself remains in the mind of the Cainish brother-murderer—in pride, greed, envy, and anger, in persecution, in war and strife. She fights over the sacrifice and over the cloak <note>original: *Deckmantel*, meaning a cover, pretext, or facade of piety.</note>, so that it is not taken from her; and under it she fattens herself with the animalistic sacrifice of the fatness of the earth, and remains the beast of Cain. She murders Abel continually in the members of Christ <note>That is, the true, humble believers who make up the spiritual body of Christ.</note>, and comforts herself with the death of Christ; this death must serve as the cover for the false, murderous spirit.

57. The heart and mind are far from the new creature <note>The "new creature" or "new man" is Böhme’s term for the soul that has been spiritually reborn in Christ.</note>. It is only the old Cainish brother-murderer, who covers himself with Christ’s sacrifice and sacrifices alongside Cain. Such a thing, and no more, is all that remains of Christendom today among all the sects, except for the children of Christ who are still hidden here and there with Abel.

58. The Cainish church has never been more powerful on earth than right now, when people shout with a great cry: "Run here everyone! We have found the sacrifice of Abel in Christ!" Yes, dear Babel, you have indeed found the mantle; but look closely at your Cainish heart, and you will see whether you sacrifice with Abel out of the new creature, or out of the false spirit of brother-murder. Where are your fruits? Where is love and righteousness? Where is truth? Where is patience and gentleness? Where is the mind that serves God with Paul? Where are you, beautiful Christian Church on earth? Have you not become a murder-pit of the devil? Then prove your Christian virtues; yet you are full of bickering and murder, both inside the church and outside the church. Your mouth is only a chatterer about the Kingdom of God, just as Cain’s mouth only chattered about the sacrifice, while his heart was a murderer.

59. Thus they also chatter in the stone heaps <note>original: *Steinhauffen*. A derogatory term Böhme uses for physical church buildings to contrast them with the "living temple" of the human heart.</note> about the mantle and sacrifice of Christ, and yet meanwhile murder through this chattering in the—

# Chapter 29.

## How the Adamical Human Tree has introduced and opened itself from its trunk into branches, twigs, and fruits, from which opening all arts, invention, and government have arisen.

---

->The deep gates out of the Center of Eternal and also Temporal Nature; how the Eternal Wisdom has introduced itself into a formal contemplation. <note>The state of being perceivable or made manifest to the mind.</note><-

The Eternal Divine Understanding is a free will, not arisen from something or through something; It is its own seat, and dwells solely alone in itself, ungrasped by anything; for outside and before it is nothing, and that same Nothing is one, and is yet also to itself as a Nothing: It is a single Will of the abyss <note>original: *vngrundes* (Ungrund), referring to the groundless, non-dual source of all being before any manifestation.</note>, and is neither near nor far, neither high nor low, but It is All, and yet as a Nothing: For it itself is in itself no state of contemplation or "find-ability" <note>The quality of being able to be found or perceived.</note> whereby It might find a likeness within itself.

2. Its finding is its own going forth out of itself; thus it beholds itself in the going forth, for that which has gone forth is its Eternal Delight, sensitivity, and find-ability, and is called the Divine Wisdom: Which Wisdom the bottomless Will <note>original: *vngründliche Wille*</note> grasps within itself as its Center of Delight, as an Eternal Mind <note>original: *Gemüthe*, encompassing the soul, disposition, and intellectual faculties.</note> of the Understanding; which Understanding the free will forms within itself into its own image, as an ever-speaking, talking, living Word, which the free will breathes or speaks out of itself from the formed Wisdom of Delight.

3. And that breathing out is the Spirit or the Mouth of the Understanding in the formed Will of Wisdom, which distinguishes the speaking Word, so that the Mind and the Understanding of the Mind become manifest; in which manifestation of the free Delight or Wisdom, by the free Will through the Spirit, [it] is formed into distinctness with the speaking or echoing-forth.

4. In which formation the powers of the Divine properties are understood, so that one rightly says of God: He is the Eternal Will, Understanding, Mind, Counsel, Power, Hero, and Wonder; with which wonders of powers He has moved and formed Himself from eternity: In which formation the invisible spiritual world stands, wherein the Spirit of God has played with itself from eternity, which also has neither ground, goal, nor origin.

7. For if there were no counter-will <note>Resistance or opposition.</note>, there would be no movement within the properties. 8. It is not that such a birth only began in time: It is Eternal and is the revelation of Divine contemplatibility, sensitivity, and find-ability. It was only with the act of Creation that this birth introduced itself into a "compaction" <note>A thickening or solidification into matter.</note> or external tangibility, forming a distinct, working government <note>original: *Regiment*; a system of order or rule.</note> for its own "play."

9. Out of the fiery property, all life arose in Creation, and out of the property of light arose the spirit of rational understanding. ### How the Adamical Tree from its trunk...

...Covenant of Grace, incorporated itself into the captive, faded, and—in terms of Divine Wisdom—blind **essence** <note>original: *Ens*; a Latin term for "being" or "fundamental substance"</note> of the holy world-existence, and as a Covenant, it embodied itself toward a new **rebirth** <note>original: *Wiedergeburt*</note> of a new, holy will and life.

**16.** Thus, we must now carefully consider the trunk of human life: how it has divided itself into various properties and, like a tree of good and evil, extended into boughs and branches; and how its temporal **rule** <note>original: *Regiment*</note> over the various offices and stations arose. This rule was awakened within him through the lust for both good and evil, and by this, he subjected himself to nature, because he looks into its government.

**17.** And we see clearly, as Moses has written in his first book <note>The Book of Genesis</note>, how the Human Tree opened itself into good and evil, and extended into boughs and branches toward its fruit. We also see how the fiery, wrathful property has always gone before and bore its fruit first; we have a clear understanding of this in the names of those whom the Spirit of God, through Moses, has placed in the lines of generation.

**18.** For first he places Cain: in the **language of nature** <note>original: *Natursprache*; a concept suggesting that words and names contain the inner vibrational essence of the thing they describe</note>, one understands by this a source from the **center** <note>original: *Centro*</note> of fiery desire—a self-will of the soul's fiery power, like a bough or branch from the **first principle** <note>original: *Principio*; referring to the first of the three "worlds" or "principles" of reality, associated with fire and divine wrath</note>. In this branch, the first principle specifically swung its power upward, wishing to separate into its own selfhood and break away from the lovely **essence** <note>original: *Ente/Ens*</note>. Yet it was not a dark source, but a source of its own lust, as well as fiery strength and power.

**19.** For out of Cain's **essence** <note>original: *Ente/Ens*</note>, as it was in the wrestling **wheel of life** <note>original: *LebensRade*; a recurring metaphor for the dynamic, churning forces of nature</note> within the center of birthing nature, his will arose. And out of the will came desire, and out of desire came the substance—in which substance the false mind is understood. In this, the **rule** <note>original: *Regiment*</note> of the outer world took hold; into this, the devil also struck with his desire in the wrath of nature, and he craved the lordship of this world in selfhood. For the fallen devil always craves lordship in the inner eternal and outer temporal nature, in the **place** <note>original: *Loco*</note> of this world.

**20.** However, the Word of Divine power and holiness had embodied itself into the seed of the woman—as into the faded **essence** <note>original: *Ens*</note> of the spiritual world-existence—with a Covenant of Rebirth, intending to take away the fiery power of selfhood from the fiery, wrathful will originating in the center of the dark world. Therefore, after Cain, there pushed forth from the Human Tree a branch from the goal of the Covenant: namely, Abel. In the **language of nature** <note>original: *Natursprache*</note>, this name signifies "a breathed-out angel."

# How the Adamical Tree measures itself out of its stem:

...measures itself: For *Methusael* in the **Language of Nature** <note>original: *Natur-sprache*; the idea that names reveal the inner essence of a thing</note> was intended to sound like: "Mine is the Divine power: I am an angel placed therein by God," or "I am God’s order." While this is indeed true, it is so according to the **first Principle** <note>original: *Principio*; in this philosophy, the first principle refers to the foundational, often "dark" or "fiery" power of nature</note> through external nature, acting as a natural power and order.

36. More is hidden in this name under the "Angel"—specifically the praise of the children who would exist under this power and live under it as if under Divine order. However, this Angelic name in Divine power first takes hold in fleshly selfhood; for the **syllable Me**, with which the word of the name begins, takes hold in the external birth of the world in "my-ness" <note>original: *Meinheit*; an ego-driven sense of possession or self-interest</note>. It indicates that this order does not have its origin in the Kingdom of Heaven in God's holiness, but rather out of the first Principle, which forms itself into such an order in the third principle <note>the visible, material world</note>, as in external world-nature. Therefore, it shall and must reach its end and be tested through the judgment of God.

37. And **Moses** writes further and says: *Methusael* fathered *Lamech*. In this name now lies the mystery of Divine order through the Angelic counsel; in this place, in the Language of Nature, it signifies a mission of the angel over the dominion of humanity: as over the **regions** <note>original: *Regione*</note> of the world, over the fleshly life, which would be subject to the Prince of the Upper Heights in nature.

38. For here the damage that **Adam** received is sought out: namely, that two kinds of "Princes of the Upper Heights" rule over human life—the sent good angel, and the embodied evil angel in the flesh. Also understood here is the powerful assault of the evil angel from both without and within; for the inner spirit goes out in the name of God’s covenant and travels into the external world. This signifies how man would become frivolous and also forfeit the covenant of God, yet returns with his perception into selfhood and takes hold in the outgoing Angelic name. This signifies a hypocritical harlotry <note>original: *gleißnerische Hurerey*; used here to mean spiritual infidelity or false piety</note> in angelic form, which goes back into the external and finally casts away the covenant along with the Angelic name.

39. Furthermore, **Moses** writes: *Lamech* took two wives; one was named **Adah**, the other **Zillah**. Here, in the birthing of the Tree of Life, one understands this: Human life recognized the damage that had arisen in its stem, and henceforth took two wives—these are two kinds of **essences** <note>original: *Essenz*</note> and wills. As **Adah** signifies, the soul goes with the will through the mind and takes hold with desire in the first stem of **Adam**, and would gladly be pious again. But **Zillah** he had also taken to himself as a wife of child-bearing—that is, fleshly joy and lust.

# How the Adamic Tree [branches out] from its Trunk

...be hidden; this is not an external manner, but an internal one; for God does not dwell in external eyes, but rather in internal, spiritual ones. So God said: Whoever murders Cain in his inner life, it shall be avenged sevenfold; and He placed the sign of the Covenant upon his life, so that no spirit in its wrath could murder him; for he was a branch from the Tree of Life.

56. Although the seven properties of nature had grown apart within him <note>The "seven properties" are Böhme's core system of the forces of nature—such as desire, mobility, and fire—which can be either harmonious or conflicting.</note>, he was not solely to blame for this, for he had inherited his life from his father and mother in a divided state. Therefore, grace also extended over him just as over Abel; except that Abel came from the other line, but the center of the soul was the same in both. However, the movement in the seed was unequal; for they were 
<margin><image-desc>A hand-drawn bracket grouping the following two lines of text</image-desc></margin>
the two images of the world: Cain as the image of **selfhood** <note>original: *selbheit*; the ego-driven state of being turned away from God toward the "I."</note> in wrath, and Abel as the image of **resignation** <note>original: *gelassenheit*; the state of yielding one's will to God, often translated as "yieldedness."</note> of life, from which—through death—another world sprouted from the Center.

57. It is not that Cain was born for destruction, but rather the awakened evil property in the state of inequality—as the soul of the outer world pressed forward in the seed—took control of the center of life; and into this God placed a sign, as his Covenant, so that the robbers should not murder the life of the soul.

58. If it should happen, however, that the individual's own will surrendered itself to the murderers, then Cain's life would be avenged sevenfold—that is, through all seven properties—and the free will, which murdered the life that was in the Word of God (John 1), would be punished sevenfold through all seven forms of nature, both temporally and eternally. This means: whoever murders the life—whose free will murders his life—shall be avenged eternally in the seven properties of the dark world.

59. Further, we must rightly consider the great mystery at this place, for the seven properties of the human tree for the life of the **wonders of God** <term>wonders of God: the varied expressions of God’s power, creativity, and technical arts manifest in the physical world and human culture.</term> had now distributed themselves as far as Lamech. The government of the world was now fully born in Lamech within nature; for Lamech was the seventh person in the root of wonders from the first trunk: Adam being the first; Abel does not belong to the line of wonders, but rather to the **rebirth**.

Cain was the second in the line of wonders; Enoch the third; Irad the fourth; Mehujael the fifth; Methushael the sixth; and Lamech the seventh.

### Chapter 30.

## Concerning the Line of the Covenant.

<margin>for</margin>
The <term>Line of the Covenant</term><note>The "Line of the Covenant" refers to the genealogical succession from Adam through Seth to Christ, which Böhme views as the vehicle for divine grace in history.</note> is not to be understood as if the Covenant applied only to that *Line*: No. The Covenant applies to the one Life that was within humanity in the Word in ancient times. The *Line* of Seth pertains only to the revelation in the flesh, in which *Line* the Word wished to reveal itself outwardly in the flesh within the Covenant. But the Spirit from the *Center* <note>original: "Centro"</note> of the Covenant applies to the *Line* of Cain as much as to the *Line* of Abel. However, in Cain it works in the Spirit; and in Seth it works in the outer mouth—as in the grasped Word, and in the <term>office of teaching</term><note>The "Lehrampt" refers to the formal institution of the church and the spoken ministry of the Gospel.</note>. For Seth sprouted according to the Spirit out of the Covenant, as the Spirit moved in the embodied Word within the Covenant; but Cain was within the grasp of the Spirit of Nature.

2. For through Cain's *Line*, the arts <note>Böhme refers to the "arts" of civilization mentioned in Genesis 4, such as metallurgy and music, which he sees as manifestations of divine wisdom through natural means.</note> came forth, which were a wonder of Divine Wisdom, contemplation, and formality—that is, of the formed Word through and in Nature. In Seth, the Word entered into a formal life, as into a spiritual contemplation, where the Word of God viewed itself with Wisdom in a spiritual image. In Cain's *Line*, it viewed itself in a naturally formed word; and both serve God's miraculous work.

3. It is not as <term>Babel</term><note>Böhme uses "Babel" to represent the "city of confusion"—specifically the warring theological factions of his day that argued over dogma rather than living in the Spirit.</note> judges: that God, by His own decree, has thus <term>predestined</term><note>original: "Prædestiniret"</note> and chosen one part of humanity for damnation in His wrath, and the other part for life. Those who judge in this way are still among the number seventy-and-seven in the <term>multiplication</term><note>original: "Multiplication." This refers to the fragmentation of the single Divine Word into the many conflicting "languages" or opinions of fallen humanity.</note> of the Word. For the promise was given to Adam before Cain was even conceived. The Covenant rested in Adam and Eve with grace; but the Spirit of holiness and rebirth through Christ applied only to the "Seed of the Woman," as to the enclosed seed of the Kingdom of Heaven, in the <term>Tincture of Light</term><note>An alchemical term Böhme uses to describe the spiritual essence or "soul-blood" of divine life.</note> within the <term>Matrix of Venus</term><note>original: "Veneris Matricem." In Böhme's system, this refers to the feminine, generative principle of divine love and beauty within the human soul.</note>. Within this, Adam—when he was both man and woman—should have propagated himself in his own desire and love; which, because it could not be, was taken from Adam and made into a woman.

4. But when the woman became earthly, the heavenly part of this *Matrix* <note>original: "Matricis"</note> was enclosed in death unto the heavenly birth. Into this *Matrix*, the Word of God embodied itself again with the Covenant, to open itself in this *Matrix* with a living heavenly seed and to break the power of death.

5. For the Word did not wish to open itself in the formed word of nature, as in Cain’s lineage, but rather in the faded heavenly <term>being</term><note>original: "Ente," from the Latin *ens*. Böhme refers to the "faded" spiritual substance of the original, unfallen humanity that is revived by Christ.</note>.

<summary>Böhme explains that the "Line of the Covenant" through Seth represents the formal revelation of God's Word, while Cain's line represents God's wisdom manifest through nature and the arts. He argues against rigid predestination, asserting that the potential for rebirth exists through the "heavenly seed" restored in the Covenant.</summary>

13. In Cain, the kingdom of nature was represented, and in Abel and Seth, the supernatural divine kingdom: These two rose up with and in one another for the contemplation of the divine delight in the formed Wisdom, and each one specifically pressed out as a wonder into its own contemplation.

14. For from Adam until Lamech in the line of wonders there are 7 generations, and in the other line, namely in the line of the Covenant from Adam until Enoch, there are also 7 generations: Enoch is the eighth, as a beginning of the **prophetic spirit**; for in the first 7 generations the form of the spiritual kingdom was represented out of the <margin>That</margin> Tree of Life.

15. Adam was the stem, for his life originated from the Word: But because the life of nature in him swung itself above the life in the formed Word and wanted to have the rule, and darkened the life from the Word; so the Word itself yielded into a life with a Covenant, and represented its figure in Abel—how the natural life was to be broken, and the Word of divine power was to green again out of the first life.

### Concerning the Line of the Covenant.

**16.** Thus Abel was the figure of the second Adam, Christ, and had to be murdered for the sake of the Covenant; for Christ was meant to kill the exalted natural will and establish a New one. Furthermore, Abel was not to father any natural child, otherwise it would have been foreign to Nature: For they were all to come from one single stem, and the Word wished to sprout through the one tree in the Covenant, so that the children of grace would be born out of the tree of Nature, like the dew out of the morning dawn.

**17.** For thus the figure of the **New Birth** also presented itself from the stem: As first from Adam the Lineage went forth, he was the first, Abel the second, Seth the third, Enos the fourth: at which time people began to teach of the Spiritual Kingdom; Kenan was the fifth, whose name signifies in the <term>Language of Nature</term><note>original: *Natursprache*. Jacob Böhme’s concept that the very sounds and structures of names reveal the inner essence and divine origins of the things they name.</note> an outgoing, refocused delight of Divine **contemplation**<note>original: *beschawlichkeit*. A state of mystical seeing or meditative immersion in God’s presence.</note>, in which the taught Word formed itself, as in prayer and in the desire of the will, as well as in their offerings.

**18.** Mahalaleel was the sixth, and signifies in the Language of Nature an Angelic form of an Angelic kingdom, where the Spirit prefigured the kingdom of Christ in this name.

**19.** Jared was the seventh; with his name one understands in the Language of Nature a priest or prince of the Spiritual Kingdom: For just as Irad <note>Böhme is contrasting the lineage of Seth (Jared) with the lineage of Cain (Irad, from Genesis 4:18).</note> was to be the ruler in the Kingdom of Nature: So Jared was to be a ruler in the Spiritual Kingdom, for out of Jared came the office of Moses; and out of Irad the kingdom of worldly dominion and established government.

**20.** However, the Language of Nature clearly indicates that Jared is only a prefigure of a Spiritual Kingdom, for the name carries the <term>Cherub</term><note>In Böhme’s thought, the Cherub represents the guardian of the gate to Paradise, symbolizing the divine wrath or "sternness" that fallen humanity must pass through to reach God.</note> out through the Word; for the Spiritual Kingdom was held captive on Earth within the **wrath of God** until Christ, who broke the anger.

**21.** This office of Jared is twofold: as externally, it is the figure of the Spiritual Kingdom bound with the wrath of God; and internally, it is the true holy kingdom which the repentant person takes up. Outwardly is Moses, and inwardly is Christ.

25. He also points to the means by which the <term>Turba</term><note>original: *Turba*. Böhme sees this name as the ultimate manifestation of the hidden love within the name of Jehovah.</note>, yet meanwhile played with it in the time of the Figure within the holy Wisdom, in the Line of the Covenant, as with an inward hidden holy kingdom which He would reveal in the fullness of time.

30. Here, the veil <note>A reference to the "Veil of Moses" (Exodus 34:33), which Böhme uses as a metaphor for the hidden, spiritual meaning of the Scriptures that is obscured from those without spiritual insight.</note> truly hangs before Moses’s face because of the unworthiness of mankind; and the Spirit in Moses points clearly—if we had eyes of understanding—to when these mysteries should be revealed.

31. The direct descent or lineage carrying the divine promise.</note> through which the Spirit of Wonders passes. After that, Moses says: *And he lived for such a time, and begat sons and daughters*, of whom he says nothing further: By this, he intends to signify the Spirit of the revelation of God’s wonders in every line; their age, which the Spirit sets down, signifies the times—how long each government, both the worldly and the spiritual, should stand in its state...

33. And these same Monarchs of Wonders are immediately presented from the first branches, from the beginning of the Human Tree, in each line in the number of seven: from Adam through Cain to Lamech, and in the other line from Adam to Jared. Through these numbers and names, the Spirit points specifically in each line to the seven outgoing properties of the Tree and the power of wonders; how the powers of wonders would later introduce themselves into governments, and how one figure would arise from another; and how one would break the other, and from that breaking set forth another form, as has happened in the spiritual and worldly government. For the worldly is always understood together with the spiritual; for the external formed Word in the government of Nature always sets its form alongside and upon the spiritual formation: therefore, observe closely here.

34. Seven <term>times</term><note>original: *Zeit*. Here meaning distinct chronological epochs or spiritual dispensations.</note> are determined from the Tree of Life, in the Word of Power. The first time proceeds from the pure life of Adam; for before the creature, life was in the Word, where it was introduced purely into the Image; this lasted until the Fall. Out of that same pure life, a branch sprouted within; that was Abel. But because the Fall clung to him externally, that same pure life was led through death into the holy world. This signifies the Kingdom of Christ, who was to lead us through death back into the pure life.

35. The second time begins with Seth: For Moses says, Adam was 130 years old and begat a son who was like his image, and called him Seth; understand, he was an image as Adam was after the Fall, and was in the Spiritual Line of Wonders, and Cain beneath him in a Worldly Natural Line of Wonders; for both kingdoms go together. Seth's time lasts until the <term>Deluge</term><note>original: *Sündfluth*. Literally the "sin-flood," referring to Noah's flood.</note>, and holds the supreme rule until the Deluge.

36. The third time begins with Enos during Seth's time, and continues as a spiritual preaching or knowledge of God throughout Seth's time, as a hidden kingdom, and lasts until Abraham, to whom the Covenant of Christ in the flesh was confirmed.

37. The fourth time begins with Kenan, which is the spiritual form with prayer and spiritual sacrifices, wherein the Word forms itself in Wisdom; and it continues through Seth's and Enos's time, and revealed itself with Moses: just as Enos's time first truly [revealed itself] with Abraham

# Concerning the Line of the Covenant.

...revealed with the promise in the Covenant: This <term>time of Kenan</term><note>Kenan is the grandson of Seth. In this mystical chronology, his name represents a specific era of spiritual development within the Old Testament period.</note> lasts in its revelation and dominion under Moses until Christ in the flesh.

38. The fifth time begins with **Mahalaleel**, and is the conception of the **Angelic form**<note>original: *Englischen Form*. In this context, "Englisch" refers to "Angelic" (from the German *Engel*), signifying the restoration of man's heavenly nature.</note>, as the new **Rebirth** out of the Covenant; and it passes hiddenly in the Word of the promise through the preaching of Enos, under Seth and Kenan, through all three times, and was revealed with the fulfillment of the Covenant in the humanity of Christ, when the true Mahalaleel and Angelic image, which had been extinguished in Adam, was revealed again in Christ's humanity.

39. The sixth time begins with **Jared**, which is the **Spiritual Priesthood** beneath the external one, of which Seth, Enos, Kenan, and Mahalaleel were externally in their order, in their times; just as the preaching of Enos was concerning God and his being and will, as well as the preaching of Abraham concerning the Covenant and circumcision, and also Moses with the book of the Law: underneath all these, the internal priest Jared passed hiddenly. Internally, this Spiritual Priesthood is Christ in the new man, and externally, in the self-elected priests, it is **Babel**<note>original: *Babel*. A common term in 17th-century radical theology for the institutionalized, worldly church which is seen as a site of spiritual "confusion" and corruption.</note>.

40. This sixth time began in the Kingdom of Christ (after the death of the Apostles of Christ), when people chose teachers of men out of favor and external appearance; that is, it first revealed itself there out of the hiddenness of the shadow, and stepped forward with the stone churches, where the church stood in place of the holy temple of Christ. Thus, the holy Jared did indeed rule internally in Christ's children as the voice of Christ, but externally the **Cherub with the sword** ruled: for the external power which those elected priests wield is the sword of the Cherub, which penetrates in the name of Jared in the middle of the Word in the <term>Language of Nature</term><note>original: *Natursprache*. The mystical belief that there is a primal language where the sound of a word perfectly expresses the essence of the thing named.</note>.

41. This sixth time is, in its figure, both secret and manifest; it has been recognized and also not recognized. For Christ said: <note>original Latin/German context: "Mein Reich ist nicht von dieser Welt"</note> *My kingdom is not of this world*. Therefore, this time had to pass hiddenly under the **Anti-Christ**, while internally in the children of God, Christ's kingdom was revealed; and in the others, who also lived during this time and called themselves Christians, only Babel and the Anti-Christ were manifest, both in the priest and his listeners. For those who were born of God heard the true Jared within them as the voice of Christ; the others heard only the external voice at Babel, such as quarreling and fighting about the Kingdom of Christ.

For those who were born of God heard the true Jared within them as the voice of Christ; the others heard only the external voice at Babylon, wrangling and striving over Christ’s kingdom.

### Of the beginning of the second Monarchy, and

12. Indeed, in the spiritual world there are orders, princes, and angels—yet all without coercion, in a lovely service of love and will, just as one limb in a body serves another.

13. Everything that man draws into his own power within the realm of nature and abuses for excess, and takes away from his fellow members—who must therefore suffer because their God-given rights are completely withdrawn—all of this is caught up in the **Great Turmoil** <note>original: *Turba Magna*; in Böhme's theology, this refers to the wrathful, chaotic principle that disrupts divine order</note> as an abomination of nature, and is set before the judgment of God for the Day of Separation <term>the Day of Separation: *Scheydetage*, Böhme's term for the Final Judgment, when good is permanently divided from evil</term>.

14. Nature demands only order, and provides distinctions and offices. But the **Turmoil** introduces its abomination from the desire of the dark world into it—such as pride, greed, envy, anger, and falsehood.

15. These five vices are illegitimate children <note>original: *Hurenkinder*, literally "children of whores," used here to mean things that have no rightful place in God's lineage</note> in the kingdom of nature and shall not inherit God’s kingdom. God regards the kingdom of nature as His own order and has given it into man’s power so that he may thereby separate the evil from the good, and choose for himself a judge over the wickedness of false desire and lust. For He says: "Whoever sheds human blood, by humans shall their blood be shed again" <note>A reference to Genesis 9:6</note>—namely, through the order of nature. Not that one should avenge oneself by one’s own power, but through the order of nature and through God’s laws, which are the avenger. For God says: "I will avenge the blood of your bodies, and will avenge it upon all animals"—by this He means through the order of His laws and their appointed stewards <note>original: *Amptverwalter*</note>.

16. It is not that a prince or lord has the power to shed blood outside of God’s law; if he does so, then God’s law condemns him also to death. There is no personal power here over human blood, whether it be king or prince, for they are only officials over the order of God’s law and should not reach further without divine command. They do indeed have the law of nature in their administration as its servants, but only according to justice and truth, and not through their own desire. For God created man in His own image. Over that same divine image, the kingdom of nature in its offices has no power to kill; rather, the office in its divine order applies only to the outward image of nature <note>Böhme distinguishes between the "divine image" (the eternal soul) and the "outward image" (the physical body), arguing that earthly laws only have jurisdiction over the physical</note>.

17. Therefore, if an official of nature takes the life of a righteous person, nature assigns the one who does this to God’s judgment for the Day of Separation. Where will the tyrants go then, who turn truth into lies and shamefully execute the children of God for the sake of their divine knowledge and confession, and who also bring about war and destruction upon land and people? All these belong in the **Great Turmoil** <note>original: *Turba Magna*</note> for the judgment of God,
