## How Noah cursed his son Ham, and concerning Noah’s interpretation of his three sons and their descendants from them.

Noah began and became a husbandman <note>or farmer; "Ackersman" refers to one who works the soil</note> and planted vineyards; and when he drank of the wine, he became drunk and lay uncovered in his hut. When Ham, the father of Canaan, saw his father’s nakedness <note>original: "Scham"—literally "shame," a common term for the genitals or nakedness in this period</note>, he told his two brothers outside. Then Shem and Japheth took a garment and laid it upon both their shoulders, and walked backward toward him, and covered their father’s nakedness; and their faces were turned away so that they did not see their father’s nakedness. When Noah awoke from the wine and learned what his younger son <note>original: "kleiner Sohn"—literally "small son," referring to Ham as the youngest or perhaps lower in status</note> had done to him, he said: Cursed be Canaan, and may he be a servant of all servants among his brothers; and he said further: Blessed be God the Lord of Shem, and let Canaan be his servant. God enlarge Japheth and let him dwell in the tents of Shem, and let Canaan be his servant. This is the true image of human property <note>original: "Eigenschafft"—referring to the internal nature or characteristics of a person</note> according to the three Principles or worlds: For the Spirit in Noah speaks from the **Center** <note>original: "Centro"—the divine or natural source of all being</note>, and the three sons of Noah now stood before the Spirit in a figure <note>a symbolic representation</note> of what kind of nations would arise from them.

2. From this figure, the Spirit of Noah interpreted—from the stem of the formed Word of human nature—what the second Monarchy <note>Böhme views history through "Monarchies," or spiritual-political eras</note> would be: Noah became drunk and lay exposed in his nakedness, which his son Ham mocked, and also showed to his brothers so that they should do the same. Here the Spirit indicates from what the curse arose for Ham: namely, from the nakedness of his father.

3. For that was precisely the loathing <note>original: "ekel"—a feeling of disgust or repulsion</note> for God's holiness, from which root Ham and his lineage—as the man of vanity—arise; for in the image of God, this nakedness is a loathing.

4. For this reason, God commanded Abraham to circumcise himself at this member: to show that this member was not given to Adam in the beginning, and that it must again be cut off from the image of God and not inherit God’s kingdom; for which reason the soul-spirit is also ashamed to be exposed. <note>The printer has included a vertical row of decorative floral ornaments here to mark the significance of this theological point regarding the Fall and the physical body.</note>

5. But because it was attached to Adam—since he did not persist in the image of God when his Eve was made from him—as a beastly way for reproduction, so this beastly tree has also [spread] itself out...

But their knowledge would be only an external **walled-church** <term>original: "Mawerkirche"; Böhme’s term for institutional religion that relies on stone buildings and rigid rituals rather than internal spiritual life.</term>, a habit of worship where the mouth carries the name of God, but the heart gives birth only to a beastly spirit of earthly pride and lust.

36. Thus, the spirit of Shem, Ham, and Japheth shall dwell among one another in one community. Shem’s spirit is in faith, hidden under Japheth’s in an insignificant, despised little flock. Japheth’s spirit, however, presents a great, magnificent outcry of pretentious worship, but it is only **hypocrisy** <note>original: "gleißnerey"; a glittering, deceptive outward appearance.</note> arising from the light of nature. Ham’s spirit is full of gluttony and mockery; he will mock both the children of the **Cain-like appearance** <note>Referring to the false, external "righteousness" of Japheth’s type.</note> and the children of the true light, living like wild cattle, yet wanting to be an adopted child of grace from the outside even in his **swinish life** <note>original: "Säuleben".</note>.

37. This same Ham now holds the reign in Christendom. He has played the hypocrite with Japheth, so that through the natural light he has set up an external, glistening worship as an external **mouth-god**. This same mouth-god has covered Ham—in his animalistic, **Sodomitic** spirit—with a beautiful, glistening cover under Christ’s purple mantle, and has placed great sacks full of the light of grace at his head; these the beastly mouth-spirit of Ham intends to take with him if he must indeed die—as if he then possessed great sacks full of the light of grace.

38. But the light of grace remains only in the sacks, and Ham’s spirit remains an evil beast within itself and will not be able to open the sacks or take out the light of grace. This spirit of Ham is cursed and shall not inherit God's kingdom unless he himself be born anew out of the light of grace; otherwise, the sacks and the cover help him not at all.

## The 35th Chapter.

<margin>Chap. 35.</margin>

### How the Human Tree spread in its properties through Noah’s children, and how they were divided into different nations at the Tower of Babel according to those properties through the confusion of languages.

Every tree grows first according to how it springs from its grain into a trunk, then into boughs and branches, and further brings forth the blossom and fruit from its essence <note>original: "Ente"; from the Latin "Ens," a term Böhme uses to describe the essential spiritual substance or "seed" of a thing</note>: In the same way, the Human Tree is to be understood according to its power and the revelation of its hidden wonders of Divine Wisdom, which lay hidden in the human essence and, over time, brought itself forth from every degree of its properties.

2. Adam was the first being <term>Ens: the fundamental spiritual "stuff" or essence that precedes physical form</term> serving as the grain, and that same essence for human life was in Divine Wisdom, in the Word of Divine Power and Divine Understanding. The Spirit of God led that same holy essence out of Divine Wisdom and Delight into the "Let there be" Word <note>original: "Verbum Fiat"; the creative command of God</note>, as into the desire of the forming Word—that is, into Nature. Therein, the Spirit of God shaped the essence of Divine Wisdom into a formal life through the speaking Word, and shaped the nature of the three principles into a body; into which body (understand, into the essence of Nature) the Spirit of God breathed that same shaped creaturely life of Divine Understanding.

3. Then man arose and became a living soul, derived both from the heavenly spiritual essence and from the temporal essence of the earth and the four elements, as well as from the stars of Divine Magic <note>original: "Magiæ Divinæ"</note> and Natural Magic <note>original: "Magiæ Naturalis"</note>—a complete image of God; a tree of delight of the life of Divine Wisdom and contemplation, grafted into the Paradise of God, as into heaven and into the time of this world; and standing within both for the purpose of rebirth and the forming of its kind from itself; just as many branches, boughs, and fruits grow from a tree, where every fruit is again a grain for a new trunk and little tree: so also is the Human Tree to be understood in the same way.

4. The inner spiritual essence <note>original: "Ens"</note> grew in its power in Adam’s life, until the earthly, outer, natural essence surpassed it through the Devil's poison; then the natural essence swung itself forward in the powers of the wonders of nature and led forth its boughs and branches from the essence of nature.

5. And although the holy essence from the heavenly world-being in Adam

The image of God in the formed Word was meant to bring forth the shaping of the single Word from the first *Ens* into many formations of languages, according to the manner and way of the Princely Regiments <note>Hierarchical orders of celestial spirits or angels that Böhme believes govern the natural world</note> of the high spirits, which are also distinct within the formed Word. In the depths of this world, these spirits rule over the four elements in the properties of Nature, and also over the working of the stars in the soul of the Great World <term>Macrocosm: the universe as a singular, living organism</term>. These also bear the names of God in the formed Word of Nature, acting as an instrument of God, with which He rules in a formal manner in His government and play of love <note>original: "Liebespiel"; Böhme's concept of the joyful, creative, and harmonious interaction of Divine forces</note>.

29. Although it is true that the reader might not understand us in these "tongues" <note>Referring to the "Language of Nature" mentioned below</note>, I set it down only to the end that he may learn to reflect on the great mystery which the Spirit of God indicates under these names—from which such a human undertaking arose—that it is all a wonder from which the tongues and languages originated. Who would understand this—what kind of "mighty lord and hunter before God" he was—without the understanding of the <term>Language of Nature</term> <note>original: *Natur-sprache*; the mystical concept that there is a primordial language where the sound of a name perfectly describes the inner essence of the thing named</note>? 30. **Nimrod** became a mighty Lord and a hunter before the Lord. If I may now look with the Spirit into the "essence" of the formation of the word, I see what kind of lord and hunter Nimrod was; for herein the Spirit indicates the properties of nature: how they opened themselves in human nature and were introduced into an external form as an established **government** <note>original: *Regiment*; refers to organized civil authority or rule</note> among men. With this name, the Spirit indicates how the human free will formed itself in the nature of the intellect and imagined such a model into its **mind** <note>original: *Gemüthe*; the inner disposition or soul-center</note>, and from that imagination the external work arose.

31. For the name **Nimrod** is a very clear indication in open understanding that he comes from **Chus**; for he is in himself a "grasping" or a "taking of power" out of nature—how nature grasped itself into a government within the mind, and pressed itself upward with force, and hunted and crowded the lower properties. Therefore the Spirit says, "A hunter before the Lord," just as a hunter hunts, catches, and tames wild animals. Thus the Spirit indicates that out of that same exalted human nature, such "evil beasts" would arise who would live only for their external nature.

32. Over these same foolish "beast-men," there arose out of the **nature of wrath** <note>original: *Natur des grimmes*; in Böhme's philosophy, the "wrath" is the dark, fiery quality of nature that provides the energy for existence but must be tempered by light</note> the "Hunter," acting as the external authority, which was meant to hunt, catch, kill, and restrain the "beast"—so that the Hunter might at least tame the animals and keep them under a government. Otherwise, there would have been only a general raging, tearing, biting, and devouring of one another among the "human-beasts," since they would not let themselves [be led by] God's Spirit.

38. Under **Ham’s** line, the Spirit of Moses assigns 29 names that arose from Ham: this indicates 29 properties from the **Third Principle** <term>Third Principle</term> <note>original: *dritten Principio*; in Böhme's cosmology, this is the visible, material world created from the interaction of light and dark spiritual forces</note>, which is to say, from the spirit of the external world. It shows how the **Formed Word** <term>Formed Word</term> <note>original: *geformte Wort*; the creative speech of God as it manifests in the diversity of physical nature</note> would reveal itself through external nature, both in the tongues and the properties of nature from which the governments and orders of the lands have arisen. Just as every property produces its own offspring, like a branch on a tree bears other twigs, yet the Spirit in Moses indicates the primary root of the properties under these names—what kind of nations would arise from them, and how they would take their changes and final ends; all of this lies hidden within their names.

39. Thus, Ham has 29 names of his children, and he is the 30th. 29 is the number of his children and grandchildren mentioned, and beneath this lies the "number of the end" in Ham's government. 30 is his total number; of this, the Prophet says that this Ham would sell the **Righteous One** for 30 pieces of silver, and give them for a potter’s field. Just as a pot is regarded by its master, so is the fleshly "Ham-man" regarded by God. He takes his number of 30, which he should have led into the Kingdom of God, and gives it for an earthly vessel that resembles the field, and in doing so sells the Righteous One, who lies hidden under the number 30 in the **Word of Power**. Thus, the Righteous One under the number 30 separates Himself through the death of Ham's flesh from the 29 properties which swung themselves upward in Ham. For in the 30th year, the Righteous One separated Himself into His office as **Christ**, and in the number 30 lies that very same mystery—understood by our own people here and only hinted at. <note>Böhme is connecting the 30 descendants of Ham to the 30 pieces of silver paid to Judas and the 30 years of age at which Jesus began His ministry, suggesting a mystical cycle of betrayal and redemption.</note>

For he says Shem is the father of all the children of Eber, even though Eber is only in the third generation after Shem; yet the Spirit looks so closely at the Word in the Covenant where it opens itself in a single line.

### Chapter 36.

## Of the Antichristian Babylonian Whore of all tongues, nations, and languages; what lies hidden beneath the languages and the Tower of Babel.

<margin>our</margin>
**Kind reader**, I wish to have warned you in love: do not seek to understand our meaning according to any personal bitterness or malice toward anyone, nor specifically to despise or attack anyone in their status and honors out of spite. Instead, we shall speak in general terms: Let everyone examine themselves, and they will surely find the great mystery of the **Babylonian Tower** <term>Babylonian Tower</term> <note>Symbolizes the confusion and pride of human systems that attempt to reach God through their own power rather than through divine grace.</note> within themselves, as well as the **number of the false beast** <note>A reference to the Book of Revelation (13:18) regarding the Number of the Beast, interpreted here as a spiritual condition of the soul.</note>. Let the reader read our meaning with patience and include themselves according to their own inherited evil nature; for truly, the **earthly mortal man** in all people belongs under this text.

2. We shall write here what **Time** has brought forth and revealed; and if it were not revealed through humans, then the animals would have to reveal it: For the time is born, and no resistance helps; the **Most High** <note>God</note> is carrying out His work.

3. **Moses** says: **Nimrod**, son of **Ham**, began his kingdom at **Babel**, and was the first ruler on earth after the **Great Flood** <note>original: *Sündfluth*; the biblical deluge of Noah.</note>, and the founder of the Tower and the city of **Babylon**. It is not to be understood, however, that the children of Ham alone wanted to build the tower, but also those of **Japheth** and **Shem**; for they were all still together and wanted to build a tower whose peak reached into heaven, so that they might make a great name for themselves.

4. This tower, at which the tongues were divided and where the great city of **Babel** stood, is a figure of the **fallen Earthly Man**, who has entered into **selfhood** <term>selfhood</term> <note>original: *selbheit*; a central concept in Böhme’s theology referring to the ego, or the state of being turned away from God and toward one's own desires.</note> and has made the formed Word of God within himself into an **idol**. For the nature of the Tower was this: that it should stand there as a great wonder, so that men in their **imagining** <note>original: *düncken*; refers to human conceit, false opinion, or the deceptive power of the imagination when separated from divine truth.</note>

The prototype of this was the **Tower** <note>The Tower of Babel.</note>, where the people at Babel wished to come and ascend to God through their own grasped will and thoughts. They had themselves gone out from the Spirit of God and wished to take the Kingdom of God for themselves in their own self-hood through their own power. They wished to enter into the holiness of God’s own property, into both evil and good, with their own self-born will. This signifies the **divided tongues**, where every property introduced itself into a self-hood and a private understanding out of the universal Sensual Tongue, so that they no longer understood one another. Thus, the understanding was captured and led into a self-interest, emerging out of and according to the **three alphabets** <note>Likely referring to the three sacred languages—Hebrew, Greek, and Latin—which Böhme often critiques when they are used purely as intellectual tools without spiritual life.</note>.

All those learned in reason from the schools of this world are the master builders of this Tower. All those who set themselves up as teachers and are called to it by men without the Spirit of God, these are all master craftsmen at this Tower, and they are idols of the world, none other; they all do nothing but carve stone and wood for this Tower.**

God allowed them to set forth the figure of their own property in their confused understanding, as an image of what man had become in place of God.

10. Now **Reason** <term>Reason</term> <note>original: *Vernunfft*; here referring to human logic operating independently of divine revelation.</note> asks: why did God let this happen? It had to be so, in order that the wonders of **Wisdom** in the **unformed Word** of the **five vowels** <note>original: *fünff Vocalium*; Böhme believed the five vowels represented the pure, holy breath of God, while consonants represented the material, "formed" world.</note> might introduce themselves into a form or outward contemplation through the **formed Word** of the **three principles** <term>Three Principles</term> <note>A foundational concept in Böhme's philosophy representing the three realms of reality: the dark fire-world of God's wrath, the light-world of God's love, and the external physical world.</note>, as a reproduction or shaping. 11. For the true human life was the formed Word, but in its own desire for self-hood, it became such an image before God as this Tower.

12. All men from Adam onward, who have ever taught about God without the **divine contemplation** <note>original: *göttliche beschawlichkeit*; a direct spiritual insight or inner vision granted by God's Spirit.</note> of the Spirit of God within them, have all spoken and taught from this Tower of confused tongues. And from this has arisen the strife over God and His will and essence, such that men have brawled over God in their self-hood. One said that bricks should be brought for the building of the Tower, another stones, the third lime, the fourth wood, water, or other necessities. And there were many kinds of master builders, each according to the property of his own tongue; each wanted to build the Tower upon the foundation of his own property. One had stones for it according to the property of his land, another clay, the third lime, the fourth wood; and it seemed good to each one that he should build the Tower out of the **matter** <note>original: *Materia*</note> of his own property alone, for himself, as a great wonder, so that all the world should look upon what he had built.

13. And when the other peoples of other lands saw what this one had built, they despised it and said the property of their own land's matter was better for the Tower; and they began to despise him and to build the Tower for themselves, and to praise it, which in turn was despised by others. They also held the matter of their own land to be better, until they became so divided in **pride** <note>original: *Hoffarth*</note> and strife that they abandoned the Tower and fell upon one another, murdering, killing, and persecuting each other over the knowledge of the Tower of Babel. Whichever party then prevailed would build on the Tower again according to its own property, until other peoples rose up again and deemed their own matter to be better.

21. **The Beast** is the animalistic, earthly man of Ham <note>original: *Hams Mensch*; a reference to the biblical son of Noah, often used in historical theology to represent the "earthly" or "fallen" lineage of humanity.</note>, as if made from the **slime of the earth** <note>original: *Limo der Erden*; the mud or clay from which Adam was formed.</note>, according to the earth’s coarseness and malice. This beastly nature originates from the dark world and stands under God's curse. This same Beast arose in Adam and Eve when they **imagined** <note>Böhme uses "imagination" to describe the creative power of the mind to shape one's inner reality.</note> after both good and evil; it entered into a self-interest apart from Divine power and will, and before God, it is merely a beast. The Devil infected this same Beast with his own desire and made it entirely monstrous, leading his desire into it so that it lusts only after vanity, just as a cow lusts after grass.

22. **The Whore** of the Beast, however, is the poor soul imprisoned in vanity. She once stood in the **formed Word** <note>The "formed Word" refers to the divine breath manifested into the physical and spiritual structures of the universe.</note> of the three principles and was the very image of God. But through the lust of the Beast, she has birthed for herself a **self-will** <term>Self-will</term> <note>original: *eigenen Willen*; the ego-driven desire to act independently of God's harmony.</note>. This will has turned away from God into **self-hood** <term>Self-hood</term> <note>original: *selbheit*; the state of being trapped in one's own ego.</note>, acting as a self-born creature that does what it wants rather than what God's Spirit wants. This same self-will, having turned away from God, is the Whore of the Beast, who commits harlotry with herself in the pride of her own self-hood.

23. **Now, however,** the poor imprisoned soul lies trapped within this coarse Beast and within that self-born will, as if held captive by the Whore. She longs for God, from whom she originally proceeded and into whose created image she was breathed. She looks around on all sides for her true fatherland and place of rest, but she finds she is clothed and covered by this Whore. She directs her desire into this whorish will and seeks the "cities of God" for rest; then the whorish will takes the soul's desire into itself and swings itself upward. It flatters itself into thinking that, through the soul's desire, it is the beautiful child of God that shall possess heaven. It proclaims itself holy and presents itself as a god that should be honored and worshipped.

24. **And because** this child of the whore—the false will of self-hood—cannot truly behold the cities of God, nor know what or where God is, this false will follows the path of its own property. But before God, it is only a child of the whore and is **predestined** <note>original: *Prædestiniret*</note> for damnation, for God did not create it. 59. What is all this? An idolatry and hypocrisy, an Antichrist with brilliance and outward show. 60. Now Reason speaks: "These are indeed houses of learning, where the ignorant are taught, where one sings and prays." See, on the outside, within and among literal-minded people <note>original: *buchstabischen Menschen*; those who focus only on the "dead letter" of scripture rather than its spiritual heart</note>, it is only the Tower and City of Babel. But inwardly, among the children of God, in whom the Temple of God is found—where the images are destroyed—there is Christ. This is in those who have broken all images and opinions within themselves and have entered, solely and alone, through turning away from all images into the unique grace and mercy of God. They enter into His compassion and make themselves completely unworthy, null, and as if dead; they no longer want nor desire anything but the unique purity of God in His Love-Will. ## Chapter 37.

### Of Abraham and his Seed / and of the Lineage of the Covenant in its propagation / also of the Heathen Gods.

1. When one looks at the history of the accounts of the children of the ancient holy ones <note>The German "h." is an abbreviation for "Heiligen," referring to the patriarchs or saints of the Old Testament.</note> with the right eyes of understanding, one sees pure wonders; for the lineages of the children of God are just like a tree that grows in boughs and branches until it bears fruit. Thus also the lineage of Christ in his stem of the promised Word in the Covenant has grown from bough to bough up into the height of the branches, until his right age, until the power of the tree—that is, the Word in the Covenant—revealed itself with the lovely, beautiful blossom.

2. From which blossom the holy image of God has grown again in flesh and blood, as in a holy body; one sees its boughs and branches so beautiful that the soul rejoices greatly at such a sight, and rightly desires to grow out upon these boughs and branches, to the great praise of God, in our angelic <note>The original "Englischen" refers to "angelic," describing the celestial nature of the soul's home.</note> tree of the hierarchies of Christ of the Holy Paradise.

3. God made a covenant with Adam after his fall, when the heavenly essence <note>original: "Entis," a Latin term used by Böhme to describe the spiritual substance or "being" of the soul.</note> died within him, promising that He would make him alive again and reborn. And this covenant was the root in the faded essence; it grew in this line of Adam through Seth and his children and descendants until Noah, in a stem of the tree; and with Noah, God renewed the covenant.

4. For the undivided <term>sensual tongue</term> <note>The "sensual tongue" is Böhme’s term for the original universal language of humanity, where words perfectly matched the essence of the things they described.</note>—where the spirits of the letters ruled in a harmony—lasted until the Deluge, so that all people spoke in one tongue, in which the Spirit of God of the five vowels <note>original: "fünff Vocalium"</note> hovered as the Divine Understanding.

5. But because they had introduced the image and beast of vanity into the sensual tongue, and dallied with the Babylonian harlot of selfhood, God complained about them, that they would no longer let themselves be ruled by His Spirit, and said: It repented Him that He had made man.

6. For the repentance <note>Böhme uses the word "reuen" (to repent or regret) to show a dual action: God's "regret" leads to the destruction of the old world, while human "repentance" leads to rebirth.</note> toward breaking opened itself, and so also the repentance of penance toward new rebirth out of the Covenant. Thus the repentance of the formed Word in the single sensual tongue broke all life that lived in the air—that is, in the revealed Spirit of God, as in the <term>third principle</term> <note>The "Third Principle" in Böhme's cosmology refers to the visible, material world created from the interaction of light and dark spiritual forces.</note>—and after the Deluge, the Word of the sensual tongue carried itself out in a compaction of the spirits of the letters.

7. <margin>Ch. 37</margin> For God said to Noah: Mankind is flesh, and moreover evil from youth onward; therefore, the Holy Spirit would no longer reveal Himself in the evil-conceived sensual tongues <note>original: "sensualischen Zungen." This refers to languages shaped by the physical senses and fallen human nature rather than divine unity.</note>, but let them do as they wished. Because they would not follow Him, He allowed Nature the power to reveal its wonders out of both evil and good—as in images of the dark and outer world—so that their images now paraded in the light of outer nature, where evil and good are mixed together for the contemplation of God’s wonders according to Love and Wrath. From this foundation, the Heathen origin <note>original: "uhrstandt," meaning the primordial source or foundational state.</note> with its idols was born.

8. <margin><image-desc>manicule pointing left towards the text</image-desc></margin> For the origin of the spirits of the letters led into the formation of many languages, and in the formations of selfhood <note>original: "selbheit," the state of being turned toward one's own ego.</note>, the images were born in the understanding, wherein outer nature viewed itself; and the Devil also, out of God’s wrath <note>original: "Grimm," a technical term in Böhme's theosophy for the harsh, fiery, and judgmental quality of nature.</note>, introduced his imagination and desire into it, so as to lead mankind from understanding into images, so that they would not recognize the true God.

9. For all the oracles <note>original: "Oracula"</note> of the Heathen gods originate entirely from the outer and inner nature of the dark world, as a figure or understanding of the soul—of the outer and inner dark world—just like a personal god, meaning a nature-god. Just as the sensual tongue had arrived at such a nature-god and understanding, which flattered itself and conceived images within itself: so God let it happen, that Nature also represented itself to them as a god in the oracles, and spoke through those images.

10. For the Heathens honored the stars and the four elements because they recognized that these governed the external life of all things. Thus their understanding of the compacted sensual tongues—as the conceived word of understanding—entered into the likewise conceived and formed word of Nature. Thus, in return, the spirit of the formed word of Nature unified itself within them and moved one understanding from the other: just as the human understanding, in its desire, moved the understanding in the soul of the outer world <note>Referring to the "Anima Mundi," the spiritual essence that animates the physical universe.</note>. This occurred through the pronounced and formed word from the inner dark and fire-world, and from the outer starry and four-elemental world, in which soul the understanding of the wheel of time <note>original: "Rades der zeit," the cyclical, mechanical nature of temporal existence.</note> resides.

11. Through this understanding of the soul of the outer world, the prophetic spirit—from the Spirit of God—has also interpreted how the formed and spoken word of outer nature and time would hereafter introduce itself into the formations of the breaking down and building up of peoples, such as in the revelation of kingdoms and their downfall. In this soul of the outer world, all things stand in time, goal, measure, and weight, just like a clockwork <note>original: "Uhrwerck." Böhme uses the clock as a metaphor for the predetermined, mechanical aspects of the material world.</note>, of which the Scripture says much.

16. He was the one who should open *the bond* of the mental tongues to the true Divine understanding, and kindle the Light of Grace in love once again within the formed Word—in the letters of the sensual tongues—and break the **beast** of the formed tongues, in which the Devil had played and seated himself as if he were a god.

### and of the Lineage of the Covenant in its propagation.

18. This guest <note>likely referring to the spirit of the world or the devil mentioned in previous sections</note> was driven out by the holy fiery tongue in the opening of the Covenant in Chapter 37 by the Spirit of Christ, and he took from Prince Lucifer his throne within the human nature in the children of God.

19. Moses places ten names into the pages of the lineage from Noah until Abraham: namely Shem, Arphaxad, Shelah, Eber, Peleg, Reu, Serug, Nahor, Terah, and Abram. And he presents it quite wondrously, how Terah fathered three sons, namely Nahor, Haran, and Abram; this is an image of the **3 Principles** <note>The Three Principles are a core concept in Böhme’s philosophy: 1. The dark world (fire/wrath), 2. The light world (love/majesty), and 3. The outer world (nature/materiality).</note>, showing how they would all three be opened through this holy fire in this holy, fiery Lineage of the Covenant, and be separated from vanity. It shows how the whole human being should be born and formed into the image of God through the holy fire in the Covenant. Indeed, the names of the three brothers in the **sensual tongues** <note>original: "sensualischen Zungen." This refers to the external language of the physical world as opposed to the internal, spiritual "mental tongue."</note> represent this as well; if one brings the right mental understanding to them, one sees it in the form of the spirits composed of letters. Although this could be pointed out, it would not be understood by the unenlightened reader; but for our own <note>referring to Böhme’s circle of "initiated" or spiritual readers</note>, we do not need to recount this, for they already have it in their understanding.

20. By the **ten forms of fire**, I understand first the formed Word in the **seven properties of nature** <note>Böhme's "Seven Properties" describe the process of manifestation from dark desire to light and sound.</note>; and the eighth, ninth, and tenth forms are the inner world, which is unformed. The eighth number is the fire of the eternal nature of Divine revelation, as well as strength and omnipotence, which shall sweep the threshing floor at the end of days. The ninth number is the **Heavenly Tincture** <note>original: "Himlische Tinctur," an alchemical term for the spiritual essence that transforms and heals.</note> of fire and light; and the tenth number is the fire of Love, represented as the triangle of the Holy Trinity in Majesty—this is only hinted at for our own circle. It is explained further in the *Forty Questions of the Soul*, specifically in the philosophy of its introduction.

21. Out of these ten properties of the names in the Lineage of the Covenant, the **Oracle** <note>original: "Oraculum," the divine voice or prophetic word.</note> was revealed as the Divine voice in Abraham. For this reason, the Spirit of the Lord commanded him to go out from his fatherland and from his kinship; for the voice of Divine revelation was to come with the Messiah or Christ not out of his kinship—that is, out of his own bloodline—but out of God. However, the vessel lay within him, namely the **Essence** <note>original: "Ens." A technical term for the fundamental substance or "being" of a person or thing.</note>, in which the Divine voice wished to reveal itself. And because a foreign seed—a **Heavenly Essence** (John 3)—was to be introduced into his own seed, He commanded him to go out from his own lineage.

22. For the capacity for Divine revelation did not stand in the **essence** of man, but in God’s. Yet man’s **essence** had to join with it, so that Adam's faded heavenly **essence** might become living in Christ's living essence, and rise from death in Christ. So—

# Of Abraham and his Offspring

God said to Abraham: Go out into a land that I will show you: Here the Spirit indicates that he should see God not in his father's land—that is, in the earthly man—but in the land that the Lord would show him in his Seed <note>original: "Sahmen." <margin>❦</margin> 58. ## Chapter 38.

### Explanation of the beginning of the Heathen War; how Abraham rescued Lot, his brother’s son; and of the Royal Priest Melchizedek at Salem, to whom Abraham gave the tithe.

#### Genesis Chapter 14.

Here one now sees clearly what man's imagining, striving, and intent has been from youth upward—how they have led themselves out of the Image of God into half-beastly and half-devilish properties, such as pride, greed, and personal power, in the same way that the devil also desired such things and was therefore cast out from his kingdom.

2. For here the Heathens and the children of Ham <note>In the biblical narrative, Ham's descendants were often associated with the worldly powers that opposed the lineage of the promise.</note> began to rule in Sodom and Gomorrah and that whole region, among whom Abraham was only a stranger, living in the grove of Mamre as if in a wilderness, where he tended his livestock. The Heathens, however, fought over the kingdom of this world and outward might and power—how one people might rule over another. This will and governance has remained until today, and took its beginning from the Heathens and Ham’s children, arising out of Babel from the divided tongues <note>A reference to the Tower of Babel, where Böhme believes the unified "language of nature" was lost to human conflict.</note>.

3. When the powers of the formed Word <note>original: *geformten Worts*. For Böhme, the "formed word" is the divine creative breath manifest in the physical world.</note>—the properties of Nature—divided themselves and each led into its own selfhood, then strife and opposition arose among them. For the center of nature of the dark world gained the governance in the fallen human property; for humanity had died to the kingdom of God (which is love and humility) and lived now according to the outward stars and the four elements.

4. Also, the Devil had built his robber’s castle within the serpent’s sting <note>original: "Schlangen Ente," likely referring to the venomous or lower tail-end of the fallen human nature</note> in man; therefore, they sought only after that which would make them mighty and great in the world. And yet one sees how the Devil has only mocked them within the wrath of God, so that they murdered one another and valued temporal pleasure higher than life itself. This is the greatest folly: that one leads life into the danger of death for the sake of base pride, especially since one does not even know if they will be able to keep that for which they murder and strike others dead.

5. And it is soon seen how the Devil ruled in them through his envy and pride; for though they had the whole world as space to possess, and many lands and islands were uninhabited, they nevertheless began war so that they might only rule over one another and rob one another. Thus the Devil, as an enemy of mankind, led them into his pride so that they might serve him.

6. Not in vain does Christ call him a **Prince of this world**; he is a prince according to the property of the wrath of the dark world. Within that property, and according to it, he rules man in body and soul, in will and mind.

7. For all war and strife originates <note>original: "vhrständet," a term Böhme uses to describe the primordial "rising" or "emergence" of a quality</note> from the nature and property of the dark world—specifically from the four elements of the anger of God, which produces **Pride, Envy, Greed, and Anger** in the creature. These are the four elements of the dark world in which the devils and all evil creatures live, and from these four elements war arises.

8. For although God commanded the people of Israel to drive out the Heathen and commanded them to make war, this was all commanded out of the **angry, zealous God** <note>This refers to the "Deus Zelotes" or the "Grimm" (Wrath) aspect of the Divine</note>, as if from the property of fire. For the Heathen had stirred up the Wrath, which desired to devour them. But God—insofar as He is called "God"—desires no war, nor can He desire anything evil or destructive. For He is, according to the other Principle <note>Böhme's "Second Principle" is the world of Light and Love, distinct from the First Principle of Fire/Wrath</note>, namely the Light, alone good and giving, and He gives Himself to all things.

9. But according to the nature of the dark world, He is an **angry, zealous God and a consuming fire**. When His wrath is awakened, He desires to swallow and devour everything that rises and ignites within it. And out of that same property, God commanded Israel to wage war and slay the Heathen; for His wrath was kindled in them, and they were like wood that enters the fire—so does the fire desire to devour it.

10. Therefore, the Wrath of God commanded one people to murder the other, so that they would be cleared away out of His wrath; otherwise, His wrath-fire would have ignited itself [directly], as happened to the five kingdoms of Sodom and Gomorrah. Thus the Wrath of God took its satisfaction <note>original: "ergötzete sich," literally "delighted itself," but in the sense of the natural fulfillment of a spiritual Law</note> in the life of the ungodly, which it swallowed into itself by having them murder one another.

11. As happens even today, when people often cry out to God that He should give them luck and victory against their enemies so that they might murder them, but God does not give them victory in that, but rather the sword of His wrath, which they awaken with their own prayer and will. If they were truly human and children of God, they would need no war: For the Holy Spirit does not wage war, but He only loves and gives. But according to the property of wrath, it devours all godless existence, yet is only puffed up by it.

12. For the more wood one gives to a fire and the more one stirs it, the more it rises until it consumes everything it reaches. Thus it is also to be understood with the zeal of God <note>original: "Eyffer Gottes," a term describing both God’s fierce jealousy and the consuming fire of His holiness</note>; that same ignited wrath-zeal of God was set ablaze in Adam and had swallowed the image of the holy world within him, and it pressed from Adam upon all people.

13. For those in the Covenant Line <term>Covenant Line: the "Linea Christi," or the spiritual lineage through which the promise of the Savior was carried from Adam to Mary</term> also had the ignited zeal within themselves according to the first principle <note>original: "Principio," referring to the dark, fiery source of life and soul</note>, as pertains to soul and body; no one was better than the other. The serpent’s essence <note>original: "Schlangen Ens," the poisonous or fallen nature inherited from the Fall</note> lay in Abraham and his children—according to the ignited soul and according to the coarse, animalistic property of mortal man—just as much as it did in the heathens. The only difference was the Line of Christ within them, which was not the sinful man’s own selfhood, but stood in God’s power, **just as heaven stands in the world, and yet neither is the other: And as heaven stands in hell, and hell in heaven, and neither is the other or can grasp the other, or as night is in day, and day in night, or as the light of nature shines and dwells in the darkness.**

14. Thus we should understand how the children of the holy ones have waged war against the masses of the godless and driven them out; they did so in the property of wrath, which wields its sword through them to exterminate the heathens and the kind of Ham <note>original: "Hams Art," referring to the descendants of Noah's son Ham, traditionally viewed in this era as a lineage of the worldly or godless</note>. For Abraham went out with his whole house and people against the heathens who had captured and led away his brother’s son, Lot, and he struck the heathens and rescued his brother. This happened in the zeal of God, who thus rescues His children through the power of His wrath; for **that which serves as destruction for the godless serves as life and rescue for the holy ones.**

15. But as for those who want to be called Christians—who ought to have died to the wrath and fury of God through Christ’s death—yet still wage wars, they do not do so as Christians, but as heathens. No Christian wages war: For if he is a Christian, he has died to the four elements of God's wrath in his selfhood <note>original: "Selbheit," the ego-driven nature of the fallen man</note> with and in Christ’s death, and is born in Christ’s spirit of love as a new man, who lives in righteousness, in love, and in patience, and not for himself, but for God in Christ.

16. For a true Christian conducts his way of life and his will in heaven, in the life and Spirit of Christ, as St. Paul says: *Our citizenship is in heaven*; <note>original: "Unser Wandel ist im Himmel," referring to Philippians 3:20</note> but that Christians wage war, they do so out of the Heathen quality <note>In Böhme’s thought, "quality" refers to an internal driving force or characteristic</note> and not out of Christ’s quality. For a Christian is not of this world; his kingdom is in heaven, and in Christ he has died to the world according to the new spiritual man within him. The Heathen—as the half-demonic man who has desired his kingdom in this world—wants to wage war and murder within Christians. This Heathen nature has no place anywhere on Earth [spiritually], for it lives in the four elements of God’s wrath: namely, in Pride, Greed, Envy, and Wrath.

17. St. Paul says: *Yield your members as weapons of righteousness.* For why does one wage war? It is for the kingdom of this world. Yet Christ says His kingdom is not of this world; thus, the kingdom of His children in Him is also not of this world. So, if we now surrender our body and soul to be weapons of God’s wrath, and thereby seek only <term>Selfhood</term> <note>original: "Selbheit," the selfish ego that separates man from God</note> and murder one another for the kingdom of this world, then I must say we are so-called Christians with our mouths, but the heart and soul are Heathen and not born of Christ’s Spirit.

18. Abraham, when he struck down the Heathen, desired nothing of the goods he had taken, but gave back to the King of Sodom what the Heathen had taken from him. He was moved only by zeal in his heart; he did not wage war for land or kingdoms, but to rescue his brother. That was indeed a righteous zeal <note>original: "Eyffer," a holy passion or protective fire</note> which the Lord stirred within him. He did not rise up and fight for a land or a city; and even when he obtained it, he desired none of it, but returned again to his own place.

19. And here the Spirit speaks quite wonderfully through Moses, saying that as Abraham returned from the battle, the King of Sodom went out to meet him. And Melchizedek, the King of Salem, brought forth bread and wine; he was a priest of God the Most High, who possesses heaven and earth, and he blessed Abraham, and Abraham gave him a tenth of everything. And though one otherwise finds almost nothing in Holy Scripture concerning this priesthood, it was truly a figure of Christ. For the Spirit says in another place concerning Christ: *He is a High Priest after the order of Melchizedek.* <note>original: "Ordnung Melchisedech," a reference to Psalm 110:4 and Hebrews 7</note>

20. Thus, quite secretly, the Spirit of God represents the figure of Christ in Abraham, and calls him a King of Salem and a priest of God the Most High—as a priest of salvation and of anointing, according to how it sounds in the <term>Sensual Tongue</term>. <note>The "Sensual Tongue" (sensualischen Zungen) is Böhme’s term for the "Language of Nature," where the very sound of words reveals the inner essence of the thing named.</note> This means that Christ blessed Abraham and brought him bread and wine as His flesh and blood. He is the High Priest before God who reconciles Abraham and his children.

This image was divided in Adam with the creation of the woman <note>Böhme refers to the idea that the original human was a unified spiritual being, and the separation into male and female was a result of the Fall</note>; thus Christ, as the "woman’s tincture," gave him the essence of light again, so that the male and female qualities might once more become a single image. This is what the Spirit in Moses indicates here through the Royal Priest of Salem.

# The 39th Chapter.

## How God appeared to Abraham in a vision / and confirmed the Covenant with him in his Seed / and how Abraham’s Faith took hold of the Covenant / which was credited to him as Righteousness; and how God commanded him to offer sacrifice / and what is to be understood by this.

->Genesis 15<-

**Moses** says: After these events / it happened / that the Word of the Lord came to **Abraham** in a vision / and spoke: Fear not, **Abraham** / I am your Shield and very great Reward: But **Abraham** spoke: Lord, Lord / what will you give me? I go from here without children / and my steward has a son / this **Eliezer** of **Damascus**; and **Abraham** spoke further: To me you have given no Seed / and behold / this son of my household shall be my heir. And behold, the Lord spoke to him: He shall not be your heir / but he who shall come from your own body / he shall be your heir / and He commanded him to go out / and spoke: Look toward heaven and count the stars / can you count them? and spoke to him: so shall your Seed be: **Abraham** believed the Lord / and that was credited to him as righteousness.

2. In this passage lies the root of **Christian** Faith / for **God** said to **Abraham** / that He was his Shield and Reward / He wished to give him the Seed out of his own loins: **God** wished to be **Abraham’s** Reward / and give him a son out of himself / whose Seed should be like the stars in heaven / which are innumerable; and not the son of his servant should be the heir / not the animal human seed full of the Serpent **Ens** <term>Ens: a Latin term meaning "being" or "essence." Böhme uses it to describe the spiritual "substance" or quality of a thing</term> / but **God’s** Reward / **God’s** **Ens**: He wished to instill His reward into his Seed / as into the power of his loins / that should become a Seed / like the stars in heaven: He looked upon the Seed in the Covenant / as upon the Eternal Kingdom / which should be like the stars in heaven / so clear, pure, and innumerable: And this **Abraham** believed / and that was credited to him as righteousness.

<margin>Chapter 39.</margin>

3. Faith here is as much as if he grasped the Word; he took it into his desire <note>original: *Begierde*; in Böhme’s writing, this refers to the soul’s hunger or "magnetic" longing that attracts divine substance</note>, as if into a human essence <term>Ens: a Latin-derived term used by Böhme to mean the fundamental "being" or spiritual substance of a thing</term>. The goal within the Covenant—situated in the formed, compacted Word and within Abraham’s own nature and character—took on the speaking Word of God as the promise; and these two formed themselves into One. In this "One," Abraham’s faith was righteous, for God credited to Abraham the Word that he took into his faith-desire as righteousness, as his own property, and as justification.

---

4. For this incorporated Word justified the creaturely word <note>the "creaturely word" refers to the human soul as a spoken expression of God</note>, which is the spoken, created word—understand this as that which has formed itself in the human character and entered into a creaturely state, as if emerging from three principles into one image. In this image, the self-will (through desire and lust) had swung itself upward into the quality of the dark world—into the fire and wrath of God—and led into an earthly coarseness. Into this coarse image, the devil had introduced his own essence <note>original: *Ens*</note>, will, and desire by means of the serpent.

---

5. To this essence, this compacted Word, and this created image, the living, eternally-speaking holy Word—arising from the quality of Light and Divine Love—came to help and became his reward. That holy Word took Abraham’s natural word and power into itself, and that same Word of God, grasped and held in the desire, justified Abraham’s corrupted word. It became his righteousness, which broke the wrath and destroyed the devil’s desire and will; understand that this occurred within the human essence <note>original: *Ente*; likely a variation of *Ens* or essence</note>, within the formed Word.

---

6. For there is no faith without God’s Word and power. Thus, Abraham now took God’s Word, power, and promise into himself, into his essence, and grasped it into a substance of his spirit. That was the faith of justification: that God’s Word and the human will and desire entered into a single spiritual substance. Thus, God credited the incorporated or "in-spoken" grasped Word to Abraham as righteousness, as his own property. And this is the ground and root of faith: that one grasps God’s promise into one's desire as one's own property, and does not let it go in doubt. This is as **Jacob** did; he grasped the Word of promise into himself and said: *I will not let you go unless you bless me* <note>Genesis 32:26</note>. He wrestled the whole night with the Word of power until he triumphed, so that the promised Word gave itself to him as his own property—as a blessing or great reward—just as happened here with **Abraham**.

---

7. Therefore, understand us clearly: the embodied Word of the Covenant in Paradise, which God promised to **Adam** regarding the "serpent-crusher" <note>the promise in Genesis 3:15 that the seed of the woman would crush the serpent’s head</note>, wrestled through **Jacob’s** formed...

Then God presented to him the image of the Seed, which he had grasped in his faith—which had become his righteousness—and showed it to him in a symbol; for the sacrifice signifies the sacrifice of Christ. The three kinds of animals—the three-year-old heifer, the goat, and the ram—signify the part of external humanity from that time, as if from the *Limo* <note>original: *Limo*; Latin for "slime" or "clay," referring to the biblical "dust of the ground" from which man was formed.</note> of the earth.

15. 16. That Abraham divided these three animals in the middle and laid one half against the other signifies the twofold *Limum* <note>clay or substance</note> of the earth: one being the coarse property from the property of the dark world, and the other being the *Limum* from the property of the heavenly world, which lies in the earth in a *Compaction* <term>Compaction: a state of being compressed or condensed into a material form; the "thickening" of spiritual essence into matter.</term>, out of which man was created according to the body.

17. That Abraham divided them signifies that the coarseness must be separated from the subtlety of humanity—which Adam's desire introduced—through death. They must lie one against the other and be separated, each into its own property, just as light and darkness are divided and yet exist beside one another.

18. The turtle dove signifies the poor soul imprisoned in this animal property, and the young dove signifies the inner, faded humanity of the poor soul, which shall become young again in the sacrifice as a new birth.

21. And the ignition of the fire, which passed between the pieces, is now the holy fire of God. It also passed through the humanity of Christ, in both soul and body, when He stood in the Father's wrath, in death and the darkness of hell, casting the humanity of soul and body into that wrath and transforming the wrath into a love-fire. For the fierceness of the Father according to the eternal nature of the dark world, which was ignited within humanity, had to receive such a holy "Ens" <note>An "Ens" refers to a spiritual essence or "being-ness" that gives something its character.</note> of love within humanity, so that the wrath in its own fire might be transformed into a light or a love-fire.

22. This holy "Ens" in the word of faith had to enter into the great terror of the wrath of God, for the soul stood essentially <note>original: "Essentialiter"</note> within its own property. The soul is from the property of the Father's fire (from His strength and omnipotence) as if from the first <term>Principle: Böhme describes reality as three "Principles": the dark fire-world (Father), the light-world (Son), and the outer world (Spirit).</term>. Here, the second <term>Principle</term> (acting as the love-fire) came to its aid; therefore, the soul had to return to its own root, from which it had become a creature, and be <term>tinctured: in alchemy, to "tincture" means to permeate and transform the inner quality of a substance, like turning lead to gold.</term> in the power of the love-fire in the Divine Light, and be transformed into a beautiful Divine Gold. This sacrifice was a symbolic foreshadowing of that process.

23. However, the fact that birds fell upon the carcasses—which Abraham chased away—signifies the hungry essence of the fierce property of God's wrath in man. This wrath hungered after humanity and wanted to devour it into itself. But the word in Abraham's faith chased the devourer away; humanity was not to be devoured, but rather sacrificed, so that one essence might enter into the other and the second might overcome the first.

24. The sacrifice of Christ (as the humanity of Christ) indeed gave itself entirely as a sacrifice into the Father's wrath, into His fire-essence; but the love-spirit of God prevented the fierce essence of the fire from being able to swallow the humanity of Christ. It took only the "own-will" from humanity and led it back into the original, total will from which man's will was first given—the very will which had made man into a "selfhood" <note>The state of being separated from God through ego and private desire.</note> and corrupted him. Here, he was led back into the Father's will as into the first root; for thus spoke Christ (when He sweated blood in this state on the Mount of Olives):
> Father, your will be done and not my will.

### Chapter 40.

## Concerning the History and completely wonderful prefiguration of the Spirit of God with Hagar, Sarah’s maid, and her son Ishmael; concerning his expulsion from the inheritance and concerning Isaac’s heritage.

->Gen. 16.<-

Whoever wishes to read the history of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and understand it correctly—what the Spirit of God suggests through it—must not look upon it merely as a history, as if there were nothing more than a narrative beneath it. The entire Kingdom of Christ together with the Kingdom of Nature is depicted therein; not only the work of human redemption, but also who, how, or what in humanity shall inherit God’s Kingdom. It is not as the Jews boast, that they alone are God’s people—no, it is something quite different. God does not look upon a single lineage, but upon the trunk or root of the tree.

2. In the two brothers, namely Isaac and Ishmael, the two kingdoms are prefigured: in Ishmael the Kingdom of Nature, and in Isaac the Kingdom of Grace. So it is also with Esau and Jacob. For out of Abraham two lines now went forth, namely those of Japheth and Shem <note>Böhme uses these biblical names to represent different spiritual qualities or branches of humanity</note>. Ishmael was the first; just as Japheth was among Noah’s children, and Cain among Adam’s children. This signifies the Kingdom of Nature, which has its origin <note>original: "Vhrstand"</note> from the property of the Father, and must always be the first if a creature is to be born. <image-desc>decorative flourish at the end of the paragraph</image-desc>

6. Christ came to lead Adam's rebellious will into death and dying, to prove it again in the fire of God, and to give it new birth in the fire of Love. Thus, it returns to the first, single will of God, where the Father and Son are but one single will and essence in both the fierce fire of Wrath and the light-fire of Love.

7. For with the movement of the divine property—when God moved Nature and created creatures—the two properties of Love and Wrath in Nature separated from one another. This was so that through struggle and opposition <note>original: "Wider-willen," literally "counter-will"</note> the mystery of God (as the invisible spiritual world) might be revealed and enter into a wrestling game <note>original: "ringendes Spiel," a characteristic term for the dynamic interplay of spiritual forces</note>.

8. For if there were only one kind of will, then all beings would do only one thing. But in opposition, each thing raises itself within itself toward its own victory and exaltation; all life and growth consist in this struggle. Through this, the Divine Wisdom is revealed and takes a form for contemplation and for the Kingdom of Joy. For joy is found in overcoming; but a single, solitary will is not manifest to itself. In such a will there is neither evil nor good, neither joy nor sorrow. Even if such things existed there, the One (the single will) must first introduce a counter-play within itself so that it may reveal itself.

78. 79. Whoever touches the humanity of Christ in misunderstanding, as if it were his own flesh, can be forgiven; for he does not know what the humanity of Christ is. But whoever blasphemes the Holy Spirit as the only God, who has revealed Himself in humanity—where the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are one single God within—he has no forgiveness eternally; that is, whoever rejects the one God has completely broken himself off into his own self.

80. Now, the Turks <note>In the 17th century, "Turks" was the standard term for Muslims</note> do not blaspheme the Holy Spirit who revealed Himself in humanity; rather, they take issue with the humanity of Christ and say: A creature cannot be God.

81. But that God worked in Christ and performed miracles, they concede; and they do not blaspheme the Spirit which worked in Christ as in humanity. Blindness has befallen them, so that they travel under a veil.

82. Listen, O human, what was the cause that God pushed their lampstand away—as He threatened in Saint Paul—and enclosed them under the veil? Do you think it happened without His foreknowledge, without His will? No, it happened with His will.

83. He permitted the Kingdom of Nature to give them a doctrine of reason, because Christendom had become blind in Reason regarding the person of Christ, and they brawled over Christ’s humanity, and committed all kinds of shame and dishonor against it—as happened with the Arians <note>Followers of Arius, who taught that Christ was a created being and not co-eternal with God the Father</note>, when His divinity was denied. Furthermore, the bishops in their greed, for the sake of their bellies, pulled His merit in His humanity into their orders of the belly <note>original: "Bauchorden"; a satirical term for clergy focused on earthly appetite and wealth rather than spiritual service</note>, and practiced all kinds of frivolity, including swearing, cursing, and sorcery by His passion and holy wounds. Since the Holy Name of God, which had revealed itself in humanity, was thus misused, God hid Himself from them in their understanding, so that they first became blind to the divinity of Christ along with the Arians.

84. Afterward, when they insisted on being blind animals, He also hid His humanity from them through the Turkish religion, so that they would be entirely deprived of the lampstand of the world; and it happened to them as the Prophet said to Israel under their king: "Ah! I must give you judges again, as in ages past." <note>A reference to Isaiah 1:26 regarding God’s restoration of authority through judgment</note>

89. 92. If one now places "painted" Christianity <note>Böhme uses "painted" (gemahle) to describe nominal Christians who have the outward appearance of faith without the inner reality</note> and the Turks against one another and examines them rightly, one sees that (during the time since the Turks separated from them) they have been, before God in holiness and righteousness, only a single people with different names.

93. And they are like the two sons where the father says to one: "Go and do that," and he said "Yes," but did not do it; and to the other he also said, "Do that," and he said "No," but went and did it. This is why the Turks are so highly exalted in the Kingdom of Nature—which blind Christianity does not understand. <note>A reference to the parable in Matthew 21:28–31. Böhme suggests that while Muslims "denied" the specific revelation of Christ, they may follow the natural law of God more sincerely than nominal Christians who profess faith but do not live it.</note>

94. Not that we justify the Turks and say that they should remain in their blindness—no—but we say it to the "painted" Christians: that they are equal before God, in that they are just as blind to the Kingdom of Christ as the Turks. This is proven by the fact that Christianity is full of strife and bickering over Christ’s divinity and humanity. They horribly desecrate the Holy Name in His humanity, using it only for the purpose of swearing and for idolatry. They have turned from the Sword of the Holy Spirit into a "blood-sword," <note>The "blood-sword" refers to religious wars and the use of force to settle theological disputes</note> where nothing but bickering and contempt is found. The whole of so-called Christianity has become nothing but idle sects and orders, where each sect despises the other and calls it unrighteous. Thus, they have made a literal den of murderers out of Christianity, full of blasphemy concerning Christ’s person and the Spirit of Christ. Whereas a Christian should live in the highest humility, they have instead made a "disputing-order" and set foolish Reason up as the master of understanding over Christ’s Kingdom.

95. What shall one say then to compare Christianity and the Turks? We say this: The Turk is openly an Ishmaelite and a mocker of Christ’s humanity, and he does not hold Him to be the Son of God and the Son of Man simultaneously; for he does not understand the Heavenly *Ens* <term>Ens: A philosophical term for "being" or "essence." Böhme uses it to describe the spiritual substance that makes up the inner person</term> in the Person.

96. But the sects of Christianity, though they cover themselves with Christ’s cloak, actually strike at His humanity and divinity. They also shame Him in His entire person, pulling and tearing at His person—one wants it this way, the other that way. Each wants to be master over His word and Spirit, and thus they mock Christ in His members. They are just as much apostate, runaway Ishmaelites as the Turks are, and they live in their own will and serve the Kingdom of Nature for their own selfhood and pleasure.

97. A Christian should be dead to selfhood with Christ, and risen in Christ, and born out of Christ. He should have put on Christ, so that he may be a Christian in Christ—in Christ’s Spirit and Heavenly Flesh—according to the inner spiritual man.

The covenant and blessing did not apply to this [beast-like man], but rather to the formed <term>Ens</term> of the Word, [drawn] from the <term>slime of the earth</term> <note>original: "Limo der Erden" / "limus terrae". For this reason, the woman was not to put on the seal of baptism through her own will or desire, but from the man, because she had been taken from the man, so that she might become a true Woman <note>original: *Männin*; this is a specific term used in the German Bible to show that "Woman" (*Männin*) was derived directly from "Man" (*Mann*).</note> in the man’s baptism, so that the image of God in her would receive the Fire-Baptism and Tincture from the man.

32. For St. Paul understood this well when he said: The woman will be saved through childbearing, if she remains in the covenant and in love; for the woman had her soul from the man's soul, and when she joins herself to the man, she is one body with him and bears children for the man; she is his Woman, his instrument, half a man, and the man half a woman.

33. But so that the masculine property might receive the perfect love as the feminine Ens again, and the woman receive the masculine, the Holy Spirit of the man—as the Fire-Tincture—baptizes with the heavenly Holy Virginity, and the man baptizes the woman’s essence in his seed with the fiery and also Divine Tincture; therefore God commanded only the male figures to be circumcised.

34. For in the Jews’ Fire-Baptism, the Spirit alone baptized without water, but among Christians, the Spirit baptizes through water. The Jewish women could <gloss>indeed</gloss> put on the Spirit in the man’s Fire-Baptism; but now that the same fiery Word has become flesh, they should now rightly put on Christ in the flesh and be baptized. For their heavenly faded virginity must also put on Christ’s introduced heavenly virginity within her, so that she becomes a true Masculine Virgin <note>In Böhme's mysticism, the "Masculine Virgin" refers to the restored, holy state of the soul where the fiery (male) and light (female) properties are perfectly balanced as they were before the Fall.</note> in Christ's spirit and essence.

35. Now reason asks further: why then did the children, the little boys, have to be circumcised precisely on the 8th day? Why not sooner or later? Was it not in human power to delay it, if perhaps many a child had been weak? Here lies mystery and wonder—

# Of the Seal of the Covenant of Circumcision

<margin>Question 5. I</margin>
53. So hear now, you Christians, Jews, Turks <note>In the 17th century, "Turks" was a general term for Muslims.</note>, and Heathens—all peoples on earth—what is now given to you in the visitation of the merciful God, in the voice of His trumpet through His dear Will and Spirit, once more and for the last time in this temporal existence: The trumpet’s blast reaches you all; let it enter into your hearing. If you only open your ears for one hour, away from your **selfhood** <note>The German term *Selbheit* refers to the ego or the state of being centered on oneself rather than God.</note>, you will hear the sound within you. It echoes through everything to the ends of the earth, but no **self-will** can hear it.

54. The one and only Divine Way, by which one may behold God in His Word, Essence, and Will, is this: that a person becomes one within themselves and, in their own will, abandons everything they are and have—be it authority, power, honor, beauty, wealth, money and goods, father, mother, brother, sister, wife and child, body and life—and becomes a total **Nothing** to themselves. They must surrender everything and become poorer than a bird in the air, which at least has a nest. The true person should have none, for they are to wander away from this world so that they are no longer "in" this world for their own sake. They must become a "Nothing" to the world's selfhood; for the essence of this world, which a person possesses as their own property, is the **Tower of Babel** and the **Antichrist**. It is there that one wishes to be their own god, and with this self-made god, climb the tower into heaven to set themselves beside God. Understand it this way:

55. It is not meant that a person should run out of the house, away from wife, child, and siblings, or flee from the world, or leave their goods in a way that they refuse to live among them; rather, one must kill and bring to nothing the **self-will** which possesses all these things as its own personal property.

56. And one should think that all in which they exist is not their own at all—whether they win or lose, whether they are rich or poor, wise or simple, lowly or high. Whether they have *Something* or *Nothing*, they should regard it all as equal: a beautiful garment the same as a hideous one, the good fortune of the world the same as misfortune, life the same as dying, their authority the same as a servant's, a Royal Crown the same as an old hat. All this must be abandoned in the mind and not regarded as one’s own.

57. Instead, one should think—and yield their will entirely to this thought—that in everything they are, they are merely a servant of that station, essence, and order; that it belongs to God and their brothers in common. They should only serve God and their brothers within it. Whatever others do to them, they should accept it as something happening to the general brotherly order and station. God established such orders in the world as a **figure** <note>A "figure" or "type" is a physical representation or shadow of a spiritual reality.</note> of the **Angelic World** <note>The German *Englische Welt* refers to the world of angels (*Engel*), not the country of England.</note>, so that one might serve Him therein.

# of the Foreskin and of Baptism

<margin>Chapter 41</margin>
58. And he should not allow his **inner soul** <note>German: *Gemüthe*; the seat of thoughts and emotions.</note> to swing into **selfhood** <note>German: *Selbheit*; the state of being focused on one's own ego rather than God.</note>, so that he wants to think he is a king, a counselor, or a judge of the people, and is therefore somehow better before God or before men. He shall always look upon his naked breast, seeing that one naked human looks similar and equal to another, and that his official robes belong to the brotherly community, as does his office, over which he is merely a supervisor.

59. He should always think only of how he may please his brothers in his station, and not himself.

60. <meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on Genesis 18, focusing on the moment the Lord promises a son to Abraham and Sarah. The author, likely Jakob Böhme, interprets these biblical events not just as history, but as a "Language of Nature" describing how the divine essence enters into physical reality.</meta>

<sig>B u</sig>

<margin>Chapter 42. <note>Though the margin says Chapter 42, the text continues to interpret Genesis 18.</note></margin>
27. It <note>the soul or divine spark</note> is hidden within the human hut by the earthly hut, so that it does not see who is with me; and the Lord said: "I will certainly return to you when I live; behold, then shall **Sarah** your wife have a son." This means: I will return to you with the movement of your seed; when **Sarah** becomes pregnant, I will dissolve her in her enclosed seed and come into your seed—that is, to move it. For "to come" means to go, to move: When **God** comes, He moves the person and comes or goes in and with the person.

28. But as for what He says: "As I live," this is spoken in an <term>Essentialiter</term> <note>original Latin: "essentially" or "in essence"; referring to the inner, spiritual reality rather than the outward form</note> manner. For **God** told him how He wished to come—not before him, as He did this time, but *In such a way*; that is, as the sunshine and power give themselves into a fruit. It does not step alongside the fruit when it comes, but *In such a way*; that is, it penetrates <term>Essentialiter</term> with the "In such a way." For "In such a way" is as much as to say "I will look into": "As I live" is not to be understood as if He said, "if I am still alive," but rather He wished to live in that "In such a way": He wished to come in that "In such a way" <term>Essentialiter</term>, and not figuratively, as He did this time.

29. For when **God** comes, He comes in no other way than *In such a way*; that is, like a sunshine into the fruit. In the <term>Language of Nature</term> <note>German: *Natur-Sprache*; a mystical concept where the names of things reveal their inner divine essence</note>, one understands this <term>Essentialiter</term> quite beautifully: For when **God** speaks of His own coming, He speaks only <term>Essentialiter</term> in the manner of the uncompacted sensual tongues.

30. And **Sarah** laughed at this: She thought she was first to conceive a son from **Abraham’s** desire of human cohabitation in the lust of the flesh; therefore she said, "Shall I yet have pleasure, now that I and my lord are old?" The animalistic <term>Spirit of the World</term> <note>German: *Welt-Geist*; the consciousness of the physical, temporal world</note> laughed at its youth, for it was now weak and was supposed to become lusty again, and thought it were a joke, "if only you could!" It is just as if one said to an old person: "You shall now become young again, and receive such a desire and lust as when you were young"; at this, nature would laugh and think, "Yes, if only it were true," where half-doubt and half-hope were together. This is how it went for **Sarah**, for the <term>Spirit of the World</term> does not understand **God’s** mystery. Before **God**, it is only as an animal; and because the <term>Spirit of the World</term> now heard that it should happen thus, it thought: "You are to be the <term>Master Builder</term> <note>German: *Werckmeister*; an artisan or craftsman; here referring to the natural forces of procreation</note>; yes, if you only could, you would surely like to," and laughed at itself, that it should become young again.

31. This is how much the natural man understands of **God**—like an animal: when it sees hay, it thinks, "now there is something to eat"; but when it sees nothing, it hopes out of habit. But **Sarah** had now hoped until she had become ninety years old, and it seemed strange to her that **God**—

# Concerning the three men who visited **Abraham**, etc.

31. **God** wished to perform something in her that was beyond the course and habit of Nature, and He presented this to her mind in the manner of human desire. <note>Böhme suggests that Sarah’s physical reaction—laughter—was a reflection of natural human impulse being confronted by a supernatural promise that her body could not yet comprehend.</note>

32. But the **Lord** said: "Why did **Sarah** laugh?" And she was afraid and said, "I did not laugh." But the **Lord** said: "It is not so; you did laugh." Should anything be impossible for the **Lord**? Here stands the image of **Eve**, when she turned her curiosity into her own desire for the forbidden tree; and when **God** later asked her why she had done it, she also denied her own desire and blamed it on the **Serpent**.

33. Because **God** had now played here with **Abraham** concerning the new birth, He also played here with **Sarah** concerning **Eve's** desire, which this "Seed of the Woman" <note>A traditional theological reference to Christ, based on the prophecy in Genesis 3:15 that the offspring of the woman would crush the serpent's head.</note> was meant to kill as a lie. For this reason, **Sarah** had to tell a lie here—claiming she had not laughed—because **Eve** had lied. So **God** now placed **Eve's** lie before her, showing how He wished to put it to shame with the Eternal Truth and drive it back, just as He did to **Sarah** when He forced her to confront her lie so that she had to feel ashamed.
