9. But he does not possess the goods by <term>natural right</term> <note>original: "Natur-Recht." This refers to the inherent rights or powers a person thinks they possess by virtue of their birth or physical existence, as opposed to spiritual grace.</note>, as if to take them by his own will; rather, he possesses them as a gift. He shall and must surrender himself into the <term>Covenant</term> <note>original: "Bund." In Böhme's theology, the Covenant represents the spiritual contract or relationship between God and humanity, specifically through Christ.</note> as a servant of his natural will. He must give himself up in the Covenant, abandon the will toward natural right, and become the property of the Covenant. In this way, he no longer introduces his own natural will into the Covenant and the gift, but yields his will to the Covenant. Then the gift stands in place of his own will, and the nature of Adam lives within the gift; it enjoys the inheritance nonetheless, but not in its own will. It lives instead in true <term>resignation</term> <note>original: "Gelaſſenheit." A central concept in German mysticism meaning a state of yieldedness, letting go of the self, and radical openness to God's will.</note>, where the will of the Covenant becomes the will of the human being.

10. For the will of the Covenant inherits the <term>sonship</term> <note>original: "Kindſchafft." The state of being a child of God.</note> in natural right, but the will of the natural selfhood is cast out from it; it must die to its own-ness. When that happens, it rises within the Covenant in Christ and possesses the gift by the <term>right of grace</term> <note>original: "Gnadenrecht." The legal and spiritual standing granted by God's mercy rather than human merit.</note>. Christ manifested himself in the Covenant—in the gift given to Adam—within human nature, and he became the life and will of the Covenant and fulfilled it.

11. Now, however, this same gifted Covenant that God bestowed upon Adam lies within all people; for just as sin was inherited from one onto all, so too were the Covenant and the gift of grace inherited from one onto all. Every human being has Christ within them, but the self-will does not grasp Him; instead, it crucifies Him. The self-will does not want to die to its selfhood so that it might enter into Christ’s death and rise in the Covenant in the will of Christ.

12. The self-will only wants to be an "adopted child of grace," yet it is nonetheless rejected before God’s face—just as Abraham cast out his natural children from his goods and disinherited them, giving the goods to Isaac alone. Thus, the Kingdom of God belongs solely to the will of the Covenant.

13. This Kingdom indeed lies within all people, but no one can receive or behold the Kingdom of God unless they become a child of the Covenant—unless they abandon the natural, outgoing will and put on the will of Christ in the Covenant, so that their will is born anew in the Covenant in Christ. Then they are a branch on the vine of Christ and receive Christ’s spirit, will, and life, becoming, according to the Covenant, "a Christ." Thus Christ dwells in Adam and Adam in Christ; and this is what the spirit of <term>Moses</term> <note>original: "Moyſis." 25. However, the reason why the Jews—as the children of Isaac and Abraham and children in the symbol of Christ—did not all turn to Christ when He was revealed in the flesh, is interpreted thus: God gave them the Law of Nature. In this Law, the governance of nature was understood externally, while internally Christ was understood as the Covenant and the promised gift of God in Paradise. This was so that the Law of Nature should become Christ’s "housemate," meaning that the true human should live in rationality under the Law of Nature, but should also bring his own nature into Christ’s house. Thus, the symbol of the Law had to remain with some of Abraham’s children, namely some of the Jews, to signify that the Law is a housemate of Christ.

26. Understand this: human nature is meant to remain and is not entirely cast away by God, as if a completely foreign, new person were to arise out of the old one. Rather, it arises out of Adam’s nature and property combined with God’s nature and property in Christ, so that the person becomes an "Adam-Christ" and Christ becomes a "Christ-Adam": *A Man-God and a God-Man.* <note>original: "Ein Mensch Gott / vnd ein Gott Mensch." This reflects the Böhmean concept of the mystical union where the divine and human natures interpenetrate.</note> For this reason, the symbol remained with the Jews, and for these causes they were not all converted to Christ; it was so that nature might keep its symbol and right. For nature shall surrender its children under the Law—as the symbol of Christ—to God the Father in Christ. But their symbol will be tested in the fire of God, so that it may be known who was a true child of the natural Law in the symbol of Christ, born in the spirit within the Law out of the symbol of Christ, or not.

27. It is not the lip-service Jew <note>original: "Maultittel," literally a "mouth-titler," referring to someone who holds the title of a Jew in speech only but not in spirit.</note> who is born into the symbol and the Law, but rather the one born from the promise in the faith of Abraham. Whoever lives with mouth and heart in Christ’s symbol (the Law), that person has been enclosed by the Law of God within Christ’s symbol, and the Law will lead him into the fulfillment of that symbol.

28. For it does not depend solely on a person's intellectual knowledge—knowing that Christ gave Himself into the Law and is the fulfillment of the Law, as the lip-service Christian <note>original: "MaulChrist." 35. When the heathens <note>original: "Heyden." 36. And here there is no regard for the name, that one says, "I am a Jew"; the other, "I am a Christian." 41. The Jews do not want to believe in the external humanity of Christ and they deny it. The Christians, however, believe in it, but they defile it with a godless way of life; thus, before God, one is like the other, except for the children of faith among both Jews and Christians, whose stained garment is washed in the blood of Christ.

42. We do not hereby confirm the unbelief of the Jews and heathens <note>original: "Heyden." Referring to those outside the Judeo-Christian tradition.</note> so that they should remain in blindness, for the time of their visitation has dawned, that they may see. Rather, we are uncovering the false Antichrist <note>Böhme uses "Antichrist" to describe a spirit of hypocrisy and legalism found in all religions, rather than a single historical figure.</note> among both Jews and Christians, where each boasts of his name and condemns the other: the Jew in the Law, the Christian in the Gospel <note>original: "Evangelio."</note>, and the heathen in his superstition.

43. Everyone wants to be God's child through their knowledge, yet disobedience and unbelief are just as great in one people as in the other. In their formal knowledge, they are merely a figure before God, and no one is saved through knowledge alone. For me to hold it as true that Christ was born, died for me, and rose from the death does not make me a child of God. The Devil knows this too, but it does him no good. I must "put on" <note>A reference to the biblical metaphor of being "clothed" with Christ, suggesting an internal transformation rather than just intellectual belief.</note> Christ through the desire of faith, and enter into His obedience, His incarnation, suffering, and death, and rise in Him and put on the obedience of Christ; only then am I a Christian, and not before.

44. Judging and condemning without God’s command is nothing but the Antichrist among both Jews and Christians. Without God's mercy, no one attains the state of childhood <note>Being a "child of God."</note>; we must all enter through the mercy of God—the Jew and the Christian, the one who knows and the one who does not know. Our knowledge should become perfect in the love of Christ, so that we love one another; otherwise, knowledge is of no use. If I do not guide my knowledge with desire into the love of God—with which He loved us in Christ—and love my neighbor in the love of God in Christ, with the same love with which God loves and has loved us all together while we were His enemies, then I do not yet have the love of God dwelling within me.

He uses the biblical figures of Kethurah’s children and Ishmael as allegories for those who focus on external law and intellectual debate rather than spiritual rebirth.</meta>

# How Abraham took another wife

<margin>1 John 4</margin>
45. How can he love, who despises his brother for the sake of intellectual knowledge <note>original: "wissenschafft." Böhme uses this to mean theoretical or "head" knowledge of scripture, rather than living spiritual experience.</note>, seeing as God loved us when we knew nothing of His love? If a person does not have that same love of God within him, with which God loved us when we did not know Him, why then does he boast so long of his divine childship <term>Kindschafft: the state of being a child of God through spiritual rebirth</term>? If he is God’s child, then he also possesses the free love of God, with which God loves all things. If he does not have it, then he is not yet capable of that childship. So now, if someone despises and condemns his brother who does not yet have that intellectual knowledge, how can he boast of the love of God, with which God loved His enemies in Christ, and for which Christ prayed for His enemies?

46. O you false, cold love of titular Christendom <note>Christians in name only.</note>! How the Eternal Truth scolds your conscience, in that you only cling to "knowing" and quarrel over intellectual knowledge, yet do not have love! You only judge yourself in your judging, where one pack judges the other. Before God, you are nothing other than the natural children of Abraham by Kethurah <note>In Genesis, Kethurah was Abraham's second wife. Böhme uses her children to represent those who seek God through their own natural efforts or legalism rather than the spirit of the promise (Isaac).</note>, where each one blamed the other because the father had cast them out from the inheritance, and they could not see what the fault was—namely, that of the evil, corrupted nature, which was not an heir.

47. In the same way, your judging is no heir to the treasures of Christ. It shall be entirely cast out from the inheritance—both of the Jews and also of the Christians, as well as the Turks <note>A common 17th-century term for Muslims or the Ottoman world.</note>. All your quarreling is nothing other than the mocker Ishmael, who mocks Christ in His members. You all misuse the name of God with your judging, and you condemn the manifold gifts of the Spirit of God among you; you judge only in selfhood <term>Selbheit: the state of being centered on the ego or "self" rather than being surrendered to God</term> and not according to the love of Christ.

48. Your judging is only a harm to the world, with which you lead the ignorant astray and guide them toward blasphemy. You teach them how to condemn, but you yourselves do not have the true knowledge in the Spirit of God. You do not teach yourselves and yet you wish to teach and judge others; in this course, you are all together merely the cast-out children of Kethurah. You quarrel and bite one another over Abraham’s—that is, Christ’s—goods, and yet you do not possess them. Had you the same, you would have the love of Christ, which is the true treasure.

49. No knowledge without the love of Christ is of any use for divine childship; it is only Babel and a fable—to teach and yet do nothing oneself, except to honor the idol Maozim <note>Referring to the "god of fortresses" in Daniel 11:38, which Böhme interprets as an idol of worldly power and institutional force.</note> within oneself. The knowledge of the high schools <note>Universities or academic theological faculties.</note> and the knowledge of the devil, outside of the Spirit of Christ in love, both bring only strife and destruction.

50. Had the devil not known in selfhood, he would still be an angel; and had Adam not desired self-knowledge outside of God’s love, he would have remained in Paradise. If the high schools did not know their sharp disputing,

->The internal figure stands thus.<-

52. Abraham's natural children by the concubines moved toward the East; there the Spirit points to the "figure" or pattern of the whole human being. When Christ has revealed himself in a person and possessed his goods (as Isaac did here), then nature returns to the beginning, as if into the Father’s own property. It works according to the soul in the first and third <term>Principle: Böhme’s system of three "worlds"—the 1st is the dark fire-source (Father), the 2nd is the light-world (Son/Christ), and the 3rd is the visible world (Spirit/Nature).</term>. Christ sits in the middle as in the second Principle and governs that which nature forms and shapes in Divine Wisdom within the Father’s property.

53. Therefore, Moses says here that they journeyed toward the East, and in his "figure" he secretly points to the property of man: how nature possesses the "Morning" as the beginning of its dominion. Just as Christ also said, He was like a vintner who gleans <note>Likely a reference to the "laborers in the vineyard" or the concept of gathering the spiritual harvest.</note>. In the Kingdom of God, nature is Christ’s servant; but in the realm of <term>nature-selfhood: the state where nature acts for its own ego and desires</term>, Christ has given himself with his humility as a servant and helper. He serves the Father in His natural revelation and always gleans afterward; whatever the Father forms through nature, Wisdom leads into her treasury.

54. Therefore, St. Paul says that the Spirit of God is also subject to the children of God and enters with them into the search, even into the depths of the Godhead. And when it reaches that point, then man is at a restful age. When everything in him is in its proper order—with nature in the "Morning" in the Father’s property and Christ in the "Evening" in humility—then man is quite weary of the external, evil, sinful life. # The History of Isaac, also how Esau and Jacob were born, and what occurred with them, and what is to be understood by it.

->Genesis 25.<-

<margin>M</margin>
Moses says: After the death of Abraham, God blessed his son Isaac, and he lived by the well of the living and seeing <note>This refers to Beer-lahai-roi, the well mentioned in Genesis. In Hebrew, it means "the well of the Living One who sees me."</note>. Human reason understands this externally as a place where Isaac lived, but the Spirit looks at the figure or pattern of the life-form: how human nature and the creature lived by the well-spring of the Divine <term>Being</term> <note>original Latin: "Entis." In Böhme's philosophy, "Ens" refers to the spiritual substance or "soul-stuff" that makes up a being.</note> in the Covenant, which Abraham received in faith. Isaac’s soul lived by the well-spring of the <term>Holy Trinity</term>, in which the soul received its light and saw and recognized the will of God. From this well-spring, the highest love of the Deity revealed itself to the soul, and from this same well-spring later—in the fullness of time—the holy name of Jesus revealed itself out of Jehovah and betrothed itself to the soul as a bride.

2. At this well of the living and seeing, the soul of Isaac lived until that same well-spring later poured itself out and opened itself within the soul in the humanity of Christ. Thus, the soul lived in the well-spring afterward, as it was raised to the right hand of God in Christ’s person. Then the well-spring of God flowed out through the soul, where it received Divine power as a prince of God, or as a formed God, or a shaped Word of the voice of God, through which voice God became audible and revealed.

3. So it is also with our soul: when it leaves the earthly will of its adopted selfhood and grasps the <term>Being of Christ</term> <note>original Latin: "Ens Christi." This refers to the spiritual essence of Christ that a believer takes into themselves.</note> in the Covenant and turns itself to God, it also lives by the well of the living and seeing.

<margin>Chapter 52</margin>...after this time <note>Referring to the transition from temporal life to eternity.</note> as its own property; not the mortal soul, neither from the stars nor from the four elements; but rather the inner soul from the Eternal Word of God, from the Eternal Nature, from the formed Word, from God's essence, according to God's love and wrath, as if from the <term>Center</term> <note>original: "Centro." In Böhme's thought, the "center" is the point of origin or the heart of a being's nature.</note> of Eternal Nature. This inner soul possesses its understanding from the Divine Desire through the Eternal <term>Word Fiat</term> <note>original: "Verbum Fiat." The creative "Let there be" of God.</note>, through which the Divine Delight forms and shapes <term>Wisdom</term> <note>original: "Weissheit." Often personified as Sophia.</note> into a substance for the contemplation of the Godhead; this soul is then wedded to <term>Sophia</term>.

14. The outer soul is, at this time, wedded to the stars and the four elements, in order to form the wonders of God—of the formed Wisdom—into figures, both in words and in works. This outer soul only occasionally attains a glimpse of Sophia, for it contains death and mortality within itself; however, after this time, it shall be transformed back into the first image that God created in Adam. It must leave behind the <term>Serpent's Ens</term> <note>original: "Schlangen Ens." The "Ens" or essential being of the serpent, representing the corruption introduced by the Fall.</note> of the earth, which at the end of days shall be put to the test in the fire of God. There, the desire introduced by the serpent shall smoke away; then the entire image of God, consisting of all three <term>Principles</term> <note>original: "Principiis." Böhme's cosmological system of the three worlds: the dark fire-world, the light-world, and the outer world of nature.</note>, stands as one being, and God then fulfills all in all. This is to be understood by this figure.

Secondly, the spirit of <term>Moses</term> <note>original: "Moysis."</note> describes the children of Ishmael, how he fathered twelve sons, from whom twelve princes arose in their generations; and he adds at the last: *he fell before all his brothers.* <note>A reference to Genesis 25:18.</note> By this, he means in relation to Isaac’s lineage; for although Ishmael grew great in worldly dominion before them and his people became mighty, Isaac and his children and descendants were merely as pilgrims, traveling from one place to another until they were finally redeemed from Egyptian bondage and possessed the promised land.

->The Inner Figure stands thus.<-

16. Ishmael, in his twelve princes, signifies the kingdom of corrupted nature of the human property. This kingdom is twofold: six numbers from the inner life-figure, and six numbers from the earthly outer life-figure—namely, the outer visible, tangible man, and the inner spiritual soul-man. These two have twelve numbers in the figure, from which twelve princes have arisen according to the property of the inner and outer nature. These the spirit of Moses places in the figure and says: *they fell before all their brothers.* This indicates that the twelve <term>regiments</term> <note>original: "Regiment." Used here to mean governing powers or spiritual administrations.</note> of the inner and outer nature of the human property, in their corruption, have fallen before the twelve newborn regiments from the <term>Entity of Faith</term> <note>original: "Glaubens-Ente." The spiritual essence produced by faith.</note> in their corrupted selfhood; for the devil had placed his rule and power into those very properties.

### The History of Isaac / also how Esau and Jacob

17. But when the promised **Seed of Faith** was conceived in Abraham, it pressed the devil's power down into the ground within the dominion of human **selfhood** <note>original: "selbheit." This refers to the human ego or the state of being turned away from God and toward one’s own desires.</note>; thus the spiritual fall occurred in Ishmael’s lineage, in which the devil, as a proud prince, had established himself in the upper dominion—so that Christ might kill the pride of the serpent within humanity.

18. So now Moses says: Ishmael had fallen before all his brothers; this was nothing other than a spiritual fall of human **narrowness** <note>original: "Engenheit." In Böhme’s thought, this refers to the soul’s constriction or being "hemmed in" by earthly, selfish desires rather than being open to God's infinity.</note> before God. For in a physical sense, great and famous people came from them, as their princely dominion testifies; whereas Isaac’s lineage, by contrast, were merely strangers among the nations for a long time. This was to indicate that Christ’s Kingdom and dominion are not of this world’s nature, and yet the kingdoms of this world must fall before Christ and be subject to Him.

19. Afterward, the Spirit of Moses describes Isaac’s children by Rebecca, and says that she was barren; and Isaac prayed to the Lord for his wife, and God allowed Himself to be moved by the prayer. Thus Rebecca became pregnant with two sons, who jostled one another in the mother’s womb. Here the figure of the **Kingdom of Nature** and the **Kingdom of Christ** in the **new birth** <note>original: "newen Geburt." The spiritual transformation of the soul through Christ.</note> is clearly presented: how Rebecca became pregnant with two sons, Esau and Jacob, representing two lineages. Esau came from Abraham’s own Adamic, corrupted nature, and Jacob from the **Seed of Faith**, into which Abraham’s **Faith-Essence** <term>Glaubens-Ens</term> <note>The "Ens" or essential spiritual being that carries the promise of God.</note> was embodied within his Adamic nature; in this lineage stood the covenant and the line of Christ, who was to crush the head of the serpent in the Adamic nature.

20. And here it is portrayed how the two kingdoms in the two brothers—namely, the devil’s kingdom in the corrupted nature of Esau (within Adam’s own nature of the introduced **Serpent's Essence** <term>Schlangen Entis</term>) and the Kingdom of Christ in Jacob (within the **Faith-Essence**) — struggled with each other in the mother's womb. In this struggle, the Kingdom of Nature in Esau began to fall before the Kingdom of Christ in Jacob; for here, the **Seed of the Woman** <note>A reference to the prophecy in Genesis 3:15.</note> already stepped upon the head of the power of the serpent's essence in Esau, and the serpent already stung the Seed of the Woman (the Faith-Essence in Jacob) in the heel; therefore they jostled with each other in the mother's womb.

21. We also have a powerful figure here in Rebecca: that she was locked <note>original: "verschlossen," meaning closed or barren.</note> and could not be opened to be conceived by Isaac’s seed, until Isaac prayed to the Lord to open the lock in the covenant within Rebecca. There, the Lord allowed Himself to be moved within the covenant in the "lock" of Rebecca, so that He opened the **Tincture** <term>Tinctur</term> <note>In Böhme’s alchemy-influenced theology, the "Tincture" is the vital, spiritual life-force that allows for transformation and creation.</note> in the woman’s seed for this pregnancy.

->The Inner Figure stands thus:<-

22. In Isaac, the **Seed of Faith** was inherited from his father Abraham; Rebecca, however, did not possess this <term>essence</term> <note>original: "Ens." A term used by Böhme to describe a spiritual substance or "being-ness" that takes root in the soul.</note>. Although she stood within the Covenant, the **essence of faith** was not within her own substance, but only within the Covenant itself; therefore her **womb** <note>original: "Matrix." In Böhme’s thought, this refers to both the biological womb and the spiritual "mother-source" from which all things are formed.</note> was closed and not capable of receiving the essence of faith. This continued until Isaac "baptized" his **desire of faith** into the Lord—understand this as being into the center of nature within Rebecca—so that the Spirit of the Lord within the Covenant moved in Rebecca. This moved both the Covenant and her **Adamic nature**, and thus the **lock** was opened in her womb—both in the enclosed essence within the Covenant and also in her Adamic womb. Thus, she became pregnant with the characteristics of two sons, representing two kingdoms.

23. And that is what is meant by "the Lord allowed himself to be entreated," when Isaac introduced his desire of faith through both Eternal and Temporal Nature into the Lord, and with it penetrated into his wife Rebecca. Through his prayer and desire of faith, the Lord wished to open her so that she would conceive by him. This desire of faith, together with the desire of the **Adamic nature**, entered into the **lock of the womb** in Rebecca and opened it; because of this, she became pregnant with two natural characteristics from a twofold seed from Isaac.

24. This is not to be understood as if Jacob were conceived entirely out of the **essence of faith**; rather, he was also from the Adamic, sinful nature. However, the **Kingdom of Grace** within the Covenant presented its figure in the **essence of faith** within him. And in Esau, the **Kingdom of Nature**—as the truly-corrupted Adamic nature—presented its own figure. This was not as a separation or a rejection <note>Böhme argues here against strict predestination, suggesting Esau's nature wasn't "thrown away" by God but served a specific symbolic purpose in the process of salvation.</note>, but to indicate that Christ should be conceived and born in the corrupted Adamic nature with his holy, Divine <term>essence</term>. He came to break the power of death and the **lock of sin**, along with the resulting desire of human **selfhood** and ego, and to kill it with the desire of love in the Divine essence. He came to destroy the **stronghold of robbery** <note>original: "Raubschloſs." A metaphor for the devil's occupation of the human soul.</note> that the devil had made within it, and to transform the **wrath** of God—according to the Eternal Nature in the center of the dark, fiery world-property—into Divine love and joy, and to <term>tincture</term> <note>original: "tingiren." To "tincture" is an alchemical term meaning to transform or permeate a base substance with a higher, spiritual quality.</note> the Adamic nature with the holy tincture of the fire of love.

25. Therefore, the corrupted Adamic nature was represented in its image in Esau alongside the image of Christ in Jacob within the mother’s womb; they had to be formed from one seed to indicate that Christ should enter into our corrupted nature and redeem our truly-Adamic corrupted nature from its decay, leading it into His own holy nature.

26. Also, God represented in Esau the image of His wrath and the power of the Devil, which had possessed the Kingdom of Nature within humanity. This represents how it would fight against the **Essence of Faith** <note>original: "Glaubens-Ens." A term used by Böhme to describe a spiritual substance or "being-ness" of faith that takes root in the soul.</note> and the Kingdom of Grace—which was intended to take away its power—and how it would wage great enmity against it.

27. **Reason** <note>Böhme often personifies "Reason" (Vernunfft) as the limited, logical human mind that cannot grasp spiritual mysteries without divine illumination.</note> says: "Why does God allow the Devil to fight against His Kingdom of Grace?" Listen, you ignorant, blind **Reason**; learn the A-B-C in the <term>Center</term> <note>original: "Centro." In Böhme's philosophy, the "Center" refers to the underlying source or core of reality where opposing forces meet to manifest existence.</note>, how God's Love and the Kingdom of Grace and Mercy would not, and could not, be revealed without struggle and opposition. If you understand this, you will have no more questions here; go to the beginning in the **Center** of this book, and there you will find the foundation.

28. And as the struggle between the two kingdoms began in these two children within their mother's womb—so that they kicked one another—Rebecca became distressed by it and said: "If it were to go this way for me, why have I become pregnant?" And she went to ask the Lord; and the Lord said to her: "Two nations are in your womb, and two kinds of people shall be separated from your body; and one people shall be superior to the other, and the elder shall serve the younger."

29. These two nations, conceived from one seed in Rebecca, represent on one hand the human of the Adamic self-nature in <term>selfhood</term> <note>original: "selbheit." This refers to the ego or the state of being turned away from God and toward one's own will.</note>, as the human's origin; and on the other hand, the newborn spiritual human from the Kingdom of Grace within the Covenant. These came from one seed—one from the Adamic nature alone, and he was the "greater" or elder, like the first man whom God created in His image, which was corrupted and died to God; the other also came from that same Adamic nature, but the Kingdom of Grace within the **Essence of Faith** gave itself into it as a conqueror. This second one was the "smaller" according to Adamic nature, but God was revealed within him. Thus, the greater—representing the first Adamic man in Esau's lineage—was to serve and be subject to this smaller one, who was the smallest according to human characteristics but the greatest in God.

30. And since we do not actually see that Esau became subject to Jacob, it is instead the **Spiritual Figure** of how the Kingdom of Nature within humanity, among the children of God, should be broken and become subject to the Kingdom of Grace as **Divine Humility**. It must sink itself entirely into Divine Humility and be **born anew** out of that humility. Thus the Spirit of God presents Rebecca with such an answer: that it will be a "struggling kingdom," where indeed the first corrupted man—the elder in nature—will be against the smaller—the Spirit of Christ in his lowliness...

How Esau Despised His Birthright

## The 53rd Chapter.

### How Esau despised his birthright and sold it for a dish of lentils; what is to be understood by this.

<margin>Genesis 25</margin>

When the Spirit of Moses described the birth of Esau and Jacob, he immediately proceeds and shows how the natural Adamic man will value this high gift of the Covenant little or not at all, and only strive for the belly-filling of earthly life, like Esau, who gave his birthright for a dish of lentils that served his belly.

->The symbolic model <note>original: "Figur." Böhme uses this term to mean a divinely intended type or representation of a greater spiritual truth.</note> of Moses stands thus:<-

2. And Jacob cooked a dish: Then Esau came from the field and was tired, and spoke to Jacob: "Let me taste the red dish, for I am tired"; and therefore he is called Edom. But Jacob said: "Sell me today your birthright." Esau answered: "Behold, I must die anyway; what good is the birthright to me then?" Jacob said: "So swear to me today," and he swore to him, and so Esau sold Jacob his birthright. Then Jacob gave him bread and the dish of lentils, and he ate and drank and stood up and went away. Thus Esau despised his birthright. This symbolic model looks childish on the outside, and yet it is a model of the greatest mysteries: For **Esau signifies the first power of the natural, created Adam, and Jacob signifies the power of the other Adam, Christ; thus the Spirit** plays here with the symbolic model.

3. For Adam’s nature came from the field and was tired, and lusted after the dish that Jacob had; Adam was a <term>Limus</term> <note>Latin: "slime" or "mud." Böhme uses this to refer to the "extraction" or "essential matter" from which man was formed.</note> of the earth, and a <term>Limus</term> of heaven: But as he had died to the <term>Limus</term> of heaven, the earthly nature had made him tired in its struggle, in which symbolic model Esau stood here.

4. The red dish of lentils that Jacob had, for which the tired Adam in Esau lusted, was the faith-<term>Ens</term> <note>A spiritual essence or "beingness." Böhme uses this term to describe the divine substance that exists within the soul.</note>, as the <term>Ens</term> of Christ: The Adamic nature in Esau, in its anguish and toil within its corruption, lusted after this dish that was in Jacob: But the earthly nature of Esau did not understand this, but rather the soul-nature, which also stood in the desire for Christ’s <term>Ens</term>, which was foreign to Reason <note>Böhme uses "Reason" (Vernunfft) to denote the limited human intellect that cannot grasp spiritual mysteries without divine illumination.</note>.

Esau represents the exhausted, earthly man who values immediate physical satisfaction over his eternal, spiritual inheritance.</summary>

5. Esau’s soulful nature spoke in its lust to Jacob: "let me taste the red dish, for I am tired from the driver of the anxious birth" <note>This "anxious birth" refers to the constant, restless striving of the natural world and the human ego.</note>; and because of this lust he is called Edom. In the compaction of the Word—that is, in the formation of the sensual tongues—this name signifies the immersion of the imprisoned angelic quality into this dish. This occurred when the soulful lust (in which the angelic character still stood, though imprisoned) immersed itself with desire into the Holy <term>Ens</term> <note>original Latin: "Ens." A technical term in Böhme’s philosophy referring to the essential, spiritual substance or "being" of a thing.</note>. It wished to seize the Holy *Ens* within the divine judgment <note>original: "Gerichte." Böhme plays on the double meaning of the German word *Gericht*, which means both a "dish of food" and "judgment."</note> as a heavenly essence to be used for the pleasure of selfhood. This is why the symbolic model is called "Edom" in the high tongues.

6. For the desire of Esau’s soul spoke to the divine *Ens* in Jacob: "Give me your flavor into the essence of my creaturely selfhood." But Jacob—that is, the Spirit of Christ in the *Ens* of faith—spoke: "Sell me your birthright for the dish." This means: "give me the form of your soul-life, as the center of the soulful nature, in exchange. If your birthright, as the soulful center, becomes my own, then I will give you the *Ens* of God."

7. For Esau had inherited the first soulful power from his father and held the soulful center by natural right. Following this, the *Ens* of Christ came as a divine gift without a soulful center of its own, for the Holy *Ens* was meant to take the soulful center from the Adamic nature. Thus, here the Adamic soulful nature wooed the *Ens* of Christ, and the Spirit in Christ's *Ens* wooed the soulful nature. The Spirit of Christ in Jacob did not want to give the flavor of the divine *Ens* to the soulful nature in Esau unless she first gave her fiery center <note>The "fiery center" refers to the raw, consuming energy of the soul before it is lightened by divine love.</note>—the very beginning of the soulful creature—as a possession. That is to say, she must surrender herself entirely, in her natural selfhood, into God’s will, leave the first birth of the creature behind, and regard herself in her selfhood as if dead; she must hand over the government and will of life to the Spirit of Christ in this heavenly dish.

8. But because Reason in Esau did not understand this, he spoke to Jacob: "Behold, I must die anyway; what good is the birthright to me then?" Thus Reason went its easy way and did not know what the poor soul lacked. But the Spirit of Moses played here with the inner symbolic model and secretly hinted at what the external events signified.

9. And Jacob spoke: "Swear to me today." This means that the life of Adam in Esau should freely surrender itself out of the fiery power and yield entirely to the divine *Ens*, leaving the fiery right of self-ownership. It should do this "today," meaning from now into eternity. In God, this is called "swearing"—to sell oneself entirely and surrender into divine power, no longer resisting, to avoid divine expulsion.

### How Esau Despised His Birthright

10. And he swore to him; and here, as he swore, he was named Edom <note>The name Edom is traditionally associated with "red."</note>. And here the Spirit of the World <note>original Latin: *Spiritus Mundi*.</note> plays out the symbolic figure: how the soulful quality in the fire’s essence—and Christ’s incarnation in the covenant of Divine Light and Love-Being—must completely surrender and eternally immerse itself in the Divine Delight. It shows how the Being of Light would take upon itself the corrupted, fiery soul-nature and satisfy its craving, and also how the soul would hand over its natural right in exchange for this "red dish" <note>Böhme plays on the German word *Gericht*, which means both a "dish of food" and "judgment." 11. For this is exactly the figure of how God the Father gives His nature (as the soul) entirely to His Son Christ within the Being of Love as His own possession, where the fiery right becomes subject to Love in the Light. It happens exactly like this in our own **new birth**: the soul also hungers for this "dish" <note>the spiritual judgment/nourishment</note>; but if the soul wishes to taste this, it must surrender its first birth. To do this, it must "swear" today—that is, in eternity—to God to abandon its natural right. Earthly reason looks upon this mockingly; when the children of earthly desire see a person give up honor, goods, or even their physical life for the sake of this spiritual "dish," they call him a fool, just as Esau is viewed here.

12. In this figure there is a twofold understanding: internally, it is the figure of Christ and Adam (as mentioned above); externally, it is the figure of the earthly man, how he so easily passes away and sells or hands over the heavenly for the sake of a full belly and the will of his desires. The poor soul certainly hungers in its essence for this "red dish" <note>the divine essence</note>, but earthly reason only desires a dish of lentils for the craving belly—as is to be understood in the case of Esau.

13. Esau’s soul hungered for Jacob’s heavenly <term>Ens</term> <note>Being/Substance</note>, but the earthly Esau, following the outer soul, only intended earthly power. The kingdom of nature in him had become so hardened and earthly that he neither understood nor respected the eternal, but said: "What good is the birthright to me, since I must die anyway?" He sat himself down, ate and drank earthly food instead of the heavenly.

14. And Moses says: When he had eaten and drunk, he went his way. That is: he filled his belly with the dish of lentils, sold the "Natural Right" to Jacob, and walked away from the **Divine Calling** as an earthly man.

### The Inner Divine Figure is as follows.

15. Abraham received the Divine <term>Being</term> <note>original: *Ens*, a Latin term Böhme uses to describe a spiritual substance or the "stuff" of a being.</note> in his desire of faith <margin>f</margin>, and that was the stem and the root of Israel. But he himself was not yet Israel; for the kingdom of corrupted nature and the kingdom of grace—as the received <term>Being</term> of faith—were not yet one within him. This is just like when a grain of seed is sown in the earth: the seed does not yet have a root upon which the stalk and fruit should grow. However, the power of the seed draws the essence of the earth into itself, and from these two—the seed and the earth's power—grow the root, the stalk, and eventually the manifold fruit at the top.

16. It is also to be understood in this way: the Divine holy <term>Being</term> is not of nature; the soul, however, is of nature. If the Divine <term>Being</term> is to be revealed, it must happen through a natural being, wherein the invisible enters into a visible being.

17. The Divine <term>Being</term> of faith, which Abraham received, was of an invisible spiritual quality. It desired to introduce itself through human nature into a visible, substantial, creaturely, and natural being for an active life, where the natural <term>Being</term> of the holy light and the <term>Being</term> of the soul's fiery nature would work together in one essence and bear fruit. For the Adamic nature <note>The state of humanity before the Fall, which Böhme believes lost its divine inner substance.</note> had departed from the holy <term>Being</term>, which had faded within it; and here was once again the ground of reunion. It is just as it is with the seed in the field, where the power in the seed mingles with the earth's essence and then leaves its own isolation, as the earth's essence and the seed's essence are transformed into a single <term>Being</term>; this is how it is to be understood here.

18. Abraham received the Divine <term>Being</term> of faith, in which his justification stood, but his life-nature had not yet seized it as its own power. For the Divine Being does not give itself over to the self-will of nature; it certainly gives itself into the essence of nature, but the Divine Desire does not unite with nature in nature's own will, so that nature would have the upper hand. We have an illustration of this in the seed that is sown.

19. Earthly nature cannot, by its own power, create another seed. Even though it draws the seed's essence into itself, it only gives birth to a stalk, in which stalk the seed's essence turns green and leads itself <margin>out.</margin> into a blossom and back into a seed. In this process, the earthly nature with its own essence must only be a servant.

### Regarding the 27th Chapter of Genesis. Explaining how Isaac unknowingly blessed Jacob in Esau’s place when he was old and about to die, and what is to be understood by this.

->The Gates of the Great Mystery of the Entire Bible.<-

When <term>Reason</term> <note>The author often uses "Reason" (Vernunfft) to describe the limited, purely intellectual understanding of a person not enlightened by the Spirit.</note> reads this history of the 27th chapter of Genesis, it holds two kinds of thoughts about it. One is as if Rebecca loved Jacob more than Esau, and therefore brought him to the point of receiving his father’s blessing through trickery. Secondly, it thinks that it was surely an act of God’s providence because Esau was not worthy of the blessing, and it wishes to condemn Esau entirely; upon this, Reason has established the doctrine of <term>predestination</term> <note>original: "Prædestination"; the theological concept that God has pre-determined who will be saved and who will be damned.</note>, yet it understands nothing at all of this wonderful <term>figure</term> <note>A "figure" is a prophetic type—a person or event in the Old Testament that foreshadows a spiritual reality in the New Testament.</note>.

2. If we now wish to correctly understand and interpret this figure, we must place the <term>Patriarch</term> Isaac in the position of God the Father in this figure, for He alone can bless; He also blessed Isaac in the <term>seed of Abraham</term>, so that Isaac should in turn bless his own seed within the <term>Line of the Covenant</term>.

3. And we place Esau in the position of the <term>corrupted Adam</term>, representing the realm of corrupted nature in the human <term>property</term> <note>In this context, "property" (Eigenschaft) refers to the inherent spiritual qualities or characteristics of a person.</note> seized within the wrath of God.

4. And we place Jacob in the <term>new rebirth</term> within the humanity of Christ, whom God the Father blessed in the place of the corrupted Adam, when He brought forth a new rebirth out of our humanity in this Line.

5. And here we see how Adam forfeited and lost the blessing and divine <term>anointing</term>, and how he is rejected by God in the earthly image; how he lost his right to the divine anointing, just as here Esau lost his <term>birthright</term> and also the blessing.

->The inner spiritual figure stands thus:<-

6. Isaac was old and awaited death; and he called his firstborn son Esau, that he might bless him with the blessing of Abraham, and told him to catch and prepare <term>venison</term> <note>original: "Wildbradt"; here representing the fruits of natural human effort.</note> as he liked to eat it, so that his soul might be refreshed and the blessing of the Lord might be stirred within him, that he might bless Esau. And Esau went out to do as his father desired so that he might bless him; which is to say, in the inner understanding of the figure:

Hence also *Isaac* blessed *Esau* with the word of strife, when he said to him in the blessing: You will live by your sword, and tear the burden of your brother from your neck; this was to indicate that the corrupted nature in him is now a servant of God’s wrath, and would lead and be a servant of the strife which *Adam* had awakened in the properties of life.

The Divine cunning killed the Devil’s cunning.

20. Understand this correctly: Every instance of "cunning" arises from <term>Lust</term> <note>original: "Lust"; here meaning a deep, formative desire or delight.</note>. The Devil’s cunning arose from a false desire. Therefore, God’s "delight" came back into the woman’s seed—into that <term>heavenly Matrix</term> <note>original: "Himmlische Matricem"; the spiritual "womb" or creative essence from which life is birthed.</note> into which the Devil had cast his own desire— and it broke the Devil’s desire.

21. It was from God that *Jacob* received the blessing, entirely against the thinking and willing of human Reason. For he stood as a figure of *Christ*, while *Esau* stood as a figure of the corrupted *Adam*.

22. For this reason, *Esau* was entirely hairy on his skin; this signifies the monstrous, animalistic property which *Adam* had awakened through his "Lust" during the Fall. When *Adam’s* desire introduced itself into a physical being, the flesh became coarse and animal-like. Thus, the "animal" swallowed the "heavenly" within itself, and death became manifest in the flesh. We see here in this figure a clear image of how things were to go.

23. *Isaac* wished to bless the animalistic man in *Esau*, but God did not want that. Instead, the Divine blessing belonged to *Christ*. <margin>// // //</margin> Therefore, the corrupted *Adam* could not become capable of receiving God’s blessing unless *Christ* took on this "hairy animal skin" which *Adam* had pulled over himself—just as here *Jacob* could not be blessed unless he also stood in a hairy, animal-like skin.

29. For just as Jacob was smooth and pure beneath this animal skin, so also must we be smooth and pure in our inner ground beneath the animal skin, if we wish for God’s blessing to rest upon us. ### How Isaac unknowingly blessed Jacob in Esau's place.

35. Furthermore, we see in this <term>figure</term> <note>original: "Bilde"; in Böhme's writing, a historical event that serves as a symbolic blueprint for spiritual truths</note> what happens to the children of God. For when Isaac had blessed Jacob, Esau came with his venison, at which Isaac his father was terrified and said: "What? Who are you?" and he was struck with fear because he had blessed Jacob unknowingly. This is a figure of how the <term>Adamic man</term> <note>Falled humanity, governed by earthly desires and logic rather than divine spirit</note> understands nothing of God’s ways; how God often leads him so wonderfully according to the inner ground that, although he is being led upon God’s path, he nonetheless looks more toward outer <term>Reason</term> <note>original: "Vernunfft"; the human intellect which, according to Böhme, is blind to spiritual realities unless enlightened by God</note>. He often stumbles over the external, rational things of temporal orders and goods, and allows fear to enter him, wanting only for the will of his Reason to be done—just as Isaac here was terrified because the will of his Reason had been broken.

36. And herein we recognize the misery and the ignorance of the children of God: how Reason enters into its own governance and will not leave itself entirely to God, and is terrified when things go differently than it had imagined.

37. And then we see how God finally breaks through with his light in the understanding and shows man his path, so that he is satisfied—just as Isaac did here when he said: "This Jacob is blessed; he shall indeed remain blessed." For he now understood God’s will.

38. Furthermore, we see in this history how Esau wept so lamentably before his father for the blessing, and said to his father: "Bless me also, my father! Have you then only one blessing? This signifies the **Kingdom of Christ**, how God has made it Lord over the **Kingdom of Nature**, just as Christ said: <note>Matthew 28:18</note> "All power in heaven and on earth has been given to me by my Father."

39. It further signifies how the corrupted Adamic nature in Esau and in all men cannot become a partaker of this blessing unless they first die to their own rights and will. Just as Esau could not be blessed with the holy blessing by his father—for he was the figure of the corrupted Adam according to the Kingdom of Nature—so also the earthly nature cannot become capable of the Holy Spirit in its own essence. Concerning this, Christ said (John 6): <note>While the text cites John 6, this is a common paraphrase of 1 Corinthians 15:50</note> "Flesh and blood shall not inherit God’s kingdom," unless it falls into the earth and enters again into its first mother’s womb like a grain of wheat, and surrenders its nature to the first mother.

### How Isaac unknowingly blessed Jacob in Esau's place.

<margin>Chapter 55.</margin>

40. And then we see here how Isaac gives his son Esau a temporal blessing, and only indicates to him how the natural man is led by the spirit of this world, as by the <term>Spirit of the world</term> <note>original Latin: "Spiritu mundi"; in Böhme's thought, this is the soul of the physical universe that governs natural life but lacks divine eternal light</note>. For to Jacob he said: "God give you of the dew of heaven and of the fatness of the earth, and plenty of corn and wine." But to Esau he said only: "Behold, you shall have a fat dwelling on earth, and from the dew of heaven from above; by your sword you shall nourish yourself, and serve your brother; and it shall happen that you will also be a lord and tear his yoke from your neck."

41. And he indicates by this what kind of <term>governance</term> <note>original: "Regiment"; refers to the ruling principle or spiritual administration of a person's life</note> the outer natural man is led, driven, and nourished by, and what his desire and doing are: namely, that in his mind he is only a robber, murderer, and evil beast, who desires only to draw everything to himself with violence and murder.

42. For Isaac did not say: "You *shall* nourish yourself by the sword," but "you *will* do it," as God’s wrath in the realm of corrupted nature, by the devil’s will, will move you to draw the fatness of the earth to yourself. You will be ruled and driven from above by the <term>stars</term> <note>original: "Gestirne"; the astral influences that Böhme believed governed the physical and emotional impulses of the "natural" or "unregenerate" person</note>, and in natural strength you will drive away from you the children of God who rule in God’s power. That is, you will drive the yoke from your neck when the Holy Spirit rebukes the children of God because of their tyranny; then they murder and kill them and tear the Holy Spirit’s sword from their neck, as Isaac says here: "You will do it."

43. Just as Esau did immediately afterward, wanting to kill Jacob so that Jacob had to flee from him while carrying God’s blessing. There, he had torn the Holy Spirit’s burden from his neck. This indication or prophecy of the patriarch Isaac is a <term>figure</term> <note>a symbolic pattern or archetype</note> of how the "Esauites" and tyrants, as fleshly brothers of the Christians, would dwell among the Christians. They are born of the same parents in a brotherly way—like Esau and Jacob—and yet they would only pursue them with the sword and plagues and push them away. They would still stand there as Christians and desire the blessing of God, just as Esau stood and wept for the blessing; and yet it was not the Kingdom of God they were after, but that they might be a lord on earth over their brothers and other people, and might have wealth and a full belly.

44. This Esau in his blessing is a true figure of the **Antichrist**, who approaches God with his lips and enters into an outward appearance of Christ's service—as if he were doing it for God—and stands and boasts with <term>hypocrisy</term> <note>original: "Gleißnerey"; literally "shining," referring to a false, outward spiritual luster that hides a dark interior</note>, acting devout so that he may be honored by men.

45. Reason thinks that because Isaac said to Esau: "By your sword you shall nourish yourself," that God had commanded it to him, and so Reason stands firm upon that. But it is otherwise: God wants no war, but the <term>Kingdom of Nature</term> <note>In Böhme’s philosophy, this is the physical, worldly realm driven by self-interest and survival, as opposed to the Kingdom of Grace.</note> in <term>God's Wrath</term> <note>The "fire-principle" or the harsh, judging aspect of God that exists when separated from His light and love.</note> wants it. 46. This is to indicate how the true children of Christ would be hated, persecuted, and killed by the children in the Kingdom of Nature because of this blessing. And the cause is this: that the Kingdom of Grace shall rule over the Kingdom of Nature, and shall break it at the end of days and transform it into its own power; and therefore there is a struggle between both kingdoms.

48. Therefore the children of this world are bitter toward them and persecute them, just as Esau did his brother Jacob.

49. For wherever the Kingdom of Christ begins to flourish, there the kingdom of the devil immediately begins to rage. This is because the Kingdom of Christ intends to and shall take away and break his power and princely throne. Hence there is a struggle in this world between the children of Jacob and the children of Esau.

50. For as soon as Jacob received the blessing, Esau already intended in his mind to murder Jacob. This is a <term>figure</term> <note>A symbolic representation or "type" in biblical interpretation where an Old Testament event foreshadows a New Testament reality.</note> of Christ, because God's wrath was to murder Him in this blessing within our assumed humanity according to the Kingdom of Nature; and it shows how the children of Christ would be murdered in God's wrath according to this natural kingdom, and shed their blood in this murderous spirit, so that God's wrath might thereby be extinguished and transformed into love.

->On the 28th Chapter of Genesis<-

**A**s Jacob had received the blessing, he had to wander away from his father's house, from father and mother, and flee from the <term>wrath</term> <note>original: "Grimm"; in Böhme's writing, this refers to the harsh, fiery quality of the material world or "fallen nature" that opposes spiritual life.</note> of Esau. This is now a figure of Christ: how he, after he had taken on our humanity and been anointed, would flee with our humanity out of his father's <term>Adamic house</term> <note>The state of fallen human nature inherited from Adam.</note> back into the first <term>Paradisical house</term>.

2. And it further indicates how the children of Christ, immediately after their anointing and blessing—wherein the <term>new birth</term> <note>The spiritual transformation where a person is "born again" into the light of Christ.</note> begins in them through Christ's blessing—shall and must flee with their senses and minds out of their father's Adamic house of corrupt nature. As soon as the devil and the world become hateful toward them, they must immediately set out upon Christ's <term>pilgrim path</term> and live in misery and constraint under the world's servile yoke. For God leads them immediately with their senses and minds out of the house of their father—that is, out of the desire in flesh and blood—so that they disregard the world's pleasure and flee from it, just as Jacob fled from his father's house.

3. And then we see how God leads his children so wondrously and shields them from their enemies, so that the devil may not murder them in <term>God's wrath</term> <note>The "fire-principle" or the judging, harsh aspect of existence that consumes the soul if it is not tempered by God's love.</note> unless it be God's will; just as he protected Jacob from the wrath of Esau and led him away. And we have a beautiful example in Jacob, how he left his father's house, as well as father and mother, for the sake of this blessing, and loved God more than all temporal goods, gladly leaving everything to Esau so that he might only be the "Blessed of God."

4. And how immediately—after he had left the riches of this world in his father's house—the Lord appeared to him with eternal goods and showed him the ladder upon which he could climb into God's eternal kingdom. This ladder was none other than Christ, whom he had put on in the <term>Line of the Covenant</term> <note>original: "Bunds-Linea"; Böhme's term for the spiritual lineage of the promise, tracing from Adam through the Patriarchs to the physical birth of Christ.</note>; thus an image was presented to him there of what kind of person Christ would be.

5. For this ladder reached—according to his perception—from the earth, with its highest tip even into heaven, upon which the angels of God ascended and descended. This signifies how the **eternal Word**, together with the power of heaven (as with the <term>Angelic Divine World-Being</term> <note>original: "Englischen Göttlichen Welt-Wesen"; Böhme uses "angelic" to describe the pure, light-filled substance of the heavenly realm, distinct from our heavy, earthly matter.</note>), would sink itself into our being—which has turned away from God and is blind toward God—and take on our humanity. Thus, it would unite heaven with the world within man, so that through this entry of the <term>Godhead</term> into humanity, mankind might have a ladder to God.

6. And just as people would come into the <term>company of angels</term> through Christ’s humanity (Matthew 13:22 <note>This citation likely refers to the spiritual state of the soul; while Matthew 13:22 discusses the world's cares, Böhme may be connecting the "good soil" to the heavenly kingdom, or referencing the general promise of angelic association found in Hebrews 12:22.</note>), this clearly signifies that the angels of God ascend and descend upon this ladder. This means that heaven would be opened again within man through this entry of the Divine Being into humanity, and that the children of God would have the angels as companions in this world—which God showed to Jacob by the angels of God ascending and descending to him upon this ladder.

<margin><image-desc>A vertical decorative mark consisting of three small fleur-de-lis symbols connected by thin lines, used as a section break.</image-desc></margin>

7. This shall be a great comfort to the children of God who turn away from their father’s house (meaning the vanity of this world) toward this ladder of Jacob. They shall know for certain that God’s angels come to them and gladly remain around them upon this ladder to which they have turned.

8. For this ladder actually signifies the **pilgrim path** of Christ through this world into the Kingdom of God. Because the kingdom of the <term>corrupt Adamic nature</term> <note>The fallen state of man inherited from Adam, characterized by selfish desire and distance from God.</note> still clings to the children of God for a time, holding them back in flesh and blood within the spirit of this world, they must—according to the <term>inner man</term>—unceasingly climb this ladder in the Spirit of Christ through much cross and tribulation, following after Christ under his cross and <term>blood-banner</term> <note>original: "Blutfahne"; a frequent image in Böhme's work representing Christ's suffering and his victory over death, which the believer must follow as a soldier follows a standard.</note>.

9. In contrast, "the world" lives in luxury and lust in the house of their father Adam, in mockery and resentment. Anything they can do to oppose these children of Jacob is a joy to them, and they only mock them. We have an example of this in Esau: how he, out of defiance and to the resentment of his father and mother, took Ishmaelite wives from the <term>lineage of mockery</term>, both of whom caused Isaac and Rebecca nothing but pure heartache.

10. There one sees clearly how the Devil holds his power in the kingdom of this world, in the corrupt human <term>property</term> <note>original: "Eigenschafft"; refers to the inherent qualities or "drives" of the soul. In the fallen state, these properties are out of balance and ruled by self-will.</note>, and unceasingly resists, distresses, and plagues God’s children. He fights with them over his kingdom, which he has lost, and begrudges them their progress.

28. This enclosed spiritual image—which was the seed of faith that Abraham grasped in faith—passed to Isaac and from Isaac to Jacob. 29. Within this incorporated ground, the goal of God’s covenant remained in a spiritual form until Mary, and was propagated from person to person—from Adam and Eve until Mary. There, the Word of Divine Power moved and essentially took on our human flesh and blood, together with the soul, and made the faded "Heavenly <term>Ens</term> Seed" <note>Latin: 'Ens' means 'being' or 'essence'. This revelation also penetrated Mary's heavenly essence so that her "Heavenly Virginity"—which had faded in Eve—became alive. 30. She is the first in whom what was locked away became revealed; for in her, the goal of the covenant reached its end in the spiritual image, and in her, it was fulfilled in our humanity.

31. But she is truly the daughter of Adam, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—both according to humanity and according to the covenant of the divine figure. When, in her conception, the inner incorporated image of the "spoken" <term>Covenant of Grace</term> (grasped in faith) took on our human property, the Kingdom of Christ became manifest in the flesh.

32. Thereafter, the faithful "clothed" themselves with Christ in their faith and in the flesh—but only according to that same heavenly "Word" <note>original: 'Werde' or 'Wort'. Böhme refers to the 'becoming' or the 'spoken word' of the divine essence.</note> that had faded in Adam. 9. For the **Humanity of Christ** does not immediately give itself to the **fiery soul** <note>original: "fewrischen Seelen." The wedding joy passes, and the soul feels as if the love of this bride has been taken away.

11. In the meantime, Leah breaks forth under the **Cross of Christ** and brings fruit. This is to say: when the soul receives the Spirit of Christ, the great joy of this marriage begins, of which Christ said: *There will be joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, more than over ninety-nine righteous people who do not need this repentance.* <note>A reference to Luke 15:7.</note>

12. For that is the **Wedding of the Lamb**: when God and man are wed and Christ is born. 20. 21. This indicates that he had sprouted from the line of zeal <note>original: *Eyffer*; meaning a heated, jealous, or wrathful passion</note>. Leah was zealous because she was held in such low esteem, as she then said: "The Lord has heard that I am so unvalued, and has given me this one also."

23. But as she cried out to the Lord in her zeal for deliverance from contempt, she became pregnant and gave birth to **Levi**, as the root of the **Levitical Priesthood** <note>The priesthood of the Old Covenant, which Böhme views as a necessary but "external" precursor to the internal Kingdom of Christ</note>, a type of the Kingdom of Christ. Then she cried out to God that her husband might again join himself to her in love, as she then said: "Now my husband will again be joined to me." This indicates that God, through the Levitical priesthood, would again join Himself to humanity in a symbolic image <note>original: *Fürbilde*; a prefiguration or type</note>, and would dwell among them again in a type of the Kingdom of Paradise, as happened with Moses.

24. But the Spirit of God said through Jacob when he was about to die: "My honor shall not be in their church." That is, they are of a murderous, Cain-like disposition, and serve me only as a figure for the future Kingdom of Christ. But the Spirit of my love and grace is not with them in their sacrifices and divine services—which love and grace he called his "honor," and which he intended to reveal through the **Line of Judah** in Christ.

31. For Christ is the reward of the children of God. Just as they must serve their masters for a worldly <gloss>reward</gloss>, so God first rewards them with His Covenant of Grace; afterwards, they also receive the temporal reward. Just as Jacob first had to accept the gift of God as God arranged it for him—even though it was very difficult for his **Reason** <note>original: "Vernunfft"; Böhme often uses this to describe earthly, human logic that struggles to understand divine mysteries</note> to accept—he afterwards also received the reward according to his own will, for which he had to serve another seven years.

32. These seven years, in their inner ground, represent in this **figure** <note>original: "Figur"; a symbolic representation or "type" of a spiritual truth</note> the **seven properties of natural life** <note>a central concept in Böhme’s philosophy, where nature is composed of seven foundational qualities or "source-spirits"</note>, which must submit themselves to the service of God. There, the seven forms of life first help the Lord to give birth to a spiritual figure and image, and to reveal the **Line of Christ**. Afterwards, that same spiritual form also opens the natural form and gives birth to a "prince" into the natural life, in whom God works and through whom He rules the world—as can be seen in the case of Jacob.

33. He served seven years for Rachel; but because he feared God, the divine reward—the **Line of Christ**—was given to him first. Afterward, God also blessed his own human love according to the **Kingdom of Nature** <note>original: "Reiche der Natur"</note> within him, so that with Rachel (whom he had embraced in natural self-love) he fathered a prince and a wise man: namely Joseph, through whom the Spirit of God judged and whom He made into a lord.

34. ## The 58th Chapter.

### How Jacob served Laban, his father-in-law, for 20 years and fathered 12 sons and one daughter; and how God blessed him so that he obtained great wealth; and how Laban frequently changed his wages, yet could not harm him; and what is to be understood by this.

->Genesis 30<-

In this history, we see primarily how it goes for the children of God in this world—how they must live in pure suffering and adversity. We see this with Jacob and his wives: For when Rachel saw that she was barren, she envied Leah her sister. This indicates that man’s **self-love** <note>original: "eigene Liebe"; the selfish love of the ego as opposed to divine love</note> does not seek God's glory, but only itself. Thus Rachel envied Leah because Leah had a name for being blessed by God, and she said to Jacob: **“Give me children also, or else I die.”**

2. Here we see how the ways of God are entirely hidden from **Reason** <note>original: "Vernunfft"; in Böhme’s writing, this refers to human logic that lacks spiritual enlightenment</note>. Even though Reason stands within the **figure** <note>original: "Figur"; a symbolic representation or spiritual type</note> of divine wonders—as Rachel does here—she represents the **Adamic self-nature** <note>original: "Adamische eigene Natur"; the fallen human condition inherited from Adam</note>. She desired from Jacob the life-force from the blessing of God, and if she did not obtain it, she would have to die. The **zealous spirit** <note>original: "Eyffergeist"</note> in her desire certainly pointed toward her inner ground within the Covenant of God, but her Reason did not understand this. Instead, she only desired children so that she might be delivered from her shame. Yet her inner ground remained hidden, longing to manifest itself through human nature in **human essence** <note>original: "Menschlicher Essenz"</note>. Therefore, the inner ground in the **Covenant of Grace** <note>original: "Gnaden Bunde"</note> signaled through her own Adamic essence that if that same inner ground were not made manifest through the human essence, she would have to die eternally. Therefore Reason said: **“Give me children, or I die,”** which outwardly appears to be resentment and displeasure, but the Spirit of God has His "figure" here, through which He speaks.

3. We see further in these two sisters—who were nonetheless daughters of the Covenant of God in the promise—how the serpent’s poison in the **wrath of God** <note>original: "Grimme Gottes"</note> within flesh and blood set itself so vehemently against the **Line of Christ** <note>original: "Lineam Christi"</note> in the Covenant. It always disdains that Line and, like a **proud Lucifer** <note>a reference to the fallen angel's pride</note>, it elevates and swings itself upward in the rational human self-interest of its own will, desiring to hold the sovereignty.

<summary>This page provides a mystical interpretation of Rachel’s barrenness and her envy of Leah, framing it as a struggle between human "Reason" (Adamic nature) and the hidden workings of God's Covenant.</summary>

4. How Rachel here despised her sister because she was more beautiful on the outside than Leah—in that Leah was simple and weak <note>original: "blöde"; in the Biblical context of Leah, this often refers to her "tender" or weak eyes, but Böhme uses it to mean spiritually unassuming</note> before the world, while Rachel possessed the world-spirit in the refinement of **Reason** <term>Reason: "Vernunfft," which Böhme defines as the limited, earthly intellect of fallen man</term>—this was to indicate that the **Adamic nature** in Rachel ruled over the revealed blessing of the Covenant in Leah. It shows that the **Line of Christ** <note>original: "Linea Christi"</note> in this world would be revealed in such a simple, plain, and despised form among such people.

5. Such people would only be considered fools and weaklings by the world's Reason, splendor, and beauty; though they walk in such mockery and disdain and "sow with tears," they shall nevertheless give birth in their inward ground within the **Line of Christ**, and finally "reap with joy." This indicates that Christ’s kingdom is not of this world—that in this world it must be cast into God's wrath, disdain, and death. By being thus cast in, it fills the wrath of God with love and gentleness, and with that love, it sprouts forth from death through the wrath. It makes a mockery of and brings to nothing the proud Lucifer in human self-will and fleshly lust, as an inconstant life—a life which Divine Humility cannot overcome <note>meaning: the false life of pride cannot withstand the power of humility</note>.

6. This Humility blooms under all mockery and also breaks through death and the wrath of God; it turns death into life, takes away the victory of Hell, and transforms the sting of the false serpent-essence with sweet love. We see this here with Leah: although she was envied by her sister (representing Reason), the **Line of Christ** from the Covenant nonetheless bloomed within her amidst all the mockery. It made her fertile and Rachel barren, until Rachel gave her handmaid to her husband as a wife. This indicates the Adamic line as a servant-line, which enters into the marriage of the **Line of Christ** in the manner of a servant within Christ's kingdom.

7. For Adam squandered the lines; the natural right in the kingdom of God was lost in Adam and now enters into the marriage in the manner of a servant, like the handmaids of Jacob’s wives. There we see that Rachel, as the right of her own nature, could not bring forth fruit or work until the line of servitude under the yoke of the **Adamic nature** of **self-love** <note>original: "eigene Liebe"</note> became fertile from the marriage. This indicates that human nature must submit itself to service under the **Line of Christ**, because they are joined in marriage within the **Line of Christ** and appointed as heirs of God.

8. Only then does the kingdom of nature first bloom within God’s kingdom and become fertile in the blessing, just as Rachel only became fertile after her handmaid had given birth. This indicates that Rachel must also be a handmaid before the Covenant of God and the **Line of Christ**, and that the **Line of Christ** within her is also her Lord—so that she too enters the marriage of the **Line of Christ** in the manner of a handmaid; for she...

9. And he indicates by this how the **Line of Christ** is not propagated through human power alone, but rather that the Line itself penetrates its own branches. It does not look upon high names or the noble lineages of men, but instead pushes into the most miserable people in the world—those who are merely servants and maids—just as readily as into the high-born.

10. We have a powerful example of this in Jacob, who had to be subservient as a servant for twenty years before the twelve tribes of Israel were brought forth through him. This indicates that a Christian must be born under the subservient yoke of the corrupted, self-ruling, and headstrong **Adamic nature**. If one is to be born as a Christian out of the **Line of Christ**, the "procreator" <note>the person undergoing spiritual rebirth</note> must submit themselves as a servant of God. Within the **realm of Nature**, they must act only as a servant of God, forsaking all temporal things in their heart and regarding nothing as their own property, but rather seeing themselves in their station only as a servant who serves their Master therein.

11. Just as Jacob begat the tribes of Israel under such service, it indicates that they should be "foreign guests" in this world, serving God their Lord within the **realm of Nature**. God Himself would determine their reward, so that they might enter into the Kingdom of Christ with great riches from this world, as if returning to their first **Adamic-Paradisal Fatherland**—just as Jacob, during his service, obtained his father-in-law's goods with a great blessing.

->The Inner Spiritual Figure stands thus:<-

12. When Adam fell, he had to go out of Paradise and submit to service under the **Spirit of the World** <note>original Latin: "Spiritum Mundi," the astral and elemental forces governing the physical universe</note> in the kingdom of this world. He became subject to the stars and the four elements and had to serve them in their kingdom, tending to their children—the creatures of this world—as is plain to see before our eyes.

13. But as he had to go out of Paradise, just as Jacob went out of his father's house, the Lord met him and, through the **Seed of the Woman** and the **Crusher of the Serpent** <note>original: "Weibes Saamen uñ Schlangētreter"; a reference to the prophecy in Genesis 3:15</note>, showed him the way back into Paradise, just as He showed the same to Jacob with the ladder that reached up to Heaven.

14. And once Adam had gone out of Paradise, he had to submit himself to service under a foreign yoke. He had to serve the **realm of Nature** in its wonders and tend to the children of Nature. This **realm of Nature** had become foreign to him after the Fall; it now held him by force, plagued him with heat, cold, sickness, and pain, and held him captive to use him for its service—though previously, it had been his best friend and **Grandfather** <note>In Böhme's cosmology, Nature and the Stars are often described as the "grandparents" or progenitors of the physical body.</note>.
