15. Just as Jacob, in this symbolic figure, had to flee to his friend—his mother’s brother—and serve him, who held him as a servant and yet also as a son-in-law because of his daughters: so too had Adam to serve under the subservient yoke of his **Grandfather** <note>In Böhme’s cosmology, the "Grandfather" refers to the "Kingdom of Nature," the external physical world that preceded the individual human but now acts as a demanding master.</note>, the **Kingdom of Nature**. This kingdom gave him its daughters as wives, from whom he begets the children of God within God’s blessing under such a yoke; he also presented his children as subservient servants in his Father's house, that is, in the kingdom of this world.

<margin>a</margin>
16. And just as Jacob acquired great wealth through the blessing of God, and brought his master’s goods to himself through **cunning** <note>original: "Liste." In this context, it refers to a divinely inspired strategy or spiritual skill rather than a sinful deception.</note>—using the trick with the peeled rods over the watering troughs where the sheep drank, so that they conceived and brought forth spotted sheep: so too, in like manner, when Adam had come under the subservient yoke of the **Kingdom of Nature** (where the Devil's envy and cunning also ruled according to the **Kingdom of Wrath** <note>The "Kingdom of Wrath" or "Grimm" is the dark, foundational fire of existence that Böhme believes must be tempered by Light.</note>), God showed him how he should, with spiritual cunning, claim the Kingdom of Nature and its workings with all its wonders for himself. He was to make the powers of Nature his eternal property, so that his works, which he performed in the Kingdom of Nature, would follow him into his eternal Fatherland and become his own.

17. What was this "cunning" which God showed him? It was the **Crusher of the Serpent** <note>original: "Schlangentreter." A traditional title for Christ, referring to the prophecy in Genesis 3:15 that the seed of the woman would crush the serpent's head.</note>, whom Adam "put on" through the Covenant. This Crusher took the Kingdom of Nature from us humans and claimed it for Himself. With **Divine Cunning**, He took the strength and power from our "Master"—the Kingdom of God's Wrath which held us captive under its yoke—and drew all human power to Himself. He withdrew the inherent power from that Master (the Kingdom of Nature), just as Jacob took the goods from his master.

18. And as the Spirit of God showed Jacob in a vision how the rams leaped upon the speckled and spotted sheep and goats; so too was Adam shown in the Spirit of the **Covenant of Promise** how the Spirit of Grace in the Covenant would come upon the "spotted" human nature and bless it, so that it became pregnant with the Spirit in the Covenant.

19. This "spotted" human nature is nothing other than the half-earthly corrupt nature and the newly born heavenly nature within the Covenant. The Spirit of God came upon this heavenly part and made it fruitful, so that under the earthly yoke, it drew the powers of Nature into Divine power and into the Heavenly realm. Thus, the "goods" were taken away from the Master (the Kingdom of Nature), and the **Heavenly Man** within the Covenant claimed them with **Divine Wit and Cunning**. With these goods, he departed from his Master—the kingdom of external Nature—and returned to his Father’s house, which is **Paradise**, just as Jacob returned to his father’s house.

# How Jacob served Laban for 20 years #

25. And this is indicated to the Jews—who use this **figure** <note>A "figure" (Figur) in Böhme’s writing is a symbolic or prophetic representation of a deeper spiritual truth.</note> to justify themselves in their cunning and worldly deceit—that this cunning in Jacob prefigured a spiritual truth <note>original: "Geistliche Figur præfiguriret"</note> and in no way covers for their own dishonesty.

26. For He who said, "Thou shalt not covet that which is thy neighbor's," has forbidden all external cunning and deceit. But in the **battle-lines** <note>original: "Streilinien," referring to the spiritual struggle between light and darkness.</note>, the Spirit of God has used the Kingdom of Christ in this figure to point toward the inner ground of the **New Man** <note>The "New Man" is the spiritual nature restored through Christ, which struggles against the "Old Man" or the fallen earthly nature.</note> through an external image.

27. As with Ishmael, Abraham’s first son, from whom the possessions were also withdrawn, this indicates that they did not belong to Adam in his corruption, but to Christ as the **second Adam**. Christ took them with Divine virtue and **cunning** <note>original: "List." Böhme often describes "divine cunning" as the way the Spirit outmaneuvers the "wrath" of nature to reclaim what is holy.</note> from the Kingdom of God’s Wrath within man, where he first had to subject himself to God’s wrath and serve in an assumed human nature. Thus, he withdrew the goods and took all the property from it; and this is what this figure in Jacob indicates.

28. The Spirit presents a truly wonderful figure in Jacob: how Laban changed his wages ten times and yet could do him no harm. This indicates how it goes for God’s children in this service; while they are under the yoke of nature, they are to draw the goods of the Kingdom of Nature toward the **Divine Knowledge** <note>original: "Göttliche Wiß" (Wissenschaft), meaning the spiritual wisdom or awareness of God's workings.</note> and into the inner New Man. Thus, great changes come into a person’s purpose; for when he has now set out on a path he wishes to walk, the Devil comes with his envy and hinders his purpose through evil people, so that it does not proceed—just as with Jacob, when he thought, "the spotted sheep and goats shall be your reward," then his heart <note>This likely refers to Laban's heart or the general turn of circumstances changing the agreement.</note> turned the reward around.

29. This is also how it goes for God’s children in their labor: when they think, "there you will harvest God’s blessing," or "there you will meet God’s children with whom you can work and bring forth fruit," or "there you will do good and wrap this work in your **desire for faith** <note>original: "Glaubensbegierde." He must only trust God, like Jacob, and then no enemy can do him harm. And even if it might appear as if harm is being done and his works are in vain, they still produce fruit that is incomprehensible to reason; and the person finally departs with great wealth from the kingdom of this world back into his **Fatherland** <note>The spiritual homeland or Paradise.</note>, just like Jacob.

31. Which hope God fulfills in him in Christ with a heavenly end <note>The original "Ente" is likely a variant of "Ende" (end) or a typo for "Ernte" (harvest). 32. When we rightly look at and consider these histories, how God began the Kingdom of Israel with a servant shepherd, and exalted it above all the powerful kingdoms on earth until eternity; and consider how the 12 tribes of Israel were begotten under a servant's yoke in the manner of bondage, from which tribe Christ willed to be born according to His humanity: Then we see that all the world's highness, also all the art and knowledge of nature, is like foolishness before God—yet men boast so much of it, and consider their worldly practice and their high statuses as great things, and yet before God they are far from equal to a pious shepherd.

33. 35. ### ->How Jacob served Laban for 20 years<-

36. Where do the high priests and high universities remain in this matter? They who claim and take for themselves the power over these mysteries, and often trample underfoot the gifts of the Holy Spirit found in such shepherds <gloss>simple workers</gloss>, mocking them and holding them for fools. Are they not all like Cain, Ishmael, and Esau from the "left-hand" lineage—born from the kingdom of nature of this world in the hypocrisy of their own reason? In the eyes of God, such reason is not equal to even a simple shepherd.

37. O you poor humans, blinded in Adam! Turn your eyes away from "high things" and humble yourselves under the simplicity of Christ into this "shepherd-lineage." Do not look upon the prestige of cleverness and high status, or you will be miserably deceived. If you wish to become capable of joining this lineage, you may not attain it through the highness that struts in hypocrisy within this shepherd-office; rather, it is in humility and simple innocence <note>original: "alberen Einfalt," meaning a guileless or "silly" simplicity in the eyes of the world</note> that the soul submits itself to Christ’s yoke. Then, the poor soul—otherwise blind to God—is rooted into this marriage and becomes capable of this lineage.

38. These twelve children of Jacob are precisely the lineages that the Spirit of God points to from Adam through to Noah and his children. These sprouted from the Covenant Line in Paradise and pressed forward from Adam to Abel, and so on until the children of Noah, where twelve lines or tribes are also indicated. Here, that same tree opened itself again from a single stem, which was Jacob, and it signifies how all those lines should be sanctified in one stem—which is Christ. He also chose twelve Apostles to reveal this tree, which had grown out of the Covenant Line.

39. And when Jacob had fathered these twelve sons, he also fathered a daughter named Dinah. She "went out" to see the daughters of the land <note>A reference to Genesis 34:1</note> and thereby lost her honor and virginity. He fathered her through Leah, in whom the Line of Christ was revealed through the tribe of Judah. This indicates that the Line of Christ at this time still stood hidden in the woman’s <term>tincture</term> <note>Böhme uses "tincture" to describe the essential spiritual "quality" or "life-force" of a person</note>, but revealed itself through the masculine tincture as a fiery quality, until it reached Mary, the mother of Christ. We see this in the covenants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—that the covenant pressed upon their "seed"—and we also see it in circumcision, which was given only to the man.

40. And we see it even more clearly in the Law at Mount Sinai, which was also given in a "fiery" manner. This indicates that before Christ, humanity was led in the "Father’s property" <note>In Böhme’s system, the "Father" represents the divine fire or wrath, while the "Son" represents the divine light or love</note>, which held us captive in wrath until His love—as His Son—revealed itself through that wrath into the woman’s tincture, and changed the tinctures of the man and woman back into one. Therefore, the Line of Christ flourished among the fathers—

This tincture wandered away from its honor through its own curiosity <note>original: "Fürwitz," implying a meddling or impertinent curiosity</note>, just as Eve wished to behold and know the "daughters of the world" (the animalistic, creaturely lusts) and in such lust lost her Paradisiacal virginity.

In this spiritual essence, Adam died or faded away from God’s Kingdom when his will broke itself off from God. 45. The Spirit of God represents this figure in Jacob's life through Dinah: how that same seventh property of nature in Adam became a broken harlot before God. 46. 48. 49. Through Leah, Christ was represented according to his heavenly, hidden humanity; how the heavenly world-being would hide itself in our humanity under the yoke of God’s wrath, and how Christ had to appear in the form of a servant and a despised person.

50. > Now when Rachel had born Joseph, Jacob said to Laban: Let me go and travel to my own place and into my country; give me my wives and my children, for whom I have served you, so that I may go.

### The 59th Chapter.

## How Jacob departed from Laban, what this figure signifies, and what is to be understood by it.

->Genesis 31<-

1. In this chapter, the external history is mostly presented, yet beneath it the Spirit has his Heavenly figure with which he plays; for the text says: *And the words of the children of Laban came to Jacob, saying, Jacob has brought all our father’s goods to himself, and from our father’s goods he has brought such wealth to pass. And Jacob looked upon the face of Laban, and behold, it was not toward him as it was yesterday and the day before.*

2. This is a figure prefigured in the Spirit of Christ: when the Spirit of Christ in man has drawn the kingdom of human nature to itself, then the serpent’s envy <note>original: "Schlangen Neyd," referring to the venomous, prideful nature of the fallen human ego</note> wakes up in the wrath of nature in flesh and blood, in that it understands and feels that the power of nature in man is being withdrawn from it, and it attacks the Spirit of Christ in the power of nature.

3. Then the reluctance in man begins, so that the poor soul becomes anxious in all places, as she realizes that she dwells in a foreign property and the Devil is her neighbor, and he still always has an entrance to her own nature and attacks her; because she has withdrawn the kingdom of nature—as his former land or seat—from him in Christ’s Spirit, the mortal nature in God’s wrath <note>original: "Gottes Zorne," the harsh, fiery principle of nature apart from God's light</note> with its desire then presents itself as foreign and unfriendly toward the poor soul, when it sees that it is losing its voluptuous earthly inheritance. This right is signified by the children of Laban, when Reason <note>original: "Vernunfft," here meaning worldly or carnal logic</note> sees how it loses temporal honor and pleasure, and all its natural rights are withdrawn from it, just as Jacob withdrew the goods from Laban through cunning.

4. Thus God speaks there to the soul as he does here to Jacob: Return again into your fatherland, to your kindred; I will be with you. That is, the poor soul should enter again into its first fatherland, namely into the **Eternal Word** from which it came. Therein God blesses the soul, and therein it can also call to its children and members <note>The "members" or "limbs" here refer to the various faculties and powers of the human being that are unified under the enlightened soul.</note> and lead them out with it from the house of bondage of the wrath of God in the realm of nature, just as Jacob called his wives and children and led them out from the service of their father. Likewise, the enlightened soul leads its power of life in the realm of nature, together with its fellow members, out of the house of bondage of **flesh and blood** back into the first house, namely into the **Word of God**.

5. And just as Jacob fled from the house of bondage of his father-in-law and Laban pursued him and wished him harm, so likewise it happens with the children of Christ when they begin to flee out of the house of bondage of Satan—that is, out of fleshly lust—and wish to return to their first fatherland, namely into righteousness and the fear of God. Then immediately the fleshly heap of the godless world comes flying after them with grimness and frivolity, wanting to kill them and take all their possessions and goods in God’s righteousness with false tongues.

6. But the Lord threatens them so that they cannot do this, just as happened to Laban; although they indeed stand and revile the children of God as unrighteous because they turn away from their gods and abominations and no longer desire their hypocrisy, nor wish to bear their false yoke anymore, nor serve them in their unrighteousness and approve of their falsehood—just as the present world hypocritically acts under this yoke and serves falsehood, only so that their god <term>Maosim</term> <note>original: "Maosim." A reference to the "God of forces" or "fortresses" in Daniel 11:38, often used by Reformation-era writers to signify the god of worldly power, wealth, or institutionalized false religion.</note> may grow fat and be able to live.

7. Also, the Spirit of God here presents a figure of how Christ would place himself for a time under this servile yoke in the realm of nature, and would marry Adam’s daughters—that is, our flesh and blood—and draw Adam’s property and goods, namely the kingdom of human nature, to himself. This means he would draw many people to himself, and finally, with them, go out of this house of bondage of this world back into his Father’s **Eternal House**. In this departure to his Father, the devil together with the false world would despise him and entirely wish to kill him, and would want to rob and take back the goods together with his children begotten here—just as the devil did through the Pharisees and false Jews, who wanted to take away and rob Christ of all his faithful children, even as Laban pursued Jacob and wanted to take back his acquired goods.

8. 9. A biblical idiom meaning to deceive someone or act without their knowledge.</note> of Laban the Syrian, in that he did not inform him that he was fleeing. We see further how Laban, when he came to Jacob, acted so vehemently regarding the idols and searched through all of Jacob’s household goods because of them. We also see in this text how Rachel must have loved these same idols, in that she sat upon them and hid them so that her father could not get them back.

<margin>kinship</margin>
10. In these words, both an external and an internal figure are presented to us, showing how it would go with Israel in the future. For these idols were not pagan idols according to the Moloch of the stars <note>A reference to the worship of celestial bodies or the pagan god Moloch mentioned in the Old Testament.</note> such as the heathens had; rather, as one reads, they made images of their deceased as a memorial. 11. But the true figure, through which the Spirit points to the future, is this: first, that Israel would not always cling to God with their whole heart, but they would always carry these idols of carnal self-love with them, and love themselves and their own images—as a race of human highness—more than God, as indeed came to pass.

12. Specifically, this departure of Jacob indicates the departure of Israel out of Egypt into the promised land, where they also took their carnal idols with them and soon thereafter served their own idols as human highness and abandoned their God. They looked toward their Mammon <note>A biblical term for wealth or material greed personified as a false god.</note> and wanted to have kings among them according to the custom of the heathens, and they abandoned their true King who had led them out of Egypt.

13. Secondly, it indicates how Christ, in whose figure Jacob stood, would take this "Rachel" in our flesh and blood upon himself—meaning this "idol-will" of the soul, turned away from God in Adam, which had occupied itself with images and idols and possessed them just as Rachel did—and would [reclaim] the soul's turned-away will with its occupied idols and images...

...leading the images out from the house of idols; these idols—representing idol-like self-will and desire—must afterwards all be shattered in the death of Christ.

14. This is immediately presented to us as a figure (in Genesis, Chapter 35) when God said to Jacob: "Arise and go up to Bethel, and dwell there; and make there an altar to the God who appeared to you when you fled from your brother Esau." Then Jacob said to his household and to all who were with him: "Put away the foreign gods that are among you, and purify yourselves, and change your clothes; and let us arise and go up to Bethel, that I may make an altar there to the God who heard me in the time of my distress and has been with me on the way that I have gone," etc.

15. This history of Jacob indicates nothing other than this: how Christ would depart from this "house of service" <note>Also translated as "house of bondage," referring to the spiritual state of humanity before redemption.</note> with this "Idol-Rachel"—representing our flesh and blood—and go to his Father. Through his departure, when he would build the high altar for God—which altar he is himself—he would lay down these idols of ours (the human self-will and all the imagery of self-love) before God's altar in his death. He would purify our hearts as the will of the soul and change our garments (our flesh and blood), as this text in Chapter 35 clearly indicates. It focuses entirely on how Christ, upon that same altar of his New Testament, would sacrifice us to the God who appeared to us again in his Covenant of Grace during our misery and distress following the Fall.

16. However, when the text of Moses (Gen. 31) says that Jacob "stole the heart" <note>original: "sein Herz gestohlen." A biblical idiom meaning to outwit or leave without notice.</note> of Laban the Syrian, because he fled secretly with his daughters, it contains the very same internal, spiritual figure: For the Word became Man and took the daughters of the earthly Adam (represented by Laban) and led them away from Adam’s house into God’s house through Divine cunning <note>original: "Göttliche List." In this mystical context, it refers to the clever way God reclaims humanity from the power of sin.</note>. This is called "stealing" in the sense that the children of Adam are thus stolen away from the Kingdom of God's Wrath—that is, led away through Divine Knowledge.

17. For the Wrath of God had possessed humanity by natural right; but Christ came and betrothed himself to them, and stole them away from the Wrath along with the idols. He sacrificed them to God upon his altar (which he is himself), and laid aside the images of human self-love, and purified our garments before God, so that we should serve Him at this altar.

18. This is properly understood through Rachel’s idols. The figure certainly represents the external history, but the Spirit of God has His own figure hidden beneath it. # How Jacob Departed from Laban.

...and everything that happened there is a **figure** of Christ <note>A "figure" is a person or event in the Old Testament seen as a symbolic foreshadowing of Christ.</note>; for Laban stands here <margin>Chapter 50.</margin> as the figure of the Kingdom of Nature, and Jacob as the figure of Christ.

19. Laban scolded Jacob because he fled from him and had not first allowed him to kiss his children, so that he might have sent them off in joy with drums: Thus also does the Kingdom of Nature act toward Christ's children; when they secretly flee from it and leave the house of idols, then the children of the Kingdom of Nature scold these children of Christ as fugitives and perjurers, as heretics and newcomers, as **Enthusiasts** <note>In the 17th century, "Enthusiast" was a derogatory term for someone who claimed to receive direct divine revelation outside of established church structures.</note>, and whatever other names there are. And they say to them: "Since you wished to leave the godless way for another life, why did you not announce this to our high priests, so that they might have guided you there with their ceremonies—such as confessions, sacraments, and intercessions? Why do you not keep the custom of the Church, where Christ's kingdom stands in joy with noise, organs, and pipes?" Why do you steal away from us in secret and go another way than our order and statutes dictate? And for this reason, they become their enemies and persecute them, following them with condemnation and abuse, calling them evil children or perjurers who have stolen their idols and refuse to honor their hypocrisy as gods—just as Laban pursued Jacob and scolded him for not having held his pageantry beforehand and for not telling him in advance that he wished to journey away.

20. So also **Babel** <note>The author uses "Babel" to represent the institutionalized, worldly church, which he views as a place of spiritual confusion.</note> insists that the children of Christ shall enter into God only through its pageantry and **belly-orders** <note>original: "Bauchordens"—a biting critique of religious orders or clergy perceived as being more concerned with their stomachs and material comfort than spiritual truth.</note>; and whoever wishes to enter to God otherwise than through their order, and flee from this house of bondage, shall be condemned and cannot come to God.

21. But Jacob could well come to his father without Laban’s pageantry: and even though Laban scolded him and called his way wrong, yet he was right before God. For God had commanded it of him, and Laban could not hold him back at all: So also the children of Christ, when the Spirit of Christ within them commands them to flee from Babel, can in no way be held back; nor does it harm them at all, however badly the world scolds them for it and despises, laughs at, mocks, labels them as heretics, and calls them Enthusiasts.

22. Yet the Most High rebukes Laban, so that he must speak nothing but kindly with Jacob; that is, the blasphemy of Babel against Christ's children must ultimately serve their pure joy and kindness, and Laban must simply let them depart with their property and goods. For God commands His children to flee from Babel and enter again into their first fatherland, from which they departed with Adam—not through the pageantry of Babel, but through the turning of the mind and the will, as a new obedience.

30. Secondly / it is the beautiful image / of how it happens with the penitent person / when he gives himself over through earnest repentance into this struggle of Christ / as into Christ’s suffering and death in his victory / and in the Spirit of Christ [wrestles] with God’s strict Justice / which always wrestles him within the certain shield <note>original: "Schilt"; likely referring to the protective or defensive boundary of the conscience</note>.

31. 32. ### How a Man wrestled the whole Night with Jacob.

<margin>96b</margin>
The **Ungrund** <note>original: "vngrundt"; Böhme’s term for the "groundless" or "abyssal" source of all being that exists before and beyond nature</note> in the **Eternally-speaking Word**, from which the highest love and grace of God has revealed itself, seizes the soul and penetrates into it, just as the sun penetrates the essence of a plant, by which the plant becomes "half-sunny": In this same way, the soul sinks down in its own will and becomes "half-Divine." It then wrestles with God’s strict justice within flesh and blood, seeking to overcome the wrath of God.

35. Then God’s justice speaks within the conscience: "Let me go," which is to say: "Leave off from me and do not kill me, for you see clearly that the **Divine Morning Glow** <note>original: "Morgenröthe"; a reference to the dawning of divine light within the soul</note> is rising in me; stop storming against the judgment of God." But in the true spiritual warriors, the soul speaks to God’s justice: "I will not let you go unless you then bless me," which is to say: "Unless you then give me the promised grace from the death of Christ in his victory, so that I may put on my Savior Christ, that he may be mine and I may be his." Then God’s justice speaks, as it did to Jacob: "What is your name?" Then the poor soul names itself according to its own natural, created name, just as Jacob did when he named himself Jacob here. But just as the Lord said to Jacob: "You shall no longer be called Jacob, but **Israel**," that is, a **Tree of Life**. So also God says to the soul: "You shall no longer have your own name in me, but you shall be called a Christian in Christ, as a branch in the Tree of Israel, a vine on the grapevine of Christ; for you have fought with God and men and have prevailed; you have overcome God’s justice in the grimness of wrath through your struggle in the Spirit of Christ, and are now an **Essential Christian** <term>Essential Christian: one who possesses the actual substance or "essence" of Christ's nature, rather than just the name</term>, and no longer a **Title-Christian** or a **Mouth-Christian** <note>original: "TitulChriſt vnd MaulChriſt"; Böhme’s terms for those who are Christian in name or speech only, lacking true inner transformation</note>, from whom grace is still far off."

38. For God, outside of nature and the creature, has no name, but is called only the **Eternal Good**, as the **Eternal One**, the **Ungrund**.

...and the Ground of all beings: no place has been found for Him; therefore, no creature can rightly name Him, for all names reside in the **formed Word of powers** <note>the "expressed" world of nature and diversity</note>. 39. Just as creatures, as well as all plants of the earth, cannot know what the sun’s power is named, but rather they stand still before the sun, and the sun gives them power and warmth and blesses them so that they grow and bring forth fruit: so too is it to be understood here with Jacob and all people. When Jacob saw and felt the **Divine Morning Glow** <note>original: "Morgenröhte"; Böhme's symbol for the first dawning of divine light in the soul</note> in his soul, the Divine Sun blessed him in the name of Jesus through **essential working** <note>original: "Essentialische würckung"; an action that affects the very essence or substance of a being</note>.

40. And I must also point out here how it happened for Jacob and all children of God in this sunshine, and how it still happens: when the **Sun of Grace** (with its effective power) rises in the soul, the soul rejoices and always desires to see God's face in a creaturely way—just as Moses also desired—and always thinks that God is something **formal** <note>having a specific shape or form</note>. The soul does not yet see God rightly and wants to recognize God in imagery. This creaturely imagery lies so heavily upon us in our fallen self-will within the mind that we cannot understand anywhere what God is, other than that He is the **Abyss** <note>original: "Abgrundt"; the bottomless source or void beyond all nature</note> of all nature and creature Himself, as the **Eternal One**, who dwells in nothing but Himself and has no form nor anything else.

41. And it would be right and good if we were not led in such a figurative way by the **Masters of the Letter** <note>theologians who focus only on the literal text and external dogmas rather than inner spiritual experience</note> when they teach and speak of the one God, as has happened until now; for they have led us into vain images within the essential will, as if the one God willed "this" or "that." Yet He Himself is the single will toward creature and nature, and the entire creation lies solely and alone within the formation of His **exhaled Word** and will; and the distinction of the single will is understood in the speaking out and the containment within nature.

Where is God? What does God want? 43. It is to be lamented that we are led so blindly, and that the truth is held back in images; for when the Divine Power reveals itself with its brilliance and becomes active in the **inner ground** <term>the deepest, most fundamental part of the human spirit</term> of the soul, so that the human desires to leave the godless way and surrender to God, then the entire **Triune God** is present in the soul’s life and will. Then the Heaven where God dwells within is opened in the soul; and that very place is there in the soul where the Father begets His Son, and where the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son.

44. For God needs no measurable place; He also dwells in the **abyss** <note>the "Abgrund" or bottomless depth</note> of godless souls, but is ungraspable to them according to His love; rather, according to His **wrath** <note>original: "Zorn"; in Böhme's thought, this is the "dark fire" or harsh quality of nature without the light of love</note>, He is revealed and graspable in godless souls.

45. For the eternal speaking of the Word (according to its ungraspability to nature and creature) becomes **pictorial** <note>takes on a mental or representative form</note> according to the soulful will, of which the Scripture says: *With the holy You are holy, and with the perverse You are perverse.* Also: *Whatever kind of people they are, such a God they also have.* <note>Referencing Psalm 18:25-26, implying that our perception of God is a mirror of our own internal state.</note>

46. For in the thrones of the holy angels God is revealed in His love, and in the thrones of the devils He is revealed with His **grimness** <note>original: "Grimme"; the fierce, consuming fire of God’s power</note>, as according to darkness and painfulness; and yet there is only one single God and not two. According to the nature of painfulness He wills painfulness, and according to love He wills love, just as a burning fire desires only resinous sulfur in return according to its own kind, and the light from the fire desires nothing but an open place in which it may shine: it takes nothing, but gives itself for the joy of life; it only lets itself be taken, and has no other will in itself than that it wants to give itself and wants to work good. So also God, according to His holiness, has no other will in Himself than that He wants to reveal His love, power, and radiance (in the creaturely form), just as the sun reveals itself in a herb and **tinctures** <term>an alchemical term meaning to permeate and transform the inner quality of a substance</term> it and makes it good; thus it is also to be understood regarding God.

47. Therefore it is all useless chatter and creaturely imagery when people ask: "what is God’s name?" 48. They quarrel over the one God in whom we live and have our being, though through Him the kingdom of nature is revealed in its wonders and brought into symbolic forms.

49. But the true ground of what and how God is, and what the "Essence of all essences" might be, is as blind to them as one born blind is to the beauty of this world. And though they call themselves masters of the letters, they have nonetheless lost the **five vowels** <note>Böhme often associated the five vowels (A, E, I, O, U) with the breath of the Holy Spirit and the fundamental powers of divine speech.</note>, which are the power of all words. People cling merely to a historical narrative and do not see what is hinted at by this or that story.

50. For the Spirit of God did not perform such wonders and record these same stories so precisely for the sake of the outward form of simple shepherds' histories—as if He cared so much for a mere history that He had to preserve it among all nations and proclaim it as His Word. No, it was done for the sake of what is hinted at beneath such simple stories, through which God's Spirit plays in figures pointing toward the future Eternal. Therefore, one should look upon the scriptures of the Old Testament with clearer eyes, for the entire New Testament lies beneath them in the figure of simple history.

And as he passed over Penuel, the sun rose upon him; that is, when God’s Sun, as His power, is revealed in the soul, the soul's essence catches that same power into itself. ### The 61st Chapter.

# The most beautiful figure / how Jacob and Esau came together / and all sorrow and ill will was turned into great joy and compassion / and what is to be understood by this.

->Genesis 33.<-

Regarding this text, blind Reason <note>Böhme uses "Reason" (*Vernunfft*) to describe the limited, earthly intellect that cannot perceive spiritual mysteries without divine illumination.</note> should open its eyes better than it has done until now, and better consider the figure <note>original: *Figur*. In this context, it refers to a "typology"—an Old Testament event that foreshadows a New Testament spiritual truth.</note> of Jacob and Esau, and learn to rightly understand the Decree <note>original: *Decretum*. Referring to the divine ordinance or predestination.</note> regarding Jacob and Esau, where the Scripture says: **Jacob I have loved and Esau I have hated**, while the children still lay in the mother’s womb and had done neither good nor evil, so that the purpose of God might stand.

2. Here one should rightly behold the purpose of God and what God's Spirit means by it; for Esau stood in the image of the corrupted Adam, and Jacob in the image of Christ, who was to come to help poor Adam. Therefore, these two brothers had to come from one seed, to indicate that God would become man, and that God's seed as his Word, and Adam's seed in his own nature, should be manifested in one person and become one man. Thus, God's seed was to overcome the corrupted Adam’s seed with great Divine Love, and extinguish the Father’s wrath in the soul with that Love. This Divine Love was to surrender itself entirely into the wrath of the soul, so that God’s grace and compassion <note>original: *Erbärmbde*. A 17th-century term for mercy or heartfelt compassion.</note> might break through the wrath in Love, and also turn the wrath into compassion. This is seen here where Jacob, with his gifts and his great humility, surrendered himself to his brother Esau and turned Esau's wrath—which he bore against Jacob because of the natural right of the first birth and the blessing—into such great compassion that Esau fell upon his neck and wept in great mercy, and his wrath was turned into love. Just so did Christ, with his great love and humility in our assumed humanity, turn his Father’s wrath in our fire-burning wrath-souls into such great compassion that Divine Justice ceased its wrath against our souls.

3. For just as Jacob reconciled his brother Esau with gifts and humility when he surrendered himself to Esau’s wrath, so also Christ reconciled the wrath of God when he surrendered his Heavenly Blood with the great Tincture <note>original: *Tinctur*. When Christ went into his passion in our assumed humanity, the wrath of God in the four elements <note>The four classical elements (earth, water, air, fire) which Böhme believes constitute the physical body and are subject to the "wrath" of fallen nature.</note> of the body came to meet him; so Christ divided his Divinity and his Humanity—as the Heavenly world-essence <note>original: *Weltwesen*. And Rachel signifies the faded *Essence* <note>original: *Ens*</note> of the Heavenly world-essence, in which the true soul dwells, which remained [faded] in Adam’s fall and became barren, like Rachel, until God made it fruitful in the Spirit of Christ, just as happened to Rachel.

8. As Jacob bowed 7 times to the earth before the wrath of Esau, and reconciled Esau in this humility: so also here the Love in the name *JESUS* reconciled the wrath of the Father’s property in the fire, in soul and body: For the natural life from the spirit of the world <note>original: *Spiritu Mundi*</note> , as the soul of time, which was breathed into Adam’s nostrils, had to surrender its natural right and die: just as Jacob surrendered his goods and also his outer life to his brother, as to what he would do with him; so also *Christ* surrendered our life to the wrath of God, and left it willingly: But the name *JESUS* went before, and led our natural life through death, and took it to Himself again, and triumphed <note>original: *Triumphirete*</note> with our natural life over and through death.

9. 10. And as Esau wept on Jacob’s neck, he lifted up his eyes and saw the women with the children and spoke: Who are these with you? Jacob answered: They are children whom God has bestowed upon your servant, and the maidservants stepped forward with their children and bowed before him: *Leah* also stepped forward with her children and bowed before him, afterwards *Joseph* and *Rachel* stepped forward, and also bowed before him.

### The Inner Figure stands thus:

When God’s wrath held humanity captive in the darkness, they were recognized in the wrath, not as God’s holy image: But when, in the suffering of *Christ*, Love broke through the wrath in humanity, so that the wrath was transformed, then the one God looked upon them again in His image, and spoke to the name *JESUS*, Who are these who are with you? And *JESUS* answered God and spoke: these are children whom God has bestowed upon His servant.

52. Therefore, we should learn to understand the Scripture correctly: how God wills good and evil. Namely, the decree is not within His own self, but within the spoken Word—that is, within Nature and the creature. God hated Esau in the corrupt nature, in Esau's own nature. Esau was the image of hatred itself; but in God Himself, as in the spoken **Covenant of Grace** <note>original: "Gnadenbunde"</note>, He loves him.

53. Therefore, He places the image of Christ, as his brother Jacob, beside him, and let them both come from one seed. 54. Therefore, this is the understanding of Scripture: that the earthly Adam, in the realm of corrupt nature, does not and cannot find repentance in his own will; for there is no power for good within it. But the indwelling Grace awakens it when the will turns toward her. For if the self-will could work repentance and become godly on its own, it would have no need for Grace.

55. The **Decrees** <note>original: "Decreta"</note> of Scripture relate solely to the two kingdoms. For example, **hardening** <term>Verstockung: The state of a heart becoming "stiff" or "calloused" against God.</term> relates to the false will. The false will hardens itself; God’s Wrath in the will’s own essence hardens it. This is not something driving in from the outside, but something manifesting within the will’s own essence. The will is out of God, and that same God leads Himself into hardening within that will, in the same way He leads Himself into Hell, darkness, and pain <note>Böhme argues that "Hell" is not a place God sends people, but a state of being where God's presence is experienced as fire and wrath because of the soul's own internal state.</note>. The same is to be understood regarding the Kingdom of Grace.

56. God wills only good within man in the realm of His grace; when the free will yields itself to grace, then God wills good within that person through grace.

57. But to claim that man can [by his own strength] turn his will toward the good, as if toward grace, is a baseless claim <note>original: "Ungrund", meaning groundless or without foundation in truth.</note>. For grace already resides in the abyss of the **creature** <term>Creatur: The created being, specifically the human soul in its relationship to the Creator.</term> in all ungodly men; the will only needs to stand still from its false activity, and then it ceases to sink into the abyss of its own [selfish] willing.

58. For whatever stands still, stands still with the Eternal One; it becomes one essence with the One, for it enters into its "Nothing" <note>By "Nothing," Böhme refers to the state before individual desire, where the soul is at peace in God's unity.</note>. If the false will must stand still from [interfering with] right works for the sake of worldly laws and out of fear of punishment, why then not also for God’s sake? If a man can obey his worldly master and stand still wherever that master wishes him to be, why not also for God? Behold, the **ability** <note>original: "Können"</note> is immediately given, as soon as he leads the will only toward standing still.

59. But the reason that the entirely false, ungodly will does not stand still and turn toward grace is that it is already a born thistle <note>Böhme uses the thistle as a metaphor for a soul that has hardened itself in its own prickly nature.</note>, in which grace lies too deeply hidden, and the wrath of God is too strong in its nature. Grace draws him and shows him his falsehood, but he despises grace and acts like a thistle in the power of the sun. Thus God is a "good scent" <note>A reference to 2 Corinthians 2:15, where the same divine presence is a fragrance of life to some and a scent of death to those who perish.</note> leading to the condemnation of death in hell, so that grace may be distinguished from the false will.

It has no foundation either in the **Scripture** <note>original: "Schrifft"</note> or in the light of nature, provided one reads the Scripture correctly and does not look at it blindly.

61. For in God, insofar as He is called God, there is no [pre-determined] purpose nor beginning will. He is Himself the will of the **Unground** <term>Vngrundt: The primal, undifferentiated source of all being, before any "ground" or creation existed.</term> as a single unity, and He wills nothing but the good. Therefore He is Himself that very same willing; for the good that He wills is the birth of His power, as His Son <note>The "Son" here represents the manifestation of God’s power and love.</note>.

62. God wills nothing more in Himself than His own good, so that He might reveal Himself; and this could not happen if the single good substance did not introduce itself—through its out-breathing into desire—into nature and into distinctness as **Knowingness** <term>Scientz: Not "science" in the modern sense, but the inner root of perception or "knowingness" (from Latin *scientia*).</term>. For if the Good remained a single unity, there would be no [manifestation of His] works.

63. But now, the Good—as God in Himself—did not make itself evil...

# How Dinah was defiled by Hamor’s son /

The reader should pay close attention to this figure <note>Böhme uses "figure" (*Figur*) to mean a prophetic or allegorical type where Old Testament events mirror spiritual truths.</note>, and deeply contemplate the text in Moses and look it right in the eye; then he will well understand our meaning and the high, precious concept opened to us out of Divine Grace, and learn to see the writings of the First Book of Moses with the right eyes.

2. Leah, Jacob’s wife, bore Jacob six sons, who were half the tribe of Israel, and from her came Judah, as the root of David, from whom Christ was manifested according to our humanity. Afterward, she bore Dinah, a daughter. With this figure, the Spirit powerfully prefigures <note>original: "præfiguriret"</note> Christendom: that after Christ’s ascension, following the work of human redemption, the right and true Christendom would be born, just as Jacob first fathered the twelve patriarchs. But afterward, from Leah—that is, from the Mother of Christendom—a daughter of fleshly self-love <term>self-love: *Eigen-Liebe*, a core concept in Böhme's thought referring to the soul turning away from God to seek its own desires</term> would be born. This daughter would go out wandering to see the daughters of the land among whom she was supposed to be a stranger. This is the meaning within the figure:

3. When Christendom was born and its numbers became great, they would go into self-love and seek the lust of the flesh. They would direct their hearts according to the habits and customs of the nations and depart from lowliness and humility. They would want to visit the wantonness and pride of the daughters of the land—that is, of the worldly peoples. Then they would give birth to this daughter, Dinah, and commit spiritual harlotry <note>A common biblical metaphor for idolatry or worldliness.</note> in place of God’s fleshly lust. They would play the harlot with the customs of the heathens, yet they would present themselves as beautiful and adorned, like a maiden full of passion who runs out to show herself so that she might acquire suitors, just as Dinah did, who also wandered out in this way.

4. So also would Christendom adorn itself, decorating itself with great pomp with churches and schools, and putting on glinting, respectable, hypocritical clothes so that she might have a reputation before the daughters of the land (the foreign nations). Yet under such a habit <note>The "habit" refers to the outward religious dress or appearance.</note> she would be full of the passion of self-love and the addiction of the flesh, having a harlot’s heart. Just as a harlot glints on the outside and adorns herself, wanting by all means to be called a chaste virgin: so too would this adorned Christendom want to be called holy, but her heart would now flirt with fleshly lust.

5. She would indeed visit the ornament of the daughters of the land, which ornament is nothing other than heathen wisdom and philosophy <note>original: "Philosophia"</note>. They would pull these into Christ’s kingdom and, under Christ’s purple mantle, live in those same laws and customs and adorn themselves therewith. They would thereby entirely forget that their huts and dwellings are outside the

Even though Hamor and Shechem offered to pay the dowry <note>original: "Morgengabe," a traditional gift given by a husband to his bride</note>, marry their sister, live with them, undergo circumcision, and become one people—offering all love, loyalty, and <unclear>...</unclear> friendship—it all helped nothing.

11. And although they promised that if the men would be circumcised and become one people with them, they would give them their sister, they still became enraged with murdering and killing. This indicates that this story is a figure <note>A "figure" or "type" is a biblical event interpreted as a symbolic prophecy of future history.</note> of future Christendom which would arise from this lineage. We see this happening before our very eyes: people fight over "wandering" opinions and murder and kill one another for them. Yet this is done only for the sake of the opinion of the false harlot who has taken on the title of Christendom, where she parades in nothing but hypocrisy <term>hypocrisy: *Gleißnerey*, an outward shine or false appearance of holiness</term> and harlotry. They do not look to how their sister might be helped—she who has fallen into a foreign opinion—but instead, they reach for the sword and wish to kill the new opinion. They violently tear their sister, who is pregnant with another opinion along with her child of harlotry, back out of Hamor’s house, and they kill Hamor and Shechem along with all their men.

12. And even if they [the heathens] wish to unite with them upon the true Christian foundation, such as the main articles of Christian doctrine, it still avails nothing. 13. People of self-love have led their Christianity into a fleshly kingdom, adorning it beautifully with laws, ceremonies, and opinions, and covering it with Christ's purple mantle. 29. The ban <note>original: "Der Bann"—referring to the power of excommunication or spiritual condemnation</note> is your sword; however, let it be wielded in the power of the Holy Spirit in Divine Zeal against the godless, and let it not be directed toward protecting human trifles, such that one must call a spiritual harlotry in opinions a "chaste virgin," just as you, the **Babylonian Church**, have for a long time used such power only for that purpose.

30. All outward ceremonies without the inward foundation—that is, without **Christ’s** Spirit and cooperation—are a harlotry before God, in that a person wishes to make themselves God without the mediator **Christ**. For no one can serve **Christ** except a Christian, in whom **Christ’s** Spirit itself works within the service. But how will he serve **Christ** who carries the chalice of **Christ** in one hand and the sword of his own revenge in the other? Among Christians, **Christ** should blot out sin through his Spirit, and not the Father's fire-sword in the law of strict justice.

<margin>(Gen. 49)</margin>

31. O you children of **Levi** and **Simeon**, the Spirit indicated through **Jacob’s** end <note>Referring to Jacob’s deathbed prophecy in Genesis 49</note> that your swords are murderous weapons, and that **Christ** is not in your counsel; as **Jacob** said: My soul—that is, the covenant and the grace of **Christ**—is not in your churches, nor in your counsel. Just read the same passage (Genesis 49), where the counsel of the Pharisees and the scribes, who appoint themselves as shepherds without a Divine call, is thereby indicated.

32. All spiritual harlotry comes from the fact that **Christ’s** servants possess worldly power; thus one flatters the other. The lesser person outside of power flatters the powerful one so that he may also be elevated and brought to honor and fat days <note>A phrase meaning days of luxury or prosperity</note>. With this, the Zeal-Spirit <note>original: "Eyffer-Geist"—the spirit of holy passion or divine fervor</note> falls, and the truth is turned into lies; the mouth of the Zeal-Spirit is stopped by force, and a human being is honored in God’s place.

33. This history—how **Simeon** and **Levi** went into the city to **Hamor** and his children and strangled everything in this city that was male—is to be understood very well as a figure <note>Böhme uses "figure" to mean a prophetic type or symbolic representation</note> by which the Spirit indicates the future time, and was thus described as a figure.

34. The history also says that **Hamor**, together with his son **Shechem** and the whole city—all who were male—let themselves be circumcised and had become Jews, and only afterward did these two brothers, **Simeon** and **Levi**, murder them. This is truly a heavy figure for the understanding <note>meaning it is difficult for human reason to grasp</note> when reason thinks: could it have really happened this way, that two men murdered an entire city? But because it is a figure, and it was done by **Simeon** and **Levi** as the tribe and root of the Levite priesthood, and it points toward future Christendom, this is what is to be understood by it.

35. These two brothers agreed beforehand that if they [the Shechemites] would allow themselves to be circumcised and accept their laws, they would give them their sister; and afterward, when it was done, they slew them all—the innocent with the guilty. This is exactly what **Christ** said to the **Pharisees**: "Woe to you, **Pharisees**! You travel over land and sea to make a single convert <note>original: "Judengenoſſen"—literally a 'fellow of the Jews' or a proselyte</note>, and when he has become one, you make him a child of hell, twice as much as yourselves" <note>A reference to Matthew 23:15</note>.

36. So it could also be said of the **Christian Levites** <note>Böhme uses "Levites" as a term for the established priesthood or clergy of his day</note>, that they persuade peoples to allow themselves to be baptized and to call themselves Christians; and once that has happened, they thrust the murderous sword into their hearts, so that they learn to murder other peoples—who are not of their name and opinion—with words, to curse and damn them. Thus, they provide the cause for one brother to persecute, blaspheme, and condemn another, and to become hostile and bitter toward him, yet without understanding why. This is truly called: "This **Levite** promised me his sister as a wife because I have become a Christian, and now he murders me with false doctrine"—and not only me, but my entire lineage who merely listen to him and accept his blasphemy as divine, believing him that it is right for one human being to thus judge and condemn another. Yet **Christ** earnestly forbade this; by doing so, a person only judges themselves, since they do the very things they judge in others.

37. Thus, the murderous sword is thrust into many innocent hearts, so that they are innocently murdered by the **Levites**. But because **Simeon** and **Levi** are taken together—and **Jacob** also took them together when he prophesied about them at his end, calling them "murderous swords" <note>See Genesis 49:5-7</note>—it has this meaning: they would not only murder with the sword of the mouth <note>The "sword of the mouth" refers to verbal condemnation, excommunication, and hateful preaching</note>, but they would also place themselves in worldly power and physically kill others for the sake of the truth. They would do this precisely to those who were also under circumcision and under the **Gospel**, whom they had first persuaded to circumcision or to baptism.

38. This is how it has happened among the Christians: people were first persuaded to baptism, but afterward, when they saw the abominations of the clergy over time—that they lived worse than heathens—and did not wish to give them full approval in everything, then the persecution with fire and murderous swords began. They murdered them along with their innocent children, both in body and soul, which this figure of **Simeon** and **Levi** powerfully prefigures. 39. And the very greatest harlotry in this female concubine is this: that one leads the heart so completely away from God toward the servants of this concubine, and commits harlotry with them, and honors them with presents and gifts; so that they often praise evil, godless, haughty, greedy people—who only suck the poor dry and oppress them with violence—and they create great memorials and letters of praise, and give them grand <term>titles</term> <note>original: *Tituliren*; to bestow formal, high-sounding honors or positions.</note>, dressing them up highly, attributing great fear of God and love to them, setting them high in their lineages and tribes. In this way, they practice <term>trickery</term> <note>original: *Gauckeley*; deceptive or illusory behavior, like a magician's sleight of hand.</note> for the sake of money, like any other juggler, and shame God’s concubine—the Church—with hypocrisy and lies. That is truly what it means when it says: Reuben crept to his father’s concubine and committed harlotry with her. For it is they who should dwell with this concubine and be her guardians; but instead, they fill this concubine full of their false fleshly seed and bear children of harlotry in God’s concubine. Thus, the false lust of the flesh leads their heart entirely into them, and they think it counts before God and is right; their sins are thus covered by the poison of money, and they imagine this hypocrisy to themselves, so that they think they are better than others, and thus live on forever in such haughty thoughts, in such churchly harlotry.

40. And thus Reuben bears out of his father’s concubine—the Church—a heap of children of harlotry: proud, haughty, boastful, greedy people, who only defile the simple mother of humility and simplicity, **JESUS CHRIST**, as the <term>Lineage of Christ</term> <note>original: *Lineam Christi*; the spiritual path or genealogical "line" through which Christ is revealed in the soul.</note>, which lies hidden in this concubine and should be revealed and born; yet harlotry stands over her.

<summary>Böhme uses the biblical story of Reuben's infidelity to critique the corruption of the Church, arguing that those who focus on status, money, and external flattery are "fornicating" with the institution rather than finding Christ. He condemns the clergy who accept bribes to praise the wealthy, comparing such hypocrisy to bearing "children of harlotry" within the spiritual community.</summary>

<meta>This page continues Böhme’s mystical commentary on the book of Genesis, specifically the fall of Reuben. Having previously established Reuben as a symbol for the "first-born" or carnal religious man, Böhme now uses the biblical story of Reuben defiling his father’s concubine to launch a scathing critique of the corruption within the institutional Church of his day. He argues that the Church, which should be the dwelling place of Christ, has been turned into a place of pride, sectarianism, and the misuse of Holy Scripture.</meta>

<header>How Reuben committed harlotry with his father’s concubine</header>
<meta>Catchword: 43. This</meta>

And thus, God’s <term>concubine</term> <note>Böhme refers to the visible, external Church institution as a "concubine" to distinguish it from the "true, internal bride" or the spiritual Church.</note>, which is the Church, has been turned into a harlot and so greatly disgraced that her shame has come before Israel—that is, before the eyes of all God’s children—who spit upon her and regard her as an unclean, weakened harlot. In this place, such harlotry is practiced alongside all manner of pomp and haughtiness, for the Devil teaches and rules within her through <term>imagination</term> <note>In Böhme’s philosophy, "imagination" is the power of the mind to form itself into a specific desire or reality, often leading one away from God toward worldly lusts.</note> and false desires, more so than the Spirit of Christ. She is more a haughty harlot and a dark valley than a temple of JESUS CHRIST.

41. And what is even more loathsome: almost nothing but mere <term>passions</term> <note>original: "Affecten"; referring to uncontrolled emotions, biases, or sectarian zeal.</note> and insults are practiced and taught therein. People disgrace, persecute, and cry out "heresy!" against one another for the sake of mere opinions which each person has fashioned for themselves. They sow such poison in this "concubine" of the Church, whereby the simple-minded are led astray; and such poison of slander rises and grows in their hearts so that nothing but strife, quarreling, contempt, and blasphemy is taught and practiced in the Church. One brother despises, brands as a heretic, and condemns another to hellfire for the sake of his opinion, whereby all love, truth, and harmony are extinguished.

42. The greatest unchastity—at which even the heavens and the elements now tremble—which is practiced in this concubine of the Church, is this: that people even take the writings of the holy children of God, such as the Prophets and Apostles and those who followed them, and use them as a <term>cloak</term> <note>original: "Deckemantel"; a cover or justification for sinful behavior.</note> for such harlotry. They cite them falsely and embitter them, making mere sects and <term>fanaticism</term> <note>original: "Schwermereyen"; a derogatory term used during the Reformation for those deemed to have uncontrolled or "spirit-obsessed" religious views.</note> out of them. They use these writings to disgrace, insult, and persecute one another, even giving cause for war and bloodshed. The Bible is thus turned into a common, unchaste harlot, for everyone commits harlotry with her; they suck their own opinions out of her, and use her to despise, insult, and damn the opinions of others, yet they all take their justification from the Bible. In this way, they turn all their father’s concubines—the holy Prophets and Apostles—into harlots, and commit false harlotry with them. They practice only unchastity and pride with their writings and teach the laity their own lewdness and insults, so that one Christian learns from Holy Scripture how to insult another and how to gloss over their own malice with the writings of the Saints. This is truly what it means: "Reuben, you are my first strength, but you have climbed into my bed and defiled it with unchastity. You have used my concubine—my <term>formed Word</term> <note>Böhme views the scriptures as the "formed Word" of God, which is defiled when interpreted through human pride rather than divine love.</note>—for your harlotry, and have turned the Church of my children into a brothel, and have defiled my marriage bed, which I have in the Church where I beget my children."

<summary>Böhme interprets Reuben’s biblical sin as a metaphor for how contemporary religious institutions and "carnal" Christians misuse the Bible and the Church to fuel sectarianism, pride, and persecution.</summary>

43. This is clearly indicated by the Spirit of God in the interpretation of the patriarch **Jacob** (Genesis 49) when he speaks thus of this Church and her sacrifices: **Reuben, my first son, you are my first strength and my first power, the preeminent in sacrifice and the preeminent in the kingdom: He flowed away recklessly like water; you shall not be the preeminent: for you have climbed onto your father’s couch, and there you defiled my bed by your ascending.** <note>original: "Gen. 49"; this refers to Jacob's deathbed blessing and prophecy over his twelve sons.</note>

44. In this text, the Spirit speaks clearly: For **Reuben** signifies the order of the first Church, as the strength from which it was built; this is the first strength of the Christian community and is God’s **concubine** <term>concubine</term> <note>In Böhme's theology, the "concubine" refers to the external, visible church structure—holy and intended for God, yet distinct from the "Bride," which is the internal, spiritual soul-union with Christ.</note> in whom He dwells. But her servants have climbed into God's marriage-bed and pulled the concubine to themselves, taking her into their own power, and have made her pregnant with human trifles and the honors and lusts of the flesh. And it says clearly: **You are the preeminent in sacrifice and in the kingdom.** For so it should have been, had she not practiced harlotry. But because **Reuben** practices harlotry with the Church, he says: **You shall not be the preeminent.** For he flowed away recklessly like water, thereby showing how they would surrender themselves to self-love and the lust of the flesh, as well as to recklessness, and for that reason be rejected by God.

45. Thus the Spirit indicates under this figure how this concubine—the Church—would be desecrated by its first strength, namely its own children. It would be said of the Church that she is a **spiritual house of harlots**, from which one must distinguish the temple of **JESUS CHRIST**. For the Spirit says: **You shall not be the preeminent, neither in sacrifice nor in the kingdom.** Thus she has lost the true divine authority through the harlotry of her servants and now stands rightly as one put to shame, who has become a harlot. She is reviled by Israel <note>Here, "Israel" refers to the "true children of God" or the spiritual elect who recognize the corruption of the institution.</note> because of the unchastity practiced with her, and she is spat upon by almost everyone. Each party cries out that the other’s church is a house of harlots—as is plain enough to see—and all the bookstores are full of such shouting. We now stand in the midst of the storm, ready to storm that very house of harlots.

46. But to the children of God, this is said: the churches themselves do no one any harm; they were established by the first Christian strength with good intentions and would be very good and useful, needing no overturning, if only **Reuben** would cease from his harlotry with which he desecrates her. If only her servants were **renovated** and did not appoint themselves as servants of this concubine of God without the **anointing of the Holy Spirit**.

<summary>Böhme applies Jacob's prophecy regarding Reuben to the corruption of the contemporary Church, arguing that the clergy ("Reuben") have defiled the institution through pride and sectarianism, losing their divine authority. He notes that while the institutional Church has become a "house of harlots" through human misuse, the original intent of the Church remains good if its ministers were truly spirit-led.</summary>

# How God commanded Jacob to travel toward Bethel #

<margin>The "fifth wheel" of the church.</margin>
...as then happens, only for the sake of temporal honors and pleasure; such churches are as useful as a **fifth wheel** on a wagon—except that they drive their wagon with five wheels, where the fifth hovers in the air and descends into the abyss of hell with their quarreling. <note>The "fifth wheel" is a classic idiom for something redundant and useless. Böhme suggests that the external institutional trappings, when disconnected from true faith, are not only useless but lead to spiritual ruin through sectarian infighting.</note>

47. The stone house of the church has no greater holiness in itself than other houses, for it is built of stone like other houses, and God is not more powerful within it than in other houses. However, the **congregation** that enters and gathers there, uniting in prayer as one body in **Christ** (whom the church prefigures), holds the holy temple of **Jesus Christ** within itself.

48. Their song of praise is the cradle of the little child **Jesus Christ**; the infant **Jesus** is rocked with a unanimous voice in the hearts of men, and not in the physical structure of the church, which is silent.

49. Their ministers are nothing more than any other men; but the power exercised in the anointing of the **Holy Spirit** possesses the authority of the sacrifice and is the **key**. <term>the key</term> <note>This refers to the "Power of the Keys" (Matthew 16:19), the authority to forgive or retain sins, which Böhme argues belongs to the Spirit-led believer rather than just the institutional office.</note>

50. Whoever wishes to enter the church worthily must bring the temple of **Jesus Christ** in with them, or at least be of such a mind that they intend to carry Him out again in their heart. Otherwise, by entering and leaving, they have only committed a **spiritual, hypocritical harlotry**. <note>Böhme frequently uses "harlotry" as a biblical metaphor for spiritual infidelity or worshipping the "image" of religion rather than God Himself.</note> It would have been no less holy to stand in the market in their fine clothes to be seen by the people; then, perhaps, they would not have led so many pious hearts astray with their prideful display.

51. We have wished to indicate this by understanding this **figure** <term>figure</term> <note>In Böhme’s writing, a "figure" is a person or event from the Bible that serves as a symbolic pattern for spiritual truths.</note>: a Christian should not look at the outward appearance of the church, but realize that the church is only a **prefigurement** of Christ. One is not a Christian simply by entering the prefigurement and professing it. Rather, a Christian is one who enters fully into **Christ’s incarnation, suffering, and death**, dying to their own hypocrisy in Christ's death, and rising from that death with a new will and obedience. Such a person lives and exists in Christ in their innermost ground; they themselves become the temple of Christ, in whom Christ works with His power, thereby killing sin in the flesh. This is a Christian in Christ, and such a person may rightly enter the prefigurement and practice their Christianity there; they will hear God's Word and keep it in their heart.

52. And even if a **cowbell** <note>original: "Kühſchelle"</note> were to strike the name of God in its ringing, Christ would preach to him within himself. But no dead man can awaken another from death, nor can one blind man show the way to another—otherwise they both fall into the ditch, as Christ says.

53. Furthermore, the Spirit of Moses, in his figure <note>In Böhme’s writing, a "figure" is a symbolic representation where Old Testament people and events act as a "type" or mirror for spiritual and New Testament truths.</note>, presents the patriarch Isaac at his death and says: *And Jacob came to his father Isaac at Mamre in the chief city, which is called Hebron, where Abraham and Isaac had been strangers; and Isaac became 180 years old, and he declined and died, and was gathered to his people.* This is a figure of how Christ’s children are only foreign children in this pilgrimage <note>The "pilgrimage" refers to the earthly life of a believer, viewed as a temporary journey through a foreign land.</note>, and possess nothing as their own in the world, and finally all return to their first Father who created them, just as Jacob came back to his father before his end. ## The 64th Chapter.

### Concerning the 36th and 37th Chapters of Genesis. This is the beginning of the entirely beautiful figure of Joseph, Jacob’s son: what is to be understood by it?

The 36th chapter of Genesis is the genealogical register of the powerful tribe of Esau, showing how God gave him great riches and many children and grandchildren; and the Spirit sets down a large register and describes his children and grandchildren, showing how great princes came from them and possessed the splendor of the world. Yet, regarding Jacob, the Spirit says nothing of present worldly splendor, but speaks only of the future kingdom in the figure of Christ.

2. Here we see clearly how Esau stands in the figure of the Kingdom of Nature, and how the splendor of nature fell to him, and he became a great prince and fathered many princely tribes; and how God blessed him and made him great; and how the Holy Spirit recorded his lineage with special diligence to indicate that we should learn to correctly understand the figure of Jacob and Esau, and not proceed so blindly as to damn Esau to the abyss, as happens all too often. For we see how his father Isaac indicated a "fat dwelling" on earth for him, to whom God wished to give much temporal blessing. However, his figure in Adam’s nature must perish, and Christ must rise in him, so that from Esau the sow <note>The "sow" refers to the carnal, animalistic nature of the fallen man which Böhme believes must be purged so the spiritual "angelic" nature can emerge.</note> may be removed, and he may remain as an angel in the Eternal <note>original: "im E."; the abbreviation likely stands for *Ewigkeit* (Eternity).</note>, to which Christ wished to help him through the figure of Jacob.

14. This is thus the summary <note>original: "Summa"</note> of the explanation regarding Joseph’s history; but because it is so very rich, we wish to provide a thorough explanation of the entire text for the dear reader who intends to also become a "Joseph," as a guide: if he is earnest and reads this diligently, and contemplates and learns to know himself in this figure <note>original: "Figur"; Böhme uses this term to mean a symbolic or archetypal representation of spiritual truth</note>, then he will see of what spirit these writings were made: for he will find this pen in his heart.

15. The text says thus: Jacob dwelt in the land where his father had been a stranger, namely in the land of Canaan, and these are the generations of Jacob: Joseph was seventeen years old when he became a shepherd of the cattle with his brothers, and the lad was with the children of Bilhah and Zilpah, his father’s wives; and he brought an evil report <note>original: "böse Geschrey"; literally an "evil cry" or "bad noise," referring to Joseph reporting his brothers' misconduct.</note> of them to their father. But Israel loved Joseph more than all his brothers, because he had fathered him in his old age, and he made him a colorful robe: Now when his brothers saw that their father loved him more than all his brothers, they were hostile toward him and could not speak a friendly word to him.

->The inner figure stands thus:<-

16. Jacob had cast his carnal, natural love upon Rachel because she was beautiful; but because the line of Christ <note>original: "linea Christi"</note> lay in the Covenant within Jacob, Rachel was closed up, so that his seed was not manifested in her in the manner of natural flesh until Jacob and Rachel had grown old and both no longer loved each other according to carnal love, but only desired a fruit of their seed. Therefore Jacob and Rachel prayed to God that He would open her and make her fruitful; and when this happened, there arose from this seed of Jacob a line, and it formed a figure of 
<margin>note</margin>
pure, natural, truly Adam-like humanity <note>Böhme refers here to the state of humanity before the Fall of Adam, which he believes is restored through spiritual rebirth</note>, born in the figure of how Christ would once again give birth to the Adam-like humanity in its original discipline, purity, and fear of God.

17. For in Leah—as in simplicity and lowliness—the line of Christ sprouted; and in Rachel, the line of the first Adam-like man in his innocence, as a figure of the same. This figure stood as a Christian would stand in Christ’s image and in Adam’s image at the same time, and what a Christian would be in this world from within and without, and how he must become a Christian. Therefore the text says: Jacob loved Joseph more than all his children: for the cause was this, that Joseph sprang from Jacob’s own natural line—from the natural love toward Rachel—within which the line in the love of Christ in the Covenant had incorporated itself.

Through this, human nature would become **multi-colored** (that is, mingled with God), joining the inner spiritual kingdom with the outer world.

36. Joseph with his multi-colored coat was a youth; moreover, he was tender and young, and did not yet possess the world's wisdom and cunning. 37. This figure now prefigures for us the image of a **beginning Christian**; it shows how he must be if God’s Spirit is to move him. Namely: He must turn his heart toward God his Father and learn to love Him heartily, just as Joseph was glad to be near his father and reported what evil happened among his children. In the same way, a beginning Christian must daily bring all his own injuries and those of his people—as well as those of all Christendom—before God. Just as Daniel confessed the sins of **Israel** before God, and Joseph reported the harm of his brothers to his father, so too a true Christian daily confesses the misery and sin of his people with heartfelt compassion, praying that God might have mercy on them and protect them from great evil and sin.

38. And when this happens, his heart becomes quite simple, pious, and righteous; for he desires no cunning, but wants everything to go rightly and well, and all injustice is repugnant to him. Because he constantly confesses the injustice of the people before God, his mind becomes entirely simple <note>In Böhme's writing, "simplicity" (Einfalt) is a virtue meaning a heart that is "one-fold" or focused solely on God, as opposed to the "multi-fold" cunning of the world.</note> and seeks no cunning; rather, he places his hope in God and lives in simplicity and the humility of his heart before God and the world. He is like the tender young child Joseph, for he forever hopes for the good from God his Father.

39. When a person reaches this point, then "fair Joseph is born." Then God his Father clothes his soul with the **multi-colored coat**—which is to say, with **Divine Power**. Then the Spirit of God immediately begins to play <note>Böhme uses the concept of "Divine Play" (Göttliches Spiel) to describe the joyful, non-toilsome communication between God and the human soul.</note> with the soul, as He did with Joseph. For the Spirit of God looks through the soul and with the soul (just as Joseph saw future things in the vision of dreams through prefigurations, when the Spirit thus played with his soul). In this way, the Spirit of God immediately plays with the soul of a "new Joseph" within the inner spiritual world, so that the soul understands Divine mysteries and sees and recognizes **Eternal Life** and the hidden world, which [is found] in the human...
