->This figure stands thus:<-

17. The God of Love blessed the embodied covenant of grace <note>The "Covenant of Grace" refers to God’s promise of salvation, which Böhme believes was physically "implanted" or "embodied" into the human lineage leading to Christ.</note>, from which *Christ*, as the heavenly *Joseph*, was to come; just as *Jacob* here began his blessing with *Joseph* and blessed *Joseph’s* sons through *Joseph*: so also does God bless the soul and the spirit through the name of *JESUS*, for God has set the name of *JESUS* before Him as a throne of grace; and through this same throne of grace He blesses *Christ’s* children and members according to their humanity. Here, in the words of the blessing, He made no distinction between the children, to signify that the soul should enjoy the same grace and gifts as the spirit in *Christ*; yet He gave the power to the new rebirth <term>Rebirth: The process by which the "faded" heavenly image in man is restored through divine power.</term> out of the faded heavenly image, so that the soul should work through the power of this new rebirth, and spread itself out and become great with it—that is, that the soulish tree with its branches should grow out of this blessing.

18. Within the words of this blessing lies such an understanding: the embodied covenant of grace, by the power of the Word, spoke forth the power, and gathered in *Jacob* his body, soul, and spirit into one, and through him spoke itself upon the children of *Joseph*: "God, before whom my fathers *Abraham* and *Isaac* walked"—that is, through the will which my fathers directed toward God, with which they walked before God. Also: "by the power of God which has nourished me my whole life long until this day." Also: "the Angel who has redeemed me from all evil, bless the boys"—that is, he blessed them through Divine and human power through the Angel of the Great Counsel <note>original: "Engel des grossen Raths." A traditional title for Christ in Lutheran theology, derived from the Septuagint version of Isaiah 9:6.</note> in *Christ JESUS*, which Angel has redeemed man from all evil, so that they should be named after this name as children of God’s covenant, and grow and become great in this power.

19. But when *Joseph* saw that his father laid his right hand on *Ephraim’s* head, it displeased him, and he took hold of his father’s hand to move it from *Ephraim’s* head to *Manasseh’s* head, and said to him: "Not so, my father; this is the firstborn; lay your right hand on his head." But his father refused and said: "I know it, my son, I know it; he shall also become a people and shall be great; but his younger brother shall become greater than he, and his seed shall become a great people."

With the external figure <note>A "figure" in Böhme’s writing is a symbolic or prophetic representation of a deeper spiritual truth.</note>, the Spirit points toward their descendants, showing which tribe would surpass the other in size and power. But with the internal figure—concerning the reversal and new birth of man—He looks toward the inner ground <term>Ground (Grund): The deepest, most fundamental essence of a person's being or soul.</term>, showing how the inner and youngest ground of embodied grace in Christ would be greater than the ground of the first-created Adamic man.

21. However, because *Joseph* resists this and is not pleased that the youngest was placed before the eldest, this is also part of the figure: *Joseph* stood in the figure of the new rebirth. It signifies how, in the humanity of *Christ*, the inward ground—as the Eternal-speaking Word—should turn itself outward through our soul and take away the soul’s own power of self-will. The creaturely soul <note>The "creaturely soul" refers to the individual human ego or self-will that exists as a created being, distinct from God.</note> did not want this; it did not want to lose its power. It did not want to submit to the death of its own will, but rather desired to keep its first natural right.

22. We see this in the humanity of *Christ*, specifically in the human soul, when it was time for it to die to its selfhood and surrender its natural right; thus *Christ* spoke on the Mount of Olives:

> Father, if it be possible,

that is, the human soul in Him spoke out of the Father’s property <note>original: "Eigenschafft" — refers to the specific qualities or characteristics of the Father's nature.</note> within the Word:

> Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me; yet if it is not possible that I drink it, then let Your will be done. <note>A translation of the German rendering of Matthew 26:39 and 26:42.</note>

Just as here, *Joseph*, in this figure, was not happy to see the last preferred over the first.

23. The text says:

> It displeased him.

It displeases the natural man that he must surrender his natural right and allow the Kingdom of Humility to rule within him. He would rather be master himself. But his own will has forfeited this right, so that he is placed behind. For it is not possible for him to become God’s child unless he drinks the cup through which he dies to his own natural will. Therefore *Christ* said:

> Father, Your will be done, and not my natural Adamic human will; rather, let God’s will be done in my inward ground, and not the will of my Adamic soul.

The soul must be surrendered <term>Gelassenheit: A state of "letting go" or yieldedness to God's will.</term> into God; the first natural right must follow behind, and *Christ* must go before, otherwise there is no salvation.

24. With this image, the Spirit of God played among the children of the saints, showing how the new, embodied Kingdom of Grace would soar upward, and how the Kingdom of Nature would be set behind. For when *Christ* arises and is born within a human being, then *Adam* must be the servant and minister.

### And how he set the youngest before the oldest.

And the covenant has a piece of land in this world that would be a dwelling of Christendom on Earth at all times, even if that same piece of land would often be moved from one place to another with Manasseh and Ephraim.

## IV. The Testament of Judah.

38. Judah, you are he; your brothers shall praise you: Your hand shall be upon the neck of your enemies; your father's children shall bow before you. Judah is a young lion; you have come up high, my son, through great victory. He has stooped down and couched like a lion, and like a lioness; who shall rouse him? The scepter shall not be taken from Judah, nor a master from his feet, until the Hero <note>original: "Held." This refers to the "Shiloh" of Genesis 49:10, whom Böhme interprets as Christ the Victorious Hero.</note> comes, and to Him shall the people cling. He will bind his foal to the grapevine, and his donkey’s son to the noble vine. He will wash his garment in wine, and his cloak in the blood of grapes. His eyes are redder than wine, and his teeth whiter than milk.

39. In the case of the first three sons of Jacob, the Spirit points to the corrupted Adam and his children—how they were before God and what their kingdom on earth would be. But here, with Judah, he begins to point toward the kingdom of Christ, toward Christ’s Person and Office. He places Christ in the fourth line, which is a great mystery: for in the "fourth property" <note>In Böhme’s complex theosophy, the "fourth property" is the Lightning-Flash or Fire, where the dark, desiring qualities of nature are transformed into the light of the divine majesty.</note> of the birthing of nature, the fire is understood as the origin of fire, out of which the Light takes its origin. Through this, the Unground <term>Ungrund: The "Groundless" or "Abyss," referring to the absolute, unmanifested Godhead before creation</term> becomes Majestic, and within it, the origin of Life is understood—especially the Soul, which is understood there according to its specific property.

40. Because this soulful ground had fallen and been corrupted in Adam, God placed His "figure" <note>An archetypal pattern or prophetic representation.</note> with the new life within it. This figure stands in this Testament of the twelve Patriarchs, showing how the beginning of life is, and how the New Birth greens forth again in the Light through the corrupted fire-life. Also, in the Testament of Judah, all circumstances are indicated: how the new life in Christ would green forth through the soul and rule over the sting of death.

# IV. The Testament of Judah.

38. **Judah, you are he; your brothers shall praise you: Your hand shall be upon the neck of your enemies, before you your father’s children shall bow: Judah is a young lion, you have come up high, my son, through great victory. He has knelt down and couched himself like a lion, and like a lioness; who will rouse him? The scepter shall not be taken from Judah, nor a teacher** <note>original: "Meister." Often translated as "lawgiver" or "ruler's staff" in standard Bibles.</note> **from between his feet, until the Hero** <note>original: "Heldt." Refers to the Messiah/Shiloh.</note> **comes, and to him shall the nations cling: He will bind his foal to the vine, and his donkey’s son to the noble branch: He will wash his garment in wine, and his mantle in the blood of grapes: his eyes are redder than wine, and his teeth whiter than milk.**

39. With the first three sons of Jacob, the Spirit points toward the corrupted Adam and his children, how they were before God and what their kingdom on earth would be. But here with Judah, he begins to point toward the Kingdom of Christ, as toward Christ’s Person and Office, and places Christ in the fourth line, which is a great mystery; for in the fourth property of the generation of nature, the fire—as the origin of fire—is understood, out of which the light takes its origin, whereby the Abyss <term>Ungrund: Böhme's central concept of the "Groundless" or primordial nothingness/potentiality from which God and the universe emerge</term> becomes majestic; therein also the origin of life is understood, and especially the soul is understood there according to its property.

40. Because this soulful ground had fallen and been corrupted in Adam, God also placed His figure with the new life therein; and the figure stands in this Testament of the 12 Patriarchs <note>original: "Erzvätter."</note> as to how the beginning of life is, and how the new birth sprouts forth again through the corrupted fiery life into the light. Also, in the Testament of Judah, all circumstances are indicated as to how the new life in Christ would sprout forth through the soul and rule over the sting of death.

41. **Jacob said: Judah, you are he / Your brothers shall praise you:**
<margin>Chapter 76.</margin>
By this he looks outwardly upon the earthly kingdom which was to begin in the future; and inwardly he looks upon the Kingdom of Christ, which both the Jews and Gentiles would receive, and would praise and honor Christ as both God and man.

42. **And he says further: For your hand shall be upon the neck of your enemies:** by this he understands not only the external enemies of the Jews, but how the "Hand"—being the power of Christ’s grace—would essentially <note>original: *Essentialiter*; in its very essence or being</note> and effectively be upon the neck of Satan, the serpent’s venom, and the self-will in flesh and blood; and how in his children of faith, he would forever tread upon the head of that same serpent.

43. **Likewise: Before you your father’s children shall bow; that is:** before this Christ from the tribe of Judah, all of God’s children would bow, bend, and worship him as a God-Man and Man-God.

44. **Likewise: Judah is a young lion; that is: a roar against the Devil, and a breaker of death and hell, just as a spirited, young, fresh lion is mighty in power.**

45. **Likewise: You have come up high, my son, through great victory; that is:** after he has triumphed over God’s wrath, over death, sin, the Devil, and hell, he has, as a man, sat down at the right hand of the power of God and rules over all his enemies.

46. **Likewise: He has knelt down and couched himself like a lion and like a lioness; who will rouse him?** That is: He has humbled himself so deeply with his highest love, and in his assumed humanity, gave himself into the mockery and contempt of fallen man; he knelt down into God’s wrath and allowed the natural human life to be broken, and very patiently gave his strong lion’s power into it.

47. **But where the text says: "like a lion and like a lioness":** the young lion signifies the Divine Word in the soul, and the lioness signifies the name JESUS <note>original: IESV</note> in the innermost ground of the heavenly world-being, as the noble lioness Sophia <note>In Böhme's mysticism, Sophia represents Divine Wisdom, the feminine counterpart to the Word, who was lost to man at the Fall and is reunited with the soul through Christ.</note>; that is, the true Seed of the Woman from the Adamical Light Tincture <note>A "Tincture" in Böhme’s terminology refers to a transformative spiritual essence or life-force that gives quality and color to being.</note>, which faded in Adam and became alive again in this Lion through Divine power, and joined itself again to the Lion as to the soul.

48. **Likewise: Who will rouse him? That is:** who can stand up against this Lion and heavenly holy Lioness, who is God over and through all things? Who will take the power from him who is the beginning of all strength and might? Where is there a hero who can fight where there is no higher power?

49. **Likewise: The scepter shall not be taken from Judah, nor a master from between his feet, until the Hero <note>original: *Heldt*; in most Bible translations this refers to "Shiloh," interpreted here as the Messiah or Hero</note> comes, and to him shall the nations cling:** This understanding is twofold: first, outwardly regarding the Kingdom of Judah, meaning that the Jewish scepter of their kingdom should endure, and they should remain a kingdom until this Hero—as the lion with the lioness, as Christ—became the **Covenant-Man** <note>the union of the divine and human in the person of Jesus</note>. This indeed came to pass, for they retained their kingdom—even though it was often entirely devastated—until Christ's time; then it ceased entirely, and another Master now rules them, for since that time they must be a subject people. For the Hero has taken over their kingdom and has thereby stepped among the Gentiles and called them also to himself.

50. The inner ground is this: that the Kingdom of Christ, with his dominion over sin, death, the Devil, and hell, would not cease, nor would another ruler or master come from between his feet—that is, from the **Covenant of God**—until this Hero, Christ, should come again for the Judgment and separate his enemies. Then he shall deliver the kingdom back to his Father, so that God may be all in all. Therefore, the Jews hope in vain for another Master, although he will indeed come to them at the time of his revelation, which is near, when the Kingdom of Christ shall be revealed to all nations.

51. **Likewise: to him shall the nations cling:** This occurred after his incarnation and will occur even more in his final revelation, so that all nations shall cling to him and recognize him. When **Babel** <note>In this context, "Babel" represents the confusion of warring religious sects and corrupt institutional power</note> meets its end, then this shall first be fully fulfilled. Currently, the "images" and sects at Babel prevent this clinging, so that the foreign nations are offended by the squabbling of the confused languages and stay away.

52. But when the Tower of Babel falls, then all nations shall cling to him, honor him, and serve him. This "clinging" has been hindered by a supposed Christendom under the **Antichrist**, who for a long time has sat in Christ’s place as an earthly god. When he ceases to be, the Kingdom of Christ will be fully revealed, which at present is seen only in "images" <note>symbolic or outward forms rather than spiritual reality</note> by those with better understanding.

His eyes are now the fire-flaming love which penetrates through the Father’s wrath <note>In Böhme’s system, God’s "wrath" is the raw, fiery power of existence, which is only made "light" and "love" through the birth of the Son.</note> and sees through the fiery soul, wherein the Father’s wrath in the fiery soul has become a light-flaming fire of love. Thus the soul’s essence has become a sweet, pleasant-tasting, divine, red wine of love, where one quality in the soul’s essence tastes the other in great desire of love, and the Father’s quality of wrath wells up into a pure, good taste.

<margin>64. And his teeth are whiter than milk:</margin> These white teeth are the desire of the inner spiritual man, for the Holy Word is present within the desire of these teeth. These white teeth of heavenly desire grasp, eat, and drink the body and the blood of grapes of Christ; for this is the spiritual mouth to which Christ has ordained his testament, that it should eat his flesh and drink his blood with these white teeth. The Spirit in the Covenant through Jacob indicates this clearly and brightly.

65. For the testament of Judah refers entirely to Christ—to his person, office, and kingdom—since Christ was to come from Judah according to his humanity. Outwardly stands the figure of the prototype, but inwardly, within the spiritual figure, Christ stands clearly revealed.

## Chapter 77.

# Further Explanation of Jacob's Testament / concerning the other 8 sons / how both the Jewish rule or kingdom on Earth / and also Christendom are prefigured therein / and how it would fare with them.

->Genesis 49.<-

With the first three sons of Jacob <note>Reuben, Simeon, and Levi, whom Böhme previously associated with the corruption of the human will and the "Adamic" fallen state.</note>, the figure represents the realm of corrupted nature—prefigured as the Adamic man—what he is; and with Judah, Christ is prefigured, who was to come and bring the Adamic man into His kingdom. But with the other eight sons of Jacob, the figure of worldly offices and estates is now prefigured: how the Adamic man would hold the high rule, and how the inner figure of Christ’s kingdom would always stand alongside it.

2. For here, in the outer figure, it is first prefigured where each tribe would have its dwelling, and what its office in Israel would be. But alongside this, the figure always remains of how the outer and inner man would stand together; how the kingdom of nature and the kingdom of grace would dwell together, and how the seven properties of nature <term>Seven Properties; Böhme’s central mystical framework describing the qualities—such as contraction, friction, and fire—that form both the material world and the soul</term> in the wrath of God according to the first principle <term>First Principle; the dark, fiery source of divine power that serves as the foundation of all existence</term> would also unfold and lead into the figure of divine contemplation. Let the reader pay heed to this, for we wish to explain both the inner and the outer figure.

### V. The Testament of Zebulun.

3. Zebulun shall dwell at the haven of the sea and at the haven of ships, and reach unto Sidon. This is first the outer figure, where this tribe would dwell in the Promised Land; but the Spirit also has its inner figure, upon which it gazes.

4. For Zebulun, in the Language of Nature <term>Language of Nature; Böhme’s concept of a primordial language where the sound and structure of words reveal the inner essence of the things they name</term> in its sense, means a desire that goes toward God, which dwells with the Good; and it indicates here how the Adamic man would dwell near to God, and how he would have delight and refreshment from the divine presence. For Jacob fathered Zebulun by Leah, who was otherwise held in low esteem, because she was weak-eyed and not as beautiful as Rachel. But Leah directed her hope toward God, that He would bless her so she might be fruitful and bear children to her husband Jacob.

<summary>Böhme begins interpreting the blessings of the remaining eight sons of Jacob, explaining how they represent the coexistence of worldly governance and spiritual grace. He specifically identifies Zebulun as a symbol of the human desire for God residing within a humble, earthly nature.</summary>

5. When she [Leah] now gave birth to Zebulun, she said: God has well counseled me <note>original: "Gott hat mich wol berahten." Leah’s naming of Zebulun is traditionally linked to the Hebrew *zabal*, meaning to dwell or honor.</note>; that is, I have turned my desire toward Him and He has fulfilled it for me. Now His will dwells with mine; and she called him "Inhabitation" <note>original: "Beywohnung." Böhme uses this to describe a state of living together or cohabitation.</note>, which is to say: God dwells with me, and now my husband will also dwell with me in love. This indicates how the grace of God, in His mercy, would dwell with the poor, corrupted Adamic children of the flesh and not abandon them in their misery.

6. Furthermore, this points toward the Covenant: that the children of the Covenant, in their Adamic nature, will only be a "nearby inhabitation" in hope. The outer man <term>Outer Man; in Böhme’s thought, the physical, earthly part of a human that belongs to this world and cannot enter the spiritual kingdom</term> would not grasp the Kingdom of Christ, but would be a nearby dwelling, while Christ would dwell in the inner ground <term>Inner Ground; the spiritual center of the soul where the divine presence resides</term>, as if in the spiritual world, while the Adamic man remains in this time; and yet, it would be a dwelling-together.

7. For just as the Spirit pointed toward Christ in the flesh through Judah, He shows here that our outer man shall not be Christ, but rather a dwelling place for Christ. Christ would possess the inner ground, as He also says: *My kingdom is not of this world* <note>John 18:36</note>. Therefore, the outer mortal man shall not say of himself, "I am Christ." He is only a dwelling for Christ, just as the outer world is only a dwelling for the Kingdom of Christ; for Christ is the inner spiritual world, hidden within the outer visible world, just as the day is hidden in the night, and yet one dwells with the other.

## VI. The Testament of Issachar.

8. *Issachar will be a bony ass* <note>Genesis 49:14. But the powerful figure looks toward the inward ground, toward human nature.

9. Indeed it was so; but in the inner figure <note>original: "innern Figur." 12. 6. Furthermore, it looks toward the Covenant: that the children of the Covenant, in their Adamic nature, will only be a "near-dwelling" in hope. The outer man would not seize the Kingdom of Christ, but would be a "near-dwelling" <note>A place where something resides temporarily or alongside something else.</note> where Christ would dwell in the inner ground <term>Inner ground or "innern Grundt"; in Böhme's thought, the deepest part of the soul where the divine light shines.</term>—as if in the spiritual world—while Adam <note>Representing fallen humanity.</note> dwells in this time; and yet, it would be a cohabitation.

7. For as the Spirit has pointed to Christ in the flesh through Judah, so He points here to the fact that our outer man will not be Christ, but a "dwelling-with" for Christ. Christ would possess the inner ground, just as He says: *My Kingdom is not of this world.* Therefore, the outer, mortal man shall not say of himself, "I am Christ." He is only a dwelling for Christ, just as the outer world is only a dwelling for the Kingdom of Christ; for Christ is the inner spiritual world, hidden within the outer visible world, just as the day is hidden in the night, and yet one dwells with the other.

### VI. The Testament of Issachar.

8. *Issachar will be a bony donkey and lie down between the borders; and he saw the rest, that it was good, and the land, that it was pleasant. But he bowed his shoulders to bear and became a tributary servant.* <note>Genesis 49:14-15. Böhme uses the phrase "beinern Esel" (bony donkey) to emphasize the heavy, material nature of the physical body.</note> In this Testament of Issachar, the Spirit first points to the external figure of this tribe and where they should dwell—namely, in the middle of the land, in good rest, yet remaining subject to tribute. However, the powerful figure <note>The "powerful figure" refers to the deeper, spiritual significance beyond the literal history.</note> looks toward the inward ground, toward human nature.

9. For when Leah bore Issachar, she said, "God has rewarded me because I have given my maid to my husband," and she called him Issachar, as a Divine reward or return-gift: for she had given the mandrakes <note>original: "Dudaim." According to Genesis 30, Leah traded her son's mandrakes to Rachel in exchange for a night with Jacob.</note> of her son to Rachel so that she would let Jacob sleep with her that night, from which she became pregnant with this son; thus she called him a return-gift from God.

In Böhme's writing, this refers to the seat of the soul's will and desires.</note> between the borders, as if between the Kingdom of God and the kingdom of this world; his mind presses into the border of God, and the body dwells in the world.

11. Thus the mind must be like a bony, servant donkey which—although it sits in a good rest and dwelling at the border of God—must still carry the burden of sin and death in the earthly sack. There is no buying one's way out with the mandrakes <note>original: "Dudaum." Refers to the mandrakes mentioned in Genesis 30, associated with the birth of Issachar; Böhme suggests that even "holy" earthly things cannot ransom the body from death.</note> for the death of the earthly man; nor does asking God help to bring the bony donkey to Divine freedom. It must remain a donkey until Christ leads it into Himself, into the Eternal Rest. The Adamic damage <note>The corruption resulting from the Fall of Man.</note> is too great; the donkey must leave the sack in the death of Christ, otherwise it will never be rid of it.

12. But he sets forth the reasons why it must remain a bony donkey, for he says: *He saw that the rest was good, and the land that it was pleasant*; that is, that the mind will always want to rest in the lust of the flesh and will desire to indulge in earthly pleasure. Therefore, the mind must be a servant donkey and a servant of God’s wrath. He thus separates the natural Adamic man from the Seed of the Covenant (as from the person of Christ), stating that the natural Adamic man in his innate nature is only this donkey with the sack, until Christ possesses His kingdom within him. Here, neither Covenant nor prayer helps: *Adam remains a donkey in this world until the sack is gone*; only then is he called a new child in Christ. This new child is, in this time, the inner ground <term>The "inner ground" (inwendige Grundt) is the spark of the divine soul that remains connected to God despite the Fall.</term>. But the bony donkey is the tool of the new child upon which the sack is carried, for the servitude to the wrath of God lasts as long as the sack is present.

# Further Explanation of Jacob’s Testament

The Spirit speaks: Dan shall be a judge in his people, as another tribe in Israel.

->In the figure, it stands thus:<-

14. In the figure, Dan represents all external administrators of office, from the highest authority down to the governance of man's own life; thus the Spirit speaks of him: He shall exist in his own power like any other man among others. Before God, he is esteemed no greater in his nature than a servant, for he serves God in his office just as any other servant serves his master. The office is God’s, in which he sits as a judge. The office is the authority, and he himself is before God like any other man.

15. But the Spirit speaks: "Dan shall be a serpent upon the way and an adder upon the path" <note>Genesis 49:17. Böhme interprets the "way" as the path of divine justice and the "serpent" as the corruption of that office.</note>; that is, these judges in God's offices will draw poison from their authority, acting as their own will, and saying of themselves: "The power is mine; I am the office." This is what it means to be "upon the way," for the way they are meant to walk is God’s—namely, true justice. Thus Dan says: "The land, the city, the village, the estate, the money is mine; it is my own property; I will use it for my own benefit and honor, and live in this office however I wish."

<margin>steps</margin>
16. And this very I-ness <term>Ichheit: A central concept in Böhme’s philosophy referring to the ego or the self-centered will that has turned away from God to serve itself.</term> is the serpent and poisonous adder upon the path, for it takes nothing but harmful steps upon the path of justice. It turns justice into "Mine-ness" <term>Meinheit: The possessive drive to claim the world and its inhabitants as personal property rather than God's creation.</term>, so that the self may do whatever it wants. It says: "I am a lord; the city, land, village, and power are mine; I may do with the people as I wish, they are mine." And thus, it sucks nothing but poison from God's office of judgment, and through this, it torments the wretched and strikes out all around itself with this poison on the path of the office, like an adder and a serpent.

17. For the Spirit speaks: "He will bite the horse in the heels, so that its rider falls backward"; that is, he will bite the horse—which is the office he rides upon—in the heel, which is justice. This causes Justice, as the Rider of God whom he is meant to carry, to fall backward, so that he may rule in the place of justice as a "rider of God" in name only. Thereupon, the Rider of Justice speaks in his office: "LORD, I wait for your salvation" <note>original: "Heyl." Refers to the "salvation" or "healing" brought by the Messiah.</note>; that is, until you send the true Rider, Christ, who shall ride again over the adder and the serpent.

## VIII. The Testament of Gad.

26. Gad, being equipped, will lead the army and lead it back again: This figure <term>Figur: A symbolic or prophetic type that represents a deeper spiritual reality.</term> does not merely prefigure that the children of Gad should be nothing but army leaders, just as Dan’s children were not merely judges. Instead, it plays out a spiritual figure, which can also be seen in Leah, who also gave her maid to Jacob when she ceased to bear children, wishing to hurry and get ahead of Rachel. For Gad was born of Zilpah and was meant to precede Dan; for she said, "Vigorously, turn yourself before him and call out to me." This indicates human foresight, such as cunning and false cleverness, which would use every trick to precede right and justice and would soar above all truth and law.

27. For Gad and Dan are both from the handmaids, and in the figure they represent a conflict; for Rachel and Leah each wanted to get ahead of the other, and therefore their path was a total contrast. This figure also stands: Whenever DAN wishes to judge, Gad comes with his cunning speed and slips away from his office.

33. Naphtali is a swift deer and gives beautiful speeches. Naphtali is the second son of Bilhah / Rachel’s maid / whom she bore after Dan / and is a true brother to Dan: This brother Naphtali is now found among the judges and kings / and signifies the earthly wisdom from the stars <note>original: "Jrdische Weißheit vom Gestirne." The author suggests that human intellect and rhetoric are influenced by the celestial bodies, belonging to the physical world rather than the divine spirit.</note> / which adorns the judicial office with decorative, beautiful speeches / so that Dan, Gad, and Asher may be called wise, understanding lords.

34. But he also comes only from the struggle between Rachel and Jacob / For Rachel said when Bilhah her maid bore him / "God has wrestled for me <note>A reference to Genesis 30:8; the name Naphtali is derived from the Hebrew word for wrestling.</note> against my sister / and I shall prevail over her": this signifies in the figure / that these wise speeches of Naphtali in this judicial office would be able to bend and turn all matters / so that the self-will of the judges would remain the master of all things / so that no one, because of these four "laws" of the bondwomen’s sons / would be able to achieve anything / but they would have the governance in Israel and rule the world / and prevail over all men.

35. But they are all only the four sons of the bondwomen: And Sarah said to Abraham / "Cast out the son of the bondwoman / for he shall not inherit with my son Isaac" / and God was pleased with this / and commanded Abraham to do it / to signify / that these offices shall not inherit nor possess the <term>Kingdom of Christ</term> <note>The spiritual realm of grace and rebirth, which the author contrasts with worldly legal and political structures.</note> / but shall have their end / when Christ, as the Son of the Free Woman / shall take up the Kingdom / then all these estates shall be cast out / and He alone / in his children and members, shall rule.

36. In this mirror, look at yourself now, you clever / highly-wise / understanding world / in your cleverness / eloquence / favor / power and honors / and see where you sit / and whom you serve: behold your rich bread / likewise the praise of kings / whom you serve / and what you do and intend / how you stand in your figure before God and the Kingdom of Christ; your eloquence is worth nothing before God / your cleverness and cunning also nothing / if you do not counsel rightly / and speak and do the truth / and [serve] your sovereign...

## XI. The Testament of Joseph.

37. ## XII. The Testament of Benjamin.

48. *Benjamin is a ravening wolf/ in the morning he shall devour the prey/ but in the evening he shall divide the spoil:* Benjamin was Joseph’s biological brother/ and yet the Spirit says of him: He is a ravening wolf/ who shall devour prey in the morning: In this Testament of Benjamin lies the most secret figure <note>A "figure" or "type" is a person or event in the Bible that foreshadows a later spiritual reality.</note> of the entire Scripture/ and yet in its image/ as it unfolds in practice/ it is the most manifest figure/ which stands so clearly in its fulfillment/ that one sees it with physical eyes/ and yet one remains completely blind to it through mere reason.

49. This figure is fulfilled / and is still in process and shall yet be fulfilled / it is both as hidden and yet as manifest as the sunshine at midday / and yet it is not understood: But to the Magi <note>Wise men or spiritual seekers who understand the hidden mysteries of nature and God.</note> and the Wise it is known / who indeed have written much about it / but have never yet rightly unwrapped it / because the time of evening / when the spoil of Benjamin is to be divided / was still far off / but now is near: so we shall outline something of this / and give our own people the sense to think upon it / and yet also remain silent to the unwise / because they sit in darkness and only open their maws for prey.

50. The two brothers Joseph and Benjamin are the image of Christendom / and of a Christian man / who in his figure stands twofold / as the Adamic man <term>Adamische Mensch: the natural, fallen human nature inherited from Adam</term> in his nature is Benjamin / and the new man out of the Covenant in Christ’s Spirit is indicated by Joseph; and the figure stands / as to how Christ has taken the Adamic man upon himself / so that this man is half Adamic and half Heavenly / and stands there entirely as one person / which may not be separated.

51. So also he figures Christendom in this image / how they would accept Christ and become Christians / where both Christ and also the *evil wolf Adam* would rule in them / that is / when they would accept the faith / they would be as greedy and zealous as a wolf / and would draw the heathens to themselves with power / but would also devour them / that is / if people did not want to hold the same opinion as them in everything / they would begin to condemn other opinions / and also to persecute them with war and sword / as an angry lion or wolf bites and devours / so they will devour around them in their zeal with bans and the sword / and this for the sake / not that they would be so zealous in Christ’s Spirit / but out of the *wolf of the evil Adam* / which would always swing itself above the Spirit of Christ in both spiritual and worldly estates.

52. 53. So now the spirit of Jacob, within the Covenant of God, indicates the timing of how things would go: in the first era of **Christendom**, they would be zealous and hunger for God in the Spirit of Christ, yet they would have to hide themselves and crawl away from enemies, like a **wolf** that is pursued as an enemy. <note>Böhme refers to the early Christians who, though filled with spiritual zeal, were persecuted and forced into hiding like hunted animals.</note>

54. But when they would become great and possess kingdoms—that is, when the Name of Christ would come under the power of **Dan** <note>In Böhme's thought, "Dan" often represents the transition from spiritual freedom to rigid, worldly law and judgment.</note>, so that laws and ordinances would arise out of Christian liberty, and their orders would come under worldly power and dominion—then this Christendom would become a **wolf** which would no longer judge or act in the love of Christ. Instead, whoever would not approve of their **orders of the belly** <term>Bauchorden: Böhme’s derogatory term for clergy or religious orders more concerned with their own material comfort and "bellies" than with spiritual truth</term>, they would devour with the sword of the ban, fire, and vengeance. They would stir up wars over the Name of Christ and their own statutes, forcing the nations to the confession of Christ with violence, and devouring all around them like a wolf, hunting forever after prey, though mostly meaning only the goods and power of foreign peoples.

55. Thus, this wolf **Benjamin** would devour prey in the morning—that is, in his rising—and toward the evening he would distribute this devoured prey again. This means toward the end of the world, when **Joseph’s** government shall swing itself upward again so that Christ will become entirely manifest. When this wolf-nature ceases, then **Benjamin**, as the true Christendom, shall distribute the **spoil of Christ**, which Christ has wrestled away from death and hell.

<margin>[</margin>
56. This distribution is still to come and has already come, and yet is not yet here; and although it is truly here, the entire world is blind to it, except for the **Children of the Mystery**. The time *is*, and *is not*, and yet is truthful, when this spoil of Christ, and also the wolf’s spoil, shall be given through **Joseph’s** hand into **Benjamin’s** hand and be distributed.

57. Let that be a wonder to you, **Babel** <note>Böhme uses "Babel" to describe the confused, divided, and institutionalized state of the formal church.</note>, and yet no wonder at all: for you have nothing and see nothing for which you could wonder. It is just as a small sapling grows out of a seed and becomes a great tree that brings forth much beautiful fruit; one should wonder at the grain or seed, how such a precious tree and so much good fruit were hidden in a single grain, which was neither recognized nor seen. Because one has only a scientific knowledge <note>original: "Wissenschafft"</note> that it is possible for a tree to come from a seed, one does not wonder at it; for one does not see how that happens, or where the great power has been. So it is also now: one sees the grain becoming a tree, but **Reason** <term>Vernunfft: human intellect or logic when it is separated from divine revelation</term> despises it and does not believe that such a tree lies within it, from which so much good fruit shall come, so that thereby Benjamin’s kingdom at the end of time shall be called a "distribution of the spoil."

### Explanation of the Testament of Jacob /

<margin>Genesis 43</margin>
58. But Joseph must first become a regent in Egypt; only then does Benjamin come to him. Then Joseph gives him five festive garments <note>original: "Feyerkleyder"—referring to the "changes of raiment" mentioned in Genesis 45:22</note> and five times more food from his table than the others. When the famine causes the land to languish and the soul of Jacob hungers, know that God thereby intends to turn Israel toward Egypt, as if into repentance <note>original: "Busse"—meaning both penance and a change of heart</note>. This is then the time of trial, and Benjamin carries his sword of prey in his mouth. But Joseph’s countenance strikes him, so that he falls into a great terror and fear of death because Joseph’s silver cup was found in his sack, for which he is ashamed. He lets the sword of prey along with the wolf's teeth fall from him. There, Joseph reveals himself to him and all his brothers, and from this arises such joy that the wolf Benjamin becomes a lamb that patiently gives up its wool. This is the end of the speech.

59. The Testament of Jacob is a figure <note>Böhme uses "figure" to mean a prophetic archetype or symbolic representation</note> of the entire age of the world: from Adam until the end. We wish to sketch a brief figure of this for the reader who is familiar with these visions to contemplate.

60. I. **Reuben** is placed in this position because he was the first in the figure of the first world, which lived in natural law <term>Naturrecht: the state of humanity guided by conscience and nature before the formal Law of Moses</term> without legislation. That world possessed both priesthood and kingdom in natural law and was meant to be in the highest sacrifice and greatest dominion; but he passed away lightly like water and was cast out.

61. II. **Simeon** begins under Noah after the Great Flood and kept Levi with him; that was Shem. But the sword of Ham and Japheth was Simeon: thus two went together in one being, as spiritual willing and fleshly willing, until Moses, where the worldly and spiritual separated into two estates <note>original: "2. Stände"—referring to the formal division of secular and religious authority</note>.

62. III. **Levi** begins under Moses, who, through the priesthood, wielded the sword of Simeon and Levi in the Law and cut very sharply with it.

63. IV. **Judah** begins under the Prophets and reveals himself with the Incarnation of Christ, where this scepter began.

64. V. **Zebulun**, with his indwelling, placed himself in the middle as if into the Kingdom of Christ. That was the beginning of Christendom, which lived at the shore of the sea, as if among the heathens, and yet they sat well: for it was a new love.

65. VI. **Issachar** is the time when Christendom established itself in rest, that is, in power and dominions, yet always had to bear the burden of the heathens and be tributary, and be like a bony donkey <note>A reference to Genesis 49:14; Böhme interprets this "bony donkey" as a symbol of the Church enduring worldly burdens</note> under a load. For they still bore the cross of Christ and were still like the image of Christ, around the year 300 after Christ.

He emphasizes the transition of Benjamin from a "wolf" to a "lamb" as a symbol of spiritual repentance and reconciliation with Christ.</summary>

66. VII. With **Dan** began the mighty kingdom of Christendom, when they established kings, popes, great bishops, and powerful, magnificent churches and foundations; there the adder and serpent were born on the way of Christ in human honors, within Christ’s kingdom. This was when men began to dispute over the church’s splendor, prestige, and glory, and to elevate men within Christ’s kingdom and offices, placing them in Christ’s stead and honoring them in His place. Thus, Christ was suppressed, and the adder and serpent declared themselves to be in Christ’s office of judge; for there the Holy Spirit was rejected and the Councils <note>original: "Concilia"—the ecclesiastical assemblies that defined church doctrine</note> were put in its place, and the Antichrist was born. At that time, the Spirit of Christ spoke: "Lord, I wait now for your salvation"; for here my name must now be the cover for the Antichrist, until you shall release me again during Joseph’s time. In this era, the truth was violently bitten in the heels, so that the rider in Christ’s Spirit had to fall back.

67. VIII. With **Gad**, who was to be the troop leader, begins the era of the universities <note>original: "hohen Schulen"—literally "high schools," referring to the medieval universities and the rise of Scholasticism</note> among the Christians, roughly 800 years ago. This was when the Antichrist, armed with power and military force, was seated upon Christ’s throne and defended with heavy disputations and circular reasoning. There, the tail was made into the head, and the power of Christ was forced into human ordinances, making a worldly kingdom out of Christ’s kingdom.

68. IX. With **Asher** begins the time when men lived to please the king—the Antichrist—when he became "God on earth." Then the hypocrites came from the universities, who flattered this king for the sake of "fat bread"—meaning good offices, prebends <term>Prebends: A portion of the revenues of a cathedral or collegiate church, used as a stipend for a clergyman</term>, and bishoprics—and they praised his cause and did everything to please him. They placed Christ and the Antichrist together on a soft cushion, and thus they worshipped the "image" in the Apocalypse <note>original: "Apocalyphi"—referring to the Book of Revelation</note>, about 600 years ago and closer to our time.

69. X. With **Naphtali** begins the era of great wonders, when men dealt with lofty speeches and profound thoughts concerning the counsel of God. When it was seen that this figure on Christ’s throne was not Christ in power, men searched deeply to see if they could cover him with a mantle of beautiful, respectable conclusions. Then sharp Logic <note>original: "Logica"</note> arose, through which men disputed: one party said he was Christ in power and authority; the other spoke against it. While his faction, with high outward appearance, placed him within the blood of Christ and attributed all power to him, turning it into holy speech, the Spirit of Christ in the inward ground set itself against it and said: "He is the Antichrist." This era has lasted until our own time, in which we live.

70. XI. With **Joseph** begins the time when Christ becomes manifest again, when

This we have wished to outline a little for the lover of truth; may he further investigate it in the Spirit of God, which searches all things, even into the depths of the Deity, and then he will see our foundation in truth.

# Concerning the Burial of the Holy Patriarch Jacob in the Land of Canaan.

<margin>Chapter 78</margin>

2. But that many Egyptians also traveled there and accompanied Joseph signifies that Christ, when he brings his Bride <note>the soul or the collective body of believers</note> home into Paradise, will have many strangers with him who, in this life, did not recognize him in person or office, yet grew up in his love within him; all of whom will go with Christ into Paradise and dwell with him.

3. 4. Now, dearly, forgive the misdeed of us, the servants of the God of your father." But Joseph wept as they spoke such things with him; and his brothers went and fell down before him and said: "Behold, we are your servants." Joseph said to them: "Do not fear, for I am under God. You intended to do evil to me, but God intended to make it good, so that he might do as it is this day: to preserve many people. So do not fear now; I will provide for you and your children." And he comforted them and spoke kindly with them.

5. This figure <note>a symbolic or prophetic representation</note> is a mighty comfort to Joseph’s brothers; but because Joseph stands in the image of Christ, and his brothers in the figure of poor converted sinners, we must also interpret this figure thus: that is, when the poor sinful human, who has committed great sins, has turned to repentance and attained grace, and perhaps commits a lapse again, he stands forever in fear and trembling before God’s grace. He thinks God will again count his first committed sin against him and take occasion from this lapse; he stands, therefore, in great anxieties and begins again to confess the first committed sin, and falls anew at the Lord’s feet, and enters again into earnest repentance and weeps for his first misdeed, as David did when he said: *Lord, do not count against me the sins of my youth.*

# Short Extract of the Highly Spiritual Contemplation of the *Great Mystery*,
## how the visible world is an outflow and reflection of Divine Knowledge and Will: How all creaturely life took its origin, and how the Divine goes out and in.

All sensory and perceptible life and being has come from the *Great Mystery* <note>original: "Mysterio Magno"; in Boehme's thought, this refers to the "chaos" or potentiality from which God brings forth the universe</note>, as from the outflow and reflection of Divine knowledge, wherein two things are to be understood by us: namely, the free will of the Unground <term>Unground: "Vngrund," the groundless abyss of God's existence prior to any self-expression or creation</term> and the essential One within the Will, how these two are a reflection of the Unground, as a ground of Divine Revelation; how they are two and yet only one, from which time and the visible world along with all creatures have flowed and entered into a created form.

2. The single One is the cause of the Will, which causes the Will to want something; and yet it has nothing it can want except itself as a ground and place for its "I-ness" <term>I-ness: "Ichheit," the quality of selfhood or the emergence of an individual identity from the void</term>. It has nothing it can grasp except the One; within that, it grasps itself into an "I-ness" so that the Will might have something in which and with which it works—which working would be no visible being if it did not go out through the Will.

3. Thus the outgoing is a spirit of the invisible Will and being, and a revelation of the Unground through the ground of Unity: through which outgoing the Will of the Unground throws itself against the Unground as a *mystery* of All-Knowing. With this outgoing is understood the cause and origin of all the distinctness of the Unity of the ungrounded Will through its own ground of its enclosed selfhood—also the eternal beginning of movement and the cause of life. This movement is an everlasting delight of the Will: For the Will thus beholds the Unity through movement, just as the Unity stands in infinite multiplicity through the Will's movement, in the manner and way that the Mind <term>Mind: "Gemüte," the deep seat of the soul, encompassing the will, reason, and senses</term> is a unity and wellspring of the senses, since such a depth of multiplicity arises from the single Mind, which are innumerable.

<summary>This page introduces a metaphysical summary of how the visible universe originated from the "Unground" (the divine abyss) through the interaction of the Divine Will and the "Great Mystery." It explains the transition from an invisible, unified state into the diverse and perceptible world of creatures and time.</summary>
<keywords>Great Mystery, Unground, Divine Will, Revelation, I-ness, Multiplicity, Mind, Outflow, Reflection</keywords>

Completed on the date of September 11, Anno 1623.

# A Short Extract of the Highly Spiritual Contemplation of the
### <term>Great Mystery</term> <note>original: *Mysterii Magni*; refers to the hidden, divine source of all creation</note>, how the visible world is an outflow and
### counter-throw <note>original: *Gegenwurff*; a central concept in Boehme's thought, suggesting the physical world is a reflection or "objectification" of the divine mind</note> of Divine knowledge and will: How all
### creaturely life took its origin / and
### how the Divine goes out and in.

All sensory and perceptible life and being has come from the <term>Great Mystery</term> <note>original: *Mysterio Magno*</note>, as the outflow and counter-throw of Divine knowledge / wherein two things are for us to understand / namely the free will of the <term>Unground</term> <note>original: *Vngrundes*; the "groundless" or "abyssal" state of God before or beyond manifestation</note> / and the essential "One" within the will / how these both are a counter-throw of the <term>Unground</term> / as a ground of Divine Revelation / how they are two and yet only one / from which time and the visible world, along with all creatures, have flowed / and have entered into a created being.

2. The single One is the cause of the will / which causes the will so that it wills something / and yet it has nothing that it can will / except only itself for a ground and a place of its <term>selfhood</term> <note>original: *Ichheit*; literally "I-ness" or the state of being an individual "I"</note>: It has nothing that it can grasp / except only the One / therein it grasps itself into a selfhood / so that the will may have something / in which and with which it works / which working would be no visible being / if it did not go out through the will.

3. Thus the outcome <note>original: *Außgang*</note> is now a spirit of the invisible will and being / and a manifestation of the <term>Unground</term> through the ground of unity: through which outcome the will of the <term>Unground</term> / throws itself toward the <term>Unground</term> / as a <term>mystery</term> <note>original: *Mysterium*</note> of omniscience / with which outcome the cause and origin of all divisibility <note>original: *schiedlichkeit*</note> of the unity of the groundless will is understood through its own ground of its enclosed selfhood / also the Eternal beginning of movement and the cause of life / which movement is an everlasting delight of the will: For the will thus beholds the unity through the movement / just as the unity stands in infinite multiplicity through the movement of the will / in the manner and way that the mind <note>original: *Gemüte*</note> is a unity and the fountainhead of the senses / since such a depth of multiplicity springs from the single mind / which are innumerable.

For this reason, during this time, they must endure the curse as the fleeing of God's will and remain in such an impression until the day of restoration.

7. No thing can rest in itself unless it returns again into the One from which it proceeded. The mind has turned away from Unity into its own desire for perception, to test the <term>distinctness</term> <note>original: *schiedlichkeit*; the state of being separate or diverse</note> of the properties; through this, distinctness and opposition have arisen within it, which now rule the mind. It cannot be delivered from this unless it abandons itself in the desire of the properties and swings itself back into the purest stillness, desiring to keep its own willing silent. In this way, the *will deepens itself above all sensory perception and imagery into the Eternal Will of the <term>Unground</term> <note>original: *Vngrund*; the "bottomless" or "abyss," referring to the absolute nothingness/everything of God before creation</note>, from which it originally arose out of the <term>Great Mystery</term> <note>original: *Mysterio Magno*; the chaos or "mother" of all beings</note>;* so that it no longer wills anything in itself except what God wills through it. Then it is in the deepest ground of Unity. And if it can stand therein for a short while without the movement of its own desire, then the Will of the Unground speaks into it from Divine movement and gathers its <term>surrendered</term> <note>original: *gelassenen*; a key term in German mysticism meaning "resigned" or "letting go"</note> will into itself as its own possession. It then leads into it the <term>essential substance</term> <note>original: *Ens*; a philosophical term for the "being" or "essence" of a thing</note> of the Eternal Incomprehensibility of the City of God, as the essential One.

8. And just as the Will of the Eternal Godhead eternally proceeds through the Eternal Spirit and creates a <term>counter-throw</term> <note>original: *Gegenwurff*; a reflection or mirror-image</note> of the <term>Unground</term>, so too is the surrendered will of the mind always carried forth and enlightened by Divine comprehension with God’s Will. Thus, the human mind rules within God’s Will, in Divine knowledge and <term>science</term> <note>original: *wissenschafft*; meaning certain, divine knowledge rather than modern laboratory science</note>, over and through all things. This is what Moses meant when he said that man should rule over all the creatures of the world. Just as God’s Spirit goes through everything and tests everything, so too may the enlightened mind rule over and through all properties of natural life and overcome them. It introduces the highest sensibility from Divine knowledge into reason, as Saint Paul says: "The Spirit searches all things, even the depths of the Godhead." And with such an introduction...

Once aligned with the Divine Will, the mind gains a spiritual dominion and insight that transcends the material world, as referenced through Moses and St. Paul.</summary>

4. With such a threefold Unity, we contemplate the Essence of God: as with the Unity, the one God; with the Will, the Father; and with the Enclosure of the Will as the place of <term>selfhood</term> <note>original: *Selbheit*; the quality of being a distinct "I"</note>—as the Eternal "Something" that works, or through which the Will works—the Son, or the Power of the Will; and with the Outgoing, the Spirit of the Will and the Power; and by the <term>Counter-reflection</term> <note>original: *Gegenwurff*; a reflection or object that stands opposite to a viewer</note> one understands the Wisdom of Understanding, out of which all wonders and essences have flowed and eternally flow.

5. From the movement of this invisible, active Essence, from the outflow of Eternal Knowledge <note>original: *wissenschafft*; used here in the archaic sense of divine "knowing"</note>, Understanding has flowed forth. There, the Delight gazed upon itself and introduced itself into a Desire for imagery <note>original: *Bildlichkeit*; the state of having form or being a representation</note>. In this Desire, the natural and creaturely foundation of all life and all essence arose, because the Desire grasped and enclosed the outflow of knowledge into "properties." From this, two kinds of will have arisen: one from Divine Science <note>original: *Scienz*; from the Latin *scientia*, meaning knowledge</note> or knowledge, and the other from the property of nature. In the latter, the properties introduced themselves into their own will and impressed themselves with self-interest and their own will, making themselves rough, sharp, prickly, and hard. Because of such properties, resistance and enmity arose against the knowledge; as can be seen in the properties of the devils, as well as in the rough earth, stones, and creatures—how the properties turned away from the Unity and entered into an "impression" <note>original: *impression*; a spiritual contraction or hardening into matter</note>. For this reason, in this time, they must also endure the curse—the fleeing of the Divine Will—and must remain in such an "impression" until the day of restoration.
